# First Section: Chapter 16 on Indicating Curses from Previous Births

The wise astrologer should declare all outcomes according to the planetary combinations. From auspicious positions, happiness is indicated; from mixed positions, mixed results are proclaimed. 46.

One should perform a ritual bathing at the Setu <note>original: "setu-snānam"; refers to the sacred bridge at Rameshwaram, a major pilgrimage site</note> and perform one hundred thousand recitations of the Gayatri mantra. A gift to the planets should be made, specifically a silver vessel filled with milk. 47.

Likewise, one should feed the Brahmins <note>The priestly and scholarly class</note> and perform circumambulations of the Ashvattha tree <note>original: "aśvattha"; the sacred fig tree (Ficus religiosa), considered a living deity in Hindu tradition</note>. This must be done with devotion, completing twenty-eight thousand rounds. 48.

O Goddess! When these things are done, there will be liberation from the curse. Afterward, he will obtain a virtuous son, and his lineage will grow. 49.

Now I shall speak of the causes of curses involving a brother and others, determined by malefic associations, the state of the astrological houses, and the strength of the significators <note>original: "kārakas"; specific planets that represent people or themes, such as Mars for brothers</note>. 50.

If the lord of the third house <note>The house representing siblings</note> is in the house of children <note>The fifth house</note> combined with Mars and Rahu, and the lords of the Ascendant and the fifth house are in the eighth house, there is a loss of offspring due to a brother's curse. 51.

If Mars and Saturn are in the Ascendant and the fifth house, while the lord of the third house is in the house of fortune <note>The ninth house</note>, and the significator is in the house of destruction <note>The eighth house</note>, there is a loss of offspring due to a brother's curse. 52.

If Jupiter <note>The significator of children</note> is in the third house in its debilitated sign, while Saturn is in the fifth house, and the lords of the eighth and ninth houses are not well-placed, there is a loss of offspring due to a brother's curse. 53.

If the lord of the Ascendant is in the twelfth house, Mars is in the fifth house, and the lord of the house of children is in the eighth house with a malefic planet, there is a loss of offspring due to a brother's curse. 54.

If the Ascendant is hemmed between malefic planets and the fifth house is also hemmed between malefics, and both their lords and the significator are in difficult houses, there is a loss of offspring due to a brother's curse. 55.

If the lord of the tenth house is in the house of brothers, and the fifth house contains a benefic planet but is also occupied by Mars, there is a loss of offspring due to a brother's curse. 56.

If the house of children falls in a sign ruled by Mercury but is occupied by Saturn and Rahu, and the twelfth house contains the Sun and Mars, then by the nature of the curse, there is a loss of offspring due to a brother's curse. 57.

If the lord of the Ascendant is in the sign representing the brother <note>the third house</note>, and the lord of the third house is in the house of children, and malefic planets are in the Ascendant and the third house, there is a loss of offspring due to a brother's curse. 58.

If the lord of the third house is in the house of destruction <note>eighth house</note> and the significator is in the house of children, joined or aspected by Rahu and Mandi <note>A mathematical point in the sky considered malefic</note>, there is a loss of offspring due to a brother's curse. 59.

If the lord of the eighth house is in the house of children joined with the lord of the third house, and Mars and Saturn are in the eighth house, there is a loss of offspring due to a brother's curse. 60.

To be liberated from a brother's curse, one should listen to the recitation of the scriptures and the chanting of the names of Vishnu. Afterward, one should perform the Chandrayana <note>A lunar penance where the practitioner's food intake increases and decreases with the phases of the moon</note> penance at the Kaveri river in the presence of Vishnu. 61.

One should plant an Ashvattha tree and donate ten cows. One should perform the Prajapatya <note>A specific three-day fast or religious vow</note> penance there and give away fertile land. 62.

He who performs this with devotion...

...an increase in sons is produced. 63.

If Mercury and Jupiter are in the house of children <note>the 5th house</note> along with Mars and Rahu, and Saturn is joined with the Ascendant, there will be a loss of sons due to a curse from a maternal uncle. 64.

If the lords of the Ascendant and the house of children are both in the 5th house along with Mercury and Mars, while Saturn is present there, progeny will be destroyed due to a maternal uncle's curse. 65.

If the lord of the house of children is weakened and placed in the Ascendant, while Saturn <note>original: "bhānu-nandane"; literally "son of the Sun," a common epithet for Saturn</note> is in the seventh house, and the lord of the Ascendant is joined with Mercury, his lineage will be destroyed. 66.

If the lord of the house of kinsmen <note>the 6th house</note> is in the Ascendant joined with the lord of the twelfth house, and the Moon, Mercury, and Mars are in the house of children, his lineage will be destroyed. 67.

If the lord of the house of children and the lord of the Ascendant are joined, or aspecting one another, or if they are positioned in each other's houses <note>specifically within the 5th house</note>, these are known as "Unions for Children" <note>term: "Putra-yogas"; planetary alignments that favor the birth of offspring</note>. 68.

To remedy that flaw, the installation of a Vishnu image <note>term: "Vishnu-sthapana"; a ritual placement of a deity statue for worship</note> is prescribed, as is the construction of stepped wells, regular wells, and ponds, or visiting the sacred bridge <note>referring to Rameshwaram</note>. 69.

Then, an increase of sons and an increase in wealth will occur for him. A wise astrologer should declare these results according to the planetary unions. 70.

# The Curse of a Brahmin

When Rahu is in a sign owned by Jupiter <note>Sagittarius or Pisces</note> while Jupiter, Mars, and Saturn are in the house of children, and the lord of the house of fortune <note>the 9th house</note> is in a house of destruction, loss of sons occurs due to a Brahmin’s curse. 71.

That mortal who, out of pride in his own learning, insults Brahmins—due to the sin of that Brahmin’s curse, his progeny will be destroyed. 72.

If the lord of the house of fortune is in the house of children, and the lord of the house of children is in a sign of destruction <note>the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses</note>, while Jupiter, Mars, and Rahu are in the house of death <note>the 8th house</note>, loss of sons occurs due to a Brahmin’s curse. 73.

If the lord of the house of fortune is in its sign of debilitation, and the lord of the twelfth house is in the sign of children <note>the 5th house</note>, and is either joined with or aspected by Rahu, loss of sons occurs due to a Brahmin's curse. 74.

If Jupiter is in its sign of debilitation while Rahu is in the Ascendant or the house of children, and the lord of the house of children is in a house of sorrow <note>the 6th, 8th, or 12th</note>, loss of sons occurs due to a Brahmin's curse. 75.

If Jupiter is the lord of the house of children but is placed in the eighth house joined with malefic planets, or if the lord of children is with the Sun and Moon, loss of sons occurs due to a Brahmin's curse. 76.

If Jupiter is in the divisional sign of Saturn <note>manda-amsha</note> and joined with Saturn and Mars, while the lord of the house of children is in the twelfth house, loss of sons occurs due to a Brahmin’s curse. 77.

If Jupiter is in the Ascendant with Saturn, and Rahu is in the house of fortune <note>9th house</note>, and the lord of the twelfth house is joined with Jupiter, loss of sons occurs due to a Brahmin’s curse. 78.

To pacify that flaw, a person should perform the Chandrayana penance <note>term: "Cāndrāyaṇa"; a fast where food intake follows the phases of the moon</note>. Having performed three "Brahma-kurcha" rituals <note>a purification rite using the five products of the cow</note>, one should gift a cow along with a cash donation. 79.

Five gems should be given along with gold. Then, one should perform the gifting of food to ten thousand or one thousand Brahmins. 80.

By doing this, he will certainly obtain a virtuous son; there is no doubt here. Liberated from the curse...

If <term>Jupiter</term> <note>original: "Jive"</note> is in the <term>Vargottama: the best division where a planet occupies the same zodiac sign in both the main chart and the 9th divisional chart</term>, and the lord of the Ascendant's divisional sign is a benefic planet, and is joined with or aspected by the **Lord of the 5th House** <note>original: "Putreshena"</note>, these are known as combinations for children. 117.

If the **Lord of the 2nd House** <note>original: "Vitteshe"; the house of wealth and family</note> is placed in the 5th house <note>the house of children</note> and is endowed with complete strength, and Jupiter is in a <term>Vaisheshika: a high-quality divisional dignity</term> portion, these are known as combinations for children. 118.

If the Lord of Children <note>5th house</note> is in its sign of exaltation <note>its highest point of strength</note> as measured from the Ascendant, and is aspected by its own lord or they exchange places <note>original: "Paraspara-sthana-gate"</note>, these are known as combinations for children. 119.

If the **Lord of the sign where the 5th house ruler is located in the 9th divisional chart** <note>original: "Putra-sthanadhipasyamsha-rashishe"</note> is joined with a benefic planet or is aspected by one, these are known as combinations for children. 120.

If the lords of the Ascendant and the 5th house are in <term>Kendras: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the pillars of the chart</term> combined with benefic planets, and the Lord of the 2nd house <note>original: "Kutumbeshe"; the house of family</note> is strong, these are known as combinations for children. 121.

If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the **house of the spouse** <note>original: "Darabhavasthe"; the 7th house</note> and the **Lord of the 7th house** <note>original: "Dareshe"</note> is placed in the Ascendant, while the Lord of the 2nd house is in the Ascendant, these are known as combinations for children. 122.

If the Lord of the 7th house is joined by a planet, or the ruler of the 9th divisional sign, or the Lords of the 5th, 2nd, and Ascendant are combined, these are known as combinations for children. 123.

...such a person obtains a child after a long time. 133. 

When a <term>benefic planet: a planet that traditionally brings good fortune, like Jupiter or Venus</term> <note>original: "saumye"</note> is in the <term>Ascendant: the first house, representing the self</term>, a <term>malefic planet: a planet that brings challenges, like Mars or Saturn</term> <note>original: "pape"</note> is in the 2nd house, and a malefic planet is in the 3rd house, while the **Lord of the 5th House** <note>original: "putreshe"</note> is situated in an auspicious sign, the person obtains a child after a long time. 134.

**Combinations for an Adopted Child** <note>original: "Dattaputra-yoga"</note>

When <term>Mars</term> <note>original: "kuje"</note> or <term>Saturn</term> <note>original: "mande"</note> is in the house of children <note>the 5th house</note>, and that house belongs to a sign ruled by <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: "budha-kshetre"; i.e., Gemini or Virgo</term>, and the Lord of the Ascendant is either aspected by or joined with Mercury, then children such as an **adopted son** are indicated. 135.

If the 5th house is in a sign of Mercury <note>Gemini/Virgo</note> or Saturn <note>Capricorn/Aquarius</note>, and is joined with or aspected by Saturn or <term>Gulika: a sensitive mathematical point in the chart considered malefic</term> <note>original: "mandi"</note>, then children such as an adopted son are indicated. 136.

If Mercury is in the 5th house, or if the 5th house is in a sign of Mercury and is aspected by Mercury, or if the Lord of the Ascendant is Saturn, then there will indeed be adopted children. 137.

When the Lord of the 5th House is joined with Saturn, and Mars is aspected by a benefic planet, or if the Lord of the Ascendant is in a <term>division of Mercury: a specific portion of the zodiac ruled by Mercury</term> <note>original: "budhamsha"</note>, then there will indeed be adopted children. 138.

When the Lord of the 7th House <note>the house of partners</note> is in the 11th house <note>the house of gains</note>, and the Lord of the 5th House is joined with a benefic, and Saturn or Mercury is in the 5th house, then there will indeed be adopted children. 139.

If the Lord of the 5th House is in the 9th house <note>the house of fortune</note>, and the Lord of the 9th House is in the 10th house <note>the house of actions/career</note>, but the 5th house is aspected by Saturn, the lineage will continue through an adopted son. 140.

If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the exaltation sign of <term>Venus</term> <note>original: "bhrigoshchocche"; i.e., Pisces</term>, and Saturn is in the 5th house while the <term>Significator of Children: Jupiter</term> <note>original: "karake"</note> is endowed with strength, the lineage continues through an adopted son. 141.

If the Lord of the 5th House is the <term>Moon</term> <note>original: "chandre"</note>, and Saturn is in the 5th house while the Moon is in the Ascendant, and Jupiter is at full strength, an excellent son will be obtained through adoption. 142.

If the <term>Sun</term> <note>original: "ravau"</note> is the Lord of the 5th House and is in the Ascendant, while Saturn and Mercury are in the 5th house, and the Lord of the 5th House is strong, an excellent son will be obtained through adoption. 143.

If the Lord of the Ascendant is Mercury and is in the 5th house joined with the aspect of Mars, while the Significator <note>Jupiter</note> is in the 11th house, an excellent son will be obtained through adoption. 144.

If the Lord of the Ascendant is Jupiter and is in the 5th house joined with the aspect of Saturn, and the Lord of the 5th House is in a sign of Mars <note>Aries or Scorpio</note>, then there will be adopted children. 145.

**Remedies for the Continuation of Lineage**

When the family lineage seems to end, the following remedies are prescribed based on the planets: if the Sun or Moon are involved, one should recite the <term>Harivansha: a sacred text detailing the lineage of Lord Krishna</term> <note>original: "hari-krishna-gau"; the footnote specifies this refers to the Harivansha scripture</note>; if Mars, one should worship the "Slayer of Tripura" <note>Lord Shiva</note> or perform rituals for the Earth; if Mercury, one should perform the ritual of the bronze vessel <note>original: "samputaka-kamsyapatra-vidhi"</note>; if Jupiter, one should feed guests in honor of the ancestors; if Venus, one should care for and protect cows; if Saturn, one should recite the <term>Mrityunjaya: a powerful mantra dedicated to Lord Shiva for overcoming death and illness</term>; if Rahu or Ketu, one should perform <term>Kanyadana: the gift of a daughter in marriage</term> or rituals involving a serpent or a Kapila cow. These provide the happiness of offspring. 146.

One should perform these rituals as many times as indicated by the number of the zodiac sign. Happiness comes from the installation of Shiva and Vishnu icons and the removal of defects that cause the loss of children. 147.

### This concludes the Sixteenth Chapter, titled "Description of the Results for the House of Children," in the Summary of the First Section of the Great Parashara Horoscopy.

<note>Technical Terms:
<term>Trikona Shodhana (Trinal Reduction)</term>: A method of reducing planetary points by comparing signs that are 120 degrees apart (sharing the same element).
<term>Ekadhipatya Shodhana (Dual-Lordship Reduction)</term>: A secondary reduction applied to signs ruled by the same planet (e.g., Mars rules both Aries and Scorpio).
<term>Pinda (Sum/Aggregate)</term>: The final mathematical product used for longevity and prosperity calculations.</note>

## Now, an example of Trinal Reduction is given.

<insert>
**Birth Chart (Janmanga Chakra)**
<note>This diagram shows the positions of the planets in the zodiac signs at the time of birth. In this North Indian style chart, the numbers represent the signs: 1 is Aries, 2 is Taurus, etc.</note>
| | | |
| :--- | :---: | ---: |
| 3 (Gemini) | 2 (Taurus) Ketu <br> Mars 12, Venus | 1 (Aries) |
| 4 (Cancer) | <center>11 (Aquarius) Sun <br> Jupiter</center> | 10 (Capricorn) Mercury |
| 5 (Leo) | <center>9 (Sagittarius) Moon</center> | 8 (Scorpio) Rahu |
| 6 (Virgo) | 7 (Libra) | |
</insert>

Among the three signs forming a trine <note>original: "Trikona." In astrology, signs of the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water) form trines. For example, Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius are the Fire trine.</note>, the lowest number of points <note>Rekha-phala: "auspicious points" or "lines."</note> must be subtracted from all three signs. For example, in the Sun's <term>Ashtakavarga</term> (the system of eight-fold points), let us look at the first trine:
*   **Aries:** 2 points
*   **Leo:** 3 points
*   **Sagittarius:** 4 points
The lowest value among these is 2. Subtracting 2 from each, we get: Sagittarius becomes 2, Aries becomes 0, and Leo becomes 1.

Similarly, for the second trine:
*   **Taurus:** 3 points
*   **Virgo:** 7 points
*   **Capricorn:** 3 points
Subtracting the lowest value (3) from all three, we get: Capricorn becomes 0, Taurus becomes 0, and Virgo becomes 4.

For the third trine:
*   **Aquarius:** 5 points
*   **Gemini:** 4 points
*   **Libra:** 6 points
Subtracting the lowest value (4), we get: Libra becomes 2, Gemini becomes 0, and Aquarius becomes 1.

For the fourth trine:
*   **Pisces:** 4 points
*   **Cancer:** 3 points
*   **Scorpio:** 4 points
Subtracting the lowest value (3), we get: Cancer becomes 0, Scorpio becomes 1, and Pisces becomes 1.
This describes the **first rule**.

If any one of the three signs in a trine already has zero points, then no trinal reduction should be performed in that group. The points should remain exactly as they are in all three places. This is shown in a hypothetical example: if Taurus has 3 points, Virgo has 5, and Capricorn has 0, then the points are left as they are because one is already zero. This is the **second rule** regarding the absence of trinal reduction.

If the points in all three signs of a trine are equal, then all three must be reduced to zero. For example, in Jupiter's <term>Ashtakavarga</term>:
*   **Taurus:** 6 points
*   **Virgo:** 6 points
*   **Capricorn:** 6 points
Since the points are equal, zero is placed in all three signs. This logic applies everywhere. This is the **third rule**.

Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, titled "Trinal Reduction," in the summary of the first part of the Great Parashara Hora.

This refers to planets that rule two different zodiac signs (e.g., Mars rules Aries and Scorpio).</note>. When a planet owns two signs and both contain points, the wise astrologer should reduce them as follows: If one sign has fewer points than the other, subtract—

...in a sign without a planet. If a sign occupied by a planet has fewer points, and the sign without a planet has more points, the difference should be calculated. ॥ 2 ॥ One should subtract the points of the sign with a planet from the points of the other sign that lacks a planet. If the sign with a planet has more points, one should discard all the points in the other empty sign. ॥ 3 ॥ If both signs are occupied by planets, no reduction should ever be made. ### Now, an Example of Reduction for Dual-Lordship.

<term>Dual-Lordship Reduction</term> <note>original: "Ekadhipatya Shodhana." This is the second step of "purifying" the points in an astrological chart. It applies to planets like Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn, who each rule two zodiac signs.</note> involves a specific logic for planets like Mars and the others who own two signs. If, of the two signs owned by a single planet, one contains a planet and has fewer points, while the second contains no planet and has more points, then you must subtract the smaller value from the larger value in the empty sign. The remainder is then placed in that empty sign.

To illustrate this, let us use a hypothetical example:
Suppose Gemini <note>ruled by Mercury</note> contains a planet and, after the previous Trinal Reduction, has 3 points. Suppose Virgo <note>also ruled by Mercury</note> contains no planet and has 4 points. In this case, the 3 points from Gemini are subtracted from the 4 points of Virgo. The remainder (1) is placed under Gemini, and the 3 is placed under Virgo. <note>The text here illustrates a specific mathematical distribution where the points are adjusted based on the lordship.</note>

Furthermore, if one sign has more points and contains a planet, while the other sign has fewer points and no planet, then the points in the sign with the planet are left as they are, and the points in the sign without the planet are completely removed (set to zero). 

For example: Suppose Pisces <note>ruled by Jupiter</note> has a planet and 4 points, while Sagittarius <note>also ruled by Jupiter</note> has no planet and fewer points. In this case, the 4 points under Pisces remain as they are, and a zero is placed under Sagittarius.

Again, if both signs owned by the same planet contain planets, then no reduction is made. For example, in the <term>Sun's Ashtakavarga</term> <note>A system of points calculated specifically for the Sun's influence.</note>, if Pisces contains a planet and has 1 point, and Sagittarius also contains a planet and has 2 points, no reduction occurs, and the points are left as they are.

Finally, if both signs are without planets and have an equal number of points, all points should be discarded. This is the rule of...

...in both [signs], a zero should be placed. For example, in the <term>Ashtakavarga</term> <note>A system of "Eight-fold Divisions" used to calculate the strength of planets based on their positions relative to others.</note> of Venus: if the result below Taurus is 1 and the result of the <term>Trinal Reduction</term> <note>original: "Trikona-shodhana." The first stage of reducing points in this system.</note> below Libra is also 1, and if both Taurus and Libra are devoid of planets, then because the results are equal, a zero is placed in both positions. Alternatively, if one has a result of 1 and the other has zero, then a zero is placed below the 1, and a 0 remains below the zero. 

For example, in the Ashtakavarga of Saturn: if the Trinal Reduction result below Aries is 0 and the result below Scorpio is 1, a zero is placed in both positions. <note>Note that Aries and Scorpio are both ruled by Mars; even in Saturn's chart, we look at the signs ruled by the same planet to perform this reduction.</note> When one position has a higher result and the other has a lower result, one should subtract the lower result from the higher one and record the remainder. 

For example, in the Ashtakavarga of the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The "Lagna" or the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of birth.</note>: if the Trinal Reduction results are 3 for Taurus and 1 for Libra, then after the reduction, 2 should be placed under Taurus and 1 should be placed under Libra. Furthermore, if one sign contains a planet and the other is empty, but the results for both are equal, the result in the sign with the planet remains as it is, while a zero is placed in the sign without the planet. 

In this hypothetical example: if Aries is occupied by a planet and has a result of 3, and Scorpio is empty of planets and has a result of 3, then because the results are equal, the 3 is retained under Aries (the occupied sign) and a 0 is placed under Scorpio. Furthermore, for the signs of Cancer and Leo, the results should always be kept as they are; there is no <term>Dual-Lordship Reduction</term> <note>original: "Ekadhipatya-shodhana-bhava." Because the Sun and Moon only rule one sign each, they do not participate in the reduction logic applied to the other five planets who rule two signs each.</note> for them. This logic should be understood for all cases. 

Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, titled "Dual-Lordship Reduction," in the Summary of the First Section of the Great Parashara Hora. ॥ 18 ॥

### Now, he describes the Generation of the Aggregated Sum.

Having established the remainder after the reductions, one should multiply it by the "sign-multiplier." If that sign is also occupied by a planet, one should further multiply it by the "planet-multiplier." ॥ 1 ॥

### Now, he states the Constant Multipliers.

Taurus and Leo are multiplied by ten; Gemini and Scorpio by eight; Libra and Aries by seven; and Virgo and Capricorn by five. The remaining signs are multiplied by their own specific measures. These are the sign-multipliers in order. ॥ 1 ॥ 

The multipliers for Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury are ten, eight, and seven respectively, while five is the multiplier for the others <note>This refers to the "Graha-guna" or planetary multipliers used to weight the points based on which planets occupy the signs.</note> in their respective order.

# Now, an Example of Calculating the Planetary and Sign Aggregate Sums.

Within the perfected digits <note>The "bindus" or points remaining after the Trikona and Ekadhipatya reductions described on the previous pages.</note> obtained after the <term>Dual-Lordship Reduction</term> <note>original: "Aikādhipatya-shodhana," a process where points are reduced in signs ruled by the same planet.</note>, one should take the points in the signs occupied by planets and multiply them by those specific planetary multipliers. The sum of these products is the **Planetary Aggregate Sum** <note>original: "Graha-piṇḍa."</note>. 

Next, the points in each sign are multiplied by their respective zodiac sign multipliers to find the **Sign Aggregate Sum** <note>original: "Rāśi-piṇḍa."</note>. To illustrate: 

Suppose the Sun and Jupiter are in Aquarius; the points remaining in Aquarius are 1. The multiplier for the Sun is 5 and for Jupiter is 10. Multiplying these, we get 5 and 10. 
Suppose Venus and Mars are in Pisces; the remaining points there are 1. The multiplier for Venus is 7 and for Mars is 8. Multiplying these, we get 7 and 8. 
The Moon is in Sagittarius with 2 points; the Moon's multiplier is 5, resulting in 10. 
Saturn and Mercury are in Capricorn; the points remaining in that sign are 0, so the product is 0. 

The sum of these planetary calculations (5 + 10 + 7 + 8 + 10) gives a **Planetary Aggregate Sum** of 40.

Now for the **Sign Aggregate Sum**: 
Aquarius has 1 point; the sign multiplier is 11, giving 11. 
Pisces has 1 point; the sign multiplier is 12, giving 12. 
Leo has 1 point; the sign multiplier is 10, giving 10. 
Sagittarius has 2 points; the sign multiplier is 9, giving 18. 
The sum of these sign products (11 + 12 + 10 + 18) gives a **Sign Aggregate Sum** of 51. 

By adding both sums together (40 + 51), the **Total Aggregate Sum** <note>original: "Yoga-piṇḍa."</note> becomes 91. In this manner, the sum for the <term>Sun’s Eight-fold Chart</term> <note>original: "Sūryāṣṭakavarga."</note> and all other planetary charts should be understood.

Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, named "Description of the Origin of the Aggregate Sum," in the summary of the First Volume of the *Great Parashara Hora*. || 19 ||

# Now, the Results of the Ashtakavarga are Told.

One should determine a person’s own influence and power, as well as matters concerning the father, from the results of the **Sun**. One should consider the clarity of mind and intellect, and matters concerning the mother, from the **Moon**. || 1 ||

One should contemplate siblings, inner strength, character, and landed property through **Mars**. || 2 ||

Commercial activities and one’s profession or means of livelihood should be contemplated through **Mercury**. Through **Jupiter**, one should consider the nourishment of the body, intellect, children, and the arrival of wealth. || 3 ||

Through **Venus**, one should examine marriage rituals, places of enjoyment, vehicles, and matters related to women and the physical body. || 4 ||

Longevity, the means of survival, sorrow, grief, great fear, total loss, and death should be observed through **Saturn** alone. || 5 ||

The Sun signifies the father; the Moon, the mother; Mars, the brother; and Mercury, the friend. Jupiter is recorded as the significator of paternal cousins <note>original: "mātuleya," though often meaning maternal cousin, here used in the context of wisdom and merit</note>, wisdom, and religious merit; Venus signifies women. Saturn causes death when transiting the signs associated with these relatives at the destined time. || 6 ||

Multiply the rectified points of the specific <term>Karaka</term> <note>A "significator" or planet that represents a specific person or area of life.</note> or house by the multiplier and divide the sum by twenty-seven. The remainder points to a <term>Nakshatra</term> <note>One of the 27 lunar mansions or star constellations used in Vedic astrology.</note>. When Saturn transits this star, the father, mother, sibling, relative, son, wife, or the self—corresponding to the significator used—undergoes destruction or a great transformation; or it may result in the gain of great fortune <note>original: "śrīnāthahetu," suggesting a turning point that could be either tragic or a source of inheritance/prosperity</note>. || 7 ||

Having laid out the **Sun’s** <term>Ashtakavarga</term> <note>The "Eight-fold Division" system of points for the Sun.</note> among the celestial wanderers, the ninth house from the Sun’s position is known as the house of the father. || 8 ||

Multiply the <term>Yoga Pinda</term> <note>The "Aggregate Sum" calculated on the previous page.</note> by the number of points in that ninth house. Divide by twenty-seven; the remainder indicates the Nakshatra through which Saturn will transit. || 9 ||

At that time, one should predict distress for that specific house. There is no doubt that during that time, the father will suffer or face difficulties. || 10 ||

When Saturn enters that specific Nakshatra or its <term>Trines</term> <note>original: "trikoṇa," referring to the 1st, 5th, and 9th positions in the sequence of 27 stars.</note>, one should know it as the time of death for the father or a father-figure; this should be calculated during the "vulnerable periods" of the planetary cycles. || 11 ||

If Rahu, Saturn, or Mars is in the fourth house from the Sun, and is not aspected by Jupiter or Venus, the person becomes one who "causes the end of the father" <note>This usually implies the father passes away early in the native's life.</note>. || 12 ||

If Saturn is in a position from the Ascendant or the Moon that corresponds to Jupiter's house, and is aspected by or joined with malefic planets, the destruction of the parents occurs at that time. || 13 ||

The expert in time <note>An astrologer.</note> should coordinate this with the favorable planetary periods. The loss of the father occurs during the period of the lord of the sign containing the lord of the 4th house from the Ascendant. || 14 ||

During the period of the lord of the 4th house, there is a doubt regarding many gains. If a person is born in the 8th house from the father's birth sign, or if the lord of that house is in the Ascendant... || 15 ||

...then by that person, the funeral rites for the father will certainly be performed; of this there is no doubt. When the lord of the 4th is in the house of gains...

...specifically from the Moon’s Ascendant. || 16 || When a planet is associated with the house of the father <note>the 9th house</note>, the one born follows the father’s will. By that very path, he shall complete the unfinished legacy of his father’s works. || 17 ||

Having understood such results, one should apply them month by month. Divide the result by twelve and count the remainder starting from Aries. In that month, or when the Sun is in its trines <note>the 1st, 5th, or 9th positions from that sign</note>, one should know that death may occur. || 22 ||

One should consider the Sun and others similarly; the tradition regarding the Sun is recorded hereafter. Specifics regarding the father’s inheritance and legacy will be explained further in the *Bhava Sutra*. || 23 ||

### An Example of This:

The ninth sign from where the Sun is situated is the "house of the father." In this example, the Sun is in Aquarius. The ninth sign from there is Libra. The points situated in Libra are 6. The rectified <term>Pinda</term> <note>Aggregate Sum</note> of the Sun is 91. This sum of 91 is multiplied by the 6 points in Libra, resulting in 546. This is divided by twenty-seven (27). The quotient of 20 is discarded, and the remainder is 6. When Saturn transits the <term>Ardra</term> <note>the 6th Lunar Mansion</note> constellation, there is hardship for the father. Hardship also occurs when Saturn transits the trines of that constellation. Thus, hardship for the father occurs when Saturn transits the <term>Ardra</term>, <term>Swati</term>, or <term>Shatabhisha</term> constellations. 

Alternatively, the rectified Sun-<term>Pinda</term> of 91 is multiplied by the eighth-house value of 3, resulting in 273. This is divided by twelve (12). The quotient of 22 is discarded, and the remainder is 9, which corresponds to the sign of Sagittarius. When Saturn transits Sagittarius or its trines (Aries and Leo), there is hardship for the father. In the absence of the father, this hardship applies to a father-like figure. || 23 ||

Specifically in the three signs belonging to Saturn... || 25 ||

### An Example of This

The Moon is in the sign of Sagittarius. The eighth house from it is Leo, whose lord is the Sun. This Sun is in the <term>Nakshatra</term> <note>lunar mansion</note> of Dhanishta. Therefore, during the periods when the Moon passes through the Nakshatras of Dhanishta, Jyeshtha, or Revati, the person may suffer from the length of an illness or various sorrows. Because of this, one should not perform auspicious activities during the third portions of these Nakshatras.

Likewise, the "place of happiness" <note>4th house</note> from the Moon is Pisces (the 12th sign). The points located in this sign are 3. The Moon's rectified aggregate sum <note>original: "shuddha-yoga-pinda"</note> is 91. These numbers multiplied by the points (91 x 3) equals 273. Dividing 273 by twenty-seven, the quotient is 10 (which is discarded) and the remainder is 3. This corresponds to the 3rd Nakshatra, Krittika. When Saturn travels through Krittika or its trines—Uttara Phalguni and Uttara Ashadha—distress for the mother occurs.

Alternatively, take the aggregate sum of 91 and multiply it by the value of the 8th house (2), which equals 182. Dividing by twelve, the quotient is 15 (discarded) and the remainder is 2. When Saturn travels through the signs of Taurus, Virgo, or Capricorn <note>the 2nd, 6th, and 10th signs</note>, distress for the mother or someone of equal status occurs. 30

### Now the Results of Mars are Described.

One should contemplate brothers, valor, and courage through the <term>Ashtakavarga</term> <note>eight-fold point system</note> of Mars. The sign where Mars is situated, and the third house from it, is known as the house of brothers. || 31 ||

After performing the rectification in the trines, wherever there are many points, land, a wife, or a house will be acquired. || 32 ||

If Mars is weak in strength, the brother will be long-lived. Where the points are diminished, those are known as the types of land <note>referring to loss or poor quality of property</note>. || 33 ||

One should multiply the point totals of that sign and rectify it as done before. When Saturn travels to the resulting Nakshatra, one should predict the loss of a brother. || 34 ||

## An Example of This <note>Regarding Mars and siblings</note>

Mars is situated in the sign of Pisces. The third sign from it is Taurus, which has a score of 2 points. The "Aggregate Sum" <term>Yoga-pinda</term> <note>a mathematical total used in these calculations</note> of Mars is 59. Multiplying this by the score (2) gives 118. Dividing this by twenty-seven (27), the quotient is 4 (which is disregarded) and the remainder is 10. The 10th <term>Nakshatra</term> <note>lunar mansion</note> is Magha. When Saturn transits through Magha, or its "trine" mansions <note>the 1st, 10th, and 19th positions in the series of 27</note>—Magha, Mula, or Ashvini—there will be distress for siblings.

Alternatively, multiply the Mars aggregate sum (59) by the points in the eighth house <note>original: "randhra-mana"</note>, which are 3, resulting in 177. Dividing by twelve (12), the quotient is 14 (disregarded) and the remainder is 9. This corresponds to the sign of Sagittarius. When Saturn transits through Sagittarius or its trines—Sagittarius, Aries, or Leo—there will be distress for siblings. || 24 ||

## Now, the Results for Mercury

From Mercury, one should consider the fourth house for family, wealth, and maternal uncles. From the fifth house from Mercury, one should contemplate the knowledge of sacred hymns <term>Mantravidya</term>, writing, and intellect. || 35 || After refining the eight-fold division of Mercury, when Saturn transits the sign indicated by the remainder, the person suffers the destruction of relatives and friends; of this, there is no doubt. || 36 ||

## An Example of This <note>Regarding Mercury</note>

Mercury is in Capricorn. The fourth sign from it is Aries, where the score is 4 points. The aggregate sum <term>Yoga-pinda</term> of Mercury is 132. Multiplying this by the score (4) gives 528. Dividing by twenty-seven (27), the quotient is 19 (disregarded) and the remainder is 15. When Saturn transits the lunar mansions of Swati, Shatabhisha, or Ardra <note>the 15th mansion and its trines</note>, there will be distress for relatives and friends.

Alternatively, multiply the aggregate sum (132) by the eighth house points (5), resulting in 660. Dividing by twelve (12), the quotient is 55 (disregarded) and the remainder is 0 <note>In this system, a remainder of 0 refers to the 12th sign, Pisces</note>. When Saturn transits the signs of Pisces, Cancer, or Scorpio <note>the 12th sign and its trines</note>, there will be distress for relatives and friends. In this same way, matters such as intellect should be judged from the fifth house position. || 35 || 36 ||

# Now, the Results of Saturn

The eighth house from the position where Saturn is situated is called the "house of death" <term>mriti</term>. One should determine the span of their own life <term>ayushya</term> through Saturn’s Eight-fold Division <term>Ashtakavarga</term>. || 63 ||

One should total the points <note>the "bindus" or dots used in this calculation system</note> beginning from the Ascendant <term>Lagna</term> up to the house occupied by Saturn <term>Manda</term>. In the year of life equal to that total, one should predict disease and enmity. || 64 ||

Total the points starting from the house of Saturn up to the Ascendant. In the year of life equal to that total, one should predict disease for the individual. || 65 ||

In the year equal to the sum of those two totals, a "combination for death" <term>mrityu-yoga</term> is declared. After performing the necessary reductions <note>the process of "shodhana," or mathematical simplification of the astrological chart</note> and carefully establishing the base sum <term>pinda</term>: || 66 ||

Multiply that sum by the points located in the eighth house and divide the result by twenty-seven. If the total is over one hundred, one should subtract one hundred from that sum. || 67 ||

One should thus know the base longevity <term>ayu-pinda</term> and calculate the timing as before. After performing the reductions for the trines <term>trikona</term> and the reduction for signs with the same lord <term>ekadhipatya</term>: || 68 ||

Having established the base sum, the wise man should multiply it by the points in the eighth house from the Ascendant. The remainder after dividing by twenty-seven will reveal the time of death. || 69 ||

In the complete Eight-fold Division, if there are no points in a particular house, Saturn yields no fruit <note>meaning no positive results or protection</note> when he transits through that house. || 70 ||

When the Sun <term>Ravi</term> and Moon <term>Chandra</term> transit through such a house during a "fissure" in the major planetary period <term>dasha-chidra</term> <note>the vulnerable transition period between two major planetary cycles</note>, death is declared. When this coincides with a "dasha-chidra," death is certain; there is no doubt. || 71 ||

Destruction occurs when Saturn transits a house with fewer points in Saturn’s Eight-fold Division. When the Sun <term>Bhaskara</term> and Saturn are both in that house, one should predict death at that time. || 72 ||

The wise and intelligent man should separately write down the purified base sum <term>shuddha-pinda</term> obtained through the previously mentioned reductions to consider the difficult years and the "yoga" for misfortune indicated by Saturn’s Eight-fold Division. || 73 ||

The sum of the points from the Ascendant to Saturn, and from Saturn to the house immediately preceding the Ascendant—in the year of life equal to that combined total, there will be disease, death, or travel to a foreign land <term>paradesha-yanam</term>. || 74 ||

Loss of wealth occurs in the year equal to that total; if the sum is doubled, that year brings great suffering. When the major period <term>paka</term> of a planet lacking strength arrives, death will then certainly occur. || 75 ||

Multiply the points found between the Ascendant and Saturn by the number of planets and divide <note>the text suggests a complex mathematical formula involving remainders</note>; when a malefic planet transits through the resulting sign, there is a loss of wealth and happiness. Following this, multiply by the points in the eighth house from the Ascendant; when Saturn transits the resulting sign, [it indicates the time of death]. || 76 ||

## Here is an Illustration:

Starting from the **Ascendant** <term>Lagna: the rising sign</term> and ending at **Saturn** <term>Manda</term>, the points <note>called bindus in the original system</note> are: 1, 4, 4, 3, 4, 3, 2, 3, 4. The sum of these is 28. In the year of life equal to this sum (age 28), the person suffers from physical illness, or perhaps death, travel to foreign lands, or loss of wealth.

Similarly, starting from the house occupied by **Saturn** and ending at the **Ascendant**, the points are 4, 5, 2. Their sum is 11. In the year equal to this (age 11), the person suffers hardships as described before. In the year equal to the total of both calculations (39), there is a similar combination for loss of wealth and other troubles, but the specific "combination for death" <term>mrityu-yoga</term> is absent.

Furthermore, the points from the Ascendant to Saturn (28) are multiplied by 7 <note>original: "naga," a code word for the number 7</note>, totaling 196. When divided by 27 <note>the number of lunar mansions or nakshatras</note>, the remainder is 7. When a malefic planet <term>khala</term> transits the 7th mansion, **Punarvasu**, there will be a loss of happiness.

Alternatively, if Saturn's **base sum** <term>yoga-pinda</term> is 169, multiply this by the 3 points located in the eighth house from the Ascendant, resulting in 507. Dividing this by 27 leaves a remainder of 21. When Saturn transits the mansions of **Uttarashadha**, **Krittika**, or **Uttaraphalguni** <note>these three are linked as they occupy the same relative positions in the three cycles of nine mansions</note>, there will be a loss of happiness and wealth. || 76 ||

> When Saturn enters a sign that has zero points <term>viyat-abdake</term>, and if there is simultaneously a period of misfortune <term>dasharishta</term>, death is certain; this is said to be never false. Even if Saturn is in a trine house <term>trikona</term>, if an evil planetary period matures, the person faces death even if Lord Shiva himself were the protector. || 77 ||

## The Meaning of This:

In the Eight-fold Division of Saturn, when Saturn transits a zodiac sign that contains **zero** <term>shunya</term> points, and there is a period of misfortune or the onset of an unfavorable planetary period, death should be predicted for that year. Furthermore, even in a trine position, if a bad planetary period is active, death occurs. Even if Shiva is the protector, death will still take place. || 77 ||

## Next, the Results of Mars:

> Total the points from the **Ascendant** <term>Tanu</term> to **Mars** <term>Kuja</term>, and similarly from Mars to the Ascendant. In the years of life equal to those totals, one will experience constant hardship and fear arising from weapons and fire. In the year equal to the combined sum of Saturn’s and Mars’s points, if there is no influence from a benefic planet <term>saumya</term>, there is fear of weapons. In the year equal to the combined points of Saturn and Mars, there is a fear of the destruction of wealth, and from the planet **Rahu**, a loss of happiness. || 78 ||

## An Illustration of This:

## Now, the Auspicious and Inauspicious Results are Described:

However, in the division of the **Son of the Earth** <note>original: "Dharani-tanaya," a name for Mars</note>, if a year matches the sum of points where malefic planets are transiting, there is a fear of death. || 79 || Within the Eight-fold Division of the **Son of the Sun** <note>original: "Martanda-putra," a name for Saturn</note>, if a specific house contains zero points <note>bindu-shunya</note>, then whenever **Saturn** <term>Ravija</term> or the **Sun** <term>Surya</term> transits that house, the body will suffer from sickness and pain. || 80 ||

## An Illustration of This:

In the **Eight-fold Division of the Moon** <term>Chandra Ashtakavarga</term>, the sum of points from the Moon to the Ascendant is 15, and from the Ascendant to the Moon is 34. In the years matching these (15 and 34), there will be happiness regarding wealth and other matters. 

In the **Eight-fold Division of Mercury** <term>Budha Ashtakavarga</term>, the sum from Mercury to the Ascendant is 14, and from the Ascendant to Mercury is 42. In these years (14 and 42), there will be happiness regarding wealth, children, and so on. 

For **Jupiter** <term>Guru</term>, the sum to the Ascendant is 8, and from the Ascendant to Jupiter is 48. In these years (8 and 48), there will be happiness and wealth. 

In the **Eight-fold Division of Venus** <term>Shukra Ashtakavarga</term>, the sum to the Ascendant is 4; in that year (age 4), happiness regarding wealth and children will occur. Regarding the **Eight-fold Division of Saturn**, it is noted that if no house has zero points, the specific suffering mentioned previously is avoided. || 80 ||

By examining the planetary periods <term>dashas</term> that match these point totals, one can predict when travel or marriage might be afflicted by "combinations for death" <term>mrityu-yukta</term>. || 81 || 

> One should calculate the total lines <note>rekha, often used interchangeably with points in this context</note> produced in the collective division for all signs starting with **Aries** <term>Mesha</term>. A total ranging from 18 to 24 is considered "lowest" <term>kanishtha</term> in strength. Those ending at 30 are of "middle" <term>madhyama</term> strength. || 82 || 

Those with more than 30 points are considered to bestow "excellent" <term>uttama</term> strength, resulting in physical health, wealth, and...

## Commentary

Regarding the signs—the twelve zodiac signs starting from the Ascendant—one should understand them in groups of three following the clockwise order of the four directions (East, South, West, North). 

*   **East:** The Ascendant <term>Lagna</term>, the 12th sign, and the 11th sign.
*   **South:** The 10th, 9th, and 8th signs.
*   **West:** The 7th, 6th, and 5th signs.
*   **North:** The 4th, 3rd, and 2nd signs.

After summing the total points for each of these three-sign directional groups, the direction with the highest points is declared auspicious <note>meaning travel or business in that direction will be successful</note>. The direction with the fewest points is declared a source of loss. || 86 ||

## Now, the results of the Houses are stated:

By observing the specific House <term>Bhava</term>, one determines if it gives good or bad results based on the total points <term>Pinda</term> produced by that sign. || 87 || 

When the total points <term>Pinda</term> are multiplied by the specific house lines and then divided by 12, the remainder indicates a sign. When **Saturn** <note>original: "Sauri," a name for Saturn meaning "Son of the Sun"</note> transits that sign or its trine <term>Trikona</term>, one should know that the specific house will suffer loss. A wise person, by calculating the timing from these points <term>Bindus</term>, should also declare the time when auspicious results will be attained. || 88 ||

# Commentary

Regarding the phrase "By the lord of death": Find the twelfth division <term>Dvadashamsha: a 2.5-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</term> in which the lord of the house of death <gloss>the 8th house</gloss> is situated. When Rahu <term>the North Node of the Moon</term>, also called the "Demon" <note>original: "Asura"</note>, transits through a trine <term>Trikona: the 5th or 9th house position</term> from that point, or when the Sun transits the trine of the lord of death, the time of passing should be declared. 

Furthermore, the calculation of Rahu’s arc-minutes <term>Lipta: minutes of a degree</term> must be performed. Multiply these by the Sun’s arc-minutes and divide the product by the total minutes in the zodiac <gloss>21,600</gloss>. The quotient obtained should be added to the Sun’s arc-minutes. Convert this back into signs and degrees. When the Sun reaches this exact position, it is predicted to be the time of death. || 95 ||

## An Example of the "Sun of Death"

Suppose the Sun is at 10 signs, 4 degrees, 14 minutes, and 22 seconds. Its total minute-count <term>Kalapinda</term> is 18,254' 22". Rahu is at 7 signs, 28 degrees, 21 minutes, and 39 seconds. Its total minute-count is 14,301' 39". 

The product of these numbers is 261,050,454. Dividing this by the total minutes of the circle <gloss>21,600</gloss> yields a quotient of 12,095 minutes. The remainder is multiplied by 60 and divided again by 21,600 to yield 40 seconds. 

Adding this result to the previously calculated Sun’s minutes (18,254' 22") gives 30,340' 2". Dividing this by 60 gives 505 degrees and 40 minutes. Dividing the degrees by 30 to find the signs results in 16 signs, 26 degrees, 40 minutes, and 2 seconds. Reducing this by 12 signs <gloss>the full circle</gloss>, the remaining "Sun of Death" <term>Nidhanarka</term> is at 4 signs, 26 degrees, 40 minutes, and 2 seconds <gloss>Leo 26° 40'</gloss>.

Alternatively, using the Sun's minutes (18,254) and Mars' minutes (21,424), their product is 381,273,696. Dividing by 21,600 gives 17,651 with a remainder of 12,096. Multiplying the remainder by 60 (725,760) and dividing by 21,600 gives 33. Adding this to the Sun's minutes results in 35,906 minutes and 55 seconds. In signs, this equals 5 signs and 18 degrees. In the month when the Sun reaches this position or its trine, there will be an end to suffering <note>klesha-kshaya: this can euphemistically refer to death or the resolution of a grave illness</note>. || 95 ||

## On the Moon of Death

> When the Moon enters a trine position from the lord of the eighth house, or from the position of the eighth lord's ninth-part division <term>Navamsha: a 3°20' subdivision of a zodiac sign</term>, death may be predicted. This is certain to occur on a day when the Moon transits a sign where it has very few points <term>Rekha: the "lines" or beneficial points assigned in the Ashtakavarga system</term>. || 98 ||

->Commentary<-

Whichever planet serves as the lord of the eighth house <gloss>the house of death and longevity</gloss>, when the Moon <note>original: "Vidhu"</note> transits a trine <term>Trikona: a 120-degree relationship, specifically the 1st, 5th, or 9th house positions</term> from it, or when the Moon transits the trine from the eighth lord’s ninth-part division <note>the Navamsha sign occupied by the 8th lord in the birth chart</note>, one should predict death with certainty on a day that produces very few points in the Moon's point-system. || 98 ||

## On the Ascendant of Death

> When the Ascendant or the Moon reaches the 64th ninth-part division <note>the "Veda-shashtyansha" or 64th Navamsha is a highly sensitive mathematical point located exactly 210 degrees from the starting point</note>, or when the Ascendant rises in the debilitation sign of the death-point, or enters a sign with zero points <gloss>Shunya</gloss> during a malefic planetary period, the liberation of the body <note>original: "Dehamukti," a respectful term for death</note> occurs. || 99 ||

->Commentary<-

The 64th ninth-part division <gloss>Navamsha</gloss> is calculated from the birth Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign</term> and the Moon. When the transit Ascendant or the Moon reaches this 64th division, the liberation of the body <gloss>death</gloss> occurs. Furthermore, one must consider the rising of the debilitation sign of the death-point. Since it is said that "the seventh from the exaltation is the debilitation," the sign of Leo is the debilitation of death <note>this refers to a specific technical calculation of a "death-point" or Mrityu-bhaga</note>. If the Ascendant transits through such a sign, or through a sign that has zero points <note>original: "Shunya," meaning it lacks any beneficial Ashtakavarga points</note> in the Ascendant's point-grid, and this coincides with a malefic planetary period <term>Dasha: a period of time ruled by a specific planet</term>, then death occurs. || 99 ||

### An Example Herein

For the Ascendant at 0 signs, 6 degrees, 3 minutes, 42 seconds and the Moon at 8 signs, 26 degrees, 29 minutes, 38 seconds:
The ninth-part measurement of 320 minutes is multiplied by 63 <note>to find the 64th division</note>, resulting in 20,160 minutes. This equals 336 degrees, which when divided by 30 results in 11 signs and 6 degrees. To find the 64th Navamsha, we add this to the original positions. 
For this example: 
The 64th Navamsha of the Ascendant falls in **Scorpio**. 
The 64th Navamsha of the Moon falls in **Cancer**. 
These are the times for the liberation of the body. In this manner, calculations should be performed in all cases. || 99 ||

<header>SUMMARY OF THE GREAT HOROSCOPY OF PARASHARA</header>

# Summary of the Great Horoscopy of Parashara
## Now, the results of the Collective Point-System are declared.

Using the results of the Collective Point-System <term>Samudaya Ashtakavarga: a method where the points (Bindus) from all seven planets are summed together for each of the twelve zodiac signs</term>, one should determine the auspicious and inauspicious outcomes for the houses, starting from the first house (the Self). One should examine the results of the planetary periods starting from birth during times of travel or marriage, as these can also be times associated with great danger or death. || 100 ||

The point-system is said to encompass the results of all actions. Without this system, it is difficult to perceive the specific qualities and defects arising from the planetary influences. || 101 || Zodiac signs that contain more than thirty points are givers of auspicious results. Signs that contain between twenty-five and thirty points are considered "medium" in their effects. || 102 ||

Signs that have very few points <gloss>low scores</gloss> bring hardship and sorrow. A wise person should ensure that all auspicious works and duties are performed when the planets are in the highest-scoring signs. || 103 || One should utilize these superior signs when selecting a favorable time <term>Muhurta: an auspicious moment chosen for a specific activity</term>. The natural power of a man's birth should be exercised in harmony with these calculations. || 104 ||

A wise person should avoid starting activities during the timings associated with "hardship signs" <note>signs with low point totals</note>. If the points are above the medium threshold, there is gain; if the points are lower than the medium, there is a decline or wasting away. || 105 || If the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> has a high number of points, that person will be wealthy and enjoy life's pleasures. If the opposite is true, they will undoubtedly face poverty. || 106 ||

One should judge the results of a planetary period based on how many points are in the Ascendant. One must look at the results of all the houses <term>Bhava: the twelve divisions of the chart representing life areas like wealth, siblings, and career</term>, from the first house to the twelfth house of loss. || 107 || Where points are high, one finds prosperity; where they are low or lacking, it leads to failure or death. In the middle range, one achieves average results, after carefully considering the nature of the house. || 108 ||

Divide the life into three segments <note>Khanda-traya: a technique for dividing the total life span into three parts to see which portion of life is most successful</note>, similar to the calculation of planetary periods. A segment occupied by a malefic planet <term>Papagraha: "cruel" planets like Saturn or Mars</term> is known to be a source of distress. || 109 || A segment influenced by benefic planets <term>Saumya: "gentle" planets like Jupiter or Venus</term> should be known as auspicious, while mixed influences produce mixed results. After understanding the results of these three segments, one should declare the results of the planetary periods. || 110 ||

Sum the points from the Ascendant up to the position of Saturn <note>original: "Manda"</note>. Multiply this total by seven and divide by twenty-seven. || 111 || When a malefic planet transits a position equal to that result, one should predict sorrow or disease. One should perform the same calculation starting from Saturn back to the Ascendant. || 112 ||

Sum the points from Mars <note>original: "Bhauma"</note> to the Ascendant, multiply as before <gloss>by 7 and divide by 27</gloss>, and determine the year of life this signifies. || 113 || In that year, if a malefic planet is also present, there will be fear of disease and death. In years or chart sections with low points, one should avoid the activities associated with that house. || 114 ||

A cattle shed, a field, or agriculture is auspicious if located in the direction of the sixth sign <note>The 6th house is traditionally associated with labor and livestock</note>. However, wealth or property placed in a sign with weak points will eventually go to ruin. || 115 ||

# First Section: Chapter 20 on the Results of the Point-System

In the direction associated with the Lord of Wealth <note>the ruler of the 2nd House</note>, one certainly obtains riches. In the direction associated with the Lord of the 8th House <note>the house of death and longevity</note>, the physical body perishes. || 116 ||

Starting from Aries, whichever zodiac signs contain eight points <note>original: "vasu-samkhyaya," referring to the eight Vasu deities</note>, they bring about physical growth, strength, and intelligence. Signs containing six, five, or seven points grant auspicious results. However, signs containing three, two, or one points are not favorable. || 117 ||

Mixed results occur when there are four points. If there are zero points <gloss>empty states</gloss>, they bring disease, scandal, and fear. I shall now declare all the results arising from the individual point-systems <term>Bhinna Ashtakavarga: the specific point-distribution calculated for each of the seven planets individually</term> for the Sun and other planets, starting from one point upwards. || 118 ||

### Now, the results of the monthly transit are described.

Based on the movement of planets on the day of transit <term>Sankranti: the moment a planet, particularly the Sun, moves from one zodiac sign to another</term>, one should determine the auspicious or inauspicious monthly results, as well as the results for major periods and specific days, by summing the points. || 119 ||

->Commentary<-

Having prepared the point-system based on the time of birth, one should declare the total results based on the points in all the point-systems on the day the planet transits into another sign. || 119 ||

### Now, the results of pacification for specific point counts are described.

If a month is associated with seven points <note>referring to a specific calculation of points during a transit</note>, it may bring death to men. To remedy this, one should donate twenty measures of gold <term>Pala: an ancient unit of weight</term> and two "mountains" of sesame seeds. || 120 ||

With eight points, a man may lose his status and quickly fall into the clutches of death. To destroy these negative effects, he should donate a weight of camphor. || 121 ||

With nine points, a man will certainly die from snakes. For the sake of gaining auspiciousness, he should donate a chariot drawn by four horses. || 122 ||

With ten points, a man loses his life to a weapon. To obtain auspicious results, he should donate armor set with diamonds <note>original: "vajra," which can mean diamond or an indestructible mythic metal</note>. || 123 ||

With eleven points <note>original: "rudrai," the eleven forms of Shiva</note>, a man may lose his life after receiving a curse. He should offer a golden image of the Moon weighing ten measures. || 124 ||

With twelve points <note>original: "adityaih," the twelve solar deities</note>, one should predict death for a man by water-related afflictions. He should donate land to a priest <term>Brahmin: a member of the scholarly or priestly class</term> so that auspicious results may follow. || 125 ||

With thirteen points, a man may meet death from tigers. He should perform a donation to Vishnu in his form as the Golden Womb <term>Hiranyagarbha: the "golden embryo" or source of the universe in Vedic philosophy</term> for the sake of auspiciousness. || 126 ||

# Now, the Celestial Formations are described.

I have previously described various planetary combinations <gloss>yogas</gloss> in great detail. Now, I shall briefly explain those known as the Celestial Formations <term>Nabhasa Yogas: planetary patterns that depend on the shape or arrangement of planets across the signs</term>, which number one thousand and eight hundred variations. || 1 ||

There are three formations known as "Refuge" <note>original: "ashraya"</note>, followed by two "Petal" formations <note>original: "dala"</note>. Then there are twenty "Pattern" formations <note>original: "akriti"</note>, and seven "Numerical" formations <note>original: "sankhya"</note> are also recognized. || 2 ||

The Rope formation <note>original: "rajju"</note>, the Pestle <note>original: "musala"</note>, the Reed <note>original: "nala"</note>, the Garland <note>original: "mala"</note>, and the Serpent <note>original: "bhujangama"</note>. || 3 ||

The Mace formation <note>original: "gada"</note>, the Cart <note>original: "shakata"</note>, the Triangle <note>original: "shringataka"</note>, and the Bird <note>original: "vihangama"</note>. The Plough <note>original: "hala"</note>, the Thunderbolt <note>original: "vajra"</note>, the Barley-corn <note>original: "yava"</note>, the Lotus <note>original: "kamala"</note>, the Reservoir <note>original: "vapi"</note>, and the Sacrificial Pillar <note>original: "yupa"</note>. || 4 ||

The Arrow <note>original: "shara"</note>, the Spear <note>original: "shakti"</note>, the Staff <note>original: "danda"</note>, the Boat <note>original: "nauka"</note>, the Peak <note>original: "kuta"</note>, the Umbrella <note>original: "chattra"</note>, and the Bow <note>original: "dhanu"</note>. The Half-Moon formation <note>original: "ardhendu"</note>, the Wheel <note>original: "chakra"</note>, and the Ocean <note>original: "samudra"</note>—these make twenty. || 5 ||

The Lute <note>original: "veena"</note>, the String <note>original: "damani"</note>, the Noose <note>original: "pasha"</note>, the Field <note>original: "kedara"</note>, the Trident <note>original: "shula"</note>, the Yoke <note>original: "yuga"</note>, and the Sphere <note>original: "gola"</note>. These are the thirty-two combinations described. || 6 ||

## Now, the three "Refuge" formations are described.

If all planets are situated in Moveable signs <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</note>, it is the Rope formation. If all are in Fixed signs <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius</note>, it is the Pestle. If all are in Dual signs <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note>, it is the Reed. These three are known as the "Refuge" formations <term>Ashraya Yogas: formations where planets take 'refuge' in a single quality of zodiac sign</term>. || 7 ||

## Now, the two "Petal" formations are described.

When all the Benefics <note>the "gentle" planets: Jupiter, Venus, and well-aspected Mercury or Moon</note> occupy three of the Centers <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</term>, it is called a Garland formation. If Malefics <note>the "harsh" planets: Sun, Mars, Saturn</note> occupy the Centers, it is called a Serpent formation. These two "Petal" formations were indeed taught by the Great Sages. || 8 ||

## Now, the twenty "Pattern" formations are described.

When planets occupy two adjacent Centers, it is the Mace formation. When they occupy the Ascendant and the Seventh house <note>the horizon line</note>, it is the Cart. When they occupy the Tenth and the Fourth houses <note>the vertical meridian</note>, it is the Bird. When planets are situated in the Ascendant, the Fifth, and the Ninth houses <note>the Trines</note>, it is called the Triangle. || 9 ||

The Plough formation is declared by those who know all the sacred scriptures to occur when planets occupy the 2nd, 6th, and 10th houses; or the 3rd, 7th, and 11th; or the 4th, 8th, and 12th. || 10 ||

If the Benefics are in the Ascendant and Seventh houses while Malefics are in the Tenth and Fourth, it is the Thunderbolt. If the positions are reversed <note>Malefics in 1st/7th, Benefics in 4th/10th</note>, it is the Barley-corn. If all planets are mixed throughout the Centers, it is the Lotus. || 11 ||

If the planets avoid the Centers and are situated in the remaining houses <note>the 2nd, 3rd, 5th, 6th, 8th, 9th, 11th, and 12th</note>, it is the Reservoir formation; so it has been stated by the ancient masters. || 12 ||

When planets occupy four houses in succession starting from the Ascendant, it is the Sacrificial Pillar; from the Fourth house, the Arrow; from the Seventh house, the Spear; and from the Tenth house, it is the Staff. This is what the experts in birth-charts have taught.

Those born under the **Serpent** formation <note>original: "sarpa"</note> are inconsistent, cruel, destitute, and always afflicted by misery and poverty. They are dependent on others for their food and drink. || 21 ||
Those born under the **Mace** formation <note>original: "gada"</note> are constantly devoted to earning wealth; they perform religious sacrifices, are skilled in the scriptures and music, and possess wealth, gold, and gems. || 22 ||

Those born under the **Bird** formation <note>original: "vihaga"</note> have a taste for wandering and serve as messengers; they are bold, live for sensual pleasures, and are constantly fond of quarreling. || 24 ||
Those born under the **Triangle** formation <note>original: "shringataka"</note> are fond of disputes but are capable in battle; they are happy, liked by kings, and have good wives. They are wealthy, though they may be disliked by or dislike young women. || 25 ||

# Chapter 21: Fruits of the Celestial Formations in the First Section

Men born under the **Plough** <term>hala: a configuration where planets occupy houses in a way that resembles a plough</term> formation are always sorrowful, anxious, abandoned by their relatives and friends, and serve others as laborers. || 26 ||

Those born under the **Thunderbolt** <term>vajra: a formation where auspicious planets are in the 1st and 7th houses, and inauspicious ones are in the 4th and 10th</term> are happy in the beginning and end of their lives, brave, handsome, and yet can be listless, unfortunate, wicked, and argumentative. || 27 ||

Men born under the **Barley** <term>yava: the reverse of the Vajra formation, with auspicious planets in the 4th and 10th houses</term> are devoted to vows, disciplines, and auspicious acts; in their middle age, they possess happiness, wealth, and children; they are charitable and firm-minded. || 28 ||

Those born under the **Lotus** <term>kamala: a formation where all planets are situated in the four "angles" or Cardinal houses (1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th)</term> are rich in wealth and virtue, live long lives, possess vast fame, and are pure; they perform hundreds of good deeds and are like lords of the earth. || 29 ||

Those born under the **Pond** <term>vāpī: a formation where planets are situated in the houses following the angles</term> are skilled in managing treasures, possess steady wealth and happiness, have children, are pleasing to the eye, and live like kings. || 30 ||

One born under the **Sacrificial Post** <term>yūpa: planets occupying the first four houses starting from the Ascendant</term> is a knower of the self, devoted to sacrifices, has a wife, is full of goodness, follows vows and rules, and is distinguished among men. || 31 ||

Men born under the **Arrow** <term>śara: planets occupying four houses starting from the 4th house</term> are fond of hunting, may deal with thieves and imprisonment, are meat-eaters, violent, and skilled in minor crafts. || 32 ||

Men born under the **Spear** <term>sakti: planets occupying four houses starting from the 7th house; the text reads 'satyam' (Truth), but contextually refers to the 'Shakti' or 'Power' formation</term> are without wealth, unsuccessful, sorrowful, lowly, and lazy; yet they are long-lived, skilled in the art of war, stable, and handsome. || 33 ||

Those born under the **Staff** <term>daṇḍa: planets occupying four houses starting from the 10th house</term> lose their children and wives, are destitute, cruel in all things, cast out by their kin, sorrowful, and serve as lowly messengers. || 34 ||

Men born under the **Boat** <term>nau: planets occupying the seven houses from the Ascendant to the 7th house</term> earn their living from the water, are filled with desires, famous yet wicked, stingy, unclean, greedy, and villainous. || 35 ||

Those born under the **Peak** <term>kūṭa: planets occupying seven houses starting from the 10th house</term> are liars, sinful, impoverished, deceptive, and cruel; they always dwell in mountains and fortresses. || 36 ||

One born under the **Umbrella** <term>chatra: planets occupying seven houses starting from the 4th house</term> provides shelter to his kin, is compassionate, favored by various kings, and highly intelligent; he is happy in the beginning and end of life, lives long, and is worthy of the royal parasol <note>a symbol of high sovereignty</note>. || 37 ||

Those born under the **Bow** <term>kārmuka: planets occupying seven houses starting from the 10th house</term> are deceitful, keepers of secrets, thieves, gamblers, and frequent the forests; they are unfortunate generally, but have good fortune in the middle of their lives. || 38 ||

All those born under the **Half-Moon** <term>ardhacandra: planets occupying seven consecutive houses starting from a house other than an angle</term> become army commanders, have handsome bodies, are loved by kings, are strong, and possess jewels and gold ornaments. || 39 ||

A man born under the **Wheel** <term>cakra: planets situated in the six odd-numbered houses (1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11)</term> becomes a king of kings, whose feet are illuminated by the light reflecting from the jewels in the crowns of all the monarchs bowing before him. || 40 ||

# Summary of the Great Parāśara Horā

Those born under the **Ocean** <term>samudra or udadhi: a formation where planets occupy the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th, 10th, and 12th houses</term> formation are prosperous with wealth and children, enjoy life's pleasures, are liked by the people, and have sons. Such men possess steady wealth and a virtuous character. || 41 ||

Those born under the **Lute** <term>vīṇā: a formation where the seven planets are distributed across seven different signs</term> are skilled in singing, dancing, and playing musical instruments; they are happy and wealthy. They become leaders with many servants. || 42 ||

Under the **Garland** <term>dāminī: seven planets distributed across six signs</term> formation, a person is helpful to others, possesses political wisdom and wealth, and is famous as a great lord. They are blessed with many sons and jewels, and are brave and learned. || 43 ||

In the **Noose** <term>pāśa: seven planets distributed across five signs</term> formation, individuals are subject to bonds <note>original: "bandhanabhājaḥ"; this implies either literal imprisonment or being heavily tied down by worldly duties</note>, are skilled in their work, and are clever in worldly dealings. They are talkative, lack character, have many servants, and large families. || 44 ||

Those born under the **Field** <term>kedāra: seven planets distributed across four signs</term> are useful to many people, are agriculturalists, truthful, and happy. They possess a flickering or changeable nature but are endowed with wealth. || 45 ||

Those born under the **Spear** <term>śūla: seven planets distributed across three signs</term> formation are sharp-tempered, lazy, and poor. They are violent, social outcasts, but also great warriors who earn a reputation in battle. || 46 ||

Those born under the **Yoke** <term>yuga: seven planets distributed across only two signs</term> formation are either heretics or devoid of wealth and are shunned by the world. They lack the happiness of children, the support of a mother, and a sense of duty. || 47 ||

Those born under the **Sphere** <term>gola: all seven planets concentrated in a single sign</term> formation are physically strong but penniless, devoid of education or scientific knowledge, and are unclean. They are constantly miserable and wretched. || 48 ||

These formations yield their results throughout all the stages of life <term>daśās: planetary periods that govern different chapters of a person's life</term>. This is how it should be understood for all living beings, as the ancient masters have declared. || 49 ||

->Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, titled "The Declaration of Results for the Celestial Formations," in the Summary of the First Section of the Illustrious Great Parāśara Horā.<-

## Now, the Elephant-Lion Formation is described.

When the Teacher of the Gods <term>Devaguru: the planet Jupiter</term> is situated in a Cardinal house <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a birth chart</note> from the Moon <term>mṛgāṅka: literally "the one with the deer-mark," a poetic name for the Moon</term>, it is called the **Elephant-Lion** <term>gajakesarī</term> formation. This occurs provided Jupiter is not in its sign of debilitation, not eclipsed by the sun, and the Moon is not in an unfavorable house. || 1 ||

One born with the **Elephant-Lion** formation will be radiant, wealthy, and highly intelligent. They will be endowed with many virtues and will be a favorite of the king <note>In a modern context, this refers to being favored by the government or high-ranking officials</note>. || 2 ||

## Now, the Stainless Formation is described.

If, at the time of a person's birth, an auspicious planet is situated in the tenth house from either the Ascendant or the Moon, then the **Stainless** <term>amalā</term> formation is present. The fame of such a person remains on earth until the end of their life, and they possess indestructible wealth and prosperity. || 3 ||
