# Part One: Chapter 22 — On the Fruits of Various Planetary Combinations

If a benefic planet <note>planets like Jupiter, Venus, or a well-placed Mercury</note> is situated in the tenth house from either the **Ascendant** <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term> or the **Moon-Ascendant** <term>Chandra-lagna: the sign where the moon is placed, used as a secondary starting point for analysis</term>, it creates the **Spotless** <term>Amala: meaning pure or stainless</term> formation. The fame of such a person will endure as long as the moon and stars exist. || 4 ||

One born under the **Spotless** formation is respected by kings, a great enjoyer of life’s pleasures, a charitable giver, and beloved by their kinsmen. They are altruistic, virtuous, and possess a noble character. || 5 ||

### The Benefic and Malefic Formations

Now, I shall describe the **Benefic** and **Malefic** <note>original: "Shubha" and "Ashubha"</note> formations. If the birth Ascendant is occupied by benefics, it is a **Benefic** formation; if by malefics, it is a **Malefic** formation. These are also formed by the "Scissors" effect, where benefic or malefic planets occupy the 12th and 2nd houses from the Ascendant <note>this "scissoring" is known as Kartari Yoga, which either protects or constricts the house in the middle</note>. || 6 ||

One born under the **Benefic** formation is an eloquent speaker, handsome, and endowed with good conduct and many virtues. One born under the **Malefic** formation is driven by desire, engages in sinful deeds, and lives off the wealth or labor of others. || 7 ||

### The Mountain Formation

If benefic planets occupy the "center" houses <term>Kendras: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</term> and the 7th and 8th houses are either empty or occupied by benefics, it is the **Mountain** <term>Parvata</term> formation. Alternatively, it occurs if the lords of the 1st and 12th houses are in mutual "centers" and are placed in the signs of friendly planets or their own signs of exaltation. || 8 ||

The person born under the **Mountain** formation is endowed with great fortune and is dedicated to learning and amusements. They are generous givers and highly passionate <note>original: "kāmī," implying a strong romantic or sensual nature</note>. They are radiant, famous, and will become the leader of a city. || 9 ||

### The Drum Formation

If the lords of the 4th house <term>Bandhu-nātha: lord of relatives/home</term> and the 9th house <term>Guru-nātha: lord of the teacher/fortune</term> are in mutual "centers" and the lord of the Ascendant is strong, the **Drum** <term>Kāhala: a large ceremonial drum or trumpet</term> formation is created. This also occurs if the lord of the 4th house is in its sign of exaltation or its own sign and is associated with or aspected by the lord of the 10th house. || 10 ||

One born under the **Drum** formation is energetic, courageous, and perhaps stubborn <note>original: "mūrkha," literally 'foolish,' but often used in these texts to describe a blunt, headstrong warrior-like temperament</note>. They command a four-fold army <note>the traditional military divisions: elephants, chariots, cavalry, and infantry</note> and will be at least a leader of a village. || 11 ||

### The Garland Formation

If the seven planets occupy the seven houses starting from the Ascendant, the **Garland** <term>Mālikā</term> formation is formed. Such a person is born a king, commanding many elephants and horses. If the row of planets begins in the 2nd house <term>Vitta: wealth</term>, they become a master of treasures, devoted to their father, brave, handsome, and a sovereign ruler of the earth. || 12 ||

If this **Garland** starts from the 3rd house <term>Vikrama: valor</term>, the person becomes a king who is brave and wealthy, yet prone to illness. If it starts from the 4th house <term>Sukha: happiness/home</term>, they enjoy the fortunes of many countries and are dedicated to great acts of charity...

...king. || 13 || If the **Garland** <term>Malika: a configuration where planets occupy seven consecutive houses like a flower garland</term> begins from the **house of children** <note>the 5th house</note>, the person becomes a ruler, a performer of sacrifices <note>Yajva: one who conducts Vedic rituals</note>, or becomes famous. If it begins from the **sixth house**, the person attains wealth and happiness but eventually becomes impoverished. || If the **Garland** begins from the **house of desire** <note>the 7th house</note>, the person will be a king beloved by many women. If it begins from the **eighth house**, the person will be a leader of men who is long-lived but devoid of wealth and dominated by women. || 14 || 

If the **Garland** begins from the **house of dharma** <note>the 9th house</note>, the person is a treasury of virtues, a performer of sacrifices, an ascetic, and powerful. If it starts from the **house of action** <note>the 10th house</note>, the person is devoted to righteous deeds and is honored by virtuous people. || If it starts from the **house of gains** <note>the 11th house</note>, the person is an excellent king, a leader among many, and skilled in all activities. If born when it starts from the **house of loss** <note>the 12th house</note>, the person spends excessively but will be respected everywhere. || 15 ||

### Now, the Whisk formation is described.
<note>original: "Chamara Yoga"</note>

When the Lord of the Ascendant is placed in a **Cardinal house** <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which act as the pillars of a chart</term>, is in its sign of exaltation, and is aspected <note>viewed</note> by Jupiter, the **Whisk** formation <term>Chamara: a fly-whisk made of yak tail, a traditional symbol of royalty and high status</term> occurs. Alternatively, if two benefic planets are placed in the Ascendant, the 7th, the 9th, or the 10th house, it is also the Whisk formation. || 16 ||

A person born under the **Whisk** formation is honored by kings, is a scholar, an eloquent speaker, or a ruler. They will be all-knowing, an authority on the Vedas and scriptures, and will live for seventy years. || 17 ||

### Now, the Conch formation is described.
<note>original: "Shankha Yoga"</note>

If the lords of the 5th house <note>children/wisdom</note> and the 6th house <note>obstacles/enemies</note> are in mutual Cardinal houses, and the Lord of the Ascendant is strong, it is the **Conch** formation <term>Shankha: the ritual conch shell, symbolizing victory and the removal of ignorance</term>. Others say it occurs if the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the 10th house are in **movable signs** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note> while the Lord of the 9th house is strong. || 18 ||

One born under the **Conch** formation is a seeker of enjoyment, compassionate, and possesses a wife, sons, and wealth. They own land, perform meritorious deeds, possess knowledge of the scriptures, and maintain virtuous conduct. They live for eighty years. || 19 ||

### Now, the Kettle-drum formation is described.
<note>original: "Bheri Yoga"</note>

If planets occupy the 2nd, 12th, 1st, and 7th houses, and the Lord of the 10th house is strong, it is the **Kettle-drum** formation <term>Bheri: a large drum used to announce royal decrees or military marches</term>. Similarly, it is said to exist if Jupiter and Venus are in the Ascendant/11th house, while the Lord of the 9th house is strong. || 20 ||

Those born under the **Kettle-drum** are long-lived, free from disease and fear, and become kings. They are famous and endowed with great wealth, land, children, and wives. They possess good conduct, immense happiness, and courage; they are skillful and of noble birth. || 21 ||

<header>First Section: Chapter 22 on the Results of Many Planetary Formations</header>

# Now, the Drum formation is described.
<note>original: "Mridanga Yoga"</note>

If the lord of the division <note>Navamsha</note> occupied by an exalted planet is situated in a **Cardinal house** <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</term> or a **Trine house** <term>Trikona: the 1st, 5th, or 9th houses</term>, and is placed in its own or exalted sign while possessing strength; and if the **Lord of the Ascendant** is also strong, the **Drum** formation occurs. This results in a person who is handsome, king-like, and endowed with great fame. || 22 ||

# Now, the Lord of Fortune formation is described.
<note>original: "Shrinatha Yoga"; named after a title for the god Vishnu</note>

If the **Lord of the seventh house** <note>the house of partnerships</note> is placed in the **tenth house** <note>the house of career</note> in its sign of exaltation, and the **Lord of the tenth** is conjoined with the **Lord of the ninth** <note>the house of fortune</note>, the **Lord of Fortune** formation then bestows auspicious results. The person born under this becomes a ruler equal to Indra <note>the king of the gods</note>. || 23 ||

# Now, the Goddess of Learning formation is described.
<note>original: "Sharada Yoga"; named after Saraswati, the goddess of wisdom</note>

The formation known as **Sharada** occurs when the **Lord of the tenth house** is in the **fifth house** <note>house of intelligence</note>, and the **son of the Moon** <note>Mercury</note> is in a Cardinal house; while the **Lord of the Day** <note>the Sun</note> is in its own sign and possesses great strength. Alternatively, if **Jupiter** <note>the Guru of the Gods</note> is in a Trine from the **Moon**, and **Mars** is in a Trine from **Mercury**, or if **Jupiter** is in the **house of gains** <note>the 11th house</note>, it is called the **Sharada** formation. || 24 ||

Those born under the **Sharada** formation are devoted to the happiness of their wives, children, and kin; they are handsome and virtuous. They are beloved by kings, devoted to their teachers, the priestly class, and the gods. They are rich in knowledge, fond of humor and entertainment, disciplined, powerful through penance, and remain constant in their own religious duties on this earth. || 25 ||

# Now, the Fish formation is described.
<note>original: "Matsya Yoga"</note>

When **malefic planets** <note>such as Saturn or Mars</note> are in the **Ascendant** and the **ninth house**, and both benefics and malefics are in the **fifth**, while malefics also occupy the **fourth and eighth houses** <note>original: "Chaturasram," referring to the 4th and 8th houses</note>, this is the **Fish** formation. || 26 ||

One born under the **Fish** formation is a **knower of time** <note>Kala-jna: an astrologer or astronomer</note>, an ocean of compassion, of a godly intellect, and possesses strength and beauty. Such a person is famous, learned, and an ascetic. || 27 ||

# Now, the Tortoise formation is described.
<note>original: "Kurma Yoga"</note>

If **benefic planets** occupy the **seventh, fifth, and sixth houses** in their exalted or friendly signs and divisions, while **malefic planets** occupy the **third, eleventh, and the Ascendant** in their friendly or exalted signs, it is the **Tortoise** formation. || 28 ||

One born under the **Tortoise** formation becomes world-famous, an enjoyer of kingdoms, highly righteous, and dominated by the **quality of purity** <term>Sattva-guna: the mode of goodness and clarity</term>. He is steady, happy, helpful in speech, or a leader of honorable men. || 29 ||

<summary>This page defines five auspicious planetary configurations (Mridanga, Shrinatha, Sharada, Matsya, and Kurma Yogas), detailing their astronomical conditions and the resulting character traits, such as royal status, wisdom, and compassion.</summary>
<keywords>Mridanga Yoga, Shrinatha Yoga, Sharada Yoga, Matsya Yoga, Kurma Yoga, Indian Astrology, Vedic Horoscopy, Jataka, planetary configurations, kingly status, Sattva guna</keywords>

<header>Summary of the Great Parashara Horoscopy</header>

## Now, the Sword formation is described.
<note>original: "Khadga Yoga"</note>

When the **Lord of the ninth house** <note>the house of fortune</note> is situated in the **second house** <note>the house of wealth</note>, and the **Lord of the second house** is placed in the **ninth house**; and additionally, the **Lord of the Ascendant** is situated in a **Cardinal house** <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</term> or a **Trine house** <term>Trikona: the 1st, 5th, or 9th houses</term>, this is called the **Sword** formation. || 30 ||

Men born under the **Sword** formation are devoted to the study of the Vedas, scriptures, and the logic and essence of all sacred traditions. They are endowed with intelligence, majesty, physical strength, and valor. They are lovers of happiness, free from envy, characterized by the great dignity of their own prowess, and are highly skilled and grateful individuals. || 31 ||

## Now, the Goddess of Wealth formation is described.
<note>original: "Lakshmi Yoga"</note>

If the **Lord of the ninth house** is in a **Cardinal house** or its **Root-Trine** <term>Mula Trikona: a specific favorable zodiacal placement</term> while also being in its sign of highest exaltation, and the **Lord of the Ascendant** is possessed of great strength, this is called the **Goddess of Wealth** formation. || 32 ||

The person is delightful in their qualities, the ruler of many lands, and possesses great learning and fame. They are as handsome as the god of love <note>original: "Ananga-rupa"</note>, a king of kings honored by other rulers from all directions, and blessed with many wives and sons. || 33 ||

## Now, the Flower formation is described.
<note>original: "Kusuma Yoga"</note>

If the birth occurs in a **Fixed sign** <term>Sthira-lagna: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</term>, and **Venus** <note>original: "Bhrigu"</note> is in a Cardinal house, the **Moon** <note>original: "Indu"</note> is in a Trine house with a malefic planet, and the **Sun** <note>original: "Sauri" (here likely referring to the Sun in the 10th, though sometimes used for Saturn, context implies the Solar "place of honor")</note> is in the **tenth house** <note>the house of career</note>, this becomes the **Flower** formation. || 34 ||

The person born of the **Flower** formation is a giver, honored by the lords of the earth, an enjoyer of life, and the leader of a great royal lineage. They possess great fame and majesty in the world and become a lord among men. || 35 ||

## Now, the Heavenly Tree formation is described.
<note>original: "Parijata Yoga"</note>

Take the lord of the sign where the **Lord of the Ascendant** is placed; then take the lord of *that* planet's sign; then take the lord of the ninth part <term>Navamsha</term> of that third planet. If this final planet is situated in a **Cardinal** or **Trine house**, or is in its own sign of exaltation, the **Heavenly Tree** formation exists. || 36 ||

The person born under the **Heavenly Tree** formation enjoys happiness in the middle and end of their life. They are honored by kings, fond of battle, and possess elephants and horses. They are devoted to their duties and religious path, compassionate, and become a king. || 37 ||

## Now, the Treasure of Arts formation is described.
<note>original: "Kalanidhi Yoga"</note>

If **Jupiter** <note>original: "Jiva"</note> is in the **second** or **fifth house**, and is either conjoined with or aspected by **Mercury** and **Venus**, or if Jupiter is placed in the signs belonging to Mercury or Venus, it is the **Treasure of Arts** formation. || 38 ||

One born of the **Treasure of Arts** formation is passionate, delightful in their good qualities, and has their feet praised by the foremost of kings. They are accompanied by armies, horses, rutting elephants, conch-shells, and drums, and are free from disease, fear, and the multitude of enemies. || 39 ||

<summary>This page defines five auspicious planetary formations (Yogas)—Sword, Lakshmi, Flower, Heavenly Tree, and Treasure of Arts—detailing their astronomical requirements and the royal or scholarly success they bestow upon the individual.</summary>
<keywords>Sword formation, Lakshmi formation, Flower formation, Heavenly Tree formation, Treasure of Arts formation, planetary combinations, Vedic astrology, Khadga Yoga, Kalanidhi Yoga</keywords>

<header>First Section, Chapter 22: Results of Various Planetary Combinations</header>

## Now, the formations starting with the Celestial Tree are described.
<note>original: "Parijatadi Yoga"</note>

When a planet attains the **Celestial Tree** level of strength <note>original: "Parijata Varga" — meaning it is in two favorable divisions of the zodiac</note>, it brings happiness and freedom from disease. If it reaches the **Temple Gateway** level <note>original: "Gopura Varga" — three favorable divisions</note>, it bestows wealth and cattle. A planet in the **Throne** level <note>original: "Simhasana Varga" — four favorable divisions</note> grants great prosperity and power. || 40 ||

A person endowed with a planet in the **Pigeon** level <note>original: "Paravata Varga" — five favorable divisions</note> gains learning, fame, and vast wealth. If in the **Realm of the Gods** level <note>original: "Devaloka Varga" — six favorable divisions</note>, the person possesses many vehicles and armies. Finally, if the planet is in the **Celestial Elephant** level <note>original: "Airavata Varga" — seven favorable divisions</note>, the individual attains kingship. || 41 ||

## Now, the Superior formation of the Ascendant is described.
<note>original: "Lagnadhi Yoga"</note>

When **benefic planets** <term>Subha: favorable planets like Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury</term> are placed in the **sixth, seventh, and eighth houses** from the **Ascendant** <term>Lagna: the rising sign</term>, and are neither joined with nor aspected by **malefic planets** <term>Papa: unfavorable planets</term>, the famous **Superior formation of the Ascendant** occurs—provided the fourth house is also free from malefics. || 42 ||

One born under this **Superior formation** will be the author of many scriptures, highly learned, humble, and a high-ranking official or commander. They will be a prominent, sincere, and great-souled person, excelling in fame, wealth, and virtuous qualities in this world. || 43 ||

## Now, the Lunar formations and others are described.

When the **Moon** is situated in a **Cardinal house** <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</term> from the **Sun** <note>original: "Sahasrarashmi" — the thousand-rayed one</note>, or in Succeedent or Cadent houses, the person's wealth, intelligence, and skill are respectively low, medium, or excellent. || 44 ||

If the **Moon** is in its own zodiacal division or that of a great friend during a birth in the **daytime**, and is aspected by **Jupiter**, the person born is endowed with wealth and happiness. || 45 ||

When the **Moon** is in its own or a great friend’s division and is aspected by the **Minister of the Demons** <note>original: "Danavamantri" — an epithet for the planet Venus</note> during a birth at **night**, it creates wealth as grand as a royal umbrella and banner. If the Moon is placed in the opposite conditions <note>e.g., aspected by Venus during the day or Jupiter at night</note>, the people born possess little wealth. || 46 ||

## Now, the Superior formation of the Moon is described.
<note>original: "Adhi Yoga"</note>

If **benefic planets** are situated in the **sixth, seventh, or eighth houses** from the **Moon**, the **Superior formation** is born. If these benefics are of high strength, the person becomes a **Ruler of the Earth** <note>a King</note>. If they are of medium strength, the person becomes a high-ranking minister or friend to a king. If they have low strength, the person becomes a commander of an army. || 47 ||

If the benefics are placed in the **houses of growth** <term>Upachaya: the 3rd, 6th, 10th, and 11th houses</term> from the **Moon**, the person is righteous and very wealthy. If two benefics are so placed, the wealth is moderate; if only one, the wealth is said to be minimal. If such formations are absent from both the **Moon** and the **Ascendant**, the person may be poor and miserable. || 48 ||

<summary>This page defines the results of planets attaining specific levels of dignity (Vargas) and describes the auspicious Adhi Yogas (Superior formations) calculated from both the Ascendant and the Moon.</summary>
<keywords>Parijata Yoga, Lagnadhi Yoga, Chandradhi Yoga, Varga, benefics, planetary strength, astrology, Parashara, kingship, wealth</keywords>

We now move to the specific lunar formations that define a person's social standing and wealth.</meta>

## Now, the formations of Sunapha, Anapha, Duradhara, and Kemadruma are described.

When planets—excluding the **Lord of the Lotus** <note>original: "pankeruha-isha" — the Sun</note>—are situated in the second house from the **Moon** <note>original: "shītāṃśu" — the cool-rayed one</note>, the **Sunapha** formation occurs. If they are in the twelfth house, it is **Anapha**. If planets are in both the second and twelfth houses, it is **Duradhara**. If there are no planets in either of these houses, then it is **Kemadruma**. These four types of lunar formations were recorded by the ancient sages. || 49 ||

## Now, the results of the Sunapha formation are described.

A person born under the **Sunapha** formation will surely be a minister to a king, virtuous, and capable. They will possess wealth earned by their own hands, be famous among all people for their vast reputation, and be exceptionally intelligent. || 50 ||

## Now, the results of the Anapha formation are described.

A person born under the **Anapha** formation will be a leader, modest, possessing pleasant and refined speech, well-behaved, and full of good qualities. They will have a generous reputation and a mind always satisfied in love. || 51 ||

## Now, the results of the Duradhara formation are described.

A person born under the **Duradhara** formation is constantly blessed with good wealth, a good wife, vehicles, land, and happiness. They are a perpetual conqueror of enemies and are particularly fond of the enchanting glances of beautiful women. || 52 ||

## Now, the results of the Kemadruma formation are described.

Lacking wealth, children, a wife, and family, the person born under **Kemadruma** becomes a servant living in a foreign land. They are constantly perverse in their thinking, dirty, and poorly dressed—even if they are the son of a king. || 53 ||

## Now, the cancellation of the Kemadruma formation is described.

Some say **Sunapha** occurs when planets are in the fourth house from the Moon, and **Anapha** when they are in the tenth. **Duradhara** occurs if they are in both houses; otherwise, the formation is named **Kemadruma**. || 54 ||
In whatever sign the Moon is placed in the **ninth-division chart** <term>Navamsha: a sub-divisional chart used in Vedic astrology to determine the internal strength of planets</term> at the time of birth, if planets are in the second house from that sign, it is also called **Sunapha**...

<summary>This page details the four major astrological formations based on the Moon's neighboring houses, outlining how they lead to political power, virtuous character, or, in the case of Kemadruma, extreme poverty and social isolation.</summary>

...is proclaimed. || 55 || The **Anapha** formation is known by planets situated in the twelfth house from the Moon. The **Duradhara** formation is spoken of when planets are in both the second and twelfth houses. Otherwise, the formation is considered **Kemadruma** <note>original: "kemadrumo" — a formation occurring when the houses adjacent to the Moon are empty, traditionally suggesting a life of struggle</note>. || 56 || 

If, at the time of birth, the **Moon** <note>original: "prāleyāṃśu" — the one with icy rays</note> is aspected by all the other planets, it creates a long life, a **Royal Yoga** <term>Rāja-yoga: a planetary combination indicating high status or political power</term>, and makes the person very wealthy, effectively destroying the ill effects of the Kemadruma. || 57 || 

If all the planets are situated in the **four angles** <note>original: "kendra" — the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note>, even this wicked Kemadruma formation becomes auspicious. The planets abandon all their bad influences and instead grant men various wonderful and good results. || 58 || 

One should carefully consider this in all lunar formations: if such conditions exist, the negative results of formations like Kemadruma will dissolve away. || 59 ||

### Now, the Solar Formations are described.

When planets—excluding the Moon—are in the twelfth house from the **Sun** <note>original: "bhānu"</note>, it is known as the **Vesi** formation. When they are in the second house, it is **Vasi**. When they are in both houses, it is called the **Ubhayachari** formation by the ancient teachers. However, some say there is no strict rule in their words; a person born under Vesi may be untruthful, face extreme hardships, and have weak or "soft" vision. || 60 ||

### Now, the results of the Vasi formation.

The person will have a slanted gaze <note>original: "tiryak-dṛṣṭi"</note>, but will be courageous, truthful, and compassionate. They will have a very tall body and be inclined toward laziness. If this **Vasi** <note>The text here uses "Vesi" and "Vasi" interchangeably in the result headers</note> formation is present at birth, the person may have little wealth but will possess great eloquence and command of speech. || 61 ||

### Now, the results of the Ubhayachari formation.

If a person is born under the **Ubhayachari** <note>original: "ubhayacarī" — moving on both sides [of the Sun]</note> formation, they will be very well-proportioned and achieve great fame. They will not be too tall, will be blessed with strong and pure offspring, and will always be prosperous. They are exceptionally steady-minded, straightforward in their dealings, patient with everyone, and possess a noble intellect. || 62 ||

### Now, the knowledge of Male, Female, and Eunuch births.

One must look at the strength and weakness of the planets that cause these formations. || 63 || From this, the determination of male or female is made; if these specific conditions are not met, then **eunuch** <note>original: "klība" — neuter or third gender</note> formations occur. || 64 || 

If the **Ascendant** <term>Lagna: the sign rising on the eastern horizon</term>, the Moon, Jupiter, and the Sun are in odd signs and in odd subdivisions, a male is born. Similarly, if they are in even signs and even subdivisions at the time of conception or birth, a female is born. || 65 || 

Apart from the Ascendant, if **Saturn** <note>original: "bhāskara-ātmaja" — the son of the Sun</note> is in an odd sign, he grants a son; in an even sign, he is said to grant a daughter, provided he is not aspected by any other planets. || 66 ||

## Now, he describes the six formations for sterility.

If the **Sun** and the **Moon** are situated in odd and even signs respectively and aspect <note>original: "ni-rīkṣyete" — to look at or cast an astrological aspect upon</note> one another; or if **Mercury** and **Saturn** do the same, they create a person who is sterile <note>original: "napuṃsakaṃ" — neuter or impotent</note>. || 67 ||

If **Mars** is in an odd sign and the **Sun** is in an even sign, and they aspect each other; or if **Mars** in an odd sign aspects the **Ascendant** <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> and the **Moon**, both of which are in even signs. || 68 ||

If **Mercury** and the **Moon** are aspected by **Mars** while they are in odd and even signs respectively; or if the **Ascendant**, the **Moon**, and **Venus** are all placed in odd-numbered **Navamshas** <term>Navamsha: a one-ninth division of a zodiac sign used for fine-tuning astrological predictions</term>. || 69 ||

## Now, he describes the determination of livelihood for living beings.

One should declare the source of wealth based on the strength of the planets located in the **tenth house** <note>original: "māna" — another term for the 10th house, representing honor and profession</note> from the Ascendant or the Moon. Wealth may come from the father, mother, enemies, friends, brothers, and so on, or even from servants. Among the **Sun**, the **Ascendant**, and the **Moon**, whoever is strongest should be noted; the experts say one's profession is determined by the lord of the **Navamsha** occupied by the lord of the tenth house from that strongest point. || 70 ||

If the lord of that Navamsha is the **Sun** <note>original: "vāsara-nāyaka" — the lord of the day</note>, the person lives by medicine, gold, trade in liquids, pearls, gems, or perhaps through deception or various forms of gambling. || 71 ||

Experts say one might also live by teaching mantras, alchemy <note>original: "rasa-vāda" — literally "the way of mercury," referring to chemical or medicinal preparations</note>, entertainment, or through the study of all the scriptures and ancient histories. Following the path of imparting knowledge, such a person is honored by kings if the Navamsha belongs to the **Sun**. || 72 ||

If it is the **Moon’s** Navamsha, the livelihood comes from the sale of aquatic products, working with wells, through pottery and clay-work, or through the uncertain service of the king's women, or perhaps the trade of garments. || 73 ||

If it is the **Son of the Earth's** <note>original: "dhara-suta" — an epithet for the planet Mars</note> Navamsha, the person lives by working with minerals and metals, through combat and battle, through alchemy involving fire, by instigating quarrels, or through daring deeds and even the profession of a thief. || 74 ||

If it is **Mercury’s** Navamsha, the livelihood is through crafts, poetry, traditional scriptures, and knowledge of the stars <note>original: "jyotir-gaṇa" — the study of the celestial bodies, astrology/astronomy</note>. It may also come from studying the meaning of the Vedas, cooking, or under the guise of being a priest. || 75 ||

If it is **Jupiter’s** Navamsha, they speak of a livelihood through serving the gods and the twice-born <note>original: "bhū-sura" — an epithet for Brahmins or the priestly class</note>, or as a teacher. It may come from the path of the ancient histories, scriptures, and ethics, or by teaching religion and lending money at interest <note>original: "kusīda"</note>. || 76 ||

The noble teachers say that a living is made from gold, rubies, elephants, and horses. By trading in jaggery, cooked rice, milk, and curds, or by the attraction of women... <note>This refers to the results of Venus, which continues on the following page.</note>

# Now, the Chapter on the Varieties of Killers.

There are three types of life-span formations: short life, middle life, and long life. A lifespan before thirty-two years is "short life," and after that is "middle life." || 1 ||

Beyond sixty-four years, it is declared "long life." O best of sages <note>original: "muni-sattama" — referring to the student Maitreya</note>, an "excellent life" is known to be beyond one hundred years. However, the lifespan of a child cannot be accurately determined before twenty-four years of age. || 2 ||

During this early period, one should protect the child through prayers, fire-offerings, and medical treatments <note>original: "japa-homa-cikitsādyair"</note>. Some children die due to the karmic faults of the father, and others due to the planetary positions of the mother. || 3 ||

Others die due to "evil-omen formations" <term>Arishta Yoga: planetary combinations signifying misfortune or early death</term>. Thus, there are three types of early childhood death. For one born with a "short life" formation, death should be predicted during the "danger star" <gloss>Vipat-tārā: the 3rd star from the birth star</gloss>. || 4 ||

For one born with a "middle life" formation, death occurs during the "adversary star" <gloss>Pratyari-tārā: the 5th star from the birth star</gloss>. For those born with "long life" formations, death occurs during the "slayer star" <gloss>Vadha-tārā: the 7th star from the birth star</gloss>. || 5 ||

Within these three general categories, each type is further divided into three sub-types. || 6 ||

Short life has three kinds: short-short, short-middle, and short-full. Likewise, the middle lifespan has three sub-types. || 7 ||

And the long lifespan also has three sub-types: short-long, middle-long, and full-long. In this way, the determination of lifespan is described in many varieties. || 8 ||

The eighth house and the third house from the Ascendant are declared the houses of life. The second and seventh houses are called the "killer houses" <term>Maraka-sthana: houses that indicate the end of life</term>. || 9 ||

One should apply the following three methods to check for consistency in determining the three types of lifespan: [1] the lords of the Ascendant and the eighth house, [2] the Ascendant and the Moon, and [3] the Ascendant and the Hora chart <note>a specific divisional chart used for wealth and longevity</note>. || 10 ||

If the indicators are in Moveable signs, they indicate Long Life; if one is in a Moveable sign and the other in a Fixed sign, they indicate Middle Life; if one is in a Moveable sign and the other in a Dual sign, they indicate Short Life. <note>The text here describes a specific mathematical method of comparing pairs of indicators to categorize longevity.</note> || 11 ||

## Commentary

**On Moveable signs, etc.:** If both the **Ascendant Lord** <term>Lagnesha: the planet ruling the first house of the birth chart</term> and the **8th Lord** <term>Ashtamesha: the planet ruling the house of longevity and death</term> are placed in **Moveable signs** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn</note>, the person will have a **long life**. 

If both the Ascendant Lord and the 8th Lord are placed in a combination of **Fixed** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius</note> and **Dual signs** <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces</note>, there is also **long life**.

If the Ascendant Lord and 8th Lord are placed in a combination of **Moveable** and **Fixed signs**, there is **medium life**. Similarly, if they are in **Fixed** and **Dual signs**, it results in **medium life**.

If both are in **Fixed signs**, there is **short life**. If they are in a combination of **Moveable** and **Dual signs**, there is also **short life**. 

These same rules should be used to determine longevity by comparing the positions of **Saturn** <note>original: "Manda"</note> and the **Moon**, and also by comparing the **Ascendant** and the **Hora Lagna** <term>a special mathematical point used specifically for longevity and wealth calculations</term>. || 11 ||

First, one must determine the extent of a person's life—whether it is **short, medium, or full**—based on these combinations <term>Yogas</term>. Only after this should the astrologer consider the **Killers** <term>Marakas: planets designated as indicators of death</term>. || 12 ||

For those born with **Scorpio** or **Capricorn** as their rising sign, **Rahu** <note>the North Node of the Moon</note> becomes the planet that grants death. Depending on the variations of planetary positions, **Saturn** will certainly be the killer. || 13 ||

The two known as **Mandi** and **Ketu** <note>shadowy mathematical points/planets</note> are designated as "Great Killers." The lords of the **7th house** <note>original: "jāyā"</note> and the **2nd house** <note>original: "kuṭumbaka"</note> are killers, as is the lord of the **8th house**. || 14 ||

Generally, death occurs during the planetary periods <term>Dashas</term> of the signs. Specifically, if the **6th house** is occupied by many malefic planets, the **lord of the 6th house** becomes the primary killer. || 15 ||

Or, the planet placed in a trine <note>the 5th or 9th house</note> from the 6th house is considered a primary killer. In the case of **medium life**, death occurs during the period of the 6th or 8th lord. || 16 ||

In cases of **long or short life**, the trines of the 6th house should be considered. If the 6th house is strong, one should predict death in its trine. || 17 ||

If the **lord of the 6th house** is powerful, death should be predicted in its trine. This entire system of arrangement should also be followed during the periods of the **Significators** <term>Karaka Dashas</term>. || 18 ||

The determination of which sign becomes the "Killer Sign" is made by the rule of **Moveable, Fixed, and Dual signs** mentioned previously. || 19 ||

Death should be predicted during the period of the **Killer Lord**, or during the period of a **malefic planet** situated in a killer house, or during the sub-periods of planets associated with the primary period lord. || 20 ||

If death does not occur then, it happens during the period of the **12th lord** <note>original: "vyayādhīśa"</note>. If that is also not the case, it occurs during the sub-periods of planets connected to the 12th house or its lord. || 21 ||

In the absence of those, death occurs in the period of the **8th lord**. If **Saturn** is joined with malefic planets and associated with a killer planet... || 22 ||

...then Saturn overpowers all other planets and becomes the killer, dealing out the results of sinful deeds. || 23 ||

When Saturn is the planet performing the malefic action and is connected to a killer planet, he certainly overpowers all other planets and becomes the bringer of death. || 24 ||

### The First Section: Chapter 23 on the Varieties of Killers

Death should be predicted only after carefully considering the sub-periods <term>Antardasha: a smaller time cycle within a major planetary period</term> and other factors. One must examine the lord of the **sixth decanate** <term>Drekkana: a 10-degree division of a zodiac sign</term> as well as the lord of the **house of destruction** <note>The 8th house, which governs death and transformation</note>. || 25 ||

The lords of the **danger, obstacle, and death stars** <note>original: "Vipat, Pratyari, and Vadha stars." These are the 3rd, 5th, and 7th Nakshatras (lunar mansions) counted from one's birth star</note> must also be known, as well as the lords of the beginning and end portions, and the planet ruling the sign occupied by the **Moon**. || 26 ||

During the designated time periods, the **Killer** <term>Maraka: a planet with the power to end life</term> brings about death. The wise have stated that the final departure occurs during the ripening of the lord of the **evil stars**. || 27 ||

If the **Ascendant Lord** <note>original: "Angapa"</note> is in a specific house <note>The text mentions "Hari," likely referring to Leo or a specific solar position</note>, the life is short; if in a friend's house, it is full; and if in a neutral house, it is medium. Scholars of the essence of horoscopy say that if the Ascendant Lord is in a friendly, neutral, or inimical sign, the life will be full, medium, or short, respectively. || 28 ||

Now, O twice-born <note>original: "Dvija," referring here to the student/Brahmin being addressed</note>, I shall describe the planet known as the **Killer**. I will explain the different results to you. || 29 ||

O best of the twice-born, one should contemplate the results from the **Soul-Significator** <term>Atmakaraka: the planet with the highest degree in the birth chart, representing the soul</term>. Check the third, sixth, eighth, twelfth, second, and seventh houses. || 30 ||

The strongest planet among all these is called the **Killer** planet. If all are equal in strength, then the planet specifically designated as the "Maraka" takes precedence. || 31 ||

The **lord of the sixth house** is generally remembered as the Killer in many ways. Among all the candidates, the sixth lord is the primary authority of death. || 32 ||

Consider the sign occupied by the Killer planet, or the lord of that Killer planet. During their **Great Periods** <term>Mahadasha: the major planetary period ruling a span of years</term>, one should apply the systems of *Vimshottari* <note>A 120-year planetary cycle system</note> or *Sthira* <note>A fixed dasha system</note>. || 33 ||

O best of the twice-born, know without a doubt that death occurs during a malefic period. If many Killer planets are endowed with great strength... || 34 ||

...then during their various sub-periods, O Brahmin, the occurrence of disease and suffering is possible. Death certainly occurs during the period of the **lord of the sixth house**. || 35 ||

Depending on the variations of strength (lesser or greater), many planets can act as Killers. The period of a lord of a sign occupied by a weak planet will give only a small amount of trouble. || 36 ||

However, during the period of a powerful [malefic], there will be great disease, agony, and death. There will be fear, grief, and danger from **thieves and fire**. || 37 ||

In the period of the Killer, one finds the great refuge of death. I shall now describe the sub-periods to you. || 38 ||

Consider the major period of the sign that hosts the Killer planet. One should calculate from the Significator, the Ascendant, the **seventh house**, or the **second house**. || 39 ||

Death occurs in the sub-period of the lords of the **sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses**. Among the lords of these sub-periods, whichever is the strongest [malefic]... || 40 ||

...death certainly occurs during that specific sub-period. Otherwise, during a malefic time, the person will suffer from disease, grief, and pain, O Brahmin. || 41 ||

For a strong **Venus** and **Saturn**, one should consider the sixth, eighth, and other houses. It should also be known through the lords of the second and seventh houses...

Between the **Ascendant** <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term> and the **seventh house**, the stronger of the two should be chosen for these considerations. The sign that is identified through these methods is agreed to be the Killer. Death occurs during its Dasha without a doubt, O best of the twice-born. || 52 ||

In this chapter, one should declare the death of the person only after carefully weighing all the planetary combinations <term>Yogas: specific alignments of planets</term> that I have spoken of. || 53 ||

->### The Beginning of the Chapter on Life Expectancy<-

->**Maitreya said:**<-

O Great Sage, O fortunate one, you are the knower of all actions <note>original: "karma-vetta"</note>. The path of **life expectancy** <term>Ayurdaya: the calculation of the span of life</term> is deep and mysterious. O Ocean of Mercy, explain it to me clearly and without doubt. || 1 ||

->**Parashara said:**<-

I shall now describe to you the path of life expectancy. By simply understanding this science, one truly becomes a **Knower of Time** <note>original: "Kalajña"; a term for an astrologer who can perceive the timing of events</note>. One should calculate the lifespan through the lords of the Ascendant and the eighth house... || 2 ||

<summary>This page concludes the rules for identifying "Killer" planets, emphasizing the roles of the 6th and 8th houses and Rahu, before transitioning into a new chapter where Maitreya asks Parashara to explain the complex calculations for determining the length of a human life.</summary>

<header>Section 1: Chapter 24 — On the Calculation of Life Expectancy</header>

...I shall now correctly describe the combinations for **long**, **medium**, and **short life** expectancy. || 3 ||

O best of the twice-born <note>original: "dvijottama"; referring to the student Maitreya</note>, if both the **lord of the Ascendant** <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term> and the **lord of the eighth house** <term>Randhra: the house associated with longevity and the cause of death</term> are situated in **movable signs** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn</note>, it should be known without a doubt as a combination for a **full lifespan** <term>Purnayu: a long life, typically 75–100+ years</term>. || 4 ||

If the lord of the Ascendant is in a **fixed sign** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius</note> and the lord of the eighth house is in a **dual sign** <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces</note>, a leader among mathematicians would say that this also results in a combination for a **full lifespan**. || 5 ||

O best of the twice-born, if the **lord of the body** <note>The lord of the Ascendant</note> is in a **dual sign** and the lord of the eighth house is in a **fixed sign**, it is also to be known as a combination for a **full lifespan** without any doubt. || 6 ||

Now, I shall describe the excellent combinations for a **medium lifespan** <term>Madhyayu: a middle-range life, typically 32–75 years</term>. O learned one, if the lord of the Ascendant is in a **movable sign** and the lord of the eighth house is in a **fixed sign**... || 7 ||

...then know it to be a **medium lifespan**. Likewise, if both are in **dual signs**, they result in a **medium lifespan**. Now, I shall speak before you regarding the combinations for a **short lifespan** <term>Alpayu: a short life, typically up to 32 years</term>. || 8 ||

O highly wise one, if the lord of the body is in a **movable sign** and the lord of the eighth house is in a **dual sign**, it is a combination for **short life**. || 9 ||

If both the lords of the Ascendant and the eighth house are in **fixed signs**, or if one is in a **fixed sign** and the other is in a **movable sign**, O twice-born, this should be understood as a **very short lifespan** <note>original: "svalpayus"</note> as ordained by the Creator. || 10 ||

Just as before, the combinations for longevity should also be considered from the perspective of the **Ascendant and the Moon**. Furthermore, one should calculate this from the **Moon and Saturn** or from the **Ascendant and the Seventh House** <note>original: "dyune"</note>. || 11 ||

A leader among mathematicians should consider these three methods of calculation equally. One should deeply contemplate the lifespan based on whether these three combinations yield the same result. || 12 ||

If two of the three combinations yield the same result and the third is different, then the result shared by the two should be accepted, and the lone result should be discarded. || 13 ||

If all three methods yield different results, O twice-born, then the longevity determined by the **Hora Lagna** <term>Hora Lagna: a special mathematical point used specifically for longevity and wealth</term> and the **Ascendant** should be taken as certain. || 14 ||

The first combination I mentioned, O twice-born, is derived from the lord of the Ascendant and the lord of the eighth house. The second combination should be considered from the Ascendant and the **Hora Lagna**. || 15 ||

The third combination should always be considered from **Saturn and the Moon**. O twice-born, some also consider the calculation from the **Ascendant and the Moon**, or even from the Seventh house. || 16 ||

I shall now describe the **construction of the mathematical diagram** <term>Yantroddharam: the drawing or extraction of a chart/grid</term>; listen to this, O best of the twice-born. Draw four horizontal lines and four vertical lines. || 17 ||

This creates a grid of nine squares <note>A 3x3 table</note> for the three types of longevity: long, medium, and short. In the first three, write "Movable" <note>Char</note>, and below them in order... || 18 ||

...O best of the twice-born, write **Movable**, **Fixed**, and **Dual**. In the middle row of squares, write **Fixed** in all three, and below that, write them as **Dual**... || 19 ||

...**Dual**, **Movable**, and **Fixed**. This should be written without doubt. In the final three, write **Dual** <note>Dvisvabhava</note>, and below that, indicate **Fixed**. || 20 ||

Then, a wise person should write **Fixed**, **Dual**, and **Movable** in order.

<header>Summary of the Great Parashara Hora</header>

According to the horizontal cells, the life span is categorized as long, medium, or short. || 21 ||
In this way, O Priest <note>original: "vipra"; a learned scholar</note>, there are three rows. Starting with the first row, the signs are categorized as movable, fixed, and then dual. || 22 ||
O twice-born <note>original: "dvija"</note>, one should draw a square diagram <term>yantra: here, a mathematical grid or chart</term> containing nine internal cells. In the three upper cells, one should write the first numbers. || 23 ||
In the horizontal rows, write the numbers two and three; do this across the three horizontal rows as well. Below that, in the upper row, write the numbers one, three, and two. || 24 ||
In the middle of the upper rows, write two, then one, then three. In the final upper row, O best of the twice-born, write three, then two, then one. || 25 ||
In this specific order, O Priest, within the three rows of cells, the long, medium, and short life spans are to be understood. || 26 ||
Following the order from top to bottom, in the three cells on the left side, one should know long life <term>Dirghayu: a full lifespan, usually 75–100 years</term> without any doubt. || 27 ||
The middle three cells represent medium life <term>Madhyayu</term>, and the three cells on the right represent short life <term>Alpayu</term>. O best of the twice-born, twenty-seven variations have been described. || 28 ||
O Priest, for the **Lord of the Ascendant** and the **Lord of the Eighth House**, there are three sets of three. One must understand these nine cells for the purpose of calculating the life span. || 29 ||
Similarly, one should understand the cells for the **Ascendant and the Moon**; and nine cells are also known for the **Ascendant and the Hourly Ascendant** <term>Hora-lagna: a specialized calculated point used for longevity and wealth</term>. || 30 ||
Thus, through the different types of movable and other signs, I shall now explain the various distinctions to you. || 31 ||

## The Longevity Chart of Various Distinctions

| **Long Life** | **Medium Life** | **Short Life** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Long Life** <br> Ascendant Lord: **Movable** (1) <br> 8th Lord: **Movable** (1) | **Medium Life** <br> Ascendant Lord: **Movable** (1) <br> 8th Lord: **Fixed** (2) | **Short Life** <br> Ascendant Lord: **Movable** (1) <br> 8th Lord: **Dual** (3) |
| **Long Life** <br> Ascendant Lord: **Fixed** (2) <br> 8th Lord: **Dual** (3) | **Medium Life** <br> Ascendant Lord: **Fixed** (2) <br> 8th Lord: **Movable** (1) | **Short Life** <br> Ascendant Lord: **Fixed** (2) <br> 8th Lord: **Fixed** (2) |
| **Long Life** <br> Ascendant Lord: **Dual** (3) <br> 8th Lord: **Fixed** (2) | **Medium Life** <br> Ascendant Lord: **Dual** (3) <br> 8th Lord: **Dual** (3) | **Short Life** <br> Ascendant Lord: **Dual** (3) <br> 8th Lord: **Movable** (1) |

<header>First Section: Chapter 24 on Determination of Lifespan</header>
<sig>11</sig>

Sometimes it is said thus, O best of the twice-born <note>original: "dvija-sattama"; a term of respect for a learned student or priest</note>: one pair is the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign</term> and the Lord of the Eighth House; another is the Ascendant and the Moon. || 32 ||

The third pair is the Ascendant and the Hora <term>Hora: a specific divisional chart or hour-unit</term>. O twice-born, these are the three methods. From the agreement of these, the various combinations <note>original: "yoga"; planetary arrangements that produce specific results</note> are spoken of. || 33 ||

Regarding the divisions of long, medium, and short life, the classification based on movable and other signs is now described. These spans are characterized by values of 32, 64, or 96 years; || 34 ||

Or they may be 36, 72, or 108 years; or likewise 40, 80, or 120 years <note>these represent three different scales used to calculate the total potential human lifespan</note>. || 35 ||

Where other planetary lifespan combinations exist, the same principles apply to the remainder. Now I shall speak of the clarification of the lifespan that has been arrived at. || 36 ||

Full value is taken at the beginning of a sign, loss is taken at the end, and by proportion <term>anupata: mathematical rule of three or interpolation</term>, the middle value is found. The "clear" <term>sphuta: the mathematically precise value</term> number of years is said to be half the sum of two values. || 37 ||

In this way, the wise should calculate for pairs or for all three methods. Where the lifespan has been determined by the web of combinations produced [by the planets], || 38 ||

If a "long" lifespan is obtained, the actual result will be within the limit of the "medium" span. O most wise one, calculate this without doubt through the proportion of the fall into the "clear" value. || 39 ||

One should add the years obtained by proportion to the middle-most value. Know that the "long life" clarified in this way is fluctuating <note>original: "capalatmakah"; literally "moving" or "unstable," referring to how the precise length of life can shift based on mathematical refinements</note> in nature. || 40 ||

If a "medium" life is obtained there, a "short" success <note>meaning a lifespan in the lower category</note> is possible. Using proportion as before, one joins it to the middle life span. || 41 ||

Sometimes, when a "short" life results from all combinations, and where the proportion of the houses is applied, then one division <term>khanda: a segment or block of time</term> is achieved. || 42 ||

I have described the determination of lifespan through the application of three divisions: those of 32, 36, and 40 years, O twice-born. || 43 ||

What should be taken? From where should it be taken? Which measure should sometimes be accepted? To remove such doubts, I shall explain them separately. || 44 ||

When the combination for longevity arises from the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Eighth House, the 40-year division should be taken, O best of the twice-born. || 45 ||

If "short" life appears in all three methods of calculation, O best of the twice-born, the 32-year division should be understood, as told by Brahma <note>referring to the divine origin of these astrological laws</note>. || 46 ||

Sometimes, through proportion, the result is attained. For the 32-year span <note>original: "dantabdena"; 'danta' (teeth) is a numerical code for 32</note>, if there is doubt, one should consider the "Rudra Shula" <note>original: "rudrashulam"; a specific method of calculation or a point of affliction named after the spear of Shiva</note>. || 47 ||

Now I shall describe the method of proportion, O twice-born. Setting aside the clear values for the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Eighth House separately... || 48 ||

<meta>catchword: Leave the signs passed, O priest, multiply by the remaining...</meta>

<header>The Essence of the Great Hora of Parashara</header>

...one should declare the years obtained for a single segment through the Rule of Three. || 49 ||

O twice-born, regarding the lifespan resulting from the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagnesha: the planet ruling the rising sign</term> and the Lord of the Eighth House <note>The 8th house is the primary house of longevity and death</note>, take the sum of the two total year-figures and divide by half to find the "clear" <term>sphuta: the mathematically precise value</term> result. || 50 ||

If a long lifespan is indicated, O priest, add it to seventy-two years. Then, when added to eighty, the definition of "Long Life" becomes precise. || 51 ||

In the case of a medium life, where the years do not reach thirty-six <note>In the 108-year system, 36 years represents one 'kakshya' or third of the total potential span</note>, the medium life is arrived at by adding the years calculated through proportion. || 52 ||

O best of the twice-born, I shall now explain the Rule of Three <term>trairashika: a mathematical method using three known values to find a fourth</term> to you. Place the "Standard" <note>original: "pramana"</note> and the "Requirement" <note>original: "iccha"</note> at the two ends. || 53 ||

In the middle, O twice-born, multiply the "Result" <note>original: "phala"</note> of a different category by the "Requirement." Dividing that by the "Standard" gives the corrected result; that is called the proportional calculation. || 54 ||

O priest, one should apply this proportion for long and medium lifespans. In the case of a short lifespan, this specific proportional calculation is absent <note>short life calculations are often treated as more fixed or less subject to this specific interpolation</note>. || 55 ||

The lifespan being lived is counted from the moment of birth. This method applies to the pair of the Ascendant and the Hora, and likewise to the Ascendant and the Moon. || 56 ||

The lifespan arrived at is made precise at its final segment. In all these planetary combinations, O priest, one must perform the refinement through proportion. || 57 ||

At the first degree of the Hora Lagna <term>Hora Lagna: a special mathematical point used specifically for longevity and wealth</term> and others, the value is full; at the end of a sign, it is nothing. This is the method of clarification for long, medium, and short lifespans. || 58 ||

Having calculated the Hora Lagna precisely down to the seconds of an arc, O best of the twice-born, one should again apply the Rule of Three as before. || 59 ||

By adding this to the final segments, the determination of lifespan is made. Within a span of two and a half *ghatikas* <term>ghatika: a traditional unit of time equal to 24 minutes; 2.5 ghatikas equals one hour</term>, there are thirty degrees <note>referring to the rate at which the Hora Lagna moves through the zodiacal signs</note>, O twice-born. || 60 ||

Having brought the years from the Sun and the signs of the Ascendant according to the previous method, I shall speak further of this in the coming chapters, O best of the twice-born. || 61 ||

Now I shall explain the causes for calculating lifespan, specifically the reduction <term>hrasa: decrease</term> and increase of the "sectors" <term>kakshya: a 36-year division of the total 108-year lifespan</term> due to the influence of Saturn, O twice-born. || 62 ||

When the Lord of the Ascendant is joined with Saturn, or when the Lord of the Hora is so joined, O twice-born... || 63 ||

...a reduction of the sector occurs, especially if Saturn is weak <note>original: "nirbala"</note>. || 64 ||

In the context of the total lifespan, three sectors are mentioned here. I shall now state the measures of the long, medium, and short forms. || 65 ||

One sector is comprised of thirty-six years. If a reduction of one sector occurs, then a medium life will undoubtedly result, O best of the twice-born. || 66 ||

If a medium life was already indicated and a reduction occurs, it certainly becomes a short life.

This movement between categories is known as "Sectoral Reduction" (Kakshya Hrasa) or "Sectoral Increase" (Kakshya Vriddhi).</meta>

<header>First Section: Chapter 24 on the Determination of Lifespan</header>

## First Section: Chapter 24 on the Determination of Lifespan

If a combination for short life is present and Saturn <note>original: "Shani"</note> also forms a specific planetary combination, a reduction of the sector occurs, O twice-born <term>dvija: a term for a Brahmin, meaning "twice-born"</term>. This reduction consists of thirty-six years. || 67 ||

One should recognize this as an indication of "extremely short life" <note>In Vedic astrology, this usually refers to a lifespan of less than 32 years</note>, and death may occur in childhood. || 68 ||

Now, O priest, if Saturn forms a combination within the three types of planetary yogas, there is a reduction of eleven years for each; this is the sequence of sectoral reduction. || 69 ||

Next, to determine specific results, I shall describe merits and defects. Saturn <term>Sauri: another name for Saturn, literally "Son of the Sun"</term>, when filled with merits, causes an "increase of the sector" <term>kakshya vriddhi: the mathematical promotion of a lifespan from one category, such as 'short', to the next, such as 'medium'</term>. || 70 ||

When associated with defects, a loss occurs; the final decision is stated based on these two. O son of the Sun, when Saturn is endowed with merits such as being in its own sign or its sign of exaltation <term>tunga: the zodiac sign where a planet is at its most powerful</term>... || 71 ||

...it causes an increase in the sector, O priest, increasing the lifespan by one division. Thus, an "extremely short life" becomes "short life," and a "short life" becomes "medium life." || 72 ||

From "medium life" arises "long life"—this is the characteristic of sectoral increase. Conversely, if Saturn is in its sign of debilitation <term>nicha: the zodiac sign where a planet is at its weakest</term> or in an enemy's sign, and is joined with the gaze of malefic planets... || 73 ||

...it causes a reduction of the sector, O priest, decreasing the life by a third. A "long life" becomes "medium life," and "medium life" becomes "short life." || 74 ||

A "short life" descends to "extremely short life," and death in childhood becomes possible. This also occurs when the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagnesha: the planet ruling the rising sign</term> or the Lord of the Hora is joined only by Saturn... || 75 ||

...in a malefic sign, joined by malefics, or viewed by malefics. However, O twice-born, one should not calculate a reduction of the sector unless the planet is in a sign of debilitation or an enemy's sign. || 76 ||

Similarly, if the planet lacks exaltation and other merits, one should not calculate an increase in the sector. But if it is in a benefic sign, joined by benefic planets, viewed by benefics, and in its sign of exaltation... || 77 ||

...and free from malefic combinations, Saturn causes an increase in the sector. In the same way, sectoral reduction arises from defects like debilitation. || 78 ||

If the planetary positions are neutral or mixed, the determination becomes extremely difficult. Now I shall describe the second method of sectoral increase... || 79 ||

...which occurs through a relationship with Jupiter <term>Guru: the planet Jupiter, considered the 'Great Benefic' or Teacher</term>, O best of the twice-born. If Jupiter is in the first house or the seventh house, and is endowed with merits like exaltation... || 80 ||

...and is in a benefic sign with benefic aspects, Jupiter causes an increase in the sector. For one whose survival is in doubt, this provides an increase to a short lifespan. || 81 ||

It turns "short life" into "medium life," and at the end of "medium life," it grants "long life." Thus, I explain these various distinctions and sub-divisions to you. || 82 ||

Now, O priest, I shall show you the factors that obstruct lifespan, even when a "long life" combination has been attained through various methods. || 83 ||

<header>Summary of the Great Parashara Horoscopy</header>

Now, regarding the desire to know in which specific planetary period <term>dasha: a period of time in a person's life ruled by a specific planet or zodiac sign</term> death will occur, I shall explain the method of decision to you. || 84 ||

When a person is found to have a "long life" <note>original: "dirghayu"</note>, one should look for the end point within that range. If the "medium life" <note>original: "madhyamayu"</note> category is determined without any contradictory factors, death is said to occur within those specific years. || 85 ||

Having obtained the combination for medium life through the previously described methods, one should consider the timing of death after the "short life" range has passed without doubt. || 86 ||

O best of the twice-born <term>dvija: a member of the priestly or scholarly class</term>, if a combination for short life is found, one should reflect upon that specific segment of time to see in which planetary period death will manifest. || 87 ||

In the case of long life, one should consider death after seventy-two years. In the case of medium life, one should consider it after thirty-six years. || 88 ||

Now I shall clearly describe death based on the "affliction" <note>original: "malina," meaning soiled, impure, or weakened by malefic planets</note> of the "Door" <term>dvara: a technical sign in Jaimini astrology used as a gateway for timing events</term> and "External" <term>bahya: the sign corresponding to the 'door' sign's position relative to the period-lord</term> signs. This was spoken of in ancient times by the Trident-Wielder <note>original: "Trishuli," referring to Lord Shiva</note>. || 89 ||

O priest, when the Door sign and the Lord of the Door sign are afflicted in the ninth-part divisional chart <term>navamsha: a chart that divides each zodiac sign into nine equal parts to see the hidden strength of planets</term>, death truly comes to the person born; of this, there is no doubt. || 90 ||

O priest, one must carefully consider both the "Period Sign" <term>paka: the sign acting as the primary ruler of a timeframe</term> and the "Experience Sign" <term>bhoga: the sign that shows the results of that timeframe</term>. If the sign is naturally malefic, aspected by malefic planets, or associated with malefic planets... || 91 ||

...death will certainly occur during the planetary period of that ninth-part <note>original: "navamsha-dasha"</note>. O wise one, death happens during the sub-period <note>original: "antar-gate"</note> within that timeframe, without a doubt. || 92 ||

O twice-born, death may occur in the ninth-part of the Door or the External sign. When there is a malefic combination, it occurs within the sub-period of the ninth-part lord. || 93 ||

When the sign providing the planetary period is classified as malefic, the "Experience Sign" <note>original: "vibhoga"</note> is as far from the period sign as the period sign is from the Ascendant <term>lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term>. || 94 ||

I shall now speak regarding the "Ninth-part Step" <note>original: "navamshaka-pada"</note>. The duration of the period is fixed at nine years for each sign's ninth-part. || 95 ||

I have specifically explained the nine-year periods of the Door and External signs. One should consider the signs related to these when calculating the "Moving Periods" <term>chara dasha: a system where the periods of life are ruled by the zodiac signs themselves rather than planets</term>. || 96 ||

O priest, one should consider the Door and External signs only after clarifying the precise mathematical points of the houses <term>bhava-sphuta: the exact degree where an astrological house begins and ends</term>. Look at the ninth-parts of the planets within those precise house positions. || 97 ||

When the years are calculated using this method, death certainly occurs. In this way, the "Body House" <note>original: "tanvadi," the 1st house</note> and the other houses should be clarified according to the facts. || 98 ||

Based on the reverse order of the ninth-parts of the planets among the twelve signs' ninth-parts, one should specify the details of the lifespan calculated by the ninth-part method. || 99 ||

O priest, one should reflect on both the Door and External signs in this manner. If there is affliction, death is indicated, but not otherwise. || 100 ||

For other men...

<header>Chapter 24 on Longevity in the First Section</header>
<meta>CC-0 Shri Krishna Museum, Kurukshetra. Digitized by eGangotri</meta>

If a sign is afflicted <note>original: "malina," meaning occupied or aspected by malefic planets like Mars or Saturn</note> in all respects, one should reflect upon it. O twice-born <term>dvija: a member of the priestly or scholarly class</term>, death occurs in the portion of the Navamsha <term>navamsha: a divisional chart where each zodiac sign is divided into nine parts, used to assess planetary strength</term> that is occupied by an afflicted sign. || 101 ||

Likewise, during the period of the "variable dasha" <term>charadasha: a system of planetary periods based on the movement of zodiac signs</term>, when the Lord of the Door <note>original: "dvaresha"</note> is in an afflicted sign, or in the portion of the sign where that lord resides, death may occur. || 102 ||

Furthermore, during the "variable dasha," one should consider the "Door" and "External" signs. When the dasha reaches a trine <note>original: "trikona," the 1st, 5th, or 9th positions</note> from these, the death of the native occurs. || 103 ||

Alternatively, O best of the twice-born, one should consider the timing of death when the calculated lifespan combinations reach their conclusion, or when the indicators of death previously described are activated. || 104 ||

If the period of the "External" sign is afflicted, even if the dasha period has not yet ended, death will occur in the year corresponding to its trine position. || 105 ||

Now I shall clearly explain the exceptions to these death-dealing combinations. If there is an aspect from a benefic planet <note>original: "shubha-drishti," a "glance" from a helpful planet like Jupiter or Venus</note>, or a combination with a benefic planet, or the presence of a benefic celestial body; || 106 ||

And if this is not in the "Door" or "External" signs, then even if the Lord of the Door is considered, death will only occur during the specific portion of the dasha of the sign where the Lord of the Door resides. || 107 ||

Now, O best of the twice-born, even in the absence of benefic aspects or combinations, I shall explain the exception regarding the Navamsha periods. || 108 ||

O scholar, if the Lord of the Ascendant <term>lagnesha: the planet ruling the first house of the birth chart</term> is in its sign of exaltation <note>original: "tunga," the sign where a planet is at its maximum strength</note> at the time of birth, then even if the "Door" and "External" signs are afflicted, and even if there is an absence of benefic aspects, death occurs only in the Navamsha portion. || 109 ||

However, in such a case, death does not actually occur; rather, one should predict an increase of life for nine years beyond the calculated span. || 110 ||

O twice-born, during the dasha of the "Door" or "External" Navamsha, even until the very end of the period, the "Door" and "External" signs continue to function for another nine-year cycle. || 111 ||

When a connection to the second sign occurs within those nine years according to the movement of the planets, then an increase of the lifespan is certain. || 112 ||

When death finally occurs after this increase, it is the work of the Soul of the Universe, the Infallible One <note>original: "Vishvatmako-achyutah," referring to the divine timing of the Supreme Being</note>. The full combination for death is only realized when the benefic aspects are considered. || 113 ||

O best of the twice-born, I have clearly spoken to resolve the inquiry regarding the Lord of the Ascendant being in its exaltation sign. || 114 ||

O scholar, I shall now state without any doubt when death occurs during the dasha of the Lord of the Pada <term>padesha: the lord of the Arudha Pada, a calculated point representing the person's status and external image</term> for one who has received an increase in life. || 115 ||

Death occurs during the dasha of the Lord of the Pada, or in its Navamsha, or when the dasha reaches a trine from the Lord of the Eighth House <note>original: "ashtapatikona," the house of longevity and death</note> from the Ascendant, for one whose life has been extended. || 116 ||

If death does not occur even after taking these additional years into account, then death will certainly happen at the end of three dasha cycles. || 117 ||

The dasha of the Lord of the Pada, the Ascendant of that Pada, and the eighth house from that Pada... <note>The text cuts off mid-calculation.</note>

In a birth chart where Cancer is the rising sign <term>karkalagna: Cancer ascendant</term>, O priest, one should consider the following: [Look at] the ascendant, the seventh house <term>madana: the house of partners</term>, or the lord of the eighth house <term>ashtamesha: the planet ruling the house of death and longevity</term>. || 5 || Between these two, identify the one that is stronger and situated in a "pivot" house <note>original: "kendra," the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>. Then, determine if the life is long, medium, or short, just as described previously. || 6 || 

By applying the mathematical "rule of three" <term>trairashika: a proportional calculation method</term> to the dual segments as before, I shall now clearly speak these words regarding the calculation of longevity. || 7 || 

O twice-born <term>dvija: a member of the scholarly class</term>, if the planets are of equal strength or if the strength does not exceed a certain limit, the classification of long life and so on may not be potent; indeed, the lifespan may become the opposite of what was predicted. || 8 || 

What was thought to be long or medium might be short, or even very brief. When the planetary combinations <note>original: "yoga-bhanga," the shattering of a favorable alignment</term> are broken, this reversal is certain and beyond doubt. || 9 || 

O priest, if the indicator planet <term>karaka: a planet representing a specific life area, like the Sun for the soul or Saturn for longevity</term> is placed in the seventh house or the ninth house from the seventh, the predicted long life and other categories will be reversed. Now, the determination of longevity through many different variations is performed. This three-fold form—long, medium, and short life—was originally spoken by Lord Brahma. || 11 || 

In a birth chart <note>original: "janmapatra," a horoscope scroll</note>, one should consider both the lord of the rising sign and the lord of the eighth house. O priest, if they are in the fifth and eleventh houses, a long life <term>dirghayu</term> is produced. || 12 || 

If they are in the eleventh and third houses, one should judge it as medium longevity <term>madhyamayu</term>. If they are in the eleventh, the second <note>original: "vitta," the house of wealth</note>, or in trines <note>original: "trikona," the 1st, 5th, or 9th houses</note>, the life will be short <term>alpayu</term>, O twice-born. || 13 || 

If the two lords are in the eleventh house while also indicating "expired life" <note>original: "gatayu," a term for a stillborn child or one who dies immediately after birth</note>, then even the newborn does not survive. One should consider such combinations for all living beings. || 14 || 

Starting from the portion of the Moon <note>original: "kshapakaramsha"</note>, one should calculate the "ascendant of longevity" <note>original: "ayurlagna"</note> using the rising times of the signs, without including the period before the actual sunrise. || 15 || 

In the calculation of the houses, a period of eight minutes <note>original: "ashta-vinadika"</note> arises. Through the rule of three, one should calculate the thirty-degree divisions of the signs. || 16 || 

O best of the twice-born, this calculation of signs, degrees, and minutes is considered an essential mathematical step for obtaining the mathematically corrected ascendant of longevity. || 17 || 

Now, longevity is described through a different path: [by looking at] the trines of the body <term>tanu: the 1st house</term>, its lord, and the lord of the sign where the 1st lord is placed. || 18 || 

Based on the measure of years assigned to each form—short, medium, or long life—a planet causes the departure from this world in conjunction with the lord of the eighth house. || 19 || 

O best of the twice-born, know without a doubt that if [the lords] are in the trine of the rising sign, the life is short. If they are in the trine of the lord of the rising sign, it is medium. || 20 || 

If the lord of the eighth house <term>randhranayaka</term> is in the trine of the lord of the sign where the first lord resides, long life is granted. This was formerly proclaimed by Lord Shiva <note>original: "Shambhu"</note>. || 21 ||

O best of the twice-born, after adding those twelve years to the previously calculated lifespan, one must then combine this with the sum of years belonging to the final planetary ruler. || 31 ||

One should naturally add the full twelve years to the "zero" starting point. In the middle degrees, one must perform a proportional calculation <term>anupata: the mathematical rule of three</term> to find the value to be added. || 34 || 

This addition should be performed confidently and naturally. In this way, the years belonging to the final planetary ruler are produced by their own nature. || 35 || 

If Venus is in a state of dissolution <note>original: "layasthita," potentially referring to combustion by the sun or a neutral state</note>, the addition of a year does not occur. If the calculation is reduced by the Sun and results in zero, the twelve-year addition is not applied. || 36 || 

If the Lord of the Eighth house alone is in its sign of highest exaltation <term>svoccha: the specific degree where a planet is most powerful</term>, it grants half of a cycle. If it is not so placed, it certainly destroys half a cycle of the lifespan. || 37 || 

Planets joined with the Lord of the Eighth house when it is in its sign of debilitation <term>neecha: the sign where a planet is weakest</term> each individually reduce the lifespan once the maximum age has been determined. || 38 || 

If planets are joined with the Lord of the Eighth in its sign of exaltation, each one increases the lifespan. The "Middle Cycle" is thus identified as the certain maximum longevity. || 39 ||

Mars, Saturn, and Rahu are progressively stronger in their power to cause death. A wise practitioner should set aside the especially weak planet and base their judgment on the strongest one. || 40 ||
