By adding half a year more, one should join it to the previously calculated lifespan. Thus, by the method of the internal lords, there is an addition to the moving cycle. || 46 ||

O best of the twice-born, even if a certain limit of longevity is granted by the Lord of the Eighth House, all of that should be increased by an additional half in this calculation. || 47 ||

Similarly, O priest, if the Lord of the Eighth House <term>randhrapati: the "Lord of the Chasm," a name for the ruler of the 8th house</term> is situated in its sign of debilitation <note>original: "neecha-rashi," the sign where a planet is at its weakest</note>, it undoubtedly destroys half of the longevity being granted. || 48 ||

Thus, O priest, if the Lord of the Eighth is joined with a debilitated planet, half of the longevity granted by that planet is lost. || 49 ||

In the same way, O priest, if the Lord of the Eighth is joined with an exalted planet <term>tunga-kheta: a planet in its highest, most powerful position</term>, the longevity granted by that planet is increased by half. || 50 ||

O King of Priests, thus the maximum lifespan is determined. When the longevity derived from the combination of the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Eighth House is calculated, || 51 ||

One should apply these refinements <note>original: "samskaram," adjustments or corrections to a mathematical result</note> based on the principles previously discussed. From the Lord of the Ascendant comes the lifespan, which is shaped by the specific quality of its mathematical combinations. || 52 ||

The planets joined with them—whether through the merits of exaltation or the faults of debilitation—cause the lifespan to increase or decrease. This should be performed according to the oral tradition. || 53 ||

The combinations for death involving two or three factors are powerful, as stated before. Even the natural lifespan yields to the strength of these combinations; death occurs during the ripening <term>paka: the period when a planet's influence comes to fruition</term> of that powerful planet. || 54 ||

Among the Sun, Mars, Rahu, and the Cripple <note>original: "pangu," a traditional epithet for Saturn because of its slow movement</note>, the strongest of these four planets determines the outcome. One should predict the native’s death according to the combination formed by that strongest planet. || 55 ||

When Saturn, Rahu, Mars, and the Sun are joined with the Lord of the Eighth House and are not aspected by other planets, one should indicate the person's death through them. || 56 ||

Among these, the strongest factor—determined by the sign it occupies—will cause death during its ripening period. Of this, one should have no doubt.

# The Summary of the Great Parashara’s Horoscopy

...O best of the twice-born. || 57 || Among these four planets, if one is notably strong, one should predict that death will occur during the sign-period <term>Rashi Dasha: a system where time periods are ruled by zodiac signs rather than planets</term> of that planet in the place of death. || 58 || When a major planetary period <term>Mahadasha</term> is identified as being overcome by death-bringing influences, it grants its results according to the sequence of its sub-periods <term>Antardasha</term>. || 59 || Even if death-inflicting qualities appear as harmless as water, death occurs during the sub-period of the house occupied by the deity of the "Trident" <note>original: "shula," referring to Shula Dasha, a timing system often used to predict periods of suffering or mortality</note>. || 60 || Even if Saturn and Rahu are connected with benefic planets, one should predict death during the planetary periods of their respective lords. || 61 || At that time, death certainly occurs during the ripening of the sign <note>original: "rashi-paka," meaning the period when the sign's influence manifests</note> where they reside. The results, as well as the timing of death, must be spoken of according to these variations. || 64 ||

If the lifespan is calculated as "middle," it should be understood that the signs of **lifespan category reduction** <term>Kaksha-hrasa: the demotion of a lifespan from one category (e.g., Long, 66–100 years) to a lower one (e.g., Middle, 33–66 years)</term> can bring it from the low category to even lower. || 75 || When a category reduction occurs, the result follows the same principles as previously stated. Now, I shall describe the exceptions to this single category reduction. || 79 || A reduction of one category might be altered if the lord of the second house is involved. Conversely, through a **benefic combination** <term>Shubhayoga</term>, there will be a **lifespan category increase** <term>Kaksha-vriddhi: the promotion of a lifespan category, such as from Short to Middle</term> as previously explained. || 80 ||

O Sage, one should contemplate the birth ascendant and the indicator planet as before. If in the first, seventh, second, twelfth, sixth, or eighth houses—these three pairs of locations— || 81 || a combination is formed by benefic planets, an increase in the lifespan category occurs. O Priest, one should also consider the two sets of trines. || 82 || If a benefic combination is formed in relation to the birth ascendant and the indicator planet, there is no doubt that an increase in lifespan category will occur, O best of the Twice-born. || 83 ||

If malefic planets are situated in their signs of debilitation <note>original: "nicastah," the weakest zodiacal position for a planet</note> and occupy trines from the indicator planet, O great wise one, a reduction of two categories will occur. || 84 || If there are benefic planets in benefic places within the trines from the indicator-portion, an increase in the lifespan category occurs there; of this there is no doubt, O best of the Twice-born. || 85 ||

If the indicator planet is preceded and followed by malefic planets, or is joined with a malefic, a reduction of the lifespan category occurs in that chart, O best of the Twice-born. || 86 || If the indicator planet is joined with a benefic, and benefic planets are in their signs of exaltation <note>original: "svatunge," the strongest zodiacal position</note>, a category increase occurs there without a doubt, O best of the Twice-born. || 87 ||

O Sage, I have described the reduction or increase caused by malefic and indicator planets. Now, I shall describe the lifespan category reduction and increase according to Jupiter. || 88 || O Priest, if two malefic planets are in the second, twelfth, first, sixth, or the trines, a reduction of the lifespan category occurs there as previously stated, O best of the Twice-born. || 89 ||

If Jupiter is debilitated, not in its exaltation, and is joined with malefic planets, a reduction of the lifespan category certainly occurs, O best of the Twice-born. || 90 || O Sage, the same application should be known regarding Jupiter's placement in the second house. All these categories are declared for the purpose of the results mentioned before. || 91 ||

Likewise, I shall state the exceptions regarding benefic combinations. If there is a combination with benefics in the aforementioned places, specifically involving the full Moon and Venus, O Twice-born... || 92 ||

## Summary of the Great Parashara Horoscopy

In this chapter on planetary combinations (*Yogas*), the focus is on the **reduction of the lifespan category** <term>Kaksha-hrasa: the demotion of a lifespan from one category, such as Long-life to Middle-life</term>, and not on its increase. In such cases, there is no doubt that the lifespan is reduced by the duration of one zodiac sign. || 93 || Among the malefic planets previously mentioned, Saturn is the primary **indicator of these combinations** <term>Yoga-karaka</term>. A reduction occurs specifically where a single sign is designated as the cause of the decrease. || 94 ||

Now, O best of the twice-born <note>original: "dvijottama," referring to the student Maitreya</note>, I shall explain death (*nidhanam*) with specificity, based on the **Fixed Period system** <term>Sthira Dasha: a timing system where signs are assigned fixed durations of 7, 8, or 9 years</term>. || 95 || The durations of seven, nine, and eight years <note>original: "shashi-nanda-pavaka," numerical codes representing 7, 9, and 3/8</note> are assigned to the signs as the "Fixed Dasha" based on the Sun's position in Movable, Fixed, or Dual signs. || 96 ||

Divide the signs into four segments (*khandas*), with three signs in each segment. One should carefully contemplate in which of these segments the combination for death occurs. || 97 || I state without any hesitation that death occurs in the specific segment where the **combination for death** <term>Mrityu-yoga</term> is observed. || 98 ||

I shall now describe the three types of combinations based on the distinctions of Long, Middle, and Short life. One must determine where the lifespan expires within the four segments. || 99 || Just as with the Long-life combinations, when a specific segment is reached, death certainly occurs in that segment; of this, there is no doubt. || 100 ||

O twice-born, in the cases of Middle and Short lifespans which I am about to describe, the period is characterized by the traits of the segments that harbor death. || 101 || Death certainly occurs during that specific period, O best of the twice-born. If death does not occur at that time, then the person will surely experience **intense suffering, sorrow, and fear**. || 102 ||

I shall now explain the refinement of this calculation again: death occurs during the period of a sign that is **hemmed between two malefic planets** <term>Papa-madhya: an astrological condition where a house or planet is "crushed" between two harmful influences</term>. || 103 || O Brahmin, if the trines <note>the 1st, 5th, and 9th houses</note> from either the Ascendant or the **indicator planet** <term>Karaka: the planet representing the self or soul</term> are occupied by malefics, or if the twelfth and eighth houses are similarly occupied by malefics... || 104 ||

...then death for the native will undoubtedly occur during that period. This must be analyzed with great effort within the segments of the Fixed Period system. || 105 || If the trines, the twelfth, or the eighth houses from a malefic-occupied sign are themselves occupied by malefics, death is certain to occur in that period. || 106 ||

Death does not occur when the period is hemmed by benefics; it only occurs when hemmed by malefics. To further clarify the matter of death, I shall now describe the **afflictions of the signs** <term>Rashi-dosha</term>. || 107 || If the waning Moon or Venus are aspected by the lords of the twelfth or eighth houses, death truly occurs in that period without a doubt. || 108 ||

Even the simple aspect of the waning Moon or the simple aspect of Venus can indicate the timing of death. One should contemplate death within the Fixed Period system through these aspects alone. || 109 || Regarding the house of death...

## Parashara said:

Now, I shall specifically explain the matter of death. O best of the twice-born, the nature of the sub-periods is known from the **Rudra** <term>Rudra: literally 'The Roarer,' a title given to the planet that acts as the harbinger of death in this specific system of calculation</term>. || 1 ||

One must consider the lords of the **Ascendant** <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term>, the seventh house (*Yuna*), or the eighth house (*Ashtama*). Among these, the strongest should be considered when joined with a **benefic aspect** <note>original: "shubha-drishti"; an 'aspect' is the way a planet 'looks at' and influences another house or planet</note>. If a planet is weak, it is called a "Secondary Rudra" (*Gauna Rudra*). || 3 ||

Life reaches its end at the "Trident of Rudra" (*Rudra-shula*), which occurs at the end of the **trines** <term>Trikona: the 1st, 5th, and 9th houses from a given point, considered the most auspicious and foundational houses</term>. Specifically, this occurs at the end of the Ascendant, the end of the fifth house, or the end of the ninth house—these are the three places. || 6 ||

One must contemplate these signs during their respective periods, O wise one. There are different combinations for short, middle, and long life; of this, there is no doubt. || 7 || In a combination for short life, death is known to occur within the first trine. Following that in sequence, for a middle-life combination, the end of life occurs in the middle trine. || 8-9 ||

If a long-life combination is obtained, O wise one, the end of life occurs in the ninth trine (the last trine) during its sub-period. || 10 || The sequence of these periods begins from either the Ascendant or the seventh house. This progression should be known from the time of birth, O best of the twice-born. || 11 || Where the Rudra planet does not appear to provide any beneficence, it is because the "life-force" (*Jiva*) has been destroyed; such is the result...

The life of the **native** <term>Jataka: The person whose birth chart is being analyzed</term> is stated according to those years || 87 || 

Having spoken of the departure from life through the refuge of Rudra, O Twice-born, the end of the lifespan occurs during difficult planetary combinations || 88 || Once longevity has been determined through the refuge of Rudra, what special forms does it take? I shall show this to you now || 89 || Specifically in the **Aries Ascendant** <note>original: "Mesha Lagna"; the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note>, at the end of the refuge of Rudra, it may cause diseases such as leprosy rather than the immediate completion of the full lifespan || 90 || 

If the two Rudra planets are situated in the sign of the **Moon**, or if the "life-breath" planet is in the two secondary positions, the end of the lifespan occurs within or at the conclusion of Rudra's refuge || 91 || I shall show you the different categories of lifespan—short, medium, and long—through various planetary combinations, following the wisdom prompted by **Lord Shiva** <note>original: "Shambhu"</note> || 92 || O Brahmin, I have stated the short and other lifespans as they were described to me || 93 || A short life ends at the first "Trident," a middle life at the second, and a long life at the conclusion of the third "Trident." At the end of the Trident, the passing occurs || 94 || 

Now, O son of a Brahmin, I shall explain death during the primary planetary periods <term>Dasha: A time-cycle in Vedic astrology where specific planets rule over certain years of a person's life</term> || 95 || To understand the specific results, scholars identify the **Maheshwara** planet <term>Maheshwara: Literally "Great Lord"; a specific planet used as a final indicator to confirm the timing of death</term>. From that planet, the lifespan is definitively determined || 96 || 

One should consider the lord of the **eighth house** <note>original: "ashtamesha"; the house traditionally associated with death and longevity</note> from the **Indicator** <term>Karaka: A significator planet; in this context, the Atmakaraka or the planet representing the self/soul</term> to be Maheshwara. Or, I shall describe the Maheshwara planet in another way || 97 || If a planet is in its exalted sign within the Indicator chart, that planet is more powerful. The lords of the **twelfth and eighth houses** <note>original: "riphara-randhra-adhipau"</note> between them may also be the Maheshwara planet || 98 || 

In the absence of a planet associated with the Indicator, the Lord of that sign becomes Maheshwara. O Brahmin, if the lords of the 12th and 8th houses are equal in strength || 99 || then both attain the status of Maheshwara, just as there are two Rudra planets. I will speak of another method to decide between them || 100 || If there is a connection with one's own Indicator planet, excluding the shadow planets **Rahu** and **Ketu** and the **Sun**, that planet becomes Maheshwara by alternative, O best of the Twice-born || 1 || A malefic planet in the eighth house from the Indicator becomes Maheshwara. The **Sun**, **Moon**, and **Mercury** <note>original: "chandri"; literally "son of the moon"</note>...

...Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, and the **Darkness** <term>Tamah: Another name for Rahu, the North Node of the Moon, referring to its eclipsing nature</term>. || 2 || In the calculation of **Ketu** <note>original: "Shikhina"</note>, the planet which is sixth from the **Significator planet** <term>Karaka-graha: A planet that represents a specific area of life, here used as a starting point for mathematical calculations</term>—that too is known as **Maheshvara** <term>Maheshvara: Literally "Great Lord" (Shiva); in this context, a planet identified with the power of dissolution and the end of life</term> due to the combination of the nine divisions. || 3 ||

Thus are the Sun's divisions and the practical movement of the zodiac signs. This third planet is the Maheshvara of the Sun and the other planets. || 4 || Or rather, O **best of the Twice-born** <note>original: "dvijottama"; an address to a high-ranking Brahmin scholar</note>, when the lord of the sixth is placed in the house of the Significator, that planet is also undoubtedly known as Maheshvara. || 5 ||

Following the description of the Maheshvara planet, which is paired with the **Brahma** <term>Brahma: In this system, a functional planet designated as the "Creator" who governs the beginning and sustenance of the lifespan</term> planet, I shall now specifically describe the Brahma planet for the purpose of accurate results. || 6 ||

O Brahmin, among the lords of the **sixth, eighth, and twelfth houses** <note>original: "ripu-randhra-vyaya-adhipa"; these houses are traditionally associated with debt, death, and loss</note> relative to either the **Ascendant** <term>Lagna: The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> or the seventh house—whichever of these is strongest and situated in an **odd sign** <note>original: "vishama-sthite"; signs like Aries, Gemini, Leo, etc.</note> starting from Aries— || 7 ||

Whichever sign is stronger between the Ascendant and the seventh house, and is associated with the **rising or back portions of the sign** <note>original: "uchcha-prishttha-bhaga"; a technical division of a sign based on its orientation on the horizon</note>— || 8 ||

The planet endowed with these three qualities is also known as the Brahma planet. O Twice-born, the six signs from the back of the Ascendant, or the **descendant** <note>original: "dyuna"; the seventh house</note> and its subsequent houses— || 9 ||

Or the six signs starting from the back of the seventh house toward the Ascendant—whichever planet is strong and in an odd sign is called the Brahma planet. || 10 ||

If a planet possessing the characteristics of Brahma is strong, or if among the **Nodes** <note>original: "patayo"; the intersection points of the Moon's orbit</note>, or if Saturn, Rahu, or Ketu is the sixth planet— || 11 ||

And in the count from the Sun onwards, if it is the third planet starting from Saturn, or if the lord of the sixth sign is placed in the sixth sign from that position— || 12 ||

That too is undoubtedly known as the Brahma planet, O best of the Twice-born. When many planets seem to qualify as Brahma, which planet should be accepted? || 13 ||

I shall now explain the resolution of this doubt before you. When a combination of two or three planets is identified as Brahma— || 14 ||

One should accept the planet of its own kind that acts as a Significator. The planet with the **highest degrees** <note>original: "adhiko bhaga"; the planet that has traveled furthest through its current zodiac sign</note> is also called the Brahma planet. || 15 ||

In the case of Rahu, due to its non-Brahma nature, if it becomes the authority, one should know it in the **reverse manner** <note>original: "viparitarn"; because the nodes Rahu and Ketu move backwards through the zodiac</note>, taking the one with the lowest degrees. || 16 ||

Thus, for a single **malefic planet** <note>original: "papa"; a naturally difficult planet</note>, the previously mentioned Brahma rule applies from the Significator planet. Or the lord of the **eighth house** <note>original: "randhadhisha"</note> situated in the eighth, according to the principle of the unity of life-force— || 17 ||

There may be two Brahmas with opposite meanings, or many Brahmas. In the case of a difference in general degrees, which one is to be accepted? || 18 ||

If all are equal in degrees, the planet associated with another planet is stronger than one that is alone. By this logic, the strongest one should be known as the Brahma planet...

One should contemplate the planetary periods beginning from the sign occupied by the Brahma planet, O Brahmin, extending until the sign of the Maheshvara planet, to determine the lifespan of the native. || 22 || When the period enters the **trines** <term>Trikona: The 1st, 5th, or 9th positions from a specific sign, considered powerful points of influence</term> of those respective signs, death occurs. O Brahmin, one should consider these periods from the **Movable** <term>Chara: Signs like Aries or Cancer that represent change</term> to the **Fixed** <term>Sthira: Signs like Taurus or Leo that represent stability</term> signs. || 23 ||

Likewise, one should look at the lifespan within the **Great Periods** <term>Mahadasha: Major cycles of planetary influence</term>. The **Vimshottari** <note>The standard 120-year planetary cycle system</note> and other systems should also be applied according to the rules. || 24 || O Brahmin, the sign which is Maheshvara is the one that houses the lord of the eighth house. When the period enters the trines of that sign, death occurs. || 25 ||

In this context, because the instruction mentions "years," the sequence follows the periods of those respective signs. A year is divided into twelve parts, and each part represents an inner sign. || 26 || Each individual one-year sub-period should be known according to the mathematical science. If the value is less than or more than twelve, one should divide the portion by **the Sun** <note>original: "Suryena"; meaning the number 12, as there are 12 solar signs</note>. || 27 || The sub-period thus obtained is known; no increase or decrease occurs. If the years exceed twelve, the sub-period is determined by the difference between the solar signs. || 28 || O Brahmins, if the period is less than twelve years, in whichever sign the period falls within the twelve divisions, it concludes thereafter. || 29 || It is taught that the calculation must be moved according to the sequence of the Great Periods. O best of the twice-born, this is the method for bringing forth the sub-periods of the solar divisions. || 130 <note>This verse is likely number 30; the manuscript contains a numbering error</note> ||

### Now the death of the father and others is explained.

Now I shall speak, O best of the twice-born, regarding the **yoga** <term>Yoga: A specific planetary combination or alignment</term> known as "Departure" <note>original: "Niryanam"; meaning death or the exit from the body</note> for the father and others, as ordained by Shambhu. || 1 || O Brahmin, between the **Ascendant** <term>Lagna: The sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term> and the seventh house, whichever sign is stronger—starting from that sign in the sequence mentioned before... || 2 || ...according to the method of the **Initiator Period** <term>Pravartaka Dasha</term>, within the sub-period of the **Trident of Rudra** <term>Rudrashoola Dasha: A specific calculation system used to predict the timing of death, named after the trident of the destroyer god Shiva</term>, the death of the father will occur without a doubt, O best of the twice-born. || 3 ||

<header>First Part, Chapter 27: On Nirvana <note>original: "Nirvana-adhyayah"; here referring to the "extinguishing" of the life force or death</note></header>

# Now, the Departure of the Mother

If the fourth house <note>The house representing the mother</note> is strong from either the **Ascendant** <term>Lagna: The sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term> or the seventh house, then in the **Shoola Dasha** <term>Shoola Dasha: A predictive cycle used specifically to determine the timing of death; literally "the period of the spear"</term> of that sign, the death of the mother will occur without a doubt. || 4 ||

## Departure of the Brother

If a strong planet aspects the third house from either the Ascendant or the seventh house, the departure of the brother will surely take place during the **Shoola Dasha** of that sign. || 5 ||

## He describes the departure of the sister and the sister's son

If the fifth house is strong from either the Ascendant or the seventh house, then in the **Shoola Dasha** of that sign, the death of the sister and her son occurs. || 6 ||

## Departure of the Elder Brother

O Brahmin, if the eleventh house <note>The house of elder siblings</note> is strong from either the Ascendant or the seventh house, the departure of the elder brother happens during its **Shoola Dasha**. || 7 || O Brahmin, if the ninth house is strong from the Ascendant or the seventh house, [death of the father] occurs; this was told by **Shambhu** <note>original: "Shambhu"; a name for Lord Shiva, the primordial source of astrological knowledge</note> in ancient times, and it happens without hesitation. || 8 ||

O Brahmin, one should contemplate the mother and father from their respective **Significators** <term>Karaka: A planet that acts as a representative for a specific person or area of life</term> as described before. One should determine their lifespan and death by distinguishing between "long life" and other categories. || 9 ||

O Brahmin, between the Sun and Venus, the one who possesses greater strength in the sequence of planets is the **Significator of the Father** <term>Pitri-karaka: The planetary representative of the father</term>. || 10 || Between the Moon and Mars—and similarly between the Sun and Venus—if a planet lacks strength and is aspected by **malefic planets** <note>original: "papa-graha"; planets like Saturn or Mars that generally cause hardship</note>, || 11 || it then represents the father and others in the proper order, O best of Brahmins. If both are equal in strength, then both can be taken as the significators for sons and other relatives. || 12 ||

In this matter, one should consider two types of significators: the **Sentient** and the **Non-sentient** <note>original: "prani-aprani"; literally "with life" and "without life"</note>. I shall now describe the "Sentient" results for the significator of the father and others. || 13 ||

O Brahmin, if the significator of the father is aspected by a **benefic planet** <note>original: "shubha-graha"; planets like Jupiter or Venus that bring harmony</note>, then in the **trine** <term>Trikona: The 1st, 5th, or 9th positions from a starting sign</term> of the sign where the significator of the mother is located, || 14 || the death of the mother or father should be predicted during that period. These are the results of the **Sentient Significator** that I have told you. || 15 || Now, regarding the **Non-sentient Significator**: find the lord of the eighth house endowed with strength. Death occurs when the period reaches the **trines** of the sign occupied by that lord. || 16 ||

O Brahmin <note>original: "dvija"; literally "twice-born," referring to the student or interlocutor</note>, when the **Lord of the Eighth House** <term>Randhresha: The planet ruling the 8th house, which governs longevity and death</term> is endowed with strength, death occurs during its **Shoola Dasha** <term>Shoola Dasha: A predictive cycle used to time death</term>. The same should be predicted for the departure of the father and mother based on the Shoola Dasha of their respective significators. || 17 ||

Or rather, one should predict the results for the "life-giving" planet <note>original: "pranikara"; a planet that sustains the life-force</note> and similarly for other signs. O Brahmin, the results are specifically determined by the lord of that house. If the house involves a "non-life-giving" planet, the result should be declared as such. || 18 ||

One should contemplate all these varieties in the same manner as the **Rudra Shoola** <note>A specific, more intense calculation of the Shoola Dasha associated with the deity Rudra/Shiva</note>. || 19 ||

O Brahmin, if there is a planetary combination for a short life, the calculation of the lifespan should be done accordingly. One should determine the lifespan through the movement of the **Dashas** <term>Dasha: A planetary period or cycle in Vedic astrology</term> as explained previously. || 20 ||

First, a decision must be made regarding the signs and their specific results. For the houses starting from the **Ascendant** <term>Tanu: The 1st house representing the body</term> to the **House of Loss** <term>Vyaya: The 12th house</term>, one should consider what is appropriate for each house. || 21 ||

By relying on the respective significator of each house, one should contemplate the **Arudha** <term>Arudha: The "reflection" or manifested status of a house</term> of the sign. O best of Brahmins, one must consider all factors like the "door" and "exterior" <note>original: "dvara-bahya"; technical terms in Jaimini astrology referring to how a dasha period enters and exits its influence</note> of the signs. || 22 ||

Now, I shall specifically explain the causes for the death of the father. O Brahmin, I am showing these specifics even if some points are repeated. || 23 ||

The **Sun** <note>The Sun is the natural significator of the father</note> should be understood in the context of action. When the Sun is situated in the twelfth house from the Ascendant, or in the sign of **Aries** <note>original: "Mesha"</note> which is the abode of Mercury and the Sun, death may occur during that Dasha. || 24 ||

O best of Brahmins, the death of the father should be spoken of without hesitation during the Dasha of the Ascendant, or Aries, or even **Leo** <note>original: "Simha"</note>. || 25 ||

If malefic planets are in the Ascendant and the Sun is in the sign of Aries, death occurs during the major or sub-period of Aries. || 26 ||

O son of a Brahmin, I shall now explain before you specifically what I have said regarding the death of the parents during one's childhood. || 27 ||

O Brahmin, if the two significators for the parents <note>The Sun for the father and the Moon for the mother</note> are devoid of life-force, are placed in the house of loss (12th), are joined with malefic planets, and are devoid of any connection with benefic planets; || 28 ||

Then the death of the parents occurs in sequence before the age of ten. However, O best of Brahmins, this combination does not apply if the Sun is aspected by benefics. || 29 ||

One should also consider the house of the parents from the **Arudha of the Sun** <note>The Arudha Lagna calculated specifically using the Sun's position to see the father's destiny</note>. In that Dasha, one should speak of the sorrows or joys of the parents. || 30 ||

### Now, he describes the departure of the wife.

When the planet that is the significator of the wife <note>Venus</note> is considered, or the "feminine sign" is analyzed, the death of the wife occurs during the Dasha of their trine signs <note>The 1st, 5th, or 9th signs from that position</note>. || 31 ||

### Now, he describes the departure of others.

Based on the placement of the respective significators, during the Dasha of the trine signs, the death of those relatives, such as the maternal uncles and others [occurs].

## Parashara said:

Now, I shall describe the supreme Royal Combinations <term>Raja Yoga: Planetary alignments indicating power, leadership, and success</term> and others, which result from the different placements of planets and the influence of their aspects upon the zodiac signs. || 1 || If the Lord of the Ninth House <note>original: "Tapas-sthana-adhipo"; the 9th house relates to fortune, piety, and father</note> and the Lord of the Fifth House <note>original: "Mantradhisho"; the 5th house relates to intelligence, children, and counsel</note> are specifically well-placed and mutually aspect each other, the person born will become a ruler. || 2 || Wherever these two are joined together, or if they are in the seventh house from each other <note>original: "sama-saptamau"; a direct opposition where planets face each other</note>, even a child born into a royal lineage will certainly become a king. || 3 || If the Lord of the Fourth House <note>original: "Vahanesha"; lord of vehicles/happiness</note> is in the tenth, and the Lord of the Tenth House <note>original: "Manesha"; lord of honor/profession</note> is in the fourth, and they are aspected by the Lords of the Fifth and Ninth houses, the person becomes a ruler in this world. || 4 || When the Lords of the Fifth, Tenth, Fourth, and the Ascendant are joined with the Lord of the Ninth, the person becomes a king who possesses many elephants <note>A traditional symbol of great wealth and military might</note> and whose brilliance pervades all directions through his own majesty. || 5 || If the Lords of the Fourth and Tenth are joined with the Lord of the Fifth, or joined with the Lord of the Ninth, the person born becomes a ruler. || 6 || If the Lord of the Fifth is joined with the Lord of the Ninth and the Lord of the Ascendant, and they are placed in the Ascendant, the Fourth, or the Tenth house, the person will be anointed as a king or will be favored by royalty. || 7 || If the Ninth house is a sign owned by Jupiter <note>Sagittarius or Pisces</note>, and Venus is placed in her own sign <note>Taurus or Libra</note> joined with the Lord of the Fifth, the person born becomes a ruler. || 8 || The period of two and a half units of time <term>Nadika: a traditional unit of 24 minutes; 2.5 nadikas equals one hour</term> after midnight or after midday is auspicious; one born then becomes a king, a wealthy man, or equal to one. || 9 || If the Moon aspects Venus and Venus aspects the Moon, or if one is in the third house from the other, or if Venus is in the third from the Moon, the person will possess many vehicles and wealth. || 10 ||

A Royal Combination can also involve the loss of fortune, or the acquisition of land and wealth alongside the expenditure of debts. || 13 || Loss of wealth and internal conflict—these are the combinations that have been remembered for all time. || 14 ||

## Now, the four types of planetary relationships are described.

The first is the relationship of position <term>Sthana-sambandha: When two planets exchange signs</term>; the second is the relationship born of mutual aspect <term>Drishti: The "glance" or influence planets cast upon each other</term>. || 15 || The third is a one-sided aspect, and the fourth is when two planets occupy the same sign. These occur when planets are in each other’s signs, in their own signs, or joined together in another sign. Alternatively, they may have a full aspect on each other or be situated in the same divisional chart <note>original: "varga"; a sub-divisional map used to determine planetary strength</note>. || 16 ||

## Next, the obstacles to Royal and Ministerial combinations are described.

In those cases, a yoga <note>planetary combination</note> does not truly manifest if the planet is repeatedly weak. If a planet is joined with or aspected by an enemy planet, or aspected by a malefic <note>original: "pāpa-vīkṣito"; influenced by planets like Mars or Saturn</note>, it does not create the yoga. If the lords of the houses of loss, death, or enemies <note>the 12th, 8th, and 6th houses</note> are involved, or if they are joined with neutral planets, || 17 || even if they are rulers of signs, they will not grant the fruits of the yoga. For Royal and Ministerial combinations, planets in retrograde motion <term>Vakra: The apparent backward motion of a planet, often considered to make it unpredictably strong or destructive</term> act as the destroyers of the result. || 18 ||

## Now, the consideration of auspicious and inauspicious results according to Parijata and other levels of strength.

When the lords of the third, sixth, eleventh, eighth, and twelfth houses are situated in the "Parijata" level of strength <note>original: "pārijāte"; this refers to a planet being in an auspicious sign in two of the divisional charts</note>, their effects must be considered according to the nature of the house they occupy. || 19 || In the second level of strength <note>Uttama</note>, they are considered excellent; in the third level, their results are of a different kind. In the fourth level, they are like kings; in the fifth, they are teachers. || 20 || In the sixth level, they are like earthly gods <note>original: "bhūdevāśca"; often referring to the learned priestly class</note>; in the seventh, they are like divine beings. In the eighth level, they are known to be like beasts that cause pain in this birth. || 21 || When planets are in the "difficult houses" (the 6th, 8th, and 12th), they become obstacles to the individual. Even when placed in the centers or trines <term>Kendra and Kona: The 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th and 1st, 5th, 9th houses, usually the most powerful positions</term>, they can act as obstacles in this birth. || 22 || In odd-numbered signs, the results apply to women, and in even-numbered signs, they are for men. In the sixth house, wealth is stolen; in the eighth house, violence is committed. || 23 || Killing and abduction occur in the twelfth house; in the third house, deceit is practiced. Unfaithfulness is spoken of in the house of bondage, and ingratitude may occur. || 24 ||

If malefic planets <note>original: "papa-yuk"</note> are in the Sixth from the **Significator** in both signs <note>possibly referring to the Rashi and Navamsha charts</note>, and if one is born of a royal lineage, O Sage, a Royal Combination occurs. || 11 ||

If from the Lord of the First or the Lord of the Seventh, a benefic planet is placed in the Twelfth, Fourth, or Fifth, O Sage, one certainly becomes a king. || 12 || If malefic planets are in the Third and Sixth houses, one certainly becomes a king. If there is a mixture of both benefics and malefics in these two yogas, how should the result be determined? || 13 || In such a case, the soul does not become a pauper, but neither is a king born, O Sage. He is a wise person born in a family of equal status, endowed with prestige and honor. || 14 ||

If Venus is in the Fifth from the **Significator**, and is joined or aspected by Venus and the Moon, and if the **Ascendant of the Mounted Sign** <note>original: "tanvarudha-pada," referring to the Arudha Lagna</note> is in the First House, the man belongs to the royal class. || 15 ||

Whether in the **Birth-Body Chart** <note>original: "janmanga"</note>, the **Time-Body Chart** <note>original: "kalanga"</note>, or the **Degree-Body Chart** <note>original: "liptanga"</note>, if ruled by the lords of the planets, the three beginning with the Sun <note>Sun, Moon, Mars</note> provide Royal Combinations. || 16 ||

In the **Birth-Body**, the **Hour-Body** <note>original: "horanga"</note>, or the **Lineage-Body** <note>original: "kulanga"</note>, by any means, if there is even just the aspect <note>visual influence</note> of the Sun and others, he certainly becomes a king. || 17 ||

If the Sun and other planets are in their own signs, their **Ninth-Division** <note>original: "navamsha"</note>, or their **Third-Division** <note>original: "dreshkana"</note>, and they aspect the First and Seventh houses, O Sage, they grant Royal Combinations. || 18 ||

With a full aspect, a full combination is formed; with a half aspect, a half-result is ordained; and with a quarter aspect, a quarter-combination—this is the sequence of the Royal Combination. || 19 ||

O most excellent of the twice-born, if the Sun and other planets look upon the inner six charts <note>original: "shat-kundala-yantare," referring to the Shadvarga or six divisional charts</note>, they grant Royal Combinations without a doubt. || 20 ||

If there is a full aspect on the First House and a slight aspect on the Seventh, a small kingdom is granted; O Sage, one should contemplate this across the six divisional charts. || 21 ||

# First Section: Chapter 21 on Royal Combinations

One should also consider the influence in the **Decanate** <term>Dreshkana; a divisional chart where each zodiac sign is split into three 10-degree sections</term>. A planet situated in the Ascendant <term>Lagna; the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term> or the Seventh House is a giver of Royal Combinations. || 22 || A Royal Combination occurs when an exalted planet is present, or if there are two Ascendants <note>This likely refers to the strength of both the birth Lagna and the Navamsha or Dreshkana Lagna</note>—whether from the Sign, the Decanate, or the Division; or from the Sign and the Division. || 23 || Or, if the Ascendant is aspected <note>original: "drishte"; a planetary gaze or influence</note> by the Sign and the Decanate through a combination, this birth chart is generally seen only for lords and rulers. || 24 || 

If the Ascendant at the time of birth is aspected by even one planet, and particularly if the Moon has reached an exalted state, || 25 || or if it is occupied by Jupiter and Venus, or by any exalted planet—provided there is an absence of **malefic obstructions** <term>argala; a planetary intervention that can "bolt" or "unbolt" the fruits of a house</term>—it is undoubtedly a Royal Combination. || 26 || 

When the Moon is in a beneficial position, and the **Teacher of the Gods** <note>original: "Devaguru," referring to Jupiter</note> is in the house of wealth <note>the Second House</note>, or if a planet is aspected by an exalted one, or is itself an exalted planet, || 27 || it becomes a giver of Royal Combinations; of this there is no doubt, O most excellent of the twice-born! <note>original: "dvijottama"</note>. Wherever the Moon is in a beneficial position, the result is the same. || 28 || 

An exalted planet grants a Royal Combination, as do the two Ascendants. The Arudha <term>the manifest or reflected position of a house</term> and its supports are remembered as combinations that grant vehicles and chariots. || 29 || 

With Venus and the Moon, if Venus is in the third house from them, the person will possess wealth and vehicles. O Sage <note>original: "vipra"</note>, if the **Teacher of the Demons** <note>original: "daityacarya"; Venus</note> and the **Lord of the Night** <note>original: "nishadhipau"; the Moon</note> aspect each other, || 30 || or if there is a similar relationship in the third from the Arudha, or if they are conjoined in the birth Ascendant, one possesses wealth and vehicles. || 31 || 

If the Ascendant is auspicious, the house of wealth is auspicious, and the third house is occupied by malefic planets, while the fourth house is auspicious, the person becomes a King or someone equal to a King. || 32 || If even a single strong planet—whether it be the **Deer-Marked One** <note>original: "harinanka"; the Moon</note>, **The Living One** <note>original: "jiva"; Jupiter</note>, or Venus—is placed in the house of wealth, it bestows prosperity upon the person. || 33 || 

All planets that aspect the Ascendant are givers of good fortune. Even if a **debilitated planet** <term>neecha-kheta; a planet in its weakest sign</term> is in the Ascendant, if it aspects [the lord/Ascendant], he is proclaimed a King. || 34 || A debilitated planet related to the sixth, eighth, third, or eleventh houses that aspects the Ascendant is a giver of Royal Combinations. || 35 || 

It is a Royal Combination if an exalted planet aspects the birth Ascendant. If a planet in the sixth or eighth house is debilitated but aspects the Ascendant, it creates this combination. || 36 || Or if the lord of the sixth or eighth house is debilitated and aspects the Ascendant, or if a debilitated planet in the third or eleventh house aspects the Ascendant, it grants a kingdom. || 37 || 

If the two planets that rule the sixth and eighth houses are benefics, are not associated with any others, and aspect the birth Ascendant, this is declared a Royal Combination. || 38 ||

Even in the absence of a full Royal Combination, this placement determines one's wealth and grain. || 43 ||

The periods <term>dashas</term> of benefic and malefic planets should be judged from the Ascendant and the central houses <term>kendras; the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</term>. For whomever the **benefic divisions** <term>saumya-amshaka</term> of the Ascendant are strong, their success is certain. || 44 ||

The specific portions of the signs are named: **Kubera** <note>the Lord of Wealth</note>, **Patanga** <note>the Sun or Bird</note>, **Hala** <note>the Plow</note>, **Kirita** <note>the Crown</note>, **Vihvala** <note>the Agitated</note>, **Samaya** <note>the Conventional</note>, **Mohana** <note>the Enchanter</note>, **Kinnara** <note>the Celestial Musician</note>, || 45 || **Bhujangendra** <note>the King of Serpents</note>, and **Lila-Kokila** <note>the Playful Cuckoo</note> is considered the best. One should predict the results based on the placement of planets within these **twelve-fold divisions** of the signs <term>Dvadashamsha; a divisional chart where each zodiac sign is divided into twelve segments of 2.5 degrees each</term>. || 46 ||

Those portions falling in the central houses are auspicious and grant the fruits of a Royal Combination. The portions in the second, sixth, and eleventh houses are described as medium. || 47 || Other portions are known as inferior; thus is the determination of the divisions. One should declare the results based on the movement of the planets and the Ascendant through these divisions. || 48 || If a human is born when the Ascendant or the planets are in these divisions, or if at birth the Moon is joined with or situated in its own division, || 49 || then these combinations are said to be fruitful and fulfilled. O Brahmin, the results may be full or diminished according to the specific planets involved. || 50 ||

# Now, the Combinations for Royal Emblems

O best of the twice-born <note>original: "dvija-sattama"; a respectful address to a Brahmin</note>, if Venus and the Moon <note>original: "sitendu"</note> are placed in the fourth house from the Significator <term>Karaka; the planet representing the soul or the self</term>, the individual is endowed with **Royal Emblems** throughout their life. || 51 || Royal flags <term>dhvaja</term> or the sounds of kettle-drums <term>dundubhi</term> will be present day and night <note>this symbolizes high status, fame, and a grand entourage</note>. One should consider these without contradicting the other general combinations in the chart. || 52 ||

# Now, the Combinations for Wisdom

If planets are placed in the third or sixth houses from the Significator or from the **Manifested Ascendant** <term>Arudha Lagna; a calculated point representing one's status and how the world perceives them</term>, or if the Ascendant is aspected by the Significator and joined with the aspect of the Lord of the Mother <note>the 4th house lord, representing education and foundational knowledge</note>, || 53 || then that child is born wise, with a sharp and discerning intellect...

## Now, on the Combination for Happiness (Sukha Yoga).

O Brahmin, if there are planets in the fourth house <note>the house of comfort and home</note> from either the Ascendant or the significator, and they are aspected by the Ascendant and the significator, those people become happy. || 56 ||

## Now, on the Combination for a Military Commander (Senadhisha Yoga).

O Brahmin, if malefic planets <note>natural "cruel" planets like Mars or Saturn</note> are situated in the third or sixth houses <note>original: "tritiye shashtabhe"; houses associated with struggle and enemies</note> from the significator, the Arudha <term>Arudha Lagna; the 'reflection' of the ascendant</term>, the Ascendant, or the seventh house, the person becomes a military commander. || 57 ||

## Now, on the Combinations for a Prime Minister (Pradhana Yoga).

If the lord of the house of kingdom <note>the 10th house of career and status</note> is joined with or aspected by the lord of the ministerial house <note>the 5th house of counsel</note> from the birth Ascendant, or is associated with the planet signifying the minister <term>Amatyakaraka</term>, one attains a prime-ministership in the king's palace. || 58 ||

If the house of gains <note>the 11th house</note> is aspected by its own lord and is free from the gaze of malefic planets, O Brahmin, one attains prominence in the king's palace and also within one's own family. || 59 ||

If the planet signifying the minister <term>Amatyakaraka</term> is joined with the lord of a center <term>Kendra; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</term> from the significator, the child will possess a sharp intellect and also become a military commander. || 60 ||

...in one’s own region, or in the middle years, or in old age, O best of Brahmins, || 61 || there will be a gradual increase in fortune, or one may take on the status and attire of a king. || 62 ||

If planets are placed in the fifth, seventh, or ninth houses from the significator or the Ascendant, it is proclaimed as a **Royal Combination** <term>Raja Yoga</term>; such a person becomes famous and victorious. || 63 ||

If planets are placed in the centers <term>Kendras</term> or trines <term>Konas</term> from the significator, or are in their signs of exaltation, and are joined with or aspected by the lord of fortune <note>the ruler of the 9th house</note>, the person becomes a royal minister. || 64 ||

If the ruler of the sign occupied by the significator is placed in the Ascendant, or is joined with or aspected by it, this is a major combination for a ministerial position in old age; of this, there is no doubt. || 65 ||

If the significator is joined with benefic planets in the fifth or seventh houses, then during the period <term>dasha</term> of that significator, one obtains the wealth associated with that planet. || 66 ||

Even if planets are weak or debilitated <note>at their lowest point of strength</note>, O Brahmin, if they are placed in the aforementioned positions and are aspected by the lord of the significator, one should still predict auspicious results. || 67 ||

# Now Begins the Chapter on the Description of Previous Births

Now I shall specifically describe the determination of sins from a previous life. One should speak of them in order, beginning with Aries, based on the sub-divisions <term>Navamshas</term> <note>a 3°20' division of a sign, used in Vedic astrology to see the "inner life" or hidden potential of a planet</note>. || 1 || After fully determining the maleficence of the lord of the Moon’s sub-division: || 2 ||

In the Aries sign and its sub-divisions, in order: In Aries, there was likely the killing of a sheep or ram. In the sign known as the Cow <note>Taurus</note>, the wise should determine the offense accordingly. In the sub-division of the Twins <note>Gemini</note>, one should certainly speak of a killing involving a fetus or embryo. In Cancer, it was the killing of a snake, and in Leo, it was certainly the killing of a four-legged animal. || 3 ||

The wise person should determine that in Leo, the killing of wild deer-like species occurred via a forest fire, O Brahmin, based on the specific sub-division. || 4 ||

In Virgo, O Sage, the learned should speak of the sin arising from the abandonment of a woman. In Libra, the wise should speak of the theft of wealth through deceptive means. || 5 ||

In Scorpio, the killing of a village sparrow or an egg-born creature <note>original: "andaja," referring to birds or reptiles</note> occurred. In Sagittarius, one should speak without hesitation of the betrayal of a friend. || 6 ||

In Capricorn, the theft or destruction of various species of trees and fruits occurred. In Aquarius, O Brahmin, the learned should speak of a death followed by another <note>original: "anumrityatam," likely referring to the sin of someone dying in consequence of the subject's actions, or following a master into death</note>. || 7 ||

In the first half of Pisces, the learned should speak of the theft of a Brahmin’s wealth. In the second half, the taking of wealth and a planned killing are to be understood. || 8 ||

One sub-division indicates one past life; two sub-divisions indicate two lives; three sub-divisions indicate three lives; and the remainder indicates four births. || 9 ||

Having determined this in all cases regarding the Ascendant in this current birth, one should certainly state the details from Cancer onwards, beginning with a Brahmin birth. || 10 ||

Otherwise, if Jupiter does not aspect the Ascendant or the Moon, the person may be born of an illicit union <note>original: "jarajo," meaning born of a paramour</note>. Thus, the 108 sub-divisions <term>Navamshas</term> <note>12 signs multiplied by 9 divisions each</note> are proclaimed. || 11 ||

In the Warrior caste <term>Kshatriya</term>, speak of warriors; in the Merchant caste <term>Vaishya</term>, speak of merchants; in the Laborer caste <term>Shudra</term>, speak of laborers; and among Brahmins, speak of the priestly class. || 12 || In the next birth...

# First Section: Chapter 33 on the Description of Happiness and Sorrow for Living Beings

...happiness. || 22 ||

Where the Moon is situated, a marriage should be envisioned there. A combination for brothers occurs where Mars <note>original: "Angaraka"</note> is situated. || 23 ||

A combination for sisters occurs where Mercury <note>original: "Jna"</note> is, and where Jupiter <note>original: "Vachaspati"</note> is situated, there a son is indicated. Where Venus <note>original: "Shukra"</note> is, there a daughter is proclaimed. || 24 ||

Where Saturn <note>original: "Manda"</note> is situated, one should predict happiness derived from the mother. In this way, one should contemplate happiness and other life outcomes according to the positions of the planets. || 25 ||

Take the lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagnadhisha</term> and the lord of the 7th house <term>Madadhisha</term> and multiply them by their portions and four <note>original: "veda," a numerical code for 4</note>. Having calculated the difference between these two results, marriage is to be predicted in the year corresponding to that number. || 26 ||

Where those two lords are situated in the combination of houses, or in their difference, or when the sign is doubled—in that year, marriage occurs. || 27 ||

One should calculate the difference between those two lords, taking the signs, degrees, and other measurements. In the year equal to the obtained number, or in a similar numerical portion, one should point out the time of marriage. || 28 ||

Similarly, from the house of children <note>the 5th house</note> and the house of gains <note>the 11th house</note>, one should contemplate the birth of sons and daughters. Likewise, from the sibling portions, one should contemplate the timing for brothers and sisters. || 29 ||

One should calculate the difference between the house of loss <note>the 12th house</note> and the house of gain <note>the 11th house</note>, and also the difference between their respective lords. The difference in houses indicates expenditure, and gain is known through the sequence of the difference between the lords. || 30 ||

For the Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn—starting from Venus—the sum of the signs and degrees of the houses they occupy should be calculated. || 31 ||

If that sum is divided by twelve <term>Tashte</term> <note>a mathematical reduction technique</note>, one should predict death in that birth month. Multiply by thirty to find the day, and similarly calculate the smaller units of time like minutes and seconds <term>Nadi-paladikam</term>. || 32 ||

The difference between the Ascendant <term>Lagna</term> and the Moon should be calculated, including the minutes and seconds. If this is less than the time of birth, a birth in water <term>Jala-prasava</term> <note>often interpreted historically as a birth in a bathroom or near a water source</note> is said to occur. || 33 ||

The difference between the Sun and the Moon should be calculated and added to the Ascendant. In the year corresponding to that measurement, one should predict abundant gain. || 34 ||

In the combination of the sign-lord and the Ascendant-lord, if they are joined with death-indicators, predict accordingly. Debt or freedom from debt occurs when there is a combination with the Moon. || 35 ||

In the combination of the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant, joined with the precise position of the sign-lord: in that year there is great suffering; if the resulting number is less, there is happiness, without a doubt. || 36 ||

The difference between the house of children and the house of fortune <note>the 9th house</note> should be calculated; in that year, smallpox <note>original: "Shitaladikam," referring to cooling-illnesses or pustules</note> or similar ailments occur. In the combination of the difference between the Ascendant and its own lord, the father's death occurs, without a doubt. || 37 ||

In the combination of the sign-lord and the house of action <note>the 10th house</note>, then one should predict the rise of one's career <term>Karmodaya</term>. In the combination of the house of piety <note>the 9th house</note> and the house of expenditure <note>the 12th house</note>, in that year, expenditure is certain. || 38 ||

In this manner, one should observe all matters regarding the 7th house and other houses. Fortune etc. <note>catchword for the next page</note>

### Maitreya said:

"O Ocean of Mercy! Please tell me, how many distinct types of states <term>avasthas</term> <note>These are specific conditions or 'moods' of a planet based on its position, which affect its power to do good or or harm.</note> are there for the Sun and the other planets?" || 1 ||

### Parashara said:

"There are many different states for the Sun and the other planets. Although there are ninety-six such states in total, I shall tell you the very essence of them. || 2 ||

### Now, the States of Awakening and Others are described:

Divide the thirty degrees of a zodiac sign into three equal parts <note>Each part consists of 10 degrees.</note>. In odd-numbered signs <note>Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, and Aquarius.</note>, the order is as follows; in even-numbered signs, the order is reversed. || 3 || One must first understand these three states for a person: Awakening, Dreaming, and Sleeping. Specifically, the 'Awakening' state is the one that achieves the desired goals. || 4 || The 'Dreaming' state yields middling or mixed results—unless a Guru <note>spiritual teacher or heavy planet like Jupiter</note> is the advisor. O best of sages, the final state, 'Sleeping,' should be known as bearing no fruit at all. || 5 ||

### Now, the Nine States beginning with 'Bright' are described:

A planet can be in one of nine states: Bright, Healthy, Joyful, Peaceful, Miserable, Extremely Grieved, Impaired, Wicked, or Angry. || 6 || A planet in its sign of exaltation is 'Bright' <term>Deepta</term>. In its own sign or a 'great friend's' sign, it is 'Healthy' <term>Svastha</term>. In a friend's sign, it is 'Joyful' <term>Mudita</term>. In a neutral sign, it is 'Peaceful' <term>Shanta</term>. In an enemy's sign, it is called 'Miserable' <term>Deena</term>. || 7 || If it is in a particularly hostile sign, it is 'Extremely Grieved' <term>Ati-dukhita</term>. If joined with a malefic <note>a naturally 'harmful' planet like Mars or Saturn</note>, it is 'Impaired' <term>Vikala</term>. If associated with a cruel planet, it is 'Wicked' <term>Khala</term>. If it is joined with the Sun <note>this usually refers to 'combustion,' where a planet is too close to the Sun's heat</note>, it is 'Angry' <term>Kopi</term>. || 8 || During the planetary period <term>paka</term> <note>also known as a Dasha, or a time-block ruled by that planet</note> of a 'Bright' planet, one gains lordship over land, enthusiasm, bravery, wealth, and vehicles. One also gains a wife, children, the favor of good relatives, and honors from kings...

...one attains knowledge. || 9 || During the planetary period <term>dasha</term> <note>A specific period of time in a person's life ruled by a particular planet.</note> of a planet in the **Healthy** <term>svastha</term> state, the person remains healthy and obtains wealth and happiness from the authorities <note>original: "king"</note>. One attains knowledge, fame, affection, and greatness, and fulfills the duties <term>dharma</term> related to land, wealth, and family. || 10 ||

During the planetary period of a **Joyful** <term>mudānvita</term> planet, one acquires fine clothing, perfumes, and the courage to visit holy places. One gains from listening to sacred legends <term>Purana</term> and moral teachings, and obtains vehicles, ornaments, and fine attire. || 11 ||

During the planetary period of a **Peaceful** <term>shānta</term> planet, one moves toward happiness and righteousness. One gains sons, a wife, and vehicles. One occupies oneself with knowledge, cultural pursuits, and the study of moral laws <term>dharmashastra</term>, attaining great wealth and the respect of national leaders. || 12 ||

Loss of position and conflict with relatives occur during the period of a **Wretched** <term>deena</term> planet. The person lives in a miserable or lowly manner, is abandoned by others, and is tormented by diseases. || 13 ||

During the period of an **Afflicted** <term>duhkhārdita</term> planet, one constantly encounters various types of grief. One travels abroad, is separated from family, and lives in fear of thieves, fire, and the government. || 14 ||

During the period of a **Deformed** <term>vaikalya</term> planet, one experiences mental disturbances and agitation. There is the death of friends, and specifically trouble regarding one's wife, children, vehicles, and clothing, along with harassment from thieves. || 15 ||

During the period of a **Wicked** <term>khala</term> planet, one faces constant conflict and separation—specifically separation from the father. One experiences the loss of wealth and land due to enemies and faces criticism from one's own kin. || 16 ||

During the period of an **Angry** <term>kopānvita</term> planet, sins and misfortunes arrive in many forms. There is the destruction of knowledge, wealth, wife, sons, and relatives, as well as hardships for children and eye diseases. || 17 ||

## Now, the results of the states of Infancy and others are described.

In odd-numbered signs <note>Aries, Gemini, Leo, etc.</note>, the states are divided into six-degree increments: **Infant** <term>bāla</term>, **Adolescent** <term>kumāra</term>, **Youth** <term>yuvan</term>, **Elderly** <term>vriddha</term>, and **Dead** <term>mrita</term>. In even-numbered signs, these states are calculated in reverse order <note>Meaning 0–6 degrees in an even sign is 'Dead,' while 24–30 degrees is 'Infant.'</note>. || 18 ||

The **Infant** state provides only a small amount of its potential results; the **Adolescent** provides half; the **Youth** provides the full result. The **Elderly** state provides poor or weak results, and the state known as **Dead** provides no results at all <note>Literally "death-like results," implying the planet is too weak to act.</note>. || 19 ||

## Now, the results of the states of Travel and others are described.

The twelve states are: **Travel** <term>pravāsa</term>, **Ruined** <term>naṣṭa</term>, **Dead** <term>mṛta</term>, **Victorious** <term>jaya</term>, **Humorous** <term>hāsya</term>, **Amorous** <term>rati</term>, **Joyful** <term>mudā</term>, **Sleeping** <term>suptā</term>, **Eating** <term>bhuktā</term>, **Feverish** <term>jvarā</term>, **Trembling** <term>kampā</term>, and **Well-situated** <term>susthiti</term>. Their effects correspond to their names. || 20 ||

O best of the twice-born! <note>An honorific for a Brahmin or a learned student.</note> To calculate these, multiply the number of signs the planet has passed by 60, add the elapsed minutes of the current position, and multiply by 4. Divide the result by 45. The remainder indicates the specific state, starting from the Sun. || 21 ||

<header>The Essence of the Great Parāśara’s Horoscopy</header>

### The Meaning of This

Regarding the phrase "multiply by sixty": In this calculation, one should take the number of elapsed constellations <term>nakshatras</term> <note>The 27 divisions of the sky along the moon's path.</note> starting from the first constellation, Ashwini. Multiply this number by sixty. To this total, add the number of elapsed <term>ghatis</term> <note>A traditional unit of time equal to 24 minutes.</note> of the current constellation. Multiply that sum by four (representing the four ages or <term>yugas</term>). Divide the resulting number by forty-five <note>original: "shara-abdhi", where 'shara' (arrows) represents 5 and 'abdhi' (oceans) represents 4, traditionally read from right to left as 45.</note>. The quotient obtained indicates the state that has passed, while the remainder indicates the current state. If the quotient exceeds twelve, divide it by twelve; the resulting number determines the specific state, such as **Exile** <term>pravāsa</term>.

**Exile** (Pravasa): If this state occurs at the time of birth, it leads to the loss of wealth. In the **Lost** (Nashta) state, there is a fear of death. In the **Dead** (Mrita) state, there is victory. **Victory** (Jaya) leads to triumph. **Delight** (Vilasa) involves laughter and pleasure with women. || 22 || In the state of **Passion** (Rati), there is playfulness that grants happiness. The **Asleep** (Prasupta) state brings sleep, discord, and physical pain. The states of **Fear**, **Loss of Heat** (Affliction), and **Happiness** occur after **Eating** (Bhuktva). One experiences fever in the **Trembling** (Kampita) state and is well-situated in the **Steady** (Susthita) state, respectively. || 23 ||

### Now, the Shamed and Other States are Described

**Shamed** (Lajjita), **Proud** (Garvita), **Hungry** (Kshudhita), **Thirsty** (Trishita), **Delighted** (Mudita), and **Agitated** (Kshobhita) are declared to be the psychological states of the planets. || 24 || A planet is in the **Shamed** state if it is placed in the fifth house <note>The house associated with children and intelligence.</note> and is joined with the shadow planets Rahu or Ketu, or if it is joined with the Sun, Saturn, or Mars. || 25 ||

O best of the twice-born! If a planet is in its sign of exaltation <note>The sign where a planet's influence is strongest.</note> or is placed in a trine <term>trikona</term> <note>Specifically the 1st, 5th, or 9th houses, considered very auspicious.</note>, it is undoubtedly called **Proud**. || 26 || If a planet is in an enemy's house, is joined with an enemy planet, or is aspected <note>A "look" or influence cast from one planet to another based on their positions.</note> by a foe, it should be known as **Hungry**. The same applies if it is joined with Saturn. || 27 ||

A planet placed in a water-sign <note>Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces.</note>, aspected by an enemy, and not seen by any beneficial planets, is called <term>Trishita</term> (**Thirsty**). || 28 || A planet in a friend's house, joined with a friend, aspected by a friend, or joined with Jupiter, is declared to be <term>Mudita</term> (**Delighted**). || 29 ||

If a planet is joined with the Sun and is aspected by malefics <note>Planets with a naturally harsh influence, like Mars or Saturn.</note> or an enemy, one should know it to be <term>Kshobhita</term> (**Agitated**). || 30 || In whatever houses these planets reside, if they are in the **Hungry** or **Agitated** states, the person will become a vessel of sorrow. || 31 || In this manner, the wise should analyze all the houses in sequence. The final judgment of life's results should be spoken only after considering these various strengths and weaknesses. || 32 || And with mutual joy...

...one should declare mixed results. If the planet is weak, there is loss; if it is strong, there is a great result. || 33 ||
If a planet is in the **Tenth House** <term>Karmasthana</term> <note>The house governing career, status, and actions.</note> and is in a **Shamed**, **Thirsty**, **Hungry**, or **Agitated** state, that person will become a vessel of sorrow. || 34 ||
If a **Shamed** planet is in the **Fifth House** <term>Sutasthana</term> <note>The house of children, creativity, and intellect.</note>, there will be the loss of children, or perhaps only one child will remain. || 35 ||
If a planet is **Agitated** or **Thirsty** in the **Seventh House** <note>The house of marriage and partnerships.</note>, the man's wife will surely die; O best of the twice-born, this is the truth. || 36 ||
The **Proud** state <term>Garvita</term> <note>original: "Garvita", a state occurring when a planet is in its sign of exaltation or its own sign.</note> bestows upon men the happiness of new houses and gardens, royalty, and skill in the arts. It specifically brings the gain of wealth and growth in business. || 37 ||
In the **Delighted** state <term>Mudita</term> <note>original: "Mudita", occurring when a planet is in a friend's sign.</note>, one gains a spacious residence, clean clothing, jewelry, and happiness from land. There is playfulness with kin, residence in a palace, the destruction of enemies, and the flourishing of intellect and knowledge. || 38 ||
The **Shamed** state <term>Lajjita</term> <note>original: "Lajjita", occurring when a planet is in the 5th house with Rahu or Ketu, or with the Sun, Saturn, or Mars.</note> causes a lack of interest in pleasure, a mind distracted from devotion, and the defeat of one's position. It brings childhood diseases, aimless wandering, an interest in quarrels, and no desire for auspicious deeds. || 39 ||
The results of the **Agitated** state <term>Kshobhita</term> <note>original: "Kshobhita", occurring when a planet is with the Sun and aspected by a cruel/malefic planet.</note> are specifically poverty, a wicked intellect, and great hardship. It causes the depletion of wealth, trouble from fire, and obstacles in gaining money due to the anger of the king. || 40 ||
Under the influence of a **Hungry** planet <term>Kshudhita</term> <note>original: "Kshudhita", when a planet is in an enemy's sign or aspected by an enemy.</note>, one falls into grief and delusion. There is physical wasting due to fear and the suffering of family members. Men face quarrels with enemies, financial obstacles, and the total blockage of their strength and intellect due to despair. || 41 ||
When a planet is in the **Thirsty** state <term>Trishita</term> <note>original: "Trishita", when a planet is in a watery sign aspected by a malefic.</note>, there is physical illness during sexual encounters and a tendency toward wicked deeds. There is a loss of wealth due to the gossip of one's own people, physical weakness, suffering caused by villains, and a constant loss of honor. || 42 ||

### Now, the States of Sleeping and Others

I shall now describe before you the twelve states of the planets: **Sleeping**, **Sitting**, **Seeing**, **Touching**, **Going**, **Coming**, **Residing in an Assembly**, **Arrival**, **Eating**, **Dancing**, **Desire**, and **Eagerness**, as well as **Sleep**. || 43–44 ||
<note>These twelve "Shayanadi" states are more complex than the previous six and are calculated using the planet's position, the birth star, and the time of day.</note>
Take the number of the constellation <term>nakshatra</term> in which the planet is placed. Multiply that by the number of the planet <note>Sun=1, Moon=2, etc.</note>. Again, multiply the result by the number of the sub-division <term>ansha</term> and add the number of one’s own birth constellation. || 45 ||
The wise man should then add the number of elapsed <term>ghatis</term> <note>Traditional units of 24 minutes.</note> and the number of the Ascendant <term>lagna</term>...

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions for calculating planetary states (Avasthas). <page-num>204</page-num>
<header>The Essence of the Great Compendium of Parashara's Horoscopy</header>

Divide by twelve <note>original: "Ravi," the Sun, symbolizing the 12 signs or months</note>, take the remainder, and apply it to the calculation. || 46 || One should then perform a completion according to the order of the **Lunar Mansions** <term>Nakshatra</term>. Then, adding the numerical value of the letters of the person's name, it should again be divided by twelve. || 47 ||

For the **Sun** <term>Surya</term>, one should add five; for the **Moon** <term>Chandra</term>, add two. For **Mars** <term>Kuja</term>, add two, and for **Mercury** <term>Budha</term>, three should be applied. || 48 || For **Jupiter** <term>Guru</term>, five <note>original: "bana," meaning arrows, of which the god of love has five</note> should be given; for **Venus** <term>Bhargava</term>, add three. For **Saturn** <term>Shani</term>, add three, and for **Rahu** <note>The North Node of the Moon</note>, add four. || 49 || Take the remainder after dividing by three <note>original: "Rama," referring to the three historical Ramas</note>; the planets will then be in one of three conditions. I shall now describe to you their **Gaze** <term>Drishti</term>, **Effort** <term>Cheshta</term>, and **Lack of Effort** <term>Vicheshta</term>. || 50 ||

### The Meaning of This

This means: for whichever constellation a planet is placed in at birth, multiply that constellation's sequence number by the planet's own number. Then, multiply that by the number of degrees the planet has traveled within its current zodiac sign. To this, add the number of the native’s **Birth Constellation** <term>Janmabha</term> and the number of their **Birth Ascendant** <term>Janmalagna</term>. From the remainder left after dividing by twelve, the planet's specific activity <note>Referring to the 12 Shayanadi Avasthas, such as "Sleeping" or "Sitting"</note> is to be known. 

Furthermore, multiply the resulting number by itself. In the process of completing the calculation based on the **Lunar Mansion** <term>Nakshatra</term>, take the first letter and vowel of the name by which the person is known. Add the numerical value associated with that letter, divide by twelve, and the result indicates the previously mentioned state. In this process, the specific "additive" <term>Kshepaka</term> <note>A constant value added to a formula</note> belonging to whichever planet is being calculated must be added. Divide the total by three, and the remainder reveals the state of the planet's gaze or "aspect."

### An Example

Here, the Sun is in the constellation **Mṛgaśīrṣa** <note>The 5th Nakshatra</note>, so its number is 5. This is multiplied by the Sun's own number (1), which equals 5. The Sun is in the second degree-segment of Gemini, so 5 is multiplied by 2, becoming 10. The "desired" number is 6; the birth constellation is **Kṛttikā** (3); the ascendant is **Cancer** (4). Adding these together <note>10 + 6 + 3 + 4</note> equals 23. Dividing 23 by 12 leaves a remainder of 11. 

By the calculation of the "Sleeping and other states," the Sun is known to be in the **Playful State** <term>Kautuka</term> <note>The 11th state in the Shayanadi system</note>. Here, the remainder is 11. Regarding the numerical position of the vowel: as is well known here, the first letter of the name "Sha" (श) falls in the row under the vowel "i." Its vowel number is 2. The remainder 11 is multiplied by 11...

# Concerning the Differences in Sight.

> Know that in the state of **Sight** <term>Drishti</term>, there is little fruit; in the state of **Effort** <term>Cheshta</term>, the fruit is plentiful.
> In the state of **Lack of Effort** <term>Vicheshta</term>, there is no fruit; thus the wise understand the results of these states. || 51 ||
> Having examined the auspicious and inauspicious nature of the planets and their relative strength and weakness,
> the wise should specifically determine their strength based on their **exaltation** <term>tungasthana</term>. || 52 ||

# Now, the results of the twelve individual states are described.

When the **Sun** <term>Aushnabhanu</term> enters the state of **Lying Down** <term>Shayana</term>, the person suffers from various digestive ailments, obesity, diseases of the feet, and aggravation of the bile. They may suffer from ulcers in the rectum and pain in the chest. || 53 ||

If the Sun is in the state of **Sitting** <term>Upaveshana</term>, the man will experience poverty and carry heavy burdens. He will be fond of debates and learning, but will be hard-hearted and suffer the loss of his wealth. || 54 ||

If the **Lord of the Day** <term>Divadhinatha</term> is in the state of **Hand to Eye** <term>Netrapani</term> <note>This state suggests looking or gazing</note>, the person is always filled with joy, wise, philanthropic, and endowed with strength and wealth. He will be very happy and proud of the favor shown to him by the king. || 55 ||

When the **Lord of the Lotus** <term>Padminisha</term> <note>A poetic name for the Sun</note> is in the state of **Shining** <term>Prakashana</term> at birth, the person is generous, possesses complete wealth, is an orator in assemblies, and a performer of many meritorious deeds. He is very strong and handsome. || 56 ||

When the **Lord of the Day** is in the state of **Traveling** <term>Gamana</term>, the man will be fond of living abroad, burdened by a necklace of sorrows, always lazy, and devoid of wisdom and wealth. He is especially prone to fear and anger. || 57 ||

When the **Lord of the Day** is in the state of **Arriving** <term>Agamana</term>, the man is devoted to others' wives, friendless, fond of frequent travel, stingy, skilled in wickedness, dirty, and of poor intellect. || 58 ||

When in the state of **Present in Assembly** <term>Sabhagata</term>, the man is intent on helping others and possesses a collection of wealth and jewels...
