When Mercury is in the state of **Eagerness** <term>Kautuka</term> at the time of birth: if it is in the first house <note>original: "angabhe," literally the "body-sign" or Ascendant</note>, the person’s knowledge of the art of music will be flawless. If it is in the seventh or eighth house, he finds pleasure with courtesans. If it is in the house of merit <note>original: "punyabhe," the 9th house</note>, his mind is joined with righteous deeds and he attains a good state of being. 
**|| 98 ||**

When the "Son of the Moon" <note>original: "Chandrasuta"</note> has taken recourse in the state of **Sleep** <term>Nidra</term>, the person never enjoys the happiness of sleep; he is constantly joined with the "meditation of disease" <note>This suggests a constant preoccupation or affliction with illness</note>. He suffers from a deficiency of brothers, great inner distress, arguments with his own kin, and the destruction of wealth and honor. 
**|| 99 ||**

### Now, the Results of Jupiter are stated:

When the "Lord of Speech" <note>original: "Vachasam-adhipa," a title for Jupiter/Brihaspati</note> is in the state of **Resting** <term>Shayana</term> at the time of birth, the person—even if naturally strong—will have a weak or feeble voice. His body is very fair, he has a long chin, and the man is significantly filled with fear of his enemies. 
**|| 100 ||**

If "Life" <note>original: "Jiva," a common name for Jupiter as the life-force</note> has gone into the state of **Sitting** <term>Upavesha</term>, the person is talkative and filled with great pride. He is distressed by the enemies of the king and is afflicted with sores or wounds on his feet, thighs, mouth, and hands. 
**|| 101 ||**

When the "One Worshipped by the King of Gods" <note>original: "Devarajarchita," referring to Jupiter as the preceptor of Indra</note> has gone into the state of **Gazing** <term>Netrapani</term> <note>literally "Hand-on-eye," signifying a state of watchful observation</note>, the person is afflicted by disease and devoid of the beauty of excellent wealth. He is a lover of music and dance, lustful, and though fair-complexioned, he is born of a pale family and is full of affection. 
**|| 102 ||**

He bestows a multitude of virtues and the root of pure happiness; he is always a mass of brilliance, like one who visits the bower of the Lord of Vraja <note>original: "Vrajapati-nikunja," a poetic reference to the sacred groves of Krishna, implying a state of divine bliss</note>. If the "Teacher of Indra" <note>original: "Vasava-guru"</note> is exalted and has reached the state of **Radiance** <term>Prakasha</term>, he brings greatness among people and a status equal to the Lord of Wealth <note>original: "Dhanapati," or Kubera</note> for the living being. 
**|| 103 ||**

The man is always courageous and joyfully filled with the happiness of his circle of friends. He is a scholar adorned with various types of wealth and knowledge of the Vedas when Jupiter has gone into the state of **Movement** <term>Gamana</term>. 
**|| 104 ||**

When the "Teacher of the Gods" <note>original: "Devaguru"</note> is in the state of **Coming** <term>Agamana</term> at the time of birth, the person has a crowd of followers and an excellent wife. The divine grace <note>original: "Hari-maya," the illusion or power of Vishnu</note> does not truly leave his home, as he is bound on all sides by the grace of Jupiter. 
**|| 105 ||**

The man becomes an eloquent speaker like the Teacher of the Gods himself, adorned with bright pearls. In the assembly, he is suddenly filled with the measure of wealth, rubies, and honor. He is rich in elephants, horses, and chariots, worshipped by the lords of the gods, and proud of his various branches of knowledge. 
**|| 106 ||**

When Jupiter is in the state of **Coming** <term>Agamana</term> <note>This verse continues the description or elaborates on the state</note>, there is happiness from a multitude of various vehicles and honors, and joy derived from servants, children, wife, and friends. His knowledge is flawless. His mind is constantly charming and equal to that of a king, and he takes delight in the joy of poetry.

In the state of **Eating** <term>Bhojana</term>, if the "Teacher of the Gods" <note>original: "Devaguru," a title for Jupiter</note> is present at birth, that person always enjoys excellent food. Prosperity <note>original: "ramalyam," literally the abode of Rama or Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth</note> never leaves him, and he is adorned with horses, elephants, and chariots. **|| 108 ||**

In the state of **Desire to Dance** <term>Nrityalipsa</term>, the person is honored by kings, wealthy, and venerated even by the lords of the gods; he is always a knower of righteousness <term>Dharma</term>. If the "Worshipped of the Immortals" <note>Jupiter</note> is in this state, the person is joined with sons and political wisdom, possesses great strength, and serves as a scholar in the palace of a great ruler. **|| 110 ||**

When Jupiter is in the state of **Sleep** <term>Nidra</term>, the person displays foolishness in all his undertakings. His home is overcome by poverty and enemies, and it is devoid of any spiritual merit. **|| 111 ||**

### Now, the Results of Venus (Bhrigu) are stated:

If Venus is in the state of **Resting** <term>Shayana</term>, the person, though powerful, suffers from dental diseases and is possessed by great anger. He becomes destitute and is a lecher, addicted to the company of courtesans. **|| 112 ||**

If Venus <note>original: "Ushana," an ancient name for the planet Venus</note> is in the state of **Sitting** <term>Upaveshana</term>, the person is adorned with ornaments of gold and the nine gems. He enjoys constant happiness, the destruction of his enemies, and receives honor and high status from the ruler of the earth. **|| 113 ||**

If the "Poet" <note>original: "Kavi," a common epithet for Venus</note> is in the state of **Looking** <term>Netrapani</term> while in the first house <note>the Ascendant</note>, the seventh house, or the tenth house <note>original: "manabhe," the house of honor</note>, there is a certain loss of wealth. However, if Venus is in any other house in this state, the person will possess a vast and spacious mansion. **|| 114 ||**

If Venus is in the state of **Radiance** <term>Prakashana</term> while in its own sign, its sign of exaltation, or a friend’s sign, the person possesses noble elephants and the grace of various arts. He is equal to a king, a lover of the arts of poetry and drama, and an expert in music. **|| 115 ||**

If Venus is in the state of **Going** <term>Gamana</term> at the time of birth, the person’s mother does not survive <note>this usually implies an early death or significant hardship for the mother</note>. He suffers from mental distress and separation from his people due to fear of his enemies. **|| 116 ||**

When the "Son of Bhrigu" <note>Venus</note> has entered the state of **Coming** <term>Agamana</term>, the man becomes a lord of wealth. He frequents virtuous holy pilgrimage sites, is perpetually enthusiastic, yet suffers from ailments in his hands and feet. **|| 117 ||**

Without effort, he quickly attains great brilliance and boldness in the royal assembly, being a connoisseur of virtues when Venus is in the state of **Appearing in Court** <term>Sabha</term>. In this assembly, he is a destroyer of enemy hosts, equal to the lord of wealth, a donor, and a leader of strong horses—a truly eminent man. **|| 118 ||** 

In the state of **Arrival** <term>Agama</term>, through Venus, there is an arrival of heaps of wealth for those born under it, and the utter destruction of enemies. However, there may be the loss of a son or a downfall of men...

The person possesses flawless knowledge of poetry and learning, a charming intellect, and always a **Desire to Dance** <term>Nrityalipsa</term> when Venus <note>original: "Bhargava," meaning descendant of Bhrigu</note> is in that state. Such a person attains skill in the sounds of conch shells, lutes, and drums, as well as in vocal music; this becomes the source of his increasing wealth. **|| 121 ||**

# Now, the Results of Saturn.

Overcome by hunger and thirst and feeling exhausted is the person with Saturn in the state of **Resting** <term>Shayana</term>. In the first period of life, he is sickly, but thereafter he becomes the best among the fortunate. **|| 124 ||**

If the "Son of the Sun" <note>original: "Bhanu-suta," an epithet for Saturn</note> is in the state of **Sitting** <term>Upaveshana</term>, the person is troubled by fierce enemies. He is prone to mishaps, suffers from skin diseases <note>original: "dadru-mali," literally 'garlanded with ringworm'</note>, is very proud, and is subject to punishment by the king. **|| 125 ||**

When the "Son of the Sun" <note>Saturn</note> is in the state of **Hand-on-Eye** <term>Netrapani</term>, the person is joined with supreme wealth and a beautiful wife. He receives benefits from the king, brings satisfaction to the mind, is skilled in many arts, and speaks pure and spotless words. **|| 126 ||**

Possessing a multitude of virtues and great wealth, such a person is always finding joy in his own intellect. When the "Son of the Sun" is in the state of **Shining** <term>Prakashana</term>, he is like a bright sun himself, filled with compassion, and a devotee of the feet of Lord Shiva <note>original: "Hara-pada-bhakta"</note>. **|| 127 ||**

He will be very wealthy and delighted by his children, though he may cause harm and seize the lands of his enemies. When Saturn is in the state of **Going** <term>Gamana</term>, he attains the status of a "King of Scholars" in the palace of the ruler of the earth. **|| 128 ||**

In the state of **Coming** <term>Agamana</term>, the person is associated with poor modes of transport <note>original: "pada-gardabha," literally meaning 'foot-donkey'</note> and is deprived of the happiness of sons and wife. When the "Son of the Sun" is in this state, the person wanders the earth daily with a dejected mind, seeking refuge in solitary places. **|| 129 ||**

Through the trade of strings of jewels, gold, and pearls, he constantly finds delight. When the "Son of the Sun" is in the state of **In Assembly** <term>Sabha</term>, the man is filled with great policy and possesses immense vigor. **|| 130 ||**

When the "Son of the Friend of the Lotuses" <note>an epithet for Saturn as the son of the Sun</note> is in the state of **Arrival** <term>Agama</term>, then diseases come to men. His movement is slow like the ruler of the earth, and his mind is always free from the need to beg. **|| 131 ||**

When the "Son of the Sun" is joined with the time of birth in the state of **Eating** <term>Bhojana</term>, the person's food is full of rich flavors. [However], he suffers from weakness of the eyes and is tormented by the heat of delusion...

## Now, the Results of Rahu.

At a person’s birth, if Rahu has gone to the state of **Resting** <term>Shayana</term>, there is an abundance of distress. However, if this occurs while Rahu is in the signs of Taurus, Gemini, Virgo, or Aries, the person will instead gain a great assembly of wealth and grain. **|| 136 ||**

When Rahu has gone to the state of **Sitting** <term>Upaveshana</term>, the person is tormented by skin diseases such as ringworm. Though he may move in royal circles and be highly respected, he will always be lacking in financial happiness. **|| 137 ||**

When the "Serpent" <note>original: "Agu," a name for Rahu</note> is in the state of **Hand on the Eye** <term>Netrapani</term>, the person's eyes are afflicted by disease. He faces fear from wicked snakes, enemies, and thieves, as well as the depletion of his wealth. **|| 138 ||**

The state of **Shining** <term>Prakashana</term> is a favorable position. It brings a rise in wealth and an increase in virtues for the learned. One attains authority from the rulers of the earth, and their fame spreads like a wide-reaching vine. Such a person attains great prosperity from foreign lands and possesses a magnificent appearance, like that of a fresh rain cloud. **|| 139 ||**

When Rahu is in the state of **Going** <term>Gamana</term>, the man is blessed with many children. He becomes a scholar, a wealthy person, a donor, and is honored by kings. **|| 140 ||**

When Rahu is in the state of **Coming** <term>Agamana</term>, the person is prone to anger and is always devoid of wisdom and wealth. He becomes deceitful, miserly, and lustful in every respect. **|| 141 ||**

When Rahu has gone to the **Assembly** <term>Sabha</term>, the man is a scholar but also a miser. He is encompassed by various good qualities and is endowed with wealth and happiness. **|| 142 ||**

If Rahu enters the state of **Arrival** <note>original: "Agama"</note>, the person experiences agitation and fear from enemies. There are great disputes with relatives, social downfall, loss of wealth, deceit, and physical weakness. **|| 143 ||**

In the state of **Eating** <term>Bhojana</term>, the person is never satisfied by food and feels distressed. He is dull-witted, afraid of taking action, and is deprived of the happiness found with a wife and children. **|| 144 ||**

When Rahu has gone to the state of **Desire to Dance** <term>Nrityalipsa</term>, there is an increase in great diseases. It brings eye ailments, fear of enemies, and the loss of both wealth and righteousness for men. **|| 145 ||**

## Now, the Results of Ketu.

If Ketu has gone to the state of **Resting** <term>Shayana</term> in the signs of Aries, Taurus, Gemini, or Virgo, there will be an abundance of wealth; in any other zodiac signs, there is an increase in disease. **|| 148 ||**

When Ketu has gone to the state of **Sitting** <term>Upavesha</term>, there is an increase in skin diseases such as ringworm. There is constant suspicion or fear from enemies, "wind" diseases <note>likely gout or arthritis</note>, kings, snakes <note>original: "vyala," which can also mean rogue elephants or tigers</note>, and thieves. **|| 149 ||**

When Ketu has gone to the state of **Hand on the Eye** <term>Netrapani</term>, eye diseases arise. There is also fear of wicked snakes, as well as trouble from enemies and the royal family. **|| 150 ||**

When Ketu is in the state known as **Radiance** <term>Prakashana</term>, the person is wealthy and always righteous. He is a constant traveler, enthusiastic, pure-hearted <note>original: "sattvika," possessing the quality of goodness and harmony</note>, and a servant of the king. **|| 151 ||**

If Ketu is in the state of **Desire to Go** <term>Gamanecha</term>, the person will have many sons and great wealth. He becomes a scholar, virtuous, charitable, and a supreme among men. **|| 152 ||**

When Ketu is in the state of **Arrival** <term>Agama</term>, there are various diseases and a loss of wealth. The person suffers from tooth injuries or ailments, is chronically ill, a backbiter, and a slanderer of others. **|| 153 ||**

If Ketu has gone to the state of **Being in the Assembly** <term>Sabhastha</term>, the person is talkative and very proud. He is miserly, licentious, and skilled in the arts of deception. **|| 154 ||**

When Ketu is in the state of **Return** <term>Agama - repeated</term>, he becomes one who performs sinful deeds. He is fond of arguing with his relatives, is wicked, and is oppressed by enemies and disease. **|| 155 ||**

In the state of **Eating** <term>Bhojana</term>, the person is always oppressed by hunger. Being poor and continuously afflicted by disease, he wanders the earth. **|| 156 ||**

When Ketu has gone to the state of **Desire to Dance** <term>Nrityalipsa</term>, the person becomes disabled by disease. He has bubble-like eyes <note>perhaps referring to cataracts or a bulging appearance</note>, is harsh and difficult to overcome, a rogue, and a cause of misfortune. **|| 157 ||**

When Ketu is in the state of **Eagerness** <term>Kautuka</term>, the person is a seeker of pleasures who enjoys the company of actors and women. Fallen from his position, ill-behaved, and poor, he wanders the earth. **|| 158 ||**

When Ketu has gone to the state of **Sleep** <term>Nidravastha</term>, there is great wealth, grain, and happiness. The life of such individuals passes in various virtuous amusements. **|| 159 ||**

## Now, the Results of All Houses.

In the states beginning with **Resting** <term>Shayana</term>, for whomsoever benefic planets are situated, their results are always auspicious...

<header>Summary of the Great Parashara Horashastra</header>

...knowledge will be free from any doubt, O Best of the Twice-born <note>original: "dvijottama," a respectful address to a Brahmin</note>. **|| 160 ||**

If a malefic planet is in the state of **Eating** <term>Bhojana</term> or similar states in any of the houses, it brings total destruction; there is no need for further deliberation on this. **|| 161 ||**

When a malefic is in the state of **Sleep** <term>Nidra</term> in the seventh house <note>the house of marriage and partnerships</note>, even if a benefic is said to be there, if it is aspected by <note>looked upon by</note> malefic planets, it will never produce good results. **|| 162 ||**

If a malefic is situated in the fifth house <note>the house of children and intelligence</note> while in the states of **Sleep** <term>Nidra</term> or **Resting** <term>Shayana</term>, then the results will actually be auspicious; there is no doubt about this. **|| 163 ||**

If a malefic is in the eighth house <note>the house of longevity and death</note> in the states of **Sleep** or **Resting**, then the person will suffer an untimely death <note>original: "apamṛtyu"</note> caused by the king or by others. **|| 164 ||**

However, if that planet is joined with or aspected by benefic planets, then the death will occur specifically at the Ganges <note>considered a holy and auspicious passing in Hindu tradition</note>. **|| 165 ||**

When a malefic is in the tenth house <note>the house of profession and action</note> in the states of **Resting** or **Eating**, then the "ripening of actions" <note>original: "karma-vipaka," the fruition of past deeds</note> will occur, bestowing various kinds of sorrow. **|| 166 ||**

If the Moon <note>original: "nishanatha," Lord of the Night</note> is in the tenth house in the states of **Amusement** <term>Kautuka</term> or **Radiance** <term>Prakashana</term>, then a <term>Rajayoga</term> <note>a combination for royal success or high status</note> is certainly formed, O Best of the Twice-born. **|| 167 ||**

By considering the relative strength and weakness of the planets, one knows the good and bad effects. In this sequence, O Wise One, the effects should be understood for all the houses. **|| 168 ||**

**Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of the Results of Planetary States," in the Summary of the Early Section of the Great Parashara Horashastra.** **|| 34 ||**

### Maitreya said:

O Great Sage, how many types of **planetary periods** <term>Dashas</term> are there? Please tell me this in truth, for you are capable and a treasure-house of compassion. **|| 1 ||**

### Parashara said:

Now I shall describe the many various types of planetary periods. First, the **120-year system** <term>Vimshottari</term> is mentioned, as well as the **116-year system** <term>Shodashottari</term>. **|| 2 ||**

The **108-year system** <term>Ashtottari</term> should be known, as well as the **112-year system** <term>Dwadashottari</term>. Similarly, there is the **105-year system** <term>Panchottari</term> and the **100-year system** <term>Shatasama</term>. **|| 3 ||**

He also spoke of the **84-year system** <term>Chaturashiti</term>, then the **72-year system** <term>Dvisaptati</term>. Likewise, the **60-year system** <term>Shashtisama</term> is mentioned, and the **26-year system** <term>Shadvimshati-sama</term>. **|| 4 ||**

The **Ninth-divisional system** <term>Navamsha-dasha</term> and the **Sign-division system** <term>Rashyamshaka-dasha</term> are remembered. Then there is the period named **Time** <term>Kala-dasha</term> and the **Cycle system** <term>Chakra-dasha</term> mentioned by the Great Sages. **|| 5 ||**

O Brahmin, there is the **Moving Cycle system** <term>Charaparya-dasha</term> and the **Fixed system** <term>Sthira-dasha</term> <note>original: "dwijottama-dasha"</note>.

<header>Section One: Chapter 35 on the Description of the Various Types of Dashas</header>

Next are the **Uttara Dasha**, O Brahmin, and another called the **Brahmata Dasha**. **|| 6 ||** The **Kendradi Dasha** should be known, as well as the **Karakadi Graha Dasha**. The **Manduki Dasha** has been described, and likewise the **Shula Dasha**. **|| 7 ||** I shall now speak of the **Yogardha Dasha**, O Brahmin, and the **Drig Dasha**. Then there is the dasha named **Trikona**, and also the **Dasha of the Zodiac Signs** <note>original: "Rashi Dasha"</note>. **|| 8 ||** The **Tara Dasha** should be known, as well as the dasha known as **Varnada**. The **Panchasvara Dasha**, O Brahmin, and the **Yogini Dasha** are also remembered. **|| 9 ||** After that, the **Pindya Dasha** should be known, and also the **Amsha Dasha**, O Twice-born. The **Naisargika Dasha** <note>the natural period of planetary influence</note>, O Brahmin, and the **Ashtakavarga Dasha** are mentioned. **|| 10 ||** The **Sandhya Dasha** should be understood, as well as the **Pachaka Dasha**, O Twice-born. There are forty-two varieties in total, which I shall explain before you. **|| 11 ||**

## Now, the Vimsottari Dasha system.

Listen, O best of the Twice-born, to the method of calculation. The base of the calculation is from the star **Krittika** <note>the third lunar mansion or Nakshatra</note> up to the birth Nakshatra. **|| 12 ||** If the birth occurs during the dark fortnight in the Sun's **Hora** <note>a one-hour planetary division of a sign</note>, or during the bright fortnight <note>original: "Sita"</note> in the Moon's Hora, one should count from **Dahana** <note>a poetic name for the Nakshatra Krittika, meaning "the fire"</note> up to one's own birth star and divide that number by nine. **|| 13 ||** The Sun, Moon, Mars, Rahu, Jupiter, Saturn, Mercury, Ketu, and Venus—these are to be known as the lords of the Dashas in this specific order. **|| 14 ||** The years for these planets, starting from the Sun, are: 6, 10, 7, 18, 16, 19, 17, 7, and 20 years. <note>The Sanskrit uses symbolic words for numbers: Rasa (6), Asha (10), Muni (7), Dhriti (18), Bhupati (16), Dhriti (19), Saptendu (17), Naga (7), and Vyomabahava (20). Together they total the 120-year cycle of the Vimsottari system.</note> **|| 15 ||** I shall provide an example of this below.

## Now, the Shodashottari Dasha system.

The years of the periods, in order, are eleven increased by one each time up to eighteen: <gloss>11</gloss> Sun, <gloss>12</gloss> Mars, <gloss>13</gloss> Jupiter, <gloss>14</gloss> Saturn, <gloss>15</gloss> Ketu, <gloss>16</gloss> Moon, <gloss>17</gloss> Mercury, and <gloss>18</gloss> Venus. **|| 16 ||** Eight dasha lords are mentioned here, using the nine planets but excluding Rahu. One should count from the star **Pushya** to the birth Nakshatra and divide by eight <note>original: "vasu," a term for the number 8</note>. **|| 17 ||** When a person is born in the Sun's Hora during the bright fortnight, or in the Moon's Hora during the dark fortnight, then the **Shodashottari** system <note>a cycle totaling 116 years</note> should be considered to determine their results. **|| 18 ||**

## Now, an example of the Shodashottari Dasha.

According to the method stated in the verse beginning with "The Moon is very clear," <note>original: "sphutataro himaguḥ"</note> etc., the longitude of the Moon is 8 [signs]...

## Now, he describes the Ashtottari Dasha.

> The Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Saturn, Jupiter, Rahu, and Venus—these are declared the lords of the periods. The nine planets are used, excluding Ketu. || 21 ||
>

>

## Now, an example of the Ashtottari Dasha.

One should count from the star Ardra (or Krittika) to the birth star. In this instance, the count from Ardra to the birth star is 15. The resulting order of planetary periods is: Sun (6), Moon (15), Mars (8), Mercury (17), Saturn (10), Jupiter (19), Rahu (12), and Venus (21). Among these, the birth falls within the period of Saturn, which has a total duration of 10 years. 

He now describes the method for calculating the "elapsed" and "remaining" time: In this chart, the Moon at birth is at 8 signs, 25 degrees, 29 minutes, and 38 seconds <note>Written as 8 | 25 | 29 | 38</note>. Its <term>Kalapinda</term> <note>the total value converted into arc-minutes</note> is 15829 minutes and 38 seconds. When this is divided by eight hundred (800) <note>the total number of minutes in one Nakshatra/star zone</note>, the quotient is 19, representing the completed stars, the last being Purva Ashadha. 

The movement within the star is 30. Using this, the remainder 729 | 38 is multiplied, resulting in 218890. When this is divided by 800, the result in years, months, and days is 2 years, 3 months, 10 days, 60 ghatikas, and 15 palas <note>Ghatikas and Palas are traditional Indian units of time; a Ghatika is 24 minutes</note>. This is the time already elapsed from a previous life. Subtracting this from the total 10 years of the Saturn period, the "remaining" time to be experienced is 7 years, 8 months, 19 days, 9 ghatikas, and 45 palas. This method should be understood for all such calculations.

# Now, he describes the Shatabdika Dasha.

> The Sun, the Moon, Venus, Mercury, Jupiter, Mars, and Saturn <note>original: Ravi, Chandra, Bhrigu, Chandri, Jiva, Vishwambharatmaja (Son of Earth/Mars), Divakari (Son of Sun/Saturn)</note> are the lords in this sequence. Their years are five, five, ten, ten, twenty, twenty, and thirty respectively. || 28 ||
> 
> These years are calculated from the day of birth. This Shatabdika (100-year) system should be considered when the Ascendant is in its Vargottama <note>a "best division" where the sign in the main chart and the ninth divisional chart are the same</note>. || 29 ||
> 
> One should count from the star Revati <note>original: Paushna</note> to the birth star and divide the total by seven. From the remainder, the periods are known starting from the Sun. This is the 100-year cycle. || 30 ||

# An Example of This.

The Moon at birth is at 8 signs, 26 degrees, 29 minutes, and 38 seconds <note>This placement is in the sign of Sagittarius</note>. Its total value in minutes (Kalapinda) is 16,929 minutes and 38 seconds. Divided by 800 <note>The mathematical span of one lunar mansion</note>, the quotient is 21, meaning 21 stars have passed and the current star is Purva Ashadha with a remainder of 729 minutes and 38 seconds. 

Counting from Revati, this falls under the period of Saturn. In the Saturn period, the total years are 30. The remainder (729' 38") multiplied [by 30] equals 21,886. When this is divided by 800, it shows that the time already elapsed (the "past") is 27 years, 4 months, 1 day, 3 hours, and 10 minutes. 

Subtracting this from the total of 30 years, the period remaining to be experienced in this life is 2 years, 7 months, 19 days, 50 hours, and 0 minutes. This logic should be understood everywhere.

## Now, he describes the Chaturasityabdika Dasha.

> The Sun, the Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn—excluding the shadow planets Rahu and Ketu <note>original: "tamadhvajau vina" meaning without Rahu (darkness) and Ketu (the banner).</note>—all these planets have periods of twelve years each. || 31 ||
> 
> Starting from the star Swati to the birth star, divide the count by seven; the remainder determines the current period. This 84-year system <note>term: Chaturasityabdika (chatur = four, asiti = eighty, abdika = years).</note> is to be known and applied when the Lord of the 10th House is situated within the 10th House itself. || 32 ||

### An example of this:

The Moon at birth is at 8 signs, 26 degrees, 29 minutes, and 38 seconds <note>This position corresponds to the constellation Purva Ashadha.</note>. The total value of this position converted into minutes is 15,929 minutes and 38 seconds. Dividing this by 800 <note>One star occupies 800 minutes of the zodiac.</note>, the remainder is 729 and the quotient is 19. This means 19 stars have passed, and the current star is Purva Ashadha, which falls under the period of Venus lasting 12 years. 

The remaining balance of the star is 729 minutes and 38 seconds. Multiplying these values to find the elapsed time, we get 8,756' 36". Dividing this by 800 shows that in the "previous birth" <note>This refers to the portion of the 12-year period that had already expired before the moment of birth.</note>, 10 years, 11 months, 10 days, 1 hour, and 12 minutes had passed. Subtracting this from the total 12-year period, the balance to be experienced in this life is 1 year, 0 months, 29 days, 58 hours, and 48 minutes. This same logic should be understood and applied in all such calculations.

## Now, he describes the 72-year period system <note>term: Dvisaptatika Dasha (dvi = two, saptati = seventy, abdika = years).</note>.

> When the Lord of the Ascendant <note>original: "Lagnasha"</note> is located in the seventh house, or when the Lord of the seventh house <note>original: "Madanadhipa," the 7th house governs passion and partnerships.</note> is located in the Ascendant, the 72-year period system should be considered. || 33 ||
> 
> In this system, each of the eight planets—excluding Ketu <note>original: "viketūnam," without the descending node of the moon.</note>—is assigned nine years. To calculate the starting period, count from the star Mula to the birth star and divide the total by eight. The remainder identifies the specific planetary period to be analyzed, O Great Sage! || 34 ||

->**An example of this calculation:**<-

The Moon’s position at birth is 8 signs, 26 degrees, 29 minutes, and 38 seconds. This is converted into a total value of 15,929 minutes and 38 seconds <note>term: Kalapinda (the total sum of minutes of arc).</note>. Dividing this by 800 <note>The span of one Nakshatra is 800 minutes.</note>, we get a quotient of 19, with a remainder of 729 minutes and 38 seconds. The 20th star is Purva Ashadha. In this 72-year system, each planet's period is 9 years. To find the portion of the 9-year period already passed at birth, we take the remainder (729' 38"), multiply it, and divide by 800. This yields 8 years, 2 months, 16 days, 0 hours, and 54 minutes already passed. Subtracting this from the total 9 years, the remaining time to be experienced at birth <note>term: Bhogya-varsha (the period yet to be enjoyed/experienced).</note> is 0 years, 9 months, 14 days, 59 minutes, and 6 seconds. This method should be understood for all calculations.

->**Description of the 36-Year Period System**<-

One should count from the star Shravana to the birth star and divide that number by eight. The planets [associated with the remainders] are the Moon, Sun, Jupiter, Mars, Mercury, Saturn, Venus, and Rahu. || 37 || 

The years assigned to these planets are one [through eight] respectively, according to the remainder. For a birth during the day, if the Sun is in the Sun's hour <note>term: Hora (an astrological hour, half of a zodiac sign's duration)</note>, this 36-year cycle <note>original: "shat-gunabdika," meaning six-multiplied-by-six years</note> should be considered. || 38 ||

For a birth at night, one should count from the Moon’s position... [using the remainder of] the birth star of the king <note>note: "king" here likely refers to the person for whom the chart is cast</note> divided by eight. The planets are the Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, || 39 ||

Venus, Saturn, Rahu, and Ketu <note>original: "shikhin," the descending node of the moon</note>, and their periods are determined by their placement in the Ascendant. Their years should be assigned according to their exact longitudinal positions in the signs. || 40 ||

The period should be considered according to the sequence of the planets when Saturn is situated in the Ascendant. Occasionally, when a planet is exceptionally powerful, its period is not considered in the standard way but rather by its strength. || 41 ||

The calculation example for this system should be understood similarly to the 120-year system <note>term: Vimshottari (the most common 120-year period system)</note>.

<header>First Section: Chapter 35 on the Description of Various Planetary Periods</header>

# Now, the description of the nine periods based on the Ninth Division.
<note>term: Navamshaka (the ninth division of a zodiacal sign, used for fine-tuning astrological predictions)</note>

> Now I shall describe the sequence of the signs; listen, O best of the twice-born <note>original: "dvija-pungava"; a respectful address to a learned person</note>. The planet whose position in signs and degrees is the least shall have the first period. || 42 ||
>
> Then, the period of the one with more longitude follows, and so on. If the longitudes are equal, the order is determined by their natural strength. One should consider the sequence of periods from the lord of the sign or the lord of the ninth division. || 43 ||
>
> The first period is considered to belong to the one situated in the first ninth division. Here, the planets are placed in order from the Moon to Ketu <note>the South Node of the Moon</note>. || 44 ||
>
> I shall now state the duration of these periods as declared by Brahma in ancient times. Having converted the planet's position into minutes <note>term: liptikrtva (the process of converting degrees and signs into minutes of arc)</note>, divide it by ten thousand eight hundred. || 45 ||
>
> Multiply the result by the Sun <note>note: original "surye" here likely refers to the number 12, as the Sun moves through 12 signs</note> to obtain the period in years and further subdivisions. These periods should be reflected upon for all human beings. || 46 ||

## Commentary

Now, the venerable Teacher <note>term: Acharya</note> speaks of nine varieties contained within the forty-two types of planetary periods he has previously mentioned. "Now" <note>original: "atha"</note>—after the previously mentioned periods, "O best of the twice-born, I shall speak of the sequence of the signs; listen to it," he says to the student to prepare him for the teaching.

The word "Planet" <note>original: "grahe"</note> is used here in the singular to represent the whole class. Among the planets, that one whose signs, degrees, minutes, and seconds are the least—meaning smaller than all others—his period shall be the first. By saying "the first," it is understood that the others follow in order. 

This means: the planet whose longitude is greater than the first but less than the remaining ones takes the second place. In this way, the sequence for all nine should be understood. This is the first method.

"Then, of the one with more..." refers to the next method. Among those planets, the one who is the greatest—the one with the highest signs and degrees—becomes the first. This is the reverse of the previous order and represents a second variation.

Regarding "If equal, then from natural strength": if, while applying these two methods, two planets happen to have the exact same longitude, then in the first method, the one with the least natural strength <note>term: naisargika-bala (the inherent, fixed strength of a planet regardless of its position)</note> is taken first, followed by the one with more natural strength. In the second method, however, the one with the most natural strength...

In the case of a planet with more longitude [than another], if it has less natural strength, it should be taken later even if the longitudes are equal; there is no contradiction in these two types of differences.

Now, the **third variety**: "From natural strength" refers to the third method where the planet with the least natural strength <note>term: Naisargika-bala (the inherent, permanent strength of a planet regardless of its current position)</note> is assigned the first period, followed by the one with more strength for the second, and so on. In these first three varieties, the inclusion of Rahu and Ketu <note>the North and South Nodes of the Moon</note> should be understood. Otherwise, it would be impossible to find all nine periods, as these nodes possess positions in signs and degrees and have their own natural strength.

If it is asked why "natural strength" is mentioned as two different types, it is simply to complete the count of nine varieties; the phrase is repeated for the sake of the classification system.

"From the lord of the birth sign or the lord of the seventh...": The "lord of the sign" <note>term: Rashisha</note> refers to the planetary ruler of a zodiac sign. This means: if the birth sign <note>term: Janma Rashi (the sign the Moon occupied at birth)</note> is Gemini, its lord is Mercury; his period comes first. Then the lord of Cancer is the Moon; his period comes second, and so on.

Now, a doubt may arise: should we follow the order of the zodiac signs or the order of the planets? In this case, the sequence of the signs is used, because of the rule: "the period follows the sequence of signs." If it is then argued that in the sequence starting from Gemini, Mercury would get the first period and also the fourth (because he also rules Virgo), this is not an error. In this system, we take the lords of the twelve signs in order; therefore, the repetition of a single planet as a ruler is not a flaw.

The duration of years here should be taken as the number nine for each sign, as the total sum of one hundred and eight years is obtained <note>original: "ashtottara"; 108 is a significant number in Vedic astrology, often representing the 108 quarters of the lunar mansions</note>. This is the **fourth variety**.

"From the lord of the seventh and the body": This refers to starting the sequence of periods from the ruler of the seventh house relative to the Ascendant <note>term: Lagna (the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth)</note>. This is the **fifth variety**.

Similarly, starting from the "lord of the body" (the ruler of the Ascendant), the first period belongs to him, the second to the ruler of the second house, and so on. The sequence of periods should be understood from the sequence of signs as described before. This is the **sixth variety**. Note that from the fourth variety through the sixth, only the seven primary planets (ending with Saturn) are used, as Rahu and Ketu are not considered primary rulers of signs in this specific context.

"In which [Ninth Division]": Whichever ninth division <note>term: Navamsha (a 3°20' sub-division of a sign)</note> the Ascendant is located in—starting from the ruler of that division, the periods of the nine planets should be known in order. This is the **seventh variety**.

"From the end": Starting from the "Agra" (the end or ninth planet) and moving backward to the first, the periods of the planets should be known sequentially. This is the **eighth variety**.

"From the Moon": Starting from the Moon, the nine periods should be taken in order. In this variety...

In the three types of period variations <term>Dasha-bheda</term>, to indicate the inclusion of Rahu and Ketu <note>the North and South Nodes of the Moon</note>, it is clearly written: "The planets are situated in order, ending with Ketu" <note>original: "kheṭāḥ ketvantāḥ saṃsthitāḥ kramāt"</note>. ## Now, an example of the Nine-fold Navamsha Period is given.

For example, the Moon at birth is at 8 signs, 26 degrees, 29 minutes, and 38 seconds <note>This position corresponds to the sign of Sagittarius</note>. Its total minutes <term>Kalapinda</term> is 15,929 minutes and 38 seconds. Dividing this by 20, the resulting figure is 796. This, when divided by twelve (12), gives the elapsed years and further units: 66 years, 0 months, 19 days, 0 hours, and 0 minutes. This should be subtracted from 108 <note>the total cycle of the Ashtottari system</note>. The remaining period to be experienced <term>Bhogya</term> is then 43 years, 11 months, 11 days, 0 hours, and 0 minutes. This method should be understood everywhere. Furthermore, wherever there are planetary periods, twelve (12) years are to be taken for each individual planet; where there are sign periods, nine (9) years are to be taken for each sign. In all cases, the total measure of 108 years should be recognized.

## Now, the Sign-Division Period is described.

> The houses, starting from the body <note>term: Tanu-bhava (the first house or Ascendant)</note>, should be brought to their clear positions according to the prescribed method. Wherever the lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagnesha</term> is situated in its division <term>Amsha</term>, these are remembered as its periods. [47]
> Starting from the lord of the second house and proceeding forward, the Sign-Division periods <term>Rashyamshaka Dasha</term> are to be known. These should be considered when the Ascendant is strong or when the lord of the Ascendant is endowed with strength. [48]

The example for this period should be understood in the same way as the Nine-fold Division <term>Navamsha</term> example above.

<header>Summary of the Great Parashara Hora</header>

...the divisions known as "Sudha" <note>Nectar</note> consist of ten <term>nadikas</term> <note>A unit of time equal to 24 minutes, also called a ghatika</note>. In the "Purna" <note>Full</note> and "Mugdha" <note>Innocent/Enchanting</note> divisions, the elapsed time should be multiplied by six and written in nine positions. || 52 || Likewise, in the "Khanda" <note>Fragmented</note> and "Sudha" divisions, one should multiply the time by twelve and write it in nine positions. These are then divided by forty-five <note>original: "indriya-yugai"; in traditional Sanskrit numerology, Senses (Indriya) represent 5 and Ages (Yuga) represent 4, totaling 45</note> to find the results known as "Gana." || 53 || The great sages have stated these measures for the Sun and the other planets in their proper order. When each planet’s individual measure is multiplied by its own specific number, the resulting years and other time units are determined. || 54 ||

# Commentary

**"Of the day"**: In this context, the word "day" refers to the full twenty-four-hour cycle of day and night <note>original: "ahoratra"</note>. A full day-night cycle consists of sixty <term>ghatikas</term>. Within this period, five <term>ghatikas</term> are designated as <term>Sandhya</term> <note>A "junction" or twilight period</note>. These junctions are of two main types, which are further divided into four variations. 

To explain: from the half-setting and half-rising of the Sun’s disk, five <term>ghatikas</term> before and five after are to be known as the Eastern and Western junctions. Thus, these two types of junctions, each lasting ten <term>ghatikas</term>, are said to total twenty <term>ghatikas</term>. 

The remaining twenty <term>ghatikas</term> of the day are named **"Purna"** <note>The "Full" portion of the day</note>. The remaining twenty <term>ghatikas</term> of the night are named **"Mugdha"** <note>The "Enchanting" portion of the night</note>. The five <term>ghatikas</term> occurring before and after sunrise, totaling ten <term>ghatikas</term>, are called **"Khanda"**. Thus, there are four distinct divisions: Purna, Mugdha, Khanda, and Sudha. 

When a birth occurs during the Purna or Mugdha divisions, the elapsed time <note>the time passed since the division began</note> is multiplied by six. This value is then written in nine positions. Alternatively, if the birth occurs in the Khanda or Sudha divisions, the elapsed time is multiplied by twelve and written in nine positions. 

When these figures are divided by forty-five (45), the resulting quotient is what the illustrious Teacher calls the **"Mana"** <note>The standard measure or weight of influence</note> of the Sun and the other planets. When each planet's measure is multiplied by its own specific numerical factor, the years and subsequent time units <note>months, days, etc.</note> are produced.

# An Example of This

The **"Wheel of Time"** <term>Kala Chakra</term> is divided into two distinct methods. An example of the first method is given here: 

Suppose a birth occurs at 8 <term>ghatikas</term> and 16 <term>vighatikas</term> <note>roughly 3 hours and 18 minutes after sunrise</note> into the day. From this time, the 5 <term>ghatikas</term> belonging to the sunrise junction must be subtracted. The remaining time is 3 <term>ghatikas</term> and 16 <term>vighatikas</term>. This birth falls within the **"Purna"** division. Consequently, these figures are multiplied by six, resulting in the numbers 19 and 36. This is then divided by forty-five (45)...

# Now, he describes the Moving Cycle Period.

O Maitreya, O most wise one, who works for the benefit of others! The consideration of <term>Ayurdaya</term> <note>The determination of the span of life or longevity.</note> is always a profound and deep subject, O twice-born. || 66 || Longevity was spoken of in many ways by Brahma in ancient times. O Brahmin, the longevity based on the stars <term>Nakshatras</term> has already been told by me in your presence. Now, O best of the twice-born, I shall thoroughly explain longevity based on the signs <term>Rashis</term>. || 68 ||

O Brahmin, there are twelve signs starting from the Ascendant <term>Lagna</term> and ending with the house of loss <term>Vyaya</term>. These signs provide the years of life in this <term>Chara Paryaya Dasha</term> <note>Literally the "Moving Cycle Period," a method of timing events and life span in Vedic astrology.</note>. || 69 ||

For the odd-numbered signs <term>Oja-rksha</term>, the counting is in the regular order; for the even-numbered signs <term>Sama</term>, it is in reverse order. O best of the twice-born, the years should be known without doubt by counting until the Lord of the sign is reached. || 70 ||

Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Libra, Scorpio, and Sagittarius—these are known as the "Odd" signs for the purpose of this counting. || 71 || <note>original: "Oja-sangya". Interestingly, this text includes Taurus and Scorpio in the 'odd' category for this specific calculation, which differs from standard classifications.</note>

Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces—these are known as the "Even" signs, and their years are counted in reverse, O twice-born. || 72 ||

If a planet is situated in its own sign, it grants twelve years. If it is in the second house from its sign, it grants one year; if in the third, two years. || 73 ||

O Brahmin, if in the fourth house, three years; if in the fifth, four years. If in the sixth, five years; and six years if in the seventh. || 74 ||

If in the eighth house, seven years; if in the ninth, eight years. If in the tenth, nine years; and if in the eleventh house of gains, ten years. || 75 ||

If in the twelfth house, eleven years <note>original: "Rudra-varshani"; Rudra represents the number 11.</note>. These are the sign-years as told by me, O sinless one, in the manner mentioned before. || 76 ||

O best of the twice-born, Scorpio has two lords: Mars and Ketu. For Aquarius, consider the two lords to be Saturn and Rahu. || 77 ||

If both lords are situated in their own sign, they grant twelve years. If they are in another's sign, both are considered, but do not count beyond the Lord. || 78 ||

If the two lords are in different signs, then determine which of the two is stronger. Write down the years according to the position of that stronger lord. || 79 ||

A sign with a planet is stronger than one without a planet. A sign with more planets is even stronger. If they are equal in that regard, then the "Movable," "Fixed," and "Dual" natures are considered stronger in that specific order. || 80 ||

O Brahmin, when the signs are equal in strength, the one that provides more years is considered the stronger. Beyond that, a planet that is exalted is considered powerful...

<header>The Essence of the Great Parashara’s Astrology.</header>

...the son of Subala, O twice-born. || 81 || Even if a planet is predicted to grant only a few years of life, O Brahmin, it still grants its full measure if it is exalted <note>original: "tungago," referring to a planet in its highest state of celestial strength</note> and strong. The calculation should be known by counting until the Lord of the sign is reached, following the sequence previously described. || 82 ||

One year should be added to the count for a planet situated in its house of exaltation. Similarly, O twice-born, one year should be subtracted for a planet in its house of debilitation <note>original: "neecha," the sign where a planet is weakest</note>. || 83 ||

If one ruler is in its own sign and another is placed elsewhere, one should take the ruler situated elsewhere to determine the period. || 84 || If one ruler is in its exaltation and the other is elsewhere, one must definitely take the sign of the exalted planet and disregard the other. || 85 ||

Having considered all these factors, one should predict the time of death within that period. If there is a conjunction with malefic planets, or an aspect <note>A "glance" or influence from another planet</note> from malefics, or if malefic planets occupy the trines <note>the 1st, 5th, and 9th houses</note> from that sign... || 86 || ...then death is declared in that period, just as it was spoken by Lord Brahma. Now, I shall tell you the specific results of these Moving Cycle Periods. || 87 ||

# Now, he explains an example of the Moving Cycle Period.

For <term>Odd Signs</term> <note>original: "Oja-rashi"</note>, the counting is done in the regular order. For <term>Even Signs</term> <note>original: "Sama-rashi"</note>, the counting is done in reverse. The number of years is equal to the number of signs counted from the sign in question until one reaches its Lord. The signs Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Libra, Scorpio, and Sagittarius are designated as "Odd Signs" in this system. Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces are designated as "Even Signs."

If the ruler of a sign is located within that sign itself, then twelve years should be taken. If the ruler is exalted, then one year is added to the resulting number; if the ruler is debilitated, then one year must be subtracted from the result.

The sign of Scorpio has two lords: <term>Mars and Ketu</term>. Similarly, the sign of <term>Aquarius</term> has two lords: <term>Saturn and Rahu</term>. In these cases, whichever of the two is stronger is the one that should be used for the calculation.

He now <term>explains the sequence of the periods</term>: For example, <term>Mars</term> is the ruler of <term>Aries</term>. If Mars is placed in the twelfth house from Aries, there would be eleven years <note>Following the rule of counting from the sign to the lord and then subtracting one, or according to the specific count of this system</note>. Likewise, for Taurus, if one arrives at ten years and its ruler is in its exaltation sign, one year is added, making it eleven years. <term>Saturn</term> is the ruler of Capricorn; if it is placed in its own sign, then there are twelve years. This is how the calculation should be understood everywhere.

# Now, he describes the Fixed Period based on the Ninth-Division.

> Now I shall speak specifically about the Fixed Periods (*Sthira Dasha*). I will explain the measurement of the Ninth-Divisional Period <note>original: "navamsha," a 1/9th division of a zodiac sign used for deeper analysis</note> before you. || 88 ||
> For every zodiac sign, a fixed period of nine years <note>original: "ankanka-abda," where 'anka' is a numerical code for 9</note> is prescribed. O best of the twice-born <note>a term for a Brahmin</note>, one should clarify these for the twelve houses, from the House of the Body <note>the 1st house or Ascendant</note> to the House of Loss <note>the 12th house</note>. || 89 ||
> According to the method of determining life-span from the planets' Ninth-Divisions, these periods are equal. They should be understood as "Unstable" (*Asthira*) periods; this is the sequence according to the other school of thought. || 90 ||
> I shall explain both perspectives: the Moving (*Chara*) and the Fixed (*Sthira*), O Brahmin. First, I will explain the Moving Period before you, O son of the twice-born. || 91 ||
> O twice-born, for one whose birth occurs in an **Odd Ascendant** <term>Odd Signs: Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, and Aquarius</term>, the Ninth-Divisional period begins from the Ascendant at the moment of birth. || 92 ||
> For one whose birth occurs in an **Even Ascendant** <term>Even Signs: Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricorn, and Pisces</term>, the Ninth-Divisional period begins from the [seventh] sign, as was previously ordained by Lord Shiva. || 93 ||
> When a planet <note>original: "kheta"</note> is situated in an Odd Sign, one should lead the periods in the regular order. For the Ninth-Divisions of those signs and so forth, the sequence is regular, but in an Even Sign, it is in reverse. || 94 ||
> If the planet that initiates the period is in an Odd Sign, O twice-born, one should count the nine-year periods for all signs in sequential order. || 95 ||
> In the calculation of 108 years, those divisions are known as the famous Fixed Period (*Sthira Dasha*). O best of the twice-born, know this without a doubt. || 96 ||
> If the planet that initiates the period has entered an Even Sign, O twice-born, one should calculate starting from that sign and counting...

...and by sequence. || 97 || O best of the twice-born <note>original: "dvija-uttama," a respectful address to a member of the scholarly or priestly class</note>, for those ninth-divisions <note>original: "navamsha," the 1/9th sub-division of a sign used for fine-tuned predictions</note> located in their respective signs, the total number of years for the fixed periods is one hundred and eight. || 98 || When a period of an odd-numbered sign is reached, for Aries, one should count starting from Aries. I shall now speak of the sequence for both as declared in the *Trishuli* <note>A specific astrological authority or treatise</note>. || 5 ||

Therefore, the eighth house from the ascendant is to be counted. Similarly, there are 9 years for Aries, 9 years for Taurus, and so it should be understood for all signs.

# Now, the Explanation of the Fixed Periods.

Now I shall well explain the Fixed Periods <term>Sthira Dasha: a system of astrological time-cycles used primarily to determine the timing of major life events and longevity</term>, O best of the twice-born. I shall describe two methods as taught by Lord Shiva <note>original: "Shambhu-pranoditam"</note>. || 6 || 

The signs <term>Rashis: the twelve signs of the zodiac</term> are of three types in sequence: Movable, Fixed, and Dual-natured. One should calculate the Fixed Period years as seven, eight, and nine respectively. || 7 || 

<note>Movable signs are Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn (7 years); Fixed are Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius (8 years); Dual are Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces (9 years).</note>

For Aries, it is known to be seven years; for Taurus, it is eight <note>original: "vasu," a poetic term for the number 8</note> years, O twice-born; for Gemini, it is nine years. For Cancer and the others, the order follows accordingly. || 8 || 

This is understood for all twelve signs until the end, O best of the twice-born. The total sum is ninety-six years <note>The sum of 7, 8, and 9 is 24; since there are four sets of these sign types, the total cycle is 24 x 4 = 96</note>. I shall now speak starting from that. || 9 || 

This is the accomplished Fixed Period. Its starting point begins with the sign occupied by the Brahma planet <term>Brahma Graha: a specific planet calculated through a complex formula to represent the creative or life-sustaining force in an individual's chart</term>; from there, the sequence continues as before. || 10 ||

## Now, an Example of the Fixed Period.

In this specific case, Mercury is the Brahma planet. Therefore, Mercury is placed in Capricorn. Its first major period <note>original: "Mahadasha"</note> begins with Capricorn (10), the second is Aquarius (11), and the third is Pisces (12). 

For each sign—Movable, Fixed, or Dual—the years are 7, 8, and 9; this should be understood throughout.

...through agreement. A sign provides strength when associated with its own significator <term>Karaka: a planet that acts as a functional indicator for specific life areas, such as the Sun for the soul or Venus for relationships</term>. || 12 || 

In the case of a union of significators, if the strength is equal, then the planetary unions provide the balance. O best of the twice-born, strength should be declared based on the abundance of planetary unions. || 13 || 

One should consider planetary strength according to the established logic of "planets and so forth." Even then, O Brahmin, if there is equality, one must still provide a definitive judgment. || 14 || 

When the lord of a sign is in its exaltation <term>Tunga: the specific zodiac sign where a planet functions at its highest potential</term>, or in a friend's sign and so on, the strength of that sign is known without a doubt, O best of the twice-born. || 15 || 

Beyond this, there is a special meaning to strength known as Natural <note>original: "Naisargika"</note> strength, as established of old. Therefore, Natural strength should also be grasped, O best of the twice-born. || 16 || 

A sign with a planet is stronger than one without; a sign with more planets is stronger than one with fewer. If these are equal, then the Movable, Fixed, and Dual-natured signs are respectively more powerful in that order <note>In this system, Dual signs (like Gemini) are considered stronger than Fixed signs (like Leo), which are stronger than Movable signs (like Aries)</note>. || 17 || 

Thus, among the Movable, Fixed, and Dual potencies, the Dual sign is the most powerful, O Brahmin. One should contemplate the delayed natural effects after considering this, without a doubt. || 18 || 

O best of the twice-born, one should reflect on the previously mentioned Chapter on Significators <note>Referring to the earlier chapters of the *Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra* which define planetary roles</note>. Because of the union of significators, the sign becomes "alive" <term>Pranavati: literally "possessing breath," meaning the sign becomes potent or active in the horoscope</term>. || 19 || 

When a sign is in a union of significators and is also joined by its own lord <note>original: "Nijanathena"</note>, that sign is considered powerful, O Brahmin, in the opinion of those who study the union of significators. || 20 || 

Whichever sign among the significators is joined by its lord is the powerful one, O twice-born. Within those signs, one should specifically consider the one that is further ahead in degrees. || 21 || 

If many planets are joined in a single sign, O best of the twice-born, that sign is known to be strong through its planetary occupants, especially if it is in its northward path <term>Uttarayan/Agrayana: the period when the sun moves toward the northern solstice, generally considered more auspicious</term>. || 22 || 

One with very few degrees <term>Amshas: the 30 divisions/degrees of a sign</term> is known to have little strength; one with middle degrees has medium power; and one with many degrees is known to be highly powerful, characterized by its ability to influence villages, forests, and so on. || 23 || 

In an odd-numbered sign <term>Oja Rashi: Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, and Aquarius</term>, the strength called "Potency" <note>original: "Prana"</note> is said to be given if planets are situated in the "Veshika" positions—meaning in the front, the back, or the adjacent 2nd and 12th houses. || 24 || 

-> This is the first variety of strength. <-

In whichever sign the lord is present, or if it is aspected <note>original: "Nirikshite," meaning the "glance" or mathematical influence of a planet on a sign</note> by Jupiter <note>original: "Guru"</note> or Mercury <note>original: "Chandri," literally "the son of the Moon"</note>, that sign is said to be powerful in the second type of potency. || 25 || 

The strength of the twelve signs is thus of a second type. By the method just described, this second strength is understood. || 26 || 

-> This is the second variety of potency. <-

The third type of potency regarding the lords has been told by me to you. O best of the twice-born, one should contemplate this in the chart of the Soul-Significator <term>Atmakaraka Kundali: a specialized birth chart calculated by placing the planet with the highest degrees as the primary focus</term>. || 27 || 

It is said that the lord is weak if placed in a "Kendra" or a "Panaphara" house. Specifically, the lord is weak in a Kendra <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses (the "angles")</term>, and has a specific designation in a Panaphara <term>Panaphara: the 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses (the "succedent" houses)</term>. || 28 || 

In an "Apoklima" house, the weakness is doubled. Thus is the third... <term>Apoklima: the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses (the "cadent" houses)</term>.

...one should know that sign to be "animate" <note>original: "Prani." In this context, it refers to a sign or planet possessing astrological vitality or strength.</note>, O son of the twice-born. || 29 || Thus ends the third distinction of potency.

Now I shall speak before you regarding the **fourth animate state**. A sign that is free from association with malefic planets <note>Malefic planets typically include Mars, Saturn, Rahu, and Ketu</note> and is not aspected <note>Drishti: the "glance" or mathematical influence one planet casts upon another sign or planet.</note> by malefics is considered strong. This refers to the smaller time units within a major planetary cycle.</note>, O best of the twice-born. || 31 || Thus ends the fourth distinction.

->**An Example of This**<-

In this case, Mars is the Soul-Significator <term>Atmakaraka: the planet with the highest longitude in a chart, representing the soul’s journey</term>. He is the first potency. The Moon is the fourth potency.

O best of the twice-born, however far the "Door Sign" is from the Ascendant, the "External Sign" <term>Bahyarashi</term> is located that same distance away from it. || 63 || For Movable signs, the path is as stated; for Fixed signs, the path follows the eighth, sixth, and so on. For Dual <term>Dvisvabhava: signs of a dual nature (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces)</term> signs, the "pivots" should be known from the Ascendant, the fifth, and the ninth houses. || 64 ||

In even signs, among all three types, the entire calculation must be taken in reverse. || 65 || The sign thus indicated is remembered as the "Ripening Sign" <term>Pakarashi: literally the 'cooking sign,' representing the sign where the results of a period mature or manifest</term>. In the period known as the "Trine" <term>Trikona: the 1st, 5th, and 9th houses, which are considered highly auspicious</term>, one calculates the enjoyment of the results of malefic planets. || 68 ||

Having observed the conjunction of those two with a malefic planet <term>Papa: literally "sinful" or "malefic," referring to planets like Saturn, Mars, or Rahu</term>, O Brahmin, one should consider the possibility of barrenness and similar results during that malefic planet's time-period <term>Dasha: a planetary cycle or period of time in an individual's life</term>. || 69 || O best of the twice-born, during a malefic combination and a malefic sub-period, bodily pain, mental distress, fear from the government, and great hardship occur. || 70 ||

The results for all of these are exactly as they were proclaimed by Lord Shiva <note>original: "Shambhu"</note>. || 76 ||

One should distinguish between men and women based on the difference between odd and even signs. ## Now, I Shall Describe the Angular and Other Periods

Now, O best of the twice-born <note>original: "dvijottama," a common address for a Brahmin student</note>, I shall describe the variations according to the method of the Angular Period <term>Kendra-dasha: time-periods calculated based on the angular houses: 1, 4, 7, and 10</term>. || 83 ||

If the Ascendant <note>original: "Lagna"</note> or the seventh house falls in a Movable Sign <term>Chara-rashi: the signs Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn</term>, the sequence of the time-periods begins from the stronger of these two signs, following the prescribed path. || 84 ||

Depending on whether the sign is odd or even, the first sequence proceeds in either a direct or inverse order. For the twelve signs, the sequence follows the first, second, and so on, in order. || 85 ||

Following the direct order as stated, without skipping any steps, the periods of the twelve signs are determined through the variations of direct and inverse sequences. || 86 ||

O Brahmin, if the Ascendant or the seventh house falls in a Fixed Sign <term>Sthira-rashi: the signs Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius</term>, the start of the period should be revealed through the "sixth-from-the-sixth" method <note>This refers to a specific astrological calculation where one counts six houses from the house in question</note>. || 87 ||

From the Sun, as previously stated, through the variations of direct and inverse order: the sequence is direct in Taurus and Scorpio, and inverse in Aquarius and Leo. || 88 ||

Separately, O Brahmin, for the third type, the Dual-Sign Period <term>Dvisvabhava-dasha: the signs Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces</term>, one should observe the stronger of the two: the Ascendant or the seventh house. || 89 ||

According to the direction of the four Angles (Kendras), beginning from the Ascendant, the fifth house, and the ninth house (fortune): for the Angles, the sequence starts from the Ascendant; for the Succeedent houses <term>Panaphara: the 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses</term>, it starts from the fifth house. || 90 ||

For the Cadent houses <term>Apoklima: the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses</term>, O best of the twice-born, the sequence of periods begins from the ninth house. In the clear explanation given to Maitreya <note>The disciple of the sage Parashara</note>, each period should be taken as nine years. || 91 ||

## Now, he describes the Significator-based Periods.

The nine planets, starting with the Sun, correspond to the ninth-part divisions <term>Navaṃśas: 1/9th subdivisions of a zodiac sign used for fine-tuning predictions</term> of the life-span. Each period consists of nine years, beginning from the signs located in the angles of the significator <note>original: "karakendrādikā daśā"</note>. O best of the twice-born <note>original: "dvija-sattama," a respectful term for a Brahmin student</note>, one should establish the sequence of these nine-year intervals by calculating from the significator’s angle. ##92–93##

First, the sign situated in an angle <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, which represent the pillars of a person's life</term> is considered, followed by the others in the order of their lords. These signs in the angles each provide nine years. Among those in the angles, the strongest sign provides the first period, followed by the weaker ones. ##94–95##

There are nine years for each sign counting from the sign occupied by the significator. These follow the sequence of:
1. Birth <note>Janma</note>
2. Wealth <note>Sampat</note>
3. Danger <note>Vipat</note>
4. Prosperity <note>Kṣema</note>
5. Obstruction <note>Pratyari</note>
6. Achievement <note>Sādhaka</note>
7. Destruction <note>Vadha</note>
8. Friendship <note>Maitra</note>
9. Great Friendship <note>Atimaitra</note>

One should determine the sub-periods <term>Antardaśā: a minor cycle nested within a major life period</term> for the Sun and other planets based on their positions in the angles. ##96–97##

Looking at the Significator-Ascendant <note>Kāraka-Lagna</note>, one must evaluate the strength of the first and seventh houses. Starting from the stronger of the two, the sequence proceeds in either regular or reverse order. The number of years in the period is determined by the number of signs involved. Thus, the strength is divided according to the angles and other house classifications. ##98–99##

First, consider the planets in the angles, then those in the succedent houses <term>Paṇaphara: the 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses</term>, and finally those in the cadent houses <term>Āpoklima: the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses</term>. O Brahmin, the planets in the angles are the most powerful. The calculation of years for planets in the angles and other houses has been established accordingly. ##200–1##

The duration is measured by the number of signs from the specific planet to the significator. O great sage, in this manner, one can calculate a sequence of up to ninety years. Just as there are years assigned to the significator planet, there are also years assigned to the planets associated with it. O best of the twice-born, these must be calculated. ##2–3##

Thus, the starting point for the Fixed Period <term>Sthira Daśā: a timing system where signs have fixed, rather than variable, durations</term> is shown. The sub-periods of the twelve signs should be calculated in the order of the twelve zodiac signs. If there is an imbalance of strength among the four angles starting from the Ascendant, start the calculation from that sign, assigning one year to each sign in sequence. ##4–5##

O Lord of Brahmins, among the four angles, the one that is odd or possesses the greatest strength acts as the significator for granting the period. Starting from that sub-period through the twelve signs, if one assigns one year to each sign, then all the lords of the periods are clearly established in order. ##6–7##

In this way, the major periods <term>Mahādaśā: the primary time-cycle governing a person's life</term> revolve through the twelve signs, and their sub-periods follow.

One should know the Sun as it wanders through the signs. ##8## Following the same rule for the years of the period known as the Ninth-Part <term>Navamsha: a 1/9th division of a zodiac sign</term>, O best of the twice-born <note>original: "dvija-sattama," a respectful address for a learned student</note>, the starting sign of the nine-year period should be selected. ##9##

In this way, the first period begins with the sign having the greatest strength among the angles <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</term>. For all the remaining weaker signs, one should calculate the years in their proper sequence. ##10##

### Now, an Example of the Angle-based Periods.

Now, among the distinctions of movable signs <term>Chara: Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</term> and others, whichever is stronger between the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign at birth</term> and the seventh house is to be taken first; the same logic applies to the fixed and dual signs. 

In this specific example, between the movable signs of the Ascendant and the seventh house, the seventh is stronger. That sign, Libra, marks the start of the period. Next is Capricorn, then Aries (the 4th), and so on. Following this, from the succedent houses <term>Panaphara: houses 2, 5, 8, and 11, which "follow" the angles</term>, the Scorpio period begins, then Aquarius (the 2nd), etc. Then, from the cadent houses <term>Apoklima: houses 3, 6, 9, and 12</term>, come Sagittarius (the 12th) and Pisces (the 3rd). This method should be understood for all cases. In this instance, the movable sign Libra is the strongest and is therefore chosen; one should know that nine years are assigned to each sign throughout.

### Now, the Calculation of the Significator Planet Periods.

O Brahmin, one should count in either direct or reverse order starting from the Ascendant or the seventh house. The distance to the significator sign <term>Karaka: a planet representing a specific area of life, like the soul or career</term> provides the number of years, matching the values in the diagram. ##11## 

O Brahmin, this describes the Significator Planet Period <note>original: "karakagraha-daśā"</note>; for others, the order is reversed. Depending on whether the signs are odd or even, the count to the significator is performed in direct or reverse order, O best of the twice-born. The numbers are equal... ##12##

->## Now, the Frog-Leap Period (Manduka Dasha) is described.<-

O twice-born <note>original: "dvija"; a term for the student Maitreya, meaning "twice-born" or Brahmin</note>, I shall describe the period known as the **Frog** <term>Manduka: literally "frog," so named because the calculation "leaps" across the zodiac</term>, also called the **Triple-Peak** <term>Trikuta: referring to the triangular or trine relationship between the signs used in this sequence</term>. The years assigned are seven, eight, and nine in sequence; these are known as **Fixed Periods** <term>Sthira Dasha</term>. ## 19 ##

Following the previous methods for **Moveable, Fixed, and Dual** <term>Chara, Sthira, and Dvisvabhava: the three qualities of zodiac signs</term> signs, and having brought forth the years by the numbers seven, eight, and nine, these are the Fixed Periods. ## 20 ##

O best of the twice-born, because this period is formed by a "mountain-peak" of years and because it moves through the **Trines** <term>Trikona: the 1st, 5th, and 9th houses from a starting point</term> of the Moveable, Fixed, and Dual signs, it is called the Triple-Peak. ## 21 ##

Because it proceeds in the sequence mentioned, it is called **Triple-Peak** <note>original: "Trikutaka"</note>. In ancient times, it was called the **Frog** <note>original: "Manduka"</note> as ordained by **Shambhu** <note>original: "shambhu-pranodita"; Shambhu is a name for the god Shiva</note>. ## 22 ##

Just as before, the sequence follows from the **Angles** <term>Kendra: houses 1, 4, 7, 10</term>, then the **Succedent** <term>Panaphara: houses 2, 5, 8, 11</term>, and then the **Cadent** <term>Apoklima: houses 3, 6, 9, 12</term> houses, moving through the groups of five. This is called the sequence of the Trines. ## 23 ##

O best of the twice-born, because it is composed of the Triple-Peak and follows the sequence from the Angles, and because it is composed of the **Oceans** <term>Samudra: a term used here to imply a grouping or a broad calculation</term>, this is the "Gross Triple-Peak" period. ## 24 ##

O Lord of Brahmins, if there is a difference in strength between the **Ascendant** <term>Lagna: the rising sign</term> and the **Seventh House**, the period begins from whichever sign is stronger. ## 25 ##

O Brahmin, for a male horoscope, the period should be known to start from the stronger of the two—the Ascendant or the Seventh—following the sequence mentioned before. ## 26 ##

O Brahmin, for a female horoscope, the period starts from the stronger Seventh house. Having brought this forth according to the previous rules, this has been declared again. ## 27 ##

When **Venus** <term>Shukra</term> and the **Moon** <term>Shashi</term> are strong, the Frog period is known. For a man, it is led from there; if it is a woman, it should be led as a **reflection** <term>Darpanato: literally "from a mirror," implying a reversed or symmetrical calculation</term>. ## 28 ##

The calculation should proceed through the Angles, Succedents, and Cadent houses based on which is strongest, O twice-born. In the first method, the periods are brought forth with nine years for each sign. ## 29 ##

->## Now, an example of the Frog Period is given.<-

In this case, if Aries is the Ascendant, its first period consists of 7 years. After that, the period of **Leo** <note>the 5th sign from Aries</note> would be 8 years. After that, the period of **Sagittarius** <note>the 9th sign from Aries</note> would be 9 years. Next, the sequence proceeds from **Taurus** <note>the 2nd sign</note>, then **Virgo** <note>the 6th</note>, and **Capricorn** <note>the 10th</note>. One should understand the subsequent steps in this same way. Because it moves by "leaping and falling" like a frog through the sequence of Angles and so on, it is known by the name **Frog Period** <note>Manduka-samjna</note>. This is how it should be understood!!

# Now, the Spear Period (Shula Dasha) is described.

The **Spear Period** <term>Shula Dasha: "Shula" means a spear or a sharp pain, specifically used in astrology to calculate the time of death</term> should be explained; its results are determined from the **Sign of Departure** <term>Niryana Rashi: the zodiac sign indicating death or the end of the journey</term>. O Brahmin, the indication is given from the seventh sign by means of the Spear calculation alone. ## 230 ##

Starting from the **Nakshatra of the Great Lord** <note>original: "Maheshvaraksha"; referring to the star Ardra, which is ruled by Rudra/Shiva</note>, the Spear-sign serves as the place of death. The Spear sign should be grasped through its relative strength, O best of the twice-born, to determine the time of death. ## 31 ## <note>The verse numbering in the original manuscript jumps from 230 to 31.</note>

There are many kinds of periods, O Brahmin, always consisting of seven, eight, and nine years. Among these, O most wise one, the Spear Period should be taken to certain the time of departure. ## 32 ##

Beginning from the ripening of the full lifespan, if the sign is **Odd** <note>original: "vishame"; refers to Aries, Gemini, Leo, etc.</note>, O twice-born, the progression is known to begin from the **Ascendant** <term>Lagna</term>, following the sequence of seven, eight, and nine years. ## 33 ##

If the sign is **Even** <note>original: "same"; refers to Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, etc.</note>, O Brahmin, it begins from the seventh house, using years of seven (7), eight (8), and nine (9). Having started the period, this sequence should be grasped without any doubt. ## 234 ##

# Now, an example of the Spear Period (Shula Dasha) is given.

In this regard, the sage **Bhrigu** <note>original: "bhṛgu"; can refer to the planet Venus or the sage Bhrigu</note> says: The period known as **Rudra-Shula** <term>The "Spear of Rudra," a specific variation of this time-cycle</term> commences from the seventh sign from the Sign of Death. In the case of Bhrigu <note>here referring to the position of Venus in the chart</note>, the seventh sign is **Virgo** <term>Kanya Rashi</term>; therefore, it should be understood that the sequence begins starting from the sign of Virgo.

## Now, the description of Asterismal Periods (Nakshatra Dasha).

> O highly wise one, the lifespan based on the stars <term>Nakshatra: the 27 lunar mansions or constellations that form the basis of the Hindu lunar calendar</term> was fully spoken of by me earlier. The **120-year cycle** <term>Vimshottari: the most popular period system where a human life is calculated as 120 years</term> is of five types, and the **108-year cycle** <term>Ashtottari: an alternative period system used when specific conditions are met in a birth chart</term> is considered to be of two types. || 35 ||
