## Now, the description of the Combined-Half Period (Yogardha Dasha).

> O Brahmin, whatever combination <term>Yoga: here meaning the sum or addition of two values</term> arises from the **Movable** <term>Chara: periods based on movable zodiac signs</term> and **Fixed** <term>Sthira: periods based on fixed zodiac signs</term> periods, half of that total is known as the **Combined-Half** <note>original: "Yogardha"</note> period. || 37 ||
>
> One should consider the relative strength between the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of birth</term> and the seventh house. If the Ascendant is stronger, the start of the periods should be revealed from the Ascendant. || 38 ||
>
> If the seventh house is more powerful, then the start of the periods should be calculated from there. I shall now speak of the horoscopes of men and women, based on the difference of direct and reverse orders. || 39 ||
>
> The periods for the Moon and Venus should be derived for the stronger sign. If it is a woman's chart, it should be calculated through the **Mirror Method** <note>original: "darpanato"; this refers to a reflective or symmetrical calculation technique</note>, and for a man, it should be calculated accordingly. || 40 ||

## Now, an example of the Combined-Half Period (Yogardha Dasha).

In the Combined-Half period, one must take the average <note>literally "half of the sum"</note> of the years assigned to a sign in the **Movable Period** and the years assigned in the **Fixed Period**. That result is the Combined-Half period.

For example: In the Movable Period for **Aries**, the duration is 11 years. In the Fixed Period for the same sign, the duration is 7 years. The sum of both is 18. Half of this is 9. In this manner, the values for all signs should be understood.

# Now, he describes the Period of Aspects (Drig Dasha).

This period is known to begin from Mars <note>original: "Kuja"</note> or from the ninth house of the Ascendant. It follows a triple order called the "Peak Position" <term>Kutapada: a specific technical point in calculation used to determine the sequence of signs</term>, O Twice-born Sage. || 41 ||

In the aspect chart <term>Drishti-chakra: a diagram mapping which zodiac signs 'see' or influence one another</term>, it is in front and from the beginning of the ninth sign. In some cases, this follows a direct order <note>original: "krama"</note> and in some cases, a reverse order <note>original: "vyatkrama"</note>. || 42 ||

Then, it also proceeds from the fifth sign in a direct order in some places, O Brahmin, and in other places, in a reverse order, facing the eleventh sign. || 43 ||

Its absence should not be taken as a standard proof, O best of the Twice-born. One should specifically take it from the fifth house in the aspect chart. || 44 ||

The signs "look at" <note>original: "abhipashyanti"</note> the adjacent signs, O best of the Twice-born. According to the method previously mentioned, that is called the "Triple Peak Position." || 45 ||

The Peak Position consists of three signs; then, it is also known for the tenth sign. The Drig Dasha is known to be in the eleventh, and the Drig Dasha of the ninth as well. || 46 ||

For the purpose of predicting results, O Brahmin, the Drig Dasha should also be gathered from the eleventh. I will explain its method to you again in detail. || 47 ||

Now, the order of calculation is stated according to the distinction between odd and even signs. The general rule should be understood for even signs based on the nature of the "Mother" <note>original: "Matri-dharma," likely referring to the feminine or even nature of certain signs</note>. || 48 ||

In the calculation, the general rule applies to the fifth and eleventh houses, O Brahmin. This is to be known as "sometimes" within the context of the three general Peak Positions. || 49 ||

Now, for the odd positions <note>original: "oja-pada"</note>, O Sage, the calculation should be understood in reverse. In even signs and even positions, the general logic applies. || 50 ||

The order in Taurus and Scorpio is stated as—

<header>Section One: Chapter 35 on the Description of Various Period Divisions</header>

...O best of the twice-born! <note>original: "dvijottama"</note> Here also, for signs belonging to an odd-footed group <term>Ojakuta: signs like Aries or Gemini that are classified as "odd" or "male" in certain calculations</term>, the aspect-union <term>Drig-yoga: a connection formed between signs through their visual aspect</term> occurs from the fifth and eleventh houses in direct order. || 51 ||

O Sage, this Aspect Period <note>original: "Drig Dasha"</note> bestows strength. For those in the even-footed group <term>Yugmakuta: signs like Taurus or Cancer classified as "even" or "female"</term>, the rule is general, except for Leo and Aquarius where it is applied in reverse. || 52 ||

O Sage, the fifth and eleventh houses are similarly considered aspect-unions. For the dual signs <term>Dvisvabhava: the "double-natured" signs—Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces</term>, when situated in the fifth and eleventh houses, || 53 ||

one should contemplate the absence of an aspect-union in the aspect-chart. In whatever house an aspect occurs, the effects regarding its dependencies and other factors should be understood. || 54 ||

O leader of mathematicians, the calculation should be known after the lord of the ninth house. Then, the seventh house should be understood, following the trine <note>original: "trikona"</note> starting from the ninth. || 55 ||

The sign is twofold in the Aspect Period; the two adjacent signs <note>original: "parshva-rashi"</note> constitute the period. For a dual-natured male sign, it is known in its direct order. || 56 ||

For a dual-natured female sign, O best of the twice-born, it is in reverse order. The fourth and tenth houses should be taken as the adjacent signs; of this there is no doubt. || 57 ||

Just as with the order of movable signs <term>Chararashi: Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn</term>, whether established in direct or reverse order, O Sage, the fifth and eleventh houses also form an aspect-union. || 58 ||

O Great Wise One, one should calculate the period of the adjacent sign in direct or reverse order. For dual signs, starting from the ninth, the seventh is to be known. || 59 ||

The designation "Odd" <note>original: "Oja"</note> for dual signs follows the sequence of the fourth and tenth <note>original: "vyomake," literally 'of the sky'</note> houses. For "Even" <note>original: "Sama"</note> signs, it is known in reverse, taking the tenth and then the fourth houses. || 60 ||

For each of the twelve zodiac signs, the duration is nine years each. The results of these Aspect Periods should be gathered according to the methods described previously. || 261 || <note>The verse numbering jumps significantly here, likely indicating a total count for the subsection or a manuscript error.</note>

# Now, he explains an example of the Aspect Period (Drig Dasha).

It is said that the Aspect Period follows the order of the "Triple-Peak Position" <term>Trikuta-pada: a technical grouping of signs in sets of three</term> starting from Mars <note>original: "Kuja"</note> or the ninth house from the Ascendant. First, calculation starts from the ninth, then to the facing sign in the aspect-chart. Then, in some places by direct order and in others by reverse order, it proceeds to the fifth; then again, by direct or reverse order, to the eleventh facing sign. 

There is a question as to why the fifth is not mentioned first if there is a lack of evidence: in the matter of aspects, one first looks at what is directly in front <note>the opposite sign</note>, then at the adjacent signs. This is the "Triple-Peak Position," a step consisting of three signs. From there, the Aspect Periods of the tenth and eleventh houses occur. The result is: the Ninth-Aspect Period, the Tenth-Aspect Period, and the Eleventh-Aspect Period. The calculation for the fifth and eleventh houses is part of general science, but should be known as reversed for "odd-footed" signs. For "even-footed" signs...

<header>Essence of the Great Compendium of Parashara’s Astrology</header>

This must be understood as a departure from the general rule. Similarly, in the case of Scorpio, because Taurus and Scorpio are situated in the odd-footed group <term>Ojakuta: a technical classification in this system where certain signs are grouped as "odd" or "male" to determine the direction of counting</term>, the fifth and eleventh houses in reverse order are considered fit for the aspect-union <note>original: "drig-yogya"</note>. 

Because Leo and Aquarius are situated in the even-footed group <term>Yugmakuta: signs classified as "even" or "female" in this specific calculation</term>, then according to the general rule, the fifth and eleventh houses in reverse order are the aspect-unions. In the dual signs <term>Dvisvabhava: the double-natured signs of Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces</term>, there is an absence of the fifth and eleventh houses for aspect-unions. 

In the aspect-chart <note>original: "drishti-cakre"</note>, wherever an aspect exists, the sequence of the first nine signs <note>original: "navama-rashi"</note> follows this order: if it is a male sign and dual-natured, then the sequence is direct; if it is an odd sign, then the fourth and tenth houses should be taken in reverse order. The essence is this: for movable signs <term>Chara: Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn</term>, the fifth and eleventh houses in direct order are the aspect-unions. For fixed signs <term>Sthira: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius</term>, the fifth and eleventh in reverse order are the aspect-unions. The sequence for the periods of adjacent signs <note>original: "parshva-rashi"</note> should be known in the same way. 

For dual signs, one first considers the ninth, then the seventh. If it is an odd dual sign, the sequence follows the fourth and then the seventh in direct order; otherwise, it follows the fourth and then the tenth in reverse order. Here, nine years are to be taken for each period. To illustrate this:

For an Aries Ascendant, which is a movable sign, the sequence is first Aries, then Leo, then Aquarius—thus 1, 5, 11. Among the fixed signs, for example Leo, the sequence is Leo, then Aries, then Libra—thus 5, 1, 7. For dual signs, such as the male sign Gemini, the sequence is Gemini, then Virgo, then Pisces—thus 3, 6, 12. For the reverse order of female dual signs, the sequence is Pisces, Sagittarius, and Gemini <note>original: "mina-dhana-mithunah"</note>. Thus it should be understood everywhere that there are nine years per sign.

## Now, the Trine Period is explained.

The period known as the **Trine Period** <term>Trikona Dasha: a timing system based on the three signs forming a triangle—the 1st, 5th, and 9th houses</term> is determined according to the proper rules. A sign is considered equal to its ninth-part <term>Navamsha: a one-ninth division of a zodiac sign</term>, and each period lasts for a duration of nine years. **62**

This is demonstrated by the logic mentioned in the verses regarding the **Movable Sequence** <term>Charaparyaya: a method where the sequence of planetary periods follows the movement of signs</term> and others. Between the two signs in trine to the **Ascendant** <term>Lagna: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term>, a wise person should determine which is stronger based on the previously stated reasons. When those are exhausted, the periods should be calculated like the Movable Sequence. **63**

For men born in **even signs** <term>Yugma Rashi: Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricorn, and Pisces</term>, one should take the opposite sign as the starting point. For women born in **odd signs** <term>Oja Rashi: Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, and Aquarius</term>, one should rely on the even signs. **64**

One should count in direct or reverse order for odd and even signs respectively. In this way, one should project the completed **Movable Sequence Period**. **65**

Furthermore, one should contemplate the results through the "Gate" and the "Outside" <term>Dvara and Bahya: technical points in a sign-period used to judge whether the timing brings internal or external results</term>. Oh Priest <note>original: "Vipra," an address to the student Maitreya</note>, the two-fold maturation and enjoyment <note>original: "Pakabhoga"</note> provide happiness or misery depending on the association with **malefic planets**. **66**

Oh Twice-born one, this system follows the **Movable Sequence** and **Fixed Sequence**. In this Trine Period, the "Malefic Enjoyment" must be calculated. **67**

During a **Malefic Enjoyment** and in a malefic year, there is pain in the body and mental agony. The person suffers from fear of the King <note>meaning the government or authorities</note>, anxiety, and is tormented by great illnesses. **68**

Now, I shall describe the results of the **Significators** <term>Karakas: planets or houses that "signify" or represent specific areas of life like father, health, or spouse</term>, oh Twice-born one. The seventh, the third, the first, and also the ninth houses should be considered. **69**

A small amount should be known from the ninth, through which one should contemplate the happiness of the father. From the first house, oh Twice-born one, one should think of bodily health and prosperity. **70**

## Now, an illustration of the Trine Period is provided.

The **Trine Period** begins from whichever sign is the strongest among the **Ascendant** (1st), the fifth, and the ninth houses. Starting from that initial sign, the periods of the twelve signs are known through direct or reverse order. Here, if the start is from **Aries**, the sequence is Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius; then Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn. This is how it should be understood everywhere. The years of the periods shall be like those of the **Movable Sequence**.

## Now, the sequence of Sign Periods based on Constellations is stated.

> In the Moon’s constellation at the beginning of birth, throughout the total sum of minutes <term>Ghatika: a traditional unit of time equal to 24 minutes</term>, a portion is divided by the Sun <note>original: bhānunā dīyate bhāgaṃ; here "Sun" refers to the number 12, representing the twelve solar signs</note>, and the remaining minutes should be determined. **71** Starting from the first segment up to the twelfth segment, O Brahmin <note>original: dvija; a term of address for a learned person</note>, the twelve signs from the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term> should be counted in sequence. **72** Whichever minute-segment the birth falls into, that is the starting segment. From that starting point, the counting begins from the Ascendant at birth, O Brahmin. **73** Starting from the lord of the twelfth sign from the Ascendant, O best of Brahmins, the period of the twelve signs <note>original: dvādaśarkṣadaśā; literally 'twelve-constellation period' but applied here to signs</note> is recognized through the distinction of direct and reverse order. **74**

### Example of the Constellation Period.

Whichever constellation the Moon occupies on the day of birth, its total duration (according to the standard duration of all constellations) should be divided into twelve parts. Starting from the first segment through the twelve segments, the twelve signs starting from the Ascendant are to be counted in sequence. The specific segment of minutes in which the birth occurs is the starting point for the calculation. Beginning from the sign associated with that segment, the periods <term>Dasha: a planetary or sign-based time cycle in Vedic astrology</term> of the twelve signs are derived using either the direct or reverse sequence. For each sign, a period of nine years should be taken.

For example: The birth constellation is **Purvashadha** <term>Purvashadha: the 20th of the 27 lunar mansions, located in the sign of Sagittarius</term>. Its total duration is 67 <term>Ghatikas</term> and 48 minutes. When divided by twelve, the quotient is 5 with a remainder of 7 and 48. Counting from Aries, this falls into the sign of **Sagittarius** <term>Dhanurashi: the zodiac sign of Sagittarius</term>. Therefore, the calculation should be initiated from Sagittarius; this method should be understood and applied in all instances.

# Now, the Social Order Period (Varnada Dasha) is described.

The numerical values of the birth Ascendant <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term> and the Hourly Ascendant <term>Hora Lagna: a mathematical point used to determine wealth and social status</term> should be taken separately. If the Ascendant is an odd sign, count normally; if it is an even sign, the number is subtracted from the full cycle of twelve. **76**

If both signs are either odd or even, their values should be added together; otherwise, they should be subtracted from one another. In an odd sign, the count proceeds clockwise from Aries; in an even sign, it proceeds counter-clockwise from Pisces. **77**

The sign arrived at through this calculation is proclaimed as the "Social-Giver" <note>original: "Varnada"; from 'Varna' (social order/color) and 'da' (giver)</note>. In this same manner, the Social-Giver sign should be calculated for all twelve houses of the horoscope. **78**

One should bring forth the Social-Giver signs for the twelve houses. These periods do not apply to the planets, but rather to the signs themselves. **79**

The number of years for each period should be understood according to the measurements of the Sign Movement system <term>Chara Paryaya: a method where the duration of a period depends on the distance between a sign and its ruler</term>. **80**

## Example of the Social Order Period (Varnada Dasha)

In this instance, birth occurred within Aries, which is an odd sign; therefore, the count follows the clockwise order starting from Aries. The Hourly Ascendant <note>Hora Lagna</note> is Taurus; because it is an even sign, the count follows the counter-clockwise path starting from Pisces, resulting in a value of 11. The sum of these two is 11. Counting from Aries in the clockwise direction, the 11th sign is Aquarius, which is to be known as the Social-Giver <note>Varnada</note> sign for this case.

<meta>This page continues the technical exposition of astrological periods (Dashas). Having finished the Varnada Dasha, the text now transitions into the "Five-Vowel Period" (Pancha-svara Dasha), a system where the vowels in a person's name determine their life's timing and cosmic correspondences.</meta>

<page-num>253</page-num>
<header>First Section: Chapter 35 on the Explanation of Various Period Divisions</header>

The consonants should be arranged in horizontal rows, divided into five groups of five sounds each. **82**

It is taught that the nasal sounds <note>original: "ṅa, ña, ṇa"</note> are not used at the beginning of names. Therefore, if they should occur, they are to be replaced by the sounds G, J, and D respectively. **83**

If a name contains conjunct consonants <term>Samyukta-akshara: two or more consonants joined without a vowel between them</term>, only the first consonant of the cluster should be considered; so it was declared by the creator Brahma in ancient times. **84**

The five primary vowels, beginning with 'A' <note>A, I, U, E, O</note>, correspond to the five deities beginning with Brahma. They also represent the five stages of spiritual release <term>Kalas: specifically Nivritti (retirement), Pratishtha (foundation), Vidya (knowledge), Shanti (peace), and Shantyatita (beyond peace)</term>, and the fivefold powers of the soul, such as Will <note>Iccha-shakti</note>. **85**

They also represent the different levels of the energy centers <note>Chakras</note>, beginning with the "Illusory" <note>Maya</note>, the five elements beginning with Earth, and the five objects of the senses <note>sound, touch, sight, taste, smell</note>. Because of this, these vowels are called the "Arrows of Love" <term>Kama-bana: the five arrows of the deity Kama, used here to show how vowels trigger desire and action</term>. **86**

The "rising" or beginning of these vowel-periods occurs in the order of their sequence. Each vowel governs a span of twelve years. **87**

Within these twelve-year cycles, the sub-periods are calculated as follows: a sub-period lasts one year, one month, two days, and a duration of time measured as thirty-eight <term>Palas: a traditional unit of time; 60 palas make one ghatika (24 minutes)</term> and four <term>Nadikas: also known as ghatikas</term>. **88**

These divisions, from the twelve-year cycle down to the minute <note>Nadika</note>, are determined by the vowel’s own position and its own timing. At the end of a vowel's "rise," the eleven sub-divisions occur once more. **89**

The specific vowel that is active is found where the first letter of the native's name is located. This vowel governs different states of being, such as Birth, Work, Conception, the Physical Body, and "The Vulnerable Point" <note>Chhidra: a sensitive or weak point in the horoscope</note>. **90**

From that initial sound, one should recognize the phonetic class; from that class, the month is determined. This period is known to last for two months and twelve additional days. **91**

In this way, one should sequentially understand the sounds and their five divisions. There are also nine-day periods related to various administrative and personal functions. **92**

According to traditional lineage <note>Sampradaya</note>, the months of Margashirsha and Pausha <note>roughly November–January</note> are divided into three-day increments at the beginning of the lunar year. **93**

The lunar days <term>Tithis</term> begin with the first day of the bright fortnight <note>Pratipat</note>, and the determination of the weekdays begins with Mars <note>Kuja</note>. These follow the categories of "Joyous" <note>Nanda</note>, "Fortunate" <note>Bhadra</note>, "Victorious" <note>Jaya</note>, "Empty" <note>Rikta</note>, and "Full" <note>Purna</note> in their proper order. **94**

Numerical values should be assigned in order, and the sums of these numbers should be taken. For the vowel **'A'**, the value is eighteen <note>original: "Chandra-ashta," literally Moon (1) and Eight (8)</note>. For the vowel **'I'**, the value is eighty-eight <note>original: "Naga-kunjara," both meaning eight</note>. **95**

For the vowel **'U'**, the value is thirty-nine <note>original: "Rama-rankani"</note>. For the vowel **'E'**, the value is nineteen <note>original: "Chandra-khechara"</note>. For the vowel **'O'**, the value of fifteen determines the resulting combination of circumstances. **96**

The zodiac signs associated with the vowels are as follows:
- **'A'**: Cancer, Leo, and Aries.
- **'I'**: Scorpio <note>identified here by a technical variant "Jhenduraya"</note>.
- **'U'**: Sagittarius and Pisces.
- **'E'**: Libra and Taurus. **97**

Finally, for the vowel **'O'**, the signs are Capricorn and Aquarius. These vowels are produced from the Lords of the Signs. Beneath each vowel, one should place the planets that rule over those respective signs. **98**

<summary>This page outlines the Panchasvara Dasha system, which links the five primary vowels of a person's name to 12-year life cycles, specific deities, elements, and zodiac signs to predict timing and destiny.</summary>

## Now, an example of the Five-Vowel Period is given.

In this specific case, the birth occurred within the "I" vowel group. Therefore, within the major period of the vowel "I," the sub-periods follow this sequence: first the "U" vowel, then the "E" vowel, then the "O" vowel, and finally the "A" vowel. This pattern of progression should be understood to apply in all cases.

## Now, the Yogini Periods are described.

The eight "Yoginis" <term>Yogini: specific feminine energies or deities that govern certain periods of a person's life</term> are known as: **Mangala**, **Pingala**, **Dhanya**, **Bhramari**, **Bhadrika**, **Ulka**, **Siddha**, and **Sankata**. **299**

The Sun is associated with **Pingala**, and the Moon <note>original: "Nishakara"</note> with **Mangala**. Mars <note>original: "Bhauma"</note> is associated with **Bhramari**, and Mercury <note>original: "Budha"</note> with **Bhadrika**. **300**

The planet Jupiter <note>original: "Guru"</note> is the source of prosperity for **Dhanya**, while Venus <note>original: "Kavi"</note> arises from **Siddha**. Saturn <note>original: "Bhanutanaya," literally "son of the Sun"</note> comes from **Ulka**, and the shadow planet Rahu <note>original: "Tamas," meaning "darkness"</note> comes from **Sankata**. **1** <note>Verse numbering resets or follows a different manuscript tradition here.</note>

Take the number of the birth star <term>Nakshatra: one of the 27 lunar mansions</term>, add three <note>original: "pinakina-nayana," referring to the three eyes of Shiva</note> to it, and divide the sum by eight <note>original: "Vasubhih," referring to the eight Vasu deities</note>. **2**

The remainder indicates the specific Yogini; if the remainder is zero, it is known as **Sankata**. **2**

The duration of these periods in years, starting with **Mangala**, increases by one year for each successive Yogini <note>Mangala is 1 year, Pingala is 2, etc., up to Sankata which is 8</note>. For the first period, one should multiply the years by six <note>original: "rasaih"</note> to find the subdivisions. **3**

By multiplying the elapsed time of the current lunar mansion in "nadis" <term>Nadi: a unit of time equal to 24 minutes</term> and performing the calculation, the precise remaining duration of the period can be determined with certainty. **4**

## Now, an Example of the Yogini Period.

In this specific calculation, the birth constellation <term>Nakshatra: one of the 27 lunar mansions</term> is **Purva Ashadha**. Its numerical position is 20. Adding 3 to this number results in 23. Dividing this by 8 <note>original: "vasubhi," referring to the eight Vasus, a group of deities representing the number 8</note>, we get a quotient of 2 and a remainder of 7. This indicates that the person was born during the **Siddha** period.

Next, similar to the calculation used in the **Vimshottari** system <term>Vimshottari: the standard 120-year planetary cycle used in Hindu astrology</term>, the "elapsed" and "remaining" portions of the period are determined. In the previous life, the elapsed time was 6 years, 4 months, 18 days, 20 ghati <note>a ghati is approximately 24 minutes</note>, and 42 pala <note>a pala is approximately 24 seconds</note>. In this current birth, the remaining time to be experienced is 0 years, 7 months, 11 days, 39 ghati, and 18 pala. This method of calculation should be understood to apply in all such cases.

## Now, the Example of the Sandhya (Twilight) Period is Described.

The maximum lifespan is divided into ten parts <note>original: "paramāyuḥ dashamāṃshaḥ"</note>. In this specific example, the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagnadhipati: the planet that rules the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> is Mars <term>Bhauma: another name for the planet Mars</term>. Therefore, his is the first period. The subsequent periods should be understood to follow in the order starting with Mercury <term>Budha: the planet Mercury</term>, and so on.

## Now, the Pachaka (Digestive) Period is Described.

The Sandhya value should be multiplied by six <note>original: "rasa-guṇā," where "rasa" (tastes) represents the number 6</note> and the result divided by thirty-one <note>original: "chandra-vahni"; in the Sanskrit numerical system, "chandra" (moon) is 1 and "vahni" (fire) is 3, which together represent 31</note>. Place this result in the first cell <term>Koshtha: a division or square in an astrological table</term>. || 7 || Place half of that amount in each of the [next] three cells. With great care, write one-third of the initial value in the [remaining] eight <note>original: "vasu," referring to the eight Vasu deities</note> cells. || 8 || In this manner, one should calculate the "Pachakas" (sub-dividers) for the twelve astrological houses.

## Now, an Example of the Pachaka Period.

The Sandhya period value is multiplied by six, resulting in 72. This is then divided by thirty-one. The quotient obtained—1 year, 11 months, 6 days, 46 ghati <note>a ghati is 24 minutes</note>, and 27 pala <note>a pala is 24 seconds</note>—is placed in the first cell. Again, half of this value—0 years, 11 months, 18 days, 23 ghati, and 13 pala—is placed in the [next] three cells. Then, one-third of the initial result—0 years, 7 months, 11 days, 16 ghati, 0 pala, and 27 vipala—is placed in the eight cells. This method should be understood to apply throughout the calculation.

One should understand the results in these time-periods by discerning the strength and weakness of the planets. The opposite result should always be declared if the planet is in retrograde <term>Vakragati: the apparent backward motion of a planet as seen from Earth, which is thought to alter its influence</term>. || 9 || If a planet is situated in the first decanate <term>Drekkana: a 10-degree division of a 30-degree zodiac sign</term>, it gives its results at the beginning of its period. If situated in the middle decanate, the result should be spoken of as occurring in the middle of the period. || 310 || If the planet is in the third decanate, the result occurs at the end. However, this timing is reversed when the planet is retrograde. # Parashara Said:

> Having bowed to the Sun <term>Martanda: a name for the Sun, signifying the "bird of the sky"</term>, the Lord of all worlds, the auspicious Shiva, the Bringer of Welfare, who resides in the hearts of all, the Lord of all creatures <note>original: "Pashupati"</note>, the Radiant One, and the husband of the Goddess Bhavani; and to Vishnu <note>original: "Hari"</note>, who performs the dissolution, creation, and maintenance of the worlds and is the Lord of the three realms—by the grace of the Great Lord, I shall now speak of the auspicious "Illumination of Time-periods" <note>original: "dayaprakāsham"</note>. || 1 ||

### Now, the Fivefold Internal Divisions of the Vimshottari System are Described.

Now I shall speak of the five levels of sub-periods for the lords of the planets. These are the major period <term>Dasha</term> and the sub-period <term>Antardasha</term>...

...and their sub-periods <term>Antardasha: the second level of time-division in planetary periods</term> as well. ॥ 2 ॥ The sub-sub-periods <term>Sukshma-bhukti</term> and the breath-periods <term>Prana-dasha</term>—these are known as the five types of time-periods <term>Dashas</term>. ॥ 3 ॥ The Sun, Moon, Mars, Rahu, Jupiter, Saturn, Mercury, Ketu, and finally Venus—in this order—[their years are] six, ten, seven, eighteen, sixteen, nineteen, seventeen, seven, and twenty. These are known as the lords of the nine-fold groups of the twenty-seven constellations <term>Nakshatras</term>, starting with Krittika <note>The Vimshottari cycle traditionally begins its calculation from the constellation Krittika, though the list of constellations starts with Ashvini.</note> and the others, beginning with the Sun. ॥ 4 ॥

->Now, the calculation of the elapsed and remaining portions [of a period] is explained.<-

Divide the clear position of the Moon <term>Himagu: literally 'the cold-rayed one', a name for the Moon</term>, converted into minutes of arc <term>Kalika</term>, by eight hundred <note>original: "khakhagajair" — a numerical code where 'kh' (space) is 0 and 'gaja' (elephant) is 8, read right-to-left as 800</note> to find the constellation <term>Nakshatra</term> currently occupied. Multiply the remainder by the years assigned to that constellation's planetary lord, and divide that result by eight hundred to find the elapsed years and other units. ॥ 5 ॥

->An example of this is provided.<-

Regarding the "clear position": Suppose the clear position of the Moon is 1 Sign, 8 Degrees, 56 Minutes, and 7 Seconds (1s 8° 56' 7"). This total equals 2296 Minutes and 7 Seconds. Dividing this by 800 yields a quotient of 2. This indicates that the "passed" constellation is Bharani <note>A quotient of 2 means the Moon has fully traversed the 1st (Ashvini) and 2nd (Bharani) constellations and is now in the 3rd, Krittika.</note>. Furthermore, to find the current major period, take the quotient (2), subtract 1, and the remainder determines the planet in the sequence. Here, the quotient 2 minus 1 leaves 1. Following the sequence: 1. Sun, 2. Moon, 3. Mars, 4. Rahu, 5. Jupiter, 6. Saturn, 7. Mercury, 8. Ketu, 9. Venus. Thus, the Sun's major period <term>Suryadasha</term> is active at birth. Now, to calculate the elapsed and remaining portions of this period: take the remainder of 696' 7" and multiply it by the years assigned to the lord of the birth constellation <term>Janma Nakshatra</term>. The years of the planet presiding over that constellation are used for the multiplication. In this case, it is the Sun's major period...

6 [the Sun's years] multiplied by that [the remaining portion of the constellation] results in 4170. 42 divided by eight hundred (800) yields 5 years, with a remainder of 170. 42 multiplied by twelve [to find months] results in 2048. 24 divided by eight hundred yields 2 months, with a remainder of 448. 24 multiplied by thirty [to find days] results in 13452. 0 divided by eight hundred yields 16 days etc., with a remainder of 652. 0 multiplied by sixty [to find ghatikas] results in 39120. 0 divided by eight hundred yields 48 ghatikas <term>Ghatika: a traditional unit of time equal to 24 minutes</term>, with a remainder of 720. 0 multiplied by sixty [to find palas] results in 43200. 0 divided by eight hundred yields 54 palas <term>Pala: a traditional unit of time equal to 24 seconds</term>, with a remainder of 0. When completed, the calculated figures are truly 5 [years] | 2 [months] | 16 [days] | 48 [ghatikas] | 54 [palas] as the years etc. At the time of birth, the portion of the period already experienced in the previous life is subtracted from the total of 6 years; the remainder 0 | 9 | 13 | 11 | 6 is the period to be enjoyed <term>Bhogya-dasha: the remaining time of a planetary period left to be experienced at the moment of birth</term> in this life. This calculation should be understood in this manner everywhere. ॥

### Now, the 6-year Major Period of the Sun and its Results.

An excellent major period of the Sun <note>original: "Suryottkrista-dasha"</note> produces an increase in children, intelligence, wisdom, and authority; it brings the acquisition of knowledge and wealth, fame, courage, happiness, and the grace of the Lord or the King. ॥ The malefic period of the Sun <note>original: "Bhanoḥ papa-dasha"</note> produces failed efforts, loss of wealth, diseases, royal displeasure, the anger of the monarch, and obstacles caused by fire and other calamities. ॥ 6 ॥ If the Sun is in its sign of root-trinity <term>Moolatrikona: a specific sign position where a planet is highly potent, second only to exaltation</term>, its own sign, its exaltation <note>original: "Swoccha"</note>, or its highest point of exaltation; if it is placed in the angles, trines, or the house of gains <note>original: "Kendra-trikona-labhastha"; the 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th, 5th, 9th, or 11th houses</note>, or conjunct with the lords of the 9th or 10th houses; or if the Sun is possessed of strength and occupies its own auspicious divisions <note>original: "Varga"</note>; then during that major period, there will be great happiness, gain of wealth, and other auspicious things. ॥ 7 ॥ One receives great honor from the King and auspicious things such as horses and palanquins <note>original: "Ashvandolyadikam"; symbols of high social status and luxury</note>. If conjunct with the lord of the 5th house, the person obtains a son. ॥ 8 ॥ In connection with the lord of the 2nd house, one should predict wealth as vast as an owner of elephants <note>original: "Gajantaisvarya"</note>. In connection with the lord of the 4th house, it brings the acquisition of three types of vehicles. ॥ 9 ॥ The person becomes a wealthy commander of an army, happy, and favored by the ruler. There is gain of clothing and vehicles during the period of a strong Sun. ॥ 10 ॥ If the Sun is in debilitation <note>original: "Neecha"</note>, or in the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses, or is weak and conjunct with malefic planets; or if it is conjunct with Rahu or Ketu <note>the North and South lunar nodes</term>, or conjunct with the lords of the "bad houses" <note>original: "Dusthana-adhipati"</note>; ॥ 11 ॥ then during that period, there is great suffering and the destruction of wealth and grains. There is royal anger, living abroad, punishment by the king, and loss of wealth. ॥ 12 ॥ Feverish ailments, loss of reputation, and conflict with relatives and friends will occur. There will be foreign travel, disease, hatred, and a fear of untimely death <note>original: "Apamrityu-bhayam"</note>. ॥ 13 ॥ There is also fear of thieves, snakes, and wounds.

...suffering from fever will occur. There will be fear regarding the loss of the father and inauspiciousness within the home. ॥ 14 ॥

One experiences mental distress within the paternal family and hatred from other people. However, if the Sun is aspected <note>aspected: in astrology, this refers to a "glance" or mathematical relationship between planets that influences their effects</note> by a benefic planet, there may be some happiness in the middle of this period. If the Sun is aspected by a malefic planet, the person should predict sinful or harmful results. ॥ 15 ॥

### Now, the 10-year Major Period of the Moon and its Results.

An excellent major period of the Moon <note>original: "Chandrotkrishta-dasha"</note> produces welfare for the mother, the construction of water tanks or ponds, and the acquisition of lands, gardens, houses, and fine seating. It brings the favor of excellent Brahmanas <note>Brahmanas: the priestly or scholarly class in traditional Indian society</note>, wealth, beauty, and the luxury of palanquins. Conversely, a Moon in a "malefic" or difficult state <note>original: "Indoh papadasha"</note> brings a lack of food, wretchedness, the loss of vast wealth, disease, a loss of intelligence, feelings of disgust, the death of the mother, agitation, and fevers accompanied by extreme chills. ॥ 16 ॥

If the Moon is in its sign of exaltation <note>exaltation: the zodiac sign where a planet is at its most powerful</note>, in its own sign, or placed in a quadrant or a trine <note>original: "kendra-labha-trikonage"; these are specific favorable houses in a birth chart</note>; if it is joined with a benefic planet and endowed with the strength of a waxing Moon: ॥ 17 ॥

And if the Moon is the lord of the houses of action or fortune <note>original: "karma-bhagyadhipe"; the 10th and 9th houses</note>, or is placed in the house of vehicles and endowed with strength; then from beginning to end, it grants great fortune, lordship, and the gain of wealth and grain. ॥ 18 ॥

There will be auspicious celebrations in the home, the acquisition of vehicles, and meetings with royalty. Efforts toward a goal will find success, and it brings the "glance of Lakshmi" <note>Lakshmi: the goddess of wealth and prosperity; her "glance" implies a stroke of good fortune</note> upon the household. ॥ 19 ॥

Fortune arises through the influence of friends and powerful masters, leading to the gain of status and great happiness. It also brings the acquisition of horses, palanquins, and fine white garments. ॥ 20 ॥

There is happiness from the birth of sons and a household filled with cattle and wealth. If the Moon is situated in the house of wealth <note>the 2nd house</note>, or is exalted, or in its own sign: ॥ 21 ॥

One experiences the gain of varied wealth, an increase in fortune, and great happiness. One finds hidden treasures, receives royal honors, and attains knowledge. ॥ 22 ॥

If the Moon is debilitated <note>debilitated: the zodiac sign where a planet is at its weakest</note> or waning, a loss of wealth will occur. If it is in the third house <note>original: "duschikye"</note> but endowed with strength, there is occasional happiness and some wealth. ॥ 23 ॥

If the Moon is weak and joined with malefic planets, there is physical sluggishness and mental illness. One suffers trouble from servants, loss of money, and harm from the mother’s family. ॥ 24 ॥

If the Moon is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses <note>these are traditionally "difficult" houses in Vedic astrology</note>, and is weak and joined with malefics: there is royal displeasure, mental grief, and the destruction of wealth and grain. ॥ 25 ॥

It brings distress to the mother, mental pain, physical sluggishness, and mental disease. Even in a difficult house, if it has "Lunar strength" <note>likely referring to its phase or brightness</note>, there may be occasional gain and happiness. Physical sluggishness may occur, which cannot be destroyed without performing pacification rituals <note>original: "shantyarthena"; Shanti rituals are performed to appease planetary deities</note>. ॥ 26 ॥

### Now, the 7-year Major Period of Mars and its Results.

An excellent major period of Mars <note>original: "Bhaumotkrishta-dasha"</note> produces the acquisition of land, the arrival of wealth, intelligence, a clear mind, and valor, though it may cause the loss of younger siblings <note>Mars is the traditional significator of siblings</note>. A malefic Mars brings diseases and pain...

# Chapter 36: On the Declaration of the Results of the Vimshottari Major Periods <note>Vimshottari Dasha: A 120-year cycle used in Vedic astrology to predict the timing of life events based on planetary "reigns."</note>

[The period of Mars] will grant quarrels, fear of thieves and fire, imprisonment, wounds, and persistent suffering or illness caused by the king <note>In historical texts, "the king" represents the government or state authorities.</note>, as well as injury from agitation. ॥ 27 ॥ If Mars is in its highest state of exaltation <note>exaltation: the zodiac sign where a planet’s influence is most powerful and positive.</note>, in its own exaltation sign, in its primary territory <note>original: "moolatrikona," a specific favorable area of a zodiac sign.</note>, in its own sign, or placed in a quadrant, a trine, the house of gains, or the house of wealth; ॥ 28 ॥ and if it is endowed with full strength, aspected <note>aspected: a mathematical "glance" or influence from another planet.</note> by benefic planets, or located in a favorable divisional sign, it causes the gain of a kingdom, the acquisition of land, and wealth, grain, and other such assets. ॥ 29 ॥ It brings an abundance of royal honors, vehicles, clothing, and ornaments. One obtains a position in a foreign land and experiences happiness concerning brothers. ॥ 30 ॥ If Mars is always situated in a quadrant, or in the third house <note>original: "dushchikye," a technical term for the 3rd house of a horoscope.</note> and endowed with strength, there will be wealth acquired through valor and victory over enemies in battle. ॥ 31 ॥ Prosperity for the wife and children and royal honors will follow. One finds happiness at the beginning of the major period, but should predict hardship at the end of the period. ॥ 32 ॥ If Mars is in its sign of debilitation <note>debilitation: the zodiac sign where a planet is at its weakest.</note>, or in a difficult house, devoid of strength, joined with malefic planets, or aspected by malefics, that major period does not grant desired results. ॥ 33 ॥

->**Now, the 18 years of the Rahu Major Period and its results.**<-

An excellent major period of Rahu <note>Rahu: the "North Node" of the Moon, a shadow planet associated with worldly desire and sudden changes.</note> produces all forms of welfare and the attainment of a great kingdom. It brings the arrival of righteousness and wealth, pilgrimages to holy bathing places, and an increase in knowledge, influence, and status. Conversely, a malefic period of Rahu brings fear, danger from poison, diseases affecting all limbs, injury from weapons, conflict, falling from trees, and suffering caused by enemies. ॥ 34 ॥ For Rahu, Taurus is the sign of exaltation, and for Ketu <note>Ketu: the "South Node" of the Moon.</note>, Scorpio is the sign of exaltation. Cancer is its primary territory <note>moolatrikona</note>, as are Gemini and Sagittarius. ॥ 35 ॥ Virgo is said to be its own house, and Pisces is also remembered as its own house. In such cases, the period brings much happiness and the prosperity of wealth, grain, and assets. ॥ 36 ॥ By the grace of friends and lords, one obtains desired vehicles and the birth of a son. There is the construction of a new house, thoughts of religion, and the celebration of great festivals. ॥ 37 ॥ One receives honors from a foreign king and acquires clothing and decorative ornaments—provided Rahu is joined with or aspected by benefics or joined with a planet that forms a special power-combination <note>term: "yoga-karaka," a planet that brings success and status due to its specific placement.</note>. ॥ 38 ॥ If Rahu is in a quadrant, a trine, the house of gains, or the third house in a favorable sign, then by the grace of a great king, it brings all wealth and happiness. ॥ 39 ॥ There are honors from a foreign <note>original: "Yavana-prabhu," historically referring to Greek or other non-Vedic rulers.</note> ruler and the occurrence of auspicious events in the home. However, if Rahu is in the eighth or twelfth house <note>These are traditionally considered "dusthanas" or houses of loss and suffering.</note>, it becomes a giver of hardship. ॥ 40 ॥ If connected with a malefic planet, joined with a "killer" planet <note>term: "maraka," a planet designated in a chart as having the power to end life or cause great crisis.</note>, or in its sign of debilitation, there will be a fall from one's position and mental distress. ॥ 41 ॥ The destruction of wife and children...

# Now, the Results of the Major Period of Jupiter (16 Years)

An excellent major period of Jupiter <note>original: "Jiva," meaning the life-force or soul, a name for Jupiter</note> grants authority over vast villages, the birth of sons, wealth, good fortune, an abundance of virtues, the role of a protector for others, and the splendor of palanquins <note>a historical symbol of high status and luxury transport</note>. A malefic period of Jupiter causes fear from the government, disease, loss of courage, disasters involving grains, suffering for sons, parental agitation, and extreme exhaustion. ॥ 44 ॥

If Jupiter is located in its sign of exaltation <note>the zodiac sign where a planet is most powerful</note>, in its own sign, in a quadrant <term>kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which represent the pillars of a person's life</term>, in the house of gains <note>the 11th house</note>, or in a trine <term>trikona: the 1st, 5th, or 9th houses, associated with luck and past merit</term>; or if it is in its primary territory <note>original: "moolatrikona," a particularly strong placement</note>, its highest point, or its own division; ॥ 45 ॥ it brings the acquisition of power, great happiness, royal honors, and fame. One is joined by elephants and horses <note>modern equivalent: luxury vehicles and assets</note> and becomes devoted to the worship of gods and scholars. ॥ 46 ॥ 

It brings happiness regarding one's wife and children, the acquisition of vehicles and fine clothing, success in religious rituals, and the study of Vedanta <note>the philosophical traditions of the Vedas</note>. ॥ 47 ॥ Through the favor of a great king, one’s desires are fulfilled comfortably; one gains palanquins and similar luxuries, experiencing auspiciousness and great joy. ॥ 48 ॥ 

There is the gain of sons and a wife, and a great love for the distribution of food <note>charitable acts</note>. But if Jupiter is in its sign of debilitation <note>where it is weakest</note>, combust <note>too close to the sun</note>, joined with malefic planets, or situated in the twelfth or eighth houses <note>original: "rishphashta," houses associated with loss and transformation</note>; ॥ 49 ॥ it causes displacement from one's home, mental agony, suffering to sons, great fear, loss of cattle and wealth, and leads one to go on pilgrimages to holy sites. ॥ 50 ॥ At first, the results are difficult, yet one gains four-legged animals and a livelihood; in the middle and end of the period, one finds happiness and royal honors and splendor. ॥ 51 ॥

# Now, the Results of the Major Period of Saturn (19 Years)

An excellent major period of Saturn <note>original: "Manda," meaning "the slow one"</note> brings prosperity, wisdom, the performance of sacrifices, and makes one a leader of fields, villages, and towns, as well as highly skilled and eager in various business dealings. If Saturn is malefic, it causes the use of poison, theft of wealth, bodily pain, useless efforts, anger from the authorities, contradictory actions, loss of employment, and pain in the limbs. ॥ 52 ॥

If Saturn is in its sign of exaltation, its own sign, or a friend’s sign; or if it is in its primary territory, the house of fortune <note>the 9th house</note>, its highest point, or its own division; ॥ 53 ॥ or if it is in the third house <note>original: "dushchikye"</note> or the house of gains, it brings royal honors and splendor, good fame, the gain of wealth, and an interest in education, debates, and entertainment. ॥ 54 ॥

### Now, the Results of the Major Period of Mercury (17 Years)

An excellent period of Mercury <note>original: "saumya," the gentle or son of the Moon</note> brings an abundance of fine clothing, jewels, and grains. It provides well-being, the happiness of a home and relatives, victory, and the arrival of desired objects. A malefic period causes travel to foreign lands, mental agitation, the loss of relatives, a lack of wisdom, financial distress, quarrels, and the loss of fields and wealth. ॥ 61 ॥ 

If Mercury is in its sign of exaltation, its own sign, a quadrant, a trine, or the house of gains, or if it is in the sign of a friendly planet, its period brings great happiness. ॥ 62 ॥ It brings the gain of wealth and grain, good fame, and prosperity. There is an increase in knowledge, the favor of kings, and the growth of virtuous qualities. ॥ 63 ॥ One finds happiness with children and spouse, physical health, and great joy. One enjoys food prepared with milk and wealth comes through trade. ॥ 64 ॥ 

When Mercury is aspected by or joined with auspicious planets, and is the ruler of the house of fortune <note>the 9th house</note> or the house of actions <note>the 10th house</note>, its high status and strength provide full results. ॥ 65 ॥ 

If joined with or aspected by malefic planets, it causes the hatred of kings, mental illness, conflict with relatives, and travel to foreign lands. ॥ 66 ॥ One may experience serving others, quarrels, and a great fear of urinary diseases <term>mutrakricchra: painful or difficult urination</term>. If Mercury is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, it destroys gains, enjoyment, and wealth. ॥ 67 ॥ One suffers from "wind" diseases <term>vata: one of the three bodily humors in Ayurveda, often relating to the nervous system or joints</term>, loss of wealth, and anemia <term>pandu-roga: "pale-disease"</term>. There is fear of kings, thieves, and fire, and the loss of cattle, land, and agriculture. ॥ 68 ॥ 

At the start of the period, there is wealth, grain, the gain of knowledge, and great happiness. There is prosperity through the well-being of sons, and wealth is earned through righteous means. ॥ 69 ॥ In the middle of the period, one receives honor from the king, but at the end, there will be sorrow. ॥ 70 ॥

# Now, the Results of the 7-Year Major Period of Ketu.

An excellent period of Ketu brings victory, the acquisition of wealth through bold or harsh actions, fortune obtained from foreign rulers <note>original: "mleccha-kshmapati," historically referring to non-Vedic or foreign kings</note>, the beginning of literary works, and the destruction of enemies. However, a malefic period of Ketu is extremely difficult and fruitless; it brings about wrong actions, chest pain <term>hricchula: literally "heart-spear," referring to sharp pains in the chest</term>, bone-fever, tremors, hatred from the learned, and the performance of extremely foolish deeds. ॥ 71 ॥

If Ketu is placed in a quadrant <term>kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a birth chart</term>, the house of gains <note>the 11th house</note>, a trine <term>trikona: the 5th or 9th houses</term>, or in an auspicious sign aspected by beneficial planets; ॥ 72 ॥ or if it is in its sign of exaltation or in an auspicious divisional chart, it brings royal favor but also some mental anxiety. It grants lordship over countries and villages, vehicles, and the birth of a son. It leads to travel to other lands, which brings comfort in those foreign places. ॥ 73 ॥

It brings happiness from one's wife and children, and the gain of four-legged livestock. If Ketu is located in the third, sixth, or eleventh house, its period will be happy. ॥ 74 ॥ It grants a kingdom, a friendly temperament, and the possession of elephants and horses. At the beginning of the period, there are combinations for high status <term>rajayoga: planetary alignments indicating power and success</term>, but in the middle of the period, there is great fear. ॥ 75 ॥

At the end of the period, there is wandering to distant places and exhaustion of the body. If Ketu is in the second, eighth, or twelfth house <note>traditionally difficult houses for material stability</note>, or is joined or aspected by malefic planets; ॥ 76 ॥ it leads to imprisonment <note>original: "nigadam," chains or fetters</note>, the loss of relatives, displacement from one's position, and mental agony. There may be gains from low-born sources or empty pursuits, and one will be troubled by many diseases. ॥ 77 ॥

# Now, the Results of the 20-Year Major Period of Venus.

An excellent period of Venus <note>original: "shaukri," belonging to Shukra</note> brings happiness, prosperity, high status, the use of palanquins <note>a covered litter, signifying high social rank</note>, and the "eight types of wealth." It brings a religious mind, gold, gardens, horses, music, and festivals. A malefic period of Venus brings fear regarding the spouse, loss of women and wealth, troubles arising from animals <note>original: "tiryag-jantu," literally "horizontal animals," such as cattle or wild beasts</note>, and many diseases among the women of the household. ॥ 78 ॥

If Venus is in its highest exaltation, its own sign, or in a quadrant; ॥ 79 ॥ it brings the honor of a royal coronation, vehicles, fine clothing, and ornaments. There is the gain of elephants, horses, and cattle, and the daily enjoyment of sweet foods. One receives the glory and royal respect belonging to the ruler of a vast territory. ॥ 80 ॥

The sound of drums and musical instruments will be heard in the home, signifying the glance of Lakshmi <note>the goddess of wealth</note>. If Venus is in a trine or in the sign of Pisces <note>where it is exalted</note>, it brings a kingdom, wealth, and home prosperity. ॥ 81 ॥ It brings marriage festivals, celebrations for children, leadership of armies, and reunions with beloved relatives. ॥ 82 ॥

One recovers a lost kingdom and accumulates wealth and cattle in the home. If Venus is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, or in its sign of debilitation <note>Virgo</note>, or in the house of expenditure; ॥ 83 ॥ it brings hatred from one's own relatives and suffering for the wife's family. ### Now, the Results of the Major Periods of the Lords of the Twelve Houses.

The Major Period of the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagnésha</term> brings physical strength and much wealth. The Lord of the Second House <note>Vittésha</note> brings either the state of death or great hardship. The results of the Lord of the Third House <note>the house of siblings</note> are mostly sinful or difficult. The Lord of the Fourth House brings a home. The Lord of the Fifth House brings knowledge and happiness. The Lord of the Sixth House brings fear arising from enemies. The Lord of the Seventh House brings sorrow. ॥ 90 ॥

The Lord of the Eighth House certainly brings death. The Lord of the Ninth House <note>Dharmésha</note> brings virtuous deeds. The Lord of the Tenth House brings royal patronage. The Lord of the Eleventh House brings gains. The Lord of the Twelfth House brings the destruction of wealth and many kinds of hardships. This is what the ancients have declared regarding the results of the lords of the houses, starting from the body <note>the 1st house</note>. ॥ 91 ॥

When a house lord is powerful, situated in its own house, exalted, or in its own trine or auspicious divisional chart, it bestows full results. However, if it is situated in an enemy's sign or a place of debilitation, it produces inauspicious results, especially if it lacks strength. ॥ 92 ॥

The knowers of time <note>astrologers</note> speak of the good and bad results for human beings in this way. This essence has been determined to clarify the destiny of men. ॥ 93 ॥

The Major Period of the Lord of the Fifth House, or the Major Period of the Lord of the Ninth House, is declared by the great sages who know time to be extremely auspicious. ॥ 94 ॥ The period of the Lord of Mantras <note>5th house</note> or the Lord of Penance <note>9th house</note> will grant a kingdom and sons. Likewise, those of noble mind say the period of the Lord of Fame or the Lord of Happiness <note>4th house</note> is equally beneficial. ॥ 95 ॥

...bestowing authority and kingdom. The period of a planet associated with a benefic planet brings wealth. Likewise, the major period of the lord of the fifth house when placed in the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign at birth</term> bestows status and kingdom. ॥ 97 ॥

The major period of the lord of the ninth house <note>tapa: the house of fortune and merit</note> when associated with the lord of the fifth house will bring the happiness of a kingdom, wealth, and gains. Similarly, the period of the lord of the fifth house <note>sutesha: the lord of progeny/intellect</note> associated with the lord of the tenth house <note>mana: the house of honor and profession</note> will also be auspicious. ॥ 98 ॥

The period of the lord of the tenth house joined with the lord of the fifth house is auspicious. The period of the lord of the ninth house associated with the lord of the fourth house <note>sukha: the house of happiness and comforts</note> is also favorable. Furthermore, the period of the lord of the tenth house when placed in the fifth house is auspicious. ॥ 99 ॥

Even if a planet is not placed in a specifically auspicious or inauspicious house, its period can still bring honor, wealth, and happiness. Specifically, for a person whose period is associated with the lord of the fourth house, it truly brings comfort and joy. ॥ 100 ॥

If a single planet acts as the lord of both the sixth and seventh houses <note>this occurs for Aries and Libra Ascendants</note> and is placed in the tenth house, its major period—as well as the period of any planet associated with it—is considered auspicious. ॥ 1 ॥

If a single planet is the lord of both the second and seventh houses and is placed in the fourth house, the wise sages declare that its period, and the period of those joined with it, will be auspicious. ॥ 2 ॥

Even the lords of the *dusthanas* <note>difficult houses: the sixth, eighth, and twelfth</note> become givers of good results during their periods if they are associated with the lord of the fifth house. So say the great experts in the science of time. ॥ 3 ॥

When the lord of the fourth house is in the tenth, and the lord of the tenth house is in the fourth <note>an exchange of signs known as Parivartana Yoga</note>, the experts in astrology declare their periods to be highly auspicious. ॥ 4 ॥

If the lords of the fifth, tenth, fourth, and ninth houses are all joined together in any house, their periods will bestow the fruits of kingship. This effect also applies to any other planets associated with them. ॥ 5 ॥

The period of the lord of the fifth house <note>mantranatha: the lord of counsel and mantras</note> associated with the fourth house <note>the house of vehicles</note> is auspicious. The period of the lord of the tenth house <note>karmesha: the lord of actions/career</note> when placed in the fourth house bestows kingly authority. ॥ 6 ॥

The periods of planets associated with or aspected by these two lords are also said to bestow kingdom by the learned scholars who contemplate destiny. ॥ 7 ॥

The period of the lord of the fifth house <note>buddhisha: the lord of intellect</note> placed in the tenth house brings prosperity. The period of the lord of the ninth house placed in the tenth house bestows kingly power. ॥ 8 ॥

In whichever house there is a connection with a benefic lord and an exalted planet <term>khechara: a planet or 'sky-goer'</term>, the period of that house lord will bring unbroken and immense lordship and power. ॥ 9 ॥

If a lord of a house stays in or aspects the second house from itself <note>the house of wealth relative to that specific house</note>, then during the period of that house lord, there will be a very great gain of wealth. ॥ 110 ॥

During the major period of a planet situated in the twelfth house <note>vyaya: the house of loss</note> from any house, there will be a loss of wealth related to that house. If malefic planets are placed in the trines <note>trikona: the 5th or 9th houses</note> from a particular house, they cause the destruction of the peace and vitality of that house. ॥ 111 ॥

There will be loss of sons, suffering for the father, and great mental agony if the lords of the twelfth and eighth houses, or the Sun, Moon, and Saturn <note>suryaja: the son of the Sun</note> are situated in the trines from a house. ॥ 112 ॥

<header>First Section: Chapter 36 on the Results of the Vimshottari Major Periods</header>

### First Section: Chapter 36 on the Results of the Vimshottari Major Periods

Trouble to children and loss of wealth occur when Ketu <term>the south node of the Moon</term> and Rahu <term>the north node of the Moon</term> are joined together. One wanders in foreign lands, faces hardships, and feels fear at every step. ॥ 13 ॥

When cruel <note>malefic</note> or debilitated <note>weak</note> planets are situated in the sixth or eighth houses from the planet whose major period is active, there will be diseases, enemies, and trouble from the authorities. Such a person suffers frequent and unbearable pain. ॥ 14 ॥

When a malefic planet is in the fourth house from the period-lord, it leads to the destruction of the home and the fields. If Mars <note>original: Bhauma</note> is positioned there, there is a loss of livestock and the danger of the house burning or accidents. ॥ 15 ॥

If Saturn is in that position, one suffers from chest pain; if the Sun is there, one faces the wrath of the king or government. If Rahu is there, one’s entire property may be seized, and there is fear of poison and thieves. ॥ 16 ॥

When Rahu is in the tenth house from the period-lord, one goes on pilgrimages to holy places. If benefic <note>auspicious</note> planets are placed in the tenth house of action <note>Karma</note> or the ninth house of fortune <note>Bhagya</note> from that lord... ॥ 17 ॥

...then success is achieved in education, wealth, religious duty, good deeds, fame, and personal power. When benefic planets in their signs of highest strength <note>exaltation</note> are in the fifth, seventh, or sixth houses... ॥ 18 ॥

...one gains a spouse and children, and receives great honor from the king. Wherever the lords of the tenth house <note>the house of profession</note> and the fourth house <note>the house of happiness and property</note> are situated... ॥ 19 ॥

...the fulfillment of those specific houses will manifest as blessings according to the planetary combinations. Wherever Jupiter, Venus, or the lord of a benefic house is located... ॥ 20 ॥

...there will be auspicious celebrations, prosperity, and the performance of rituals to satisfy the gods and the learned. If exalted planets or a benefic lord are in the fourth house... ॥ 21 ॥

...one gains vehicles and villages, and there is a great increase in livestock. If the lord of the Moon's sign is present there, there will be an abundance of grain and luxury liquids. ॥ 22 ॥

If the Moon is full, one may find hidden treasure or a collection of precious gems. If Venus is there, one is welcomed with the sound of drums and music. ॥ 23 ॥

If Jupiter <note>original: Jiva</note> is present, one certainly gains a palanquin, or even a golden palanquin. Through the auspicious combination of the lords of the Ascendant, the tenth house, and the ninth house when they are in their signs of exaltation... ॥ 24 ॥

...one attains supreme excellence, great wealth, and the grand results of an empire. Thus, one should contemplate the results of the periods based on the status of each house. ॥ 25 ॥

Each planetary period <term>Udu-dasha: the system of life-cycles based on the Moon's position</term> has its own nature, which is divided into eighteen distinct qualities. The ripening of these results creates a variety of diverse experiences. ॥ 26 ॥

Whether a planet is at its peak of exaltation, just below it, or just above it; whether it is in its "root-trine" <note>Moolatrikona: a sign where the planet is very comfortable</note>, its own sign, or the sign of a great friend... ॥ 27 ॥

...whether it is in the house of a temporary friend, a neutral house, an enemy’s house, or a great enemy’s house; whether it is moving away from its point of debilitation... ॥ 28 ॥

...or moving toward it, or at the very point of deepest weakness; whether it is in an auspicious divisional chart or placed in the central <term>Kendra</term> or triangular <term>Trikona</term> houses of the birth chart... ॥ 29 ॥

For a planet defeated in planetary war <term>the astronomical conjunction of two planets where one "wins" based on latitude and brightness</term> or one that is deeply hidden and eclipsed, the result of its period is a decline in its natural good qualities. ॥ 30 ॥

A planet in its highest state of exaltation <term>the specific degree where a planet is strongest</term> and possessing great vitality grants a "Complete" <note>original: "Sampurna"</note> period, which provides the enjoyment of political power and prosperity. ॥ 31 ॥ It bestows a home that is a dwelling place of consciousness and marked by the grace of Lakshmi <term>the goddess of wealth and beauty</term>. 

For a planet that is merely in its exaltation sign or possesses extra strength, its period is called "Full" <note>original: "Purna"</note>. ॥ 32 ॥ Although this period grants many kinds of wealth and sovereignty, it may also cause some illness. 

For a planet in its lowest state of debilitation <term>the sign where a planet is weakest</term> or one that is otherwise frail, ॥ 33 ॥ its period is called "Empty" <note>original: "Rikta"</note>. It yields unfavorable results, such as illness, misfortune, and even death. 

For a planet situated between its highest exaltation and its lowest debilitation, the period is called "Growing" <note>original: "Rohini"</note>. ॥ 34 ॥ If it reaches a friendly sign or its own exaltation division, the period is called "Middling" <note>original: "Madhya"</note> and provides wealth. 

From the end of the debilitation sign to the end of the exaltation sign—moving through a cycle of six signs—if a planet resides in a debilitated or enemy division, ॥ 35 ॥ the period is called "Base" <note>original: "Adhama"</note>. It increases fear, hardship, disease, and sorrow. ॥ 36 ॥

These periods give results corresponding to their names during their time of fruition <note>original: "paka-kala"</note>. If connected to the Lord of Fortune <note>the ruler of the 9th house of luck</note> or Jupiter, or to yoga-producing angles <term>Kendra</term> and similar houses, ॥ 37 ॥ one can initiate a rise in fortune even during the periods of other planets. A birth chart that is fruitful provides combinations for fortune. ॥ 38 ॥ 

A retrograde planet <term>a planet appearing to move backward in the sky</term> makes other planets—even weak and incapable ones—fruitful through its association. ॥ 39 ॥ Depending on the gradations of their relationships, these periods provide results. Depending on their position in the angles or the cardinal directions, they give results in full, half, or quarter measures. ॥ 40 ॥ 

The "Forced Doer" <note>original: "Prasahyakara"</note> planet constantly brings wealth through its sheer power. A planet in a Head-Rising sign <term>signs like Leo, Virgo, or Scorpio that rise with the 'head' first</term> gives its results at the beginning of its major period. ॥ 41 ॥ 

A planet in a Both-Ways-Rising sign <term>Gemini, which is said to rise both ways</term> gives medium results in the middle of the period. Planets in Back-Rising signs <term>signs like Aries, Taurus, or Cancer that rise with the 'back' first</term> give their results at the end of their period. ॥ 42 ॥ 

At the time of birth, one should examine the favorable positions of the period-lord. If the planet naturally moves through friendly signs at that time, it is auspicious. ॥ 43 ॥ Hardship will be produced for those whose planets move in the opposite manner <note>through enemy or debilitated signs</note>. 

The house occupied by the period-lord is the "doorway" <note>original: "dvara"</note>. ॥ 44 ॥ By evaluating the twelve signs from that position, one should determine the sub-periods <note>original: "bhukti"</note>. If a sign is a friendly sign or the planet's own sign, ॥ 45 ॥ one should predict auspiciousness, including the acquisition of kingdoms and wealth. However, if the sign is a bad house <note>the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses of loss and enmity</note>, an enemy sign, or a debilitated sign, or if it is joined by cruel planets... ॥ 46 ॥

<header>### Chapter 36: Description of the Results of the Vimshottari Planetary Periods in the First Section</header>

In that period, one may experience misfortune, quarrels, and the fear of disease or death. By analyzing the abundance or absence of points <note>original: "bindu"</note> in one’s own *Ashtakavarga* <term>a system of points used to evaluate the strength of planets based on their positions relative to others</term>, ॥ 47 ॥ one should understand the growth or decline of that sign and its associated house <term>one of the twelve divisions of the zodiac representing areas of life like wealth or family</term>. By examining the sequence from the planet itself, one can know the auspicious or inauspicious results for children and other matters. ॥ 48 ॥

Through the distinctions of elements <note>original: "dhatu"</note>, signs, and the conjunctions of planets associated with these elements, and through the variations of favorable or unfavorable periods and their associated planets, ॥ 49 ॥ one should deduce the various results based on whether a planet is placed in a desirable or undesirable position. Similarly, for all planets, one should evaluate their own sub-periods <note>original: "antardasha"</note>. ॥ 150 ॥ 

By calculating the sub-period's movement from its own sign, one should declare the results. By repeatedly dividing these sub-periods into smaller segments, ॥ 51 ॥ one can briefly state the subtle results for each individual day. This method was established by the author of the *Horagrantha* <note>a foundational manual on horoscopy</note> or through this specific tradition. ॥ 52 ॥ 

If the significators <term>planets that naturally represent a specific person or concept</term> or the lords of the houses are placed in the angles <term>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</term> or the trines <term>the 1st, 5th, or 9th houses</term>, the house flourishes. If they are placed in difficult houses <note>the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses, often associated with loss or obstacles</note>, the house is "killed" or destroyed. When these planets are in the houses of wealth, gains, or courage, the results for family members like the mother or father are assessed accordingly. ॥ 53 ॥ 

If the lord of a house aspects <term>looks at or influences through its astrological gaze</term> its own house, or if the lord of the Ascendant <term>the planet ruling the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term> is placed there, or if they are strong and in their sign of exaltation, that house will be nourished and yield desired results. ॥ 54 ॥ 

When the lord of a house is in its sign of debilitation <term>the sign where it is weakest</term>, is combust <term>hidden by the Sun's light</term>, or does not aspect its own house, one should predict a lack of vitality, laziness, and enmity for that house. ॥ 55 ॥ 

If the ruler of the sign occupied by a house-lord is placed in the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses, the destruction of that house is certain, even if it is aspected by the house-lord itself. ॥ 56 ॥ 

If the lord of the Ascendant is in its highest state of exaltation, the first house is aspected by a benefic planet <term>a naturally supportive planet like Jupiter or Venus</term>, and the Moon is joined with or aspected by a benefic, the wise say the person will live for one hundred years. ॥ 57 ॥ 

If the four houses of wealth, fortune, gains, and action are strong, the person will possess complete and constant riches, becoming like Kubera <term>the Hindu god of wealth and treasurer of the gods</term>. ॥ 58 ॥ 

A connection between the lord of the Ascendant, the lord of the 4th house <note>representing vehicles and the physical body</note>, and the body itself indicates the possession of horses and vehicles. If Venus is involved, one obtains a palanquin <note>original: "andolika," a luxury portable bed carried by people</note>; if Jupiter, an elephant for transport. ॥ 59 ॥ 

If the lords of the 10th and 4th houses are in an angle, a trine, the 11th, the 2nd, or the 3rd house, and are joined with the lords of the body, the Moon, or the Ascendant, or if they occupy each other’s houses, or are placed in each other’s highly fortunate angles, and yet they look upon their own houses despite being in difficult positions—then even a person born into a poor family will possess four types of vehicles. ॥ 160 ॥

# Summary of the Great Parashara Horoscopy

## Now, the method for calculating the sub-periods is described.

> One should multiply the duration of the major period <term>Mahadasha; the primary planetary cycle</term> by the duration of the planet's period. Divide that total by ten. The resulting whole numbers shall be the months, and the remainder, when multiplied by three, shall be the days. ॥ 1 ॥

### An Example of This:

For example, the major period of the Sun <note>original: "Surya"</note> lasts for six years (6). If one wishes to know how long the sub-period <term>Antardasha; a smaller cycle within a major period</term> of the Sun is within its own major period: multiply the period years (6) by each other (6), which results in 36. Dividing this by ten, the quotient is 3, which represents the months. The remainder of 6 is multiplied by three, resulting in 18, which represents the days. Thus, within the major period of the Sun, the Sun's own sub-period is 3 months and 18 days. In this same way, the sub-periods for the Moon and the other planets should also be understood.

### Summary of the Great Parashara Horoscopy

If a planet is placed in the <term>Navamsha</term><note>The 1/9th divisional chart, used to see the internal strength of a planet.</note> of the 4th house <note>The house of happiness and comforts.</note>, or in the specific divisions related to vehicles or the 6th part, or even in the 4th <term>Drekkana</term><note>A 1/3rd division of a sign.</note>, its sub-period will bring auspicious results and happiness. // 7 //

When the lord of the sign where the Ascendant lord is placed is in a friend's division, or is aspected by a friendly planet, or is in a friendly Drekkana or Navamsha, then they say its sub-period will be auspicious. // 8 //

Now I shall specifically describe the periods that cause suffering to men. The periods of the lords of the 6th <note>house of debt and disease</note>, 8th <note>house of death and obstacles</note>, and 12th <note>house of loss</note> houses are providers of suffering. // 9 //

This sub-period will indeed be difficult if it occurs during the major period of a <term>Maraka</term><note>A death-inflicting planet, usually the lord of the 2nd or 7th house.</note>. If the lord of the 6th house is joined with a Maraka lord and the lord of the Ascendant... // 10 //

...During that sub-period, those who know time <note>original: "kalavido jana," meaning astrologers</note> say the person will suffer from fever. If the lord of the body <note>the Ascendant lord</note> is afflicted by disease and falls within the <term>Shad-varga</term><note>The six-fold system of divisional charts used to judge a planet's power.</note> of the Moon... // 11 //

...Then in that sub-period, there will be "water-disorders" <note>such as colds or edema</note> and indigestion; of this there is no doubt. If the Ascendant lord, joined with the 6th house lord, falls within the Shad-varga of Mercury... // 12 //

...In that sub-period, there will be wind-disorders <note>Vata imbalances</note> or physical stiffness. If the lord of the 6th and the Ascendant lord are in the Shad-varga of Jupiter, in that sub-period there will be disease or trouble caused by a priest or a learned person <note>original: "brahmanena," a Brahmin</note>. // 13 //

If the lord of the birth star <note>Nakshatra lord</note> and the Ascendant lord are in the Shad-varga of Venus, then in that sub-period there will be trouble and disease arising from association with women. // 14 //

If the Ascendant lord, joined with a malefic, is in the Shad-varga of Saturn, in that sub-period there will be wind-disorders or a total collapse of the three humors <note>original: "sannipata," a dangerous fever or delirium</note> for men. When the sub-periods of Maraka planets occur for the lords of the Ascendant and 6th houses... // 15 //

...And if they are placed in the 8th house of death along with Rahu <note>original: "Saihikeya," the shadow planet</note>, Saturn <note>original: "Manda"</note>, or Ketu, then through mental distress, breathing difficulties, or cholera <note>original: "vipuchika"</note>, disease comes to men in that sub-period when joined with a death-inflicting planet. // 16 //

In this same way, one should state the results for various life areas—such as brothers and so on—based on where their respective lords are situated and their combinations within the Shad-varga. // 17 //

### Now, the results are stated hereafter.

The major and sub-periods of the lords of the <term>Kendras</term><note>The "angles" or houses 1, 4, 7, and 10.</note> and the best <term>Konas</term><note>The "trines" or houses 1, 5, and 9.</note> are auspicious. The periods of the lords of the 2nd, 3rd, and 11th houses are average. The periods of the lords of the 6th, 8th, and 12th houses are always painful. One should judge these while looking at the Ascendant and the respective lords in those specific periods. // 18 //
