<page-num>409</page-num>
### First Section: Chapter 51, Description of the Sudarshana Chakra

...should be performed. Malefic planets <note>original: "papai," planets like Mars or Saturn that generally cause challenge</note> situated in the 3rd, 6th, and 11th houses <note>original: "triṣaḍāyeṣu," known as the houses of growth or 'upachaya'</note> are actually auspicious. || 16 ||

Assign the various states <note>original: "bhavam," the twelve houses of life such as wealth, siblings, etc.</note> to the corresponding parts of the body <note>original: "angam"</note> to determine the physical results. Following the instructions of one's teacher <note>original: "gurūpadeśāt"</note>, one should also interpret the significance of food and dreams. || 17 ||

Calculate the cycles of the twelve houses over a period of ten years each <note>referring to the Sudarshana Dasha, where each house rules a 10-year block of a 120-year life</note>. Within those, the sub-periods and months should be calculated similarly; their auspiciousness depends on the strength of the planets. || 18 ||

The **Sudarshana Chakra** <note>literally "The Wheel of Auspicious Vision," named after the spinning disc of the god Vishnu</note> consists of twelve spokes and is composed of three concentric circles. In the **inner circle**, the houses and planets are drawn starting from the **Ascendant** <note>original: "janma-lagnād," the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note>. || 19 ||

In the **middle circle** above that, the houses and planets are drawn starting from the **Moon** <note>original: "candrācca"</note>. In the **outer circle** above that, the houses and planets should be written starting from the **Sun** <note>original: "sūryācca"</note>. || 20 ||

Whichever planets are situated in whichever zodiac signs <note>original: "rāśau"</note> across all three circles, they must be recorded exactly there. From those positions, one must examine the state of the houses. || 21 ||

If in any circle, Rahu <note>original: "tamah," the North Node of the Moon, associated with darkness</note> or many malefic planets are located in the 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th <note>the 'Kendras' or pillars</note>, 5th, 9th <note>the 'Konas' or trines</note>, or the 8th house from a specific house, that house is destroyed. || 22 ||

In whichever house Rahu <note>original: "saiṃhikeyo," literally 'the son of the lioness Simhika'</note> is placed, that house will certainly suffer loss. Conversely, if benefics <note>original: "saumyāḥ," gentle planets like Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury</note> are in the 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th, 5th, 9th, or 8th from a house, they grant auspicious results. || 23 ||

In such a case, that house will flourish. If auspicious planets are placed in these key positions <note>the 'Kendra' etc.</note> across all three circles, they provide an abundance of good results. || 24 ||

Similarly, if malefic planets are so placed, they provide the fruits of misfortune and suffering. However, if these are aspected <note>original: "vīkṣitāḥ," viewed by planetary 'sight'</note> by a benefic, the results for that house will be balanced <note>original: "samam"</note>. || 25 ||

->**Here follows an example.**<-

In the **Saka year 1600** <note>approximately 1678 CE</note>, during the month of Pausha, on the 5th day of the dark fortnight, on a Monday <note>original: "candre," Moon-day</note>. The time was 14 *ghatis* and 54 *palas* <note>traditional units of time; 1 ghati = 24 minutes</note>. The Moon was in the constellation **Purva Phalguni** <note>at 32 ghatis 8 palas</note>; the remaining time for **Uttara Phalguni** was 8 ghatis 30 palas. The Yoga <note>astronomical alignment</note> was Saubhagya at 45 ghatis 52 palas. The Sun was in Sagittarius <note>original: "cāpārka," Archer-Sun</note> at 23 degrees, 46 minutes, and 41 seconds. From sunrise, 42 ghatis and 4 palas had elapsed.

**Planetary positions at birth:**
*   **Sun:** 8s 23° 46' 41" <note>Sign 8 is Sagittarius</note>; Daily motion: 61' 5"
*   **Moon:** 0s 4° 28' 46" 14"' <note>Sign 0 is Aries</note>; Daily motion: 773' 16"
*   **Mars:** 4s 4° 14' 19" <note>Sign 4 is Leo</note>
*   **Mercury:** 8s 6° 26' 40" <note>Sign 8 is Sagittarius</note>
*   **Jupiter:** 11s 8° 8' 4" <note>Sign 11 is Pisces</note>
*   **Venus:** 8s 15° 48' 54" <note>Sign 8 is Sagittarius; noted as 'direct' or 'on the path'</note>
*   **Saturn:** 2s 3° 13' 12" <note>Sign 2 is Gemini</note>
*   **Rahu:** 1s 4° 26' 6" <note>Sign 1 is Taurus</note>
*   **Ketu:** 7s 4° 26' 6" <note>Sign 7 is Scorpio</note>
*   **Ascendant (Lagna):** 6s 18° 20' 31" <note>Sign 6 is Libra</note>
*   **Midheaven (10th house):** 2s 10° 6' 52" <note>Sign 2 is Gemini</note>

In this example, within the three circles of the **First House** <note>original: "tanu-bhāve," the house of the body</note>, the Sun, Mars, Moon, and Venus are present. Because there are two auspicious planets <note>Moon and Venus</note> along with the others, the physical strength and joy of the body are of a middling <note>average</note> nature. Simi-

<header>Summary of the Great Parashara’s Science of Time</header>

### Summary of the Great Parashara’s Science of Time

...analysis should also be conducted regarding the future. In that regard, a planet provides particularly **auspicious results** <note>original: "shubha-phaladah"</note> when it is in its sign of exaltation, its own sign, or the sign of a friend. Conversely, if it is in its sign of debilitation or is combust <note>rendered invisible by the Sun's proximity</note>, it provides very little good and instead gives "stout" or heavy **malefic results**. This should also be understood regarding a planet being joined with or aspected <note>original: "drishti," meaning "looked at" by another planet's influence</note> by both benefics and malefics. Specifically, one should count the "quarters" of the **auspicious aspects**; if a surplus of auspicious aspect remains, a rise in good fortune occurs. If a surplus of **malefic aspect** remains, there is an increase in hardship.

In the **Ascendant** <note>the first house or the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note>, Mercury's aspect is valued at two quarters (2) because it is looking from a trine <note>a 120-degree angle</note>. Jupiter’s aspect is full (4). Venus’s aspect is measured at one quarter (1). Thus, the sum of these three auspicious aspects is seven (7). In that same house of the body, the Sun’s aspect is one (1) quarter and Saturn’s aspect is three (3) quarters. The sum of these two is four (4). When the difference between the auspicious and inauspicious is calculated, a **surplus of three (3) auspicious aspect quarters** remains. Because of this, the person possesses the good results described for the "house of the body" <note>original: "tanu-bhava," the 1st house</note>, such as a healthy and beautiful physique.

Similarly, in the **Moon's Circle** <note>the second concentric ring of the Sudarshana Chakra</note>, within the house of the body: Mercury’s aspect is three (3) quarters, Jupiter has no aspect, and Venus’s aspect is two (2) quarters. The sum of these is five (5). Additionally, the Sun’s aspect is two (2) quarters and Saturn’s aspect is full (4) because of the "ten-three" rule <note>Saturn aspects the 3rd and 10th houses with special strength</note>. The sum of these is six (6). Because Mars is in the same sign, its aspect is also full. The sum of the full aspects of the Sun, Mars, and Saturn is ten (10). The difference between these results in a **surplus of five (5) malefic units**. Since the Moon governs the mind, the person is deeply distressed in their heart.

Finally, in the **Sun's Circle** <note>the third concentric ring</note>, within the house of the body: the Moon’s aspect is one (1). Since Venus is in the same sign, its aspect is full (4). Thus, the sum of auspiciousness is five (5) <note>the text says 7, perhaps implying other factors or a typo in the original manuscript</note>. The aspect of Mars is two (2) and Saturn’s is four (4), totaling six (6). The difference is one (1). Because an auspicious surplus remains, the person is self-possessed and favored by the king. Such is the nature of the "Soul of Time" <note>original: "Kalatma," referring to the Sun</note>. For a more precise result, one should calculate the **mathematical minutes of the aspect** <note>original: "drishti-kala"</note> to understand the exact measure of fortune or misfortune.

#### The Temporal Investigation
<note>original: "Tatkalika-vimarsha," a method for timing when specific events will happen</note>

Starting from the house of the body, one should activate the years, months, and half-months. Starting from the birth year, assign **one year** to each of the twelve houses. Thus, the first cycle lasts twelve years. In the second cycle, the house of the body represents the thirteenth year, the house of wealth represents the fourteenth year, and so on. Through ten such rotations, the **lifespan of 120 years** <note>original: "vimshadhika-shatabdam-ayuh," the traditional full human life in Vedic thought</note> is completed.

In this way, having designated the house for a specific year, one should judge the results. If the lord of that house is joined by or aspected by auspicious friends, one should predict **good results** for that house. If joined or aspected by malefics, the predicted results will be difficult. Furthermore, if the Sun, Mars, Saturn, or Ketu <note>the South Node of the Moon</note> are located in the **angles, trines, or the eighth house** <note>original: "kendra-kona-ashtameshu"</note> from that "Yearly Ascendant" <note>original: "varsha-lagna"</note>, that year will not be favorable. If, however, these same positions from the Yearly Ascendant...

<header>Early Section: Chapter 51 on the Description of the Sudarshana Chakra</header>

If **benefic planets** <note>original: "shubha-grahas," planets like Jupiter or Venus that bring positive influence</note> are present, that year is considered desirable. However, the **Moon** <note>original: "Chandra"</note> positioned in the eighth house from the Ascendant at the time of birth is not desirable. This same principle applies elsewhere: one must judge the influence during the period of the ruler of that specific house and sign every year, and similarly throughout the months and days.

### Investigation of the Months
Next, the investigation of the months <note>original: "masa-vimarsha"</note>. The twelve months are to be understood from the twelve houses starting from the **current year’s Ascendant** <note>the rising sign at the moment the solar year begins</note>. Thus, at the start of the year, the first house is the first month, the second house is the second month, and so on for all twelve months. The analysis of the planets therein is the same as described for the yearly results.

### Investigation of Daily Results
Next, the investigation of daily results <note>original: "dina-phala-vimarsha"</note>. There is an option to increase the time by two and a half days <note>2 ½; 12 houses multiplied by 2.5 days equals a 30-day month</note>. From the house representing the desired month, one should assign two and a half days to each of the twelve houses. For example, the first house of the current month lasts two and a half days; by this calculation, the twelve houses complete thirty days. One should designate the "house of the day" as the **Ascendant** <note>the temporary starting point for analysis</note> and declare results for the twelve houses just as was done for the year.

Furthermore, in these yearly, monthly, and daily houses, wherever there is a conjunction <note>planets in the same sign</note> or an **aspect** <note>original: "drishti," the "glance" or influence of a planet from a distance</note> of a benefic or malefic planet, one should predict the person's tastes, food, dreams, and behaviors based on the nature of that planet, following the instructions of one's **Guru** <note>teacher or spiritual guide</note. 

Alternatively, there is a method of "one day per house." From the house of the desired month, one day is assigned to each house. Through two and a half rotations of this cycle, the thirty days of the month are completed. In that system, by dividing the two and a half day period into twelve parts, the result for one-twelfth of a day is 12 **ghatikas** and 30 **palas** <note>units of time; a ghattika is 24 minutes</note>. If using the one-day-per-house method, the twelfth part is 5 ghatikas. These calculations should be understood to start from the exact moment the year begins.

---

### Construction of the Wheel
Now, the meaning of the previous verse is explained: One should use a **compass** <note>original: "karkataka," literally "a crab," referring to the tool's legs</note> to draw three concentric circles, one inside the other, with space between them. This becomes the **Sudarshana Chakra** <note><term>Sudarshana Chakra</term>: The "Wheel of Auspicious Vision," a unique multi-layered astrological chart used to view the birth potential, the Sun's influence, and the Moon's influence simultaneously</note> consisting of twelve segments.

1.  **Inner Circle:** In the innermost circle, write the twelve houses starting from the **Ascendant at birth** <note>Janma-Lagna</note> along with their planets.
2.  **Middle Circle:** In the circle above that, write the twelve houses starting from the sign where the **Sun** <note>Ravi</note> was located at birth, along with the planets.
3.  **Analysis:** In all three circles, if **Rahu** <note>the North Node of the Moon</note> or many **malefics** <note>original: "papas," including the Sun, Mars, Saturn, and Ketu</note> are located in the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses <note>the "Angles" or Kendras</note>, the 5th or 9th houses <note>the "Trines" or Trikonas</note>, or the 8th house from any given house, that house suffers "destruction" or loss. 

Because Rahu and the Sun are specifically mentioned as prohibited in these positions, it follows by implication that if **benefic planets** are in those Angles, Trines, or the 8th house, that house prospers. In these three circles, a majority of benefics leads to greater auspicious results, while a majority of malefics leads to greater hardship. If the influences are gentle, the results are gentle. 

**Outer Circle:** In the circle above that, the twelve houses and planets are written starting from the sign where the **Moon** <note>Chandra</note> was located at birth... 9 <note>catchword for the next page</note>

# Now, the Sudarshana Wheel

---

## Now, the aspects of Rahu are described.

The great sages say that **Rahu** <term>Tamasa; the "dark" shadow planet</term> has a full gaze <note>original: "purna-drishti," meaning 100% influence</note> upon the fifth, seventh, and ninth houses from its position. It has a half-gaze upon the second and tenth houses. They declare a quarter-gaze upon the third, sixth, and fifth houses. However, when Rahu enters its own house <note>the sign it rules</note>, it is said to be "blind in its eyes" <note>original: "lochanandhah," implying it loses its ability to cast aspects or its influence becomes unpredictable</note>. [Verse 26]

## Now, the years of maturity for the planets.

The years of maturity <note>original: "udaya-varshani," the age at which a planet's potential fully manifests in a person's life</note> for the planets starting with the **Sun** are: 22, 24, 28, 32, 16, 25, 36, and 42 respectively. Whichever planet is in its own sign, its sign of exaltation, or is pure in the six-fold divisional charts <term>shad-varga</term>, in that specific year of the person's life, there will certainly be the attainment of happiness and the dawn of good fortune. [Verse 27]

## Now, the praise of the author.

In the auspicious city of **Jaipur**, there lived a Brahmin named **Jatashankara**, who was possessed of patience, depth, and valor, and was an expert in the science of astrology <term>Jyotish-shastra</term>. [Verse 28] He was like a moon to the lotus-pond of the **Dadhichi** lineage <note>a specific Brahmin community</note>. I am his son, named **Shridhara**, who is like the sun in brilliance. [Verse 29] 

With great effort, I have composed this summary of the *Vriddha Parashari* <note>The "Old" or "Great" system of the sage Parashara</note>. Because the complete work was not available in its entirety, I took the essence of the first part and rearranged it. Here, I have spoken fifty-one chapters from the beginning. [Verses 30–31] This first half, as spoken by the sage, has been brought to its conclusion. Having decorated it with a commentary, I offer it to the learned scholars. [Verse 32] May the wise accept this first section of the Parashara system, which acts as an eye for discerning various examples. [Verse 33]

Thus ends the fifty-first chapter, titled "Description of the Sudarshana Chakra," in the summary of the First Section of the *Great Parashara Horoscopy*, composed by Shridhara, son of the astrologer Jatashankara. 

The summary of the First Section is now complete.

## The Beginning of the Text

> **Maitreya said:** O Lord, you have already narrated the science of birth charts <term>Jataka</term> to me in great detail [1] through seventy-one thousand verses spread across eighty chapters. However, because the results of the planets are so intertwined and their movements so complex, [2] ordinary men are not capable of saying with certainty, "This specific result belongs to this specific person." In this current **Age of Darkness** <term>Kali Yuga</term>, the human intellect is diminished and men are prone to sin. [3] Therefore, they cannot grasp such a vast expansion of knowledge, nor is it practical for them.

Now, the sage **Maitreya**—the son of **Mitra**—having heard the detailed path of astrology mentioned in the first half of the work from the mouth of **Parashara**, recognized the condition of those born in the **Kali Yuga**, who possess duller minds and shorter lifespans. For their benefit, and desiring to know the essence of all birth-astrology through a more concise book, he questioned the sage again: "O Lord!" <note>The commentator notes that the word "Bhagavan" (Lord) implies one who knows "the creation and destruction of all things."</note>

<summary>The commentator Shridhar concludes his family history by explaining how he compiled and corrected the Parashara texts before introducing the first chapter, where the disciple Maitreya asks for a simplified astrological method suited for the limited intellects of the Kali Yuga.</summary>

<meta>On the previous page, the commentator Shridhar completed his personal lineage and expressed his humility before beginning the technical commentary on Sage Parashara’s work. This page transitions into the actual text, explaining the opening verses where the disciple Maitreya addresses the Sage and the challenges of practicing astrology in the current age.</meta>

<page-num>416</page-num>
<header>Summary of the Essence of the Great Parashara Horoscopy</header>

“He who knows both the origin and the end, the movement and the stillness, knowledge and ignorance—He is called *Bhagavan* <note>original: "bhagavan"; a title for a divine or holy being possessing six specific perfections</note>.” By using this title, the text implies that the Sage is perfected in these six characteristics. This indicates the Sage's capacity to provide appropriate answers to the questions asked of him. Furthermore, the use of the title *Bhagavan* at the beginning of the book serves as an auspicious invocation <term>Mangalam</term>, ensuring the successful completion and wide circulation of the work.

The text mentions "ten thousand and one thousand verses"—meaning it is composed of **eleven thousand verses** <note>original: "ekādaśa-sahasra-ślokaiḥ"</note>. These verses are the "limbs" that bind the subject matter together. To address any doubt regarding the difficulty of navigating such a vast work with many different sections, the text specifies that it is **"composed of eighty chapters."** These eighty chapters are divisions that clarify the various distinct topics. 

Through these chapters, the science of **Horoscopy** <term>Jataka</term>—which indicates the karmic fruits or results for living beings—has been explained in its entirety and with great clarity by the Sage. [1]

One might ask: "If the entire system of horoscopy has already been explained clearly, why is a new question being asked?" Four verses are provided to show the reason, beginning with the phrase **"Because of confusion..."** <note>original: "saṅkarāt"</note>. 

The first reason provided is the subject matter itself. **"Because of confusion..."**: The planets <term>Grahas</term> are so named because they "seize" or influence the body and mind. Because their movements are complex and mixed together <note>original: "gati-saṅkarāt"</note>, the resulting effects on life are also mixed and reversed. For this reason, regarding the statements made in the scriptures, humans are **not capable** <note>original: "naraḥ nālaṃ"</note> of saying with absolute certainty, "This specific result will happen in exactly this way." [2]

One might then ask: "Even if the work is vast, why is there an inability to determine the results?" The text explains this is due to a **deficiency in intellect**. It says: **"In the Kali Yuga..."** <note>The current historical age in Hindu cosmology, characterized by spiritual and intellectual decline</note>. Because people in the *Kali Yuga* are predominantly influenced by sin, their intellect is naturally small or diminished. Therefore, this vast work (the first half of the scripture) may not remain in continuous practice for a long time, and the goal of obtaining true knowledge of one's fate might not be achieved. [3]

**Translation of the Vernacular Section**—In this first chapter, the Sage **Maitreya** first asks: "O **Bhagavan**! In the previous section, you spoke of eleven thousand (11,000) verses contained within eighty (80) chapters..."

<summary>This page explains the opening of the text where the Sage Parashara's divine authority is established. It justifies the need for a summary or simplified system by explaining that the vastness of the original 11,000 verses is too complex for the diminished intellect of people living in the Kali Yuga.</summary>

<meta>The previous page established the divine authority of Sage Parashara and noted that while he has already explained the vast science of horoscopy across eleven thousand verses, there is a specific need for a more accessible method due to the declining intelligence of humanity in the current age.</meta>

<page-num>417</page-num>
<header>In the Later Section, Chapter 1 on the System of Eightfold Divisions <term>Ashtakavarga</term></header>

Through these verses, the entire science of **Horoscopy** <term>Jataka-shastra</term> has been described to me in detail. [1] However, the reason for asking once again is that due to the mutual mixing of the movements of the planets, the predicted results often become reversed or confused; for this reason, no man is capable of determining with absolute certainty that "such a result must be declared from this specific scriptural statement." [2]

Furthermore, the second purpose for this inquiry is that the "First Half" <note>referring to the *Purva Khanda*, the first major section of the Parashara corpus</note> is a very extensive and detailed work. In the **Iron Age** <term>Kali Yuga</term>, humans possess limited intelligence and are often burdened by sin; therefore, the study of such a massive text is not possible for them, nor can its practical application be successfully accomplished. [3]

## In the Golden Age, and for some in the Silver and Copper Ages, all were ##
## sharp-minded, meritorious, and long-lived. [4] Therefore, tell me that ##
## science which can be understood by those of limited intelligence— ##
## providing knowledge of the world’s course and the determination of the ##
## lifespan. [5] ##

**Commentary:** One might ask: "If that is so, how did this science remain useful and in wide circulation for such a long time?" To address this doubt, the text says: *In this...* In the **Golden Age** <term>Krita Yuga</term>, since all men were merit-seeking and devoted to righteousness <term>dharma</term>, they were long-lived. By this, the author shows how the text remained in circulation even if it was occasionally forgotten. The phrase "sharp-minded" <note>original: "kushagra-matayah"; literally "intellect as sharp as the tip of a kusha grass blade"</note> refers to those with subtle intellects arising from an abundance of merit. This demonstrates their capacity to understand the complex results described in the earlier texts. Such people also existed in the **Silver Age** <term>Treta Yuga</term> and the **Bronze Age** <term>Dvapara Yuga</term>, though not everyone possessed these qualities as they did in the Golden Age. Following the flow of time through the cycles of the ages, there was a gradual decline in merit. The **Iron Age** <term>Kali Yuga</term>, however, is entirely devoid of these virtues, as mentioned in the previous verse. The conclusion is that the "First Half" of the work was the primary authority during the first three ages, and this request for the "Second Half" <note>the *Uttara Khanda*</note> was made at the end of the Bronze Age to prepare for the coming decline. [3]

Having thus shown the reason for the application of the First Half and its transition, the disciple prays to the Sage regarding the subject of the Second Half, saying *Therefore...* <note>original: "Ata iti"</note>. Because of the reasons mentioned before, "tell me that science of **Astrology** <term>Jyotisha</term> which is accessible to those of little intelligence"—meaning a system that can be understood and known even by those with diminished mental capacity. What is the nature of that science? It provides "knowledge of the world's course." The "course" <note>original: "yatra"</note> of people refers to their journey through the experiences of happiness and sorrow. This science is that which contains the thorough knowledge of how these experiences come to pass.

<header>Essence of the Great Parashara’s Horoscopy</header>

In which science there is the determination of the lifespan—the certain determination of whether a life will be short, medium, or full; that is the connection to this science. [5]

**Vernacular Translation—** Then you might ask, how was this text utilized for such a long time, and why is it not used in the same way now? The author himself explains the purpose: O Great Sage! In the **Silver Age** <term>Treta Yuga</term>, the **Copper Age** <term>Dvapara Yuga</term>, and the **Golden Age** <term>Satya Yuga</term>, humans possessed a subtle intelligence, as sharp as the tip of a blade of grass <note>original: *kusha-agra*, referring to the sharp-edged Kusha grass used in sacred rituals; a metaphor for extreme intellectual precision</note>. They were meritorious and enjoyed long lives; therefore, they were capable of comprehending the "First Half" <note>the *Purva Khanda*, the massive foundational section of the Parashara corpus</note>. [4] For this reason, in this **Iron Age** <term>Kali Yuga</term>, please tell me a science that can be understood by men of limited intelligence—by studying which one might obtain knowledge of the world's joys and sorrows and the determination of the lifespan. [5]

### Parashara said—O Brahmin! You have asked well. O one of virtuous vows, I shall tell you that which provides knowledge of the world's journey and the determination of the lifespan. [6] Listen to that which ensures there is no contradiction, which brings the scripture to fulfillment, and serves the purpose of benefiting the people. [7] The twelve **Houses** <term>Bhavas</term>, from the **Ascendant** <term>Lagna</term> to the house of **Loss** <term>Vyaya</term>, yield results according to their names. When they are aspected by or joined with benefic planets, they are considered auspicious. [8] Houses aspected by or joined with malefic planets grant results other than welfare <note>i.e., they cause misfortune</note>. This is especially true when the planets involved are in their signs of debilitation or in enemy signs, and not when they are in their signs of exaltation or in friendly signs. [9] ###

**Commentary—** Thus, following the inquiry of Maitreya expressed in the first five verses, the Rishi of that name spoke and gave a fitting reply. The name **Parashara** implies "he from whom the arrow of grief [felt by his grandfather Vashistha] was defeated," or alternatively, "the arrow that removes the suffering caused by ignorance of the scriptures." At the start, he praises the nature of the question by saying, "Well [asked]." "O one of virtuous vows" <term>Suvrata</term> refers to one whose conduct and observance of rules are excellent. Therefore, "O Brahmin" implies one who is qualified to ask the highest questions. By you, well...

<page-num>419</page-num>
<header>Latter Section, Chapter on Ashtakavarga 1.</header>

# Latter Section, Chapter on Ashtakavarga 1.

He <note>The commentator, referring to Parashara</note> acknowledges the meritorious nature of the inquiry and promises: "Having honored the question regarding the knowledge of the world's journey and the determination of the lifespan, I shall answer by repeating those two very questions." [6]

He clarifies the previously mentioned point about providing an answer suited to the question. Regarding "the confusion" <note>original: *samkara*; referring to the overlapping or conflicting results of planetary movements</note>: he says that for the sake of establishing the scripture, he will remove the cause of failure mentioned in the verse regarding the **Iron Age** <term>Kali Yuga</term>, so that this science may proceed. Furthermore, for the fulfillment of the purpose, he removes the "lack of purpose" in your question within that same verse. He says, "Listen to that which I speak for the benefit of the people, to aid in the attainment of correct knowledge of results despite the confusion of planetary movements." [7]

He begins the promise "I shall speak" with a verse and a half starting with "From the Ascendant..." The twelve **Houses** <term>Bhavas</term>, beginning from the **Ascendant** <term>Lagna</term> and ending with the **House of Loss** <term>Vyaya</term>, are to be understood as giving results in accordance with their names. Those houses that are "aspected by benefics" <note>seen by favorable planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> or joined with them are considered auspicious and bringers of good results. Those same houses, if aspected by or joined with malefic planets, are to be understood as "bringers of other-than-welfare" <note>original: *kalyan-etara*, a polite way of saying "bad" or "inauspicious"</note>, meaning they give bad results. [8]

The meaning is this: The **House of Body** <term>Tanu Bhava</term> <note>the 1st house</note>, if aspected or joined by benefics, results in vitality and beauty; if aspected or joined by malefics, it results in leanness and ugliness. Similarly, houses like **Wealth** <term>Dhana</term> <note>the 2nd house</note> increase their fruits when joined by benefics and destroy their fruits when joined by malefics. However, there is a specific direction <note>rule of thumb</note>: benefics placed in the **Sixth** <note>House of Enemies</note> or **Eighth** <note>House of Death</note> increase enemies and death, while malefics placed there are the destroyers of those same evils. [8]

He explains the excellence and the exceptions to the aforementioned combinations in the latter half of the verse, starting with "Exceedingly." When those planets are in "enemy or debilitated signs," the houses they aspect or join (as mentioned before) are "exceedingly" bringers of inauspicious results. But if those same malefic planets are in "friendly or exalted signs," then the houses they aspect or join do not give bad results, but rather give only good results. [9]

**Vernacular explanation—** Then Parashara says: O Maitreya! You have asked an excellent question so that you may understand the happiness and sorrow of the people and the measure of their lifespan; I shall tell you this. [6] And regarding the first question you asked—that due to the confusion <note>original: *samkarata*; refers to the overlapping and conflicting influences of various planetary movements</note> of planetary movements there is a reversal of results—I shall speak of the non-contradictory method and its purpose for the sake of establishing the validity of the scripture and for the benefit of the people. Listen. [7] In this science, there are twelve places in the **Zodiacal Chart** <term>Rashi-Kundali</term> starting from the **Ascendant** <term>Lagna</term> and ending with the **House of Loss** <term>Vyaya</term>; these are the twelve **Houses** <term>Bhavas</term>. If these are aspected by <note>meaning "glanced at" or influenced by from a distance</note> benefic planets or are occupied by benefic planets, they give excellent results according to their respective positions. If they are aspected by malefic planets or occupied by malefic planets, they give unfavorable results according to their positions. [8] Furthermore, if those twelve houses are influenced by inauspicious planets situated in an enemy’s zodiac sign or in a sign of debilitation <note>the sign where a planet's power is at its weakest</note>, they cause great suffering. If those twelve houses are joined with or aspected by malefic planets that are in a friend’s sign or a sign of exaltation <note>the sign where a planet's power is at its peak</note>, then they actually provide auspicious results. [9]

### Thus, this has been spoken in general by the wise ones who know the **Science of Time** <term>Hora</term>. 
### I have spoken all this following the teachings of the **Ancient Teachers** <term>Purvacharya</term>. [10] 
### Determining the lifespan and the journey of the world is the purpose of this science. 
### To determine that with certainty, even the sages **Vasistha** or **Brihaspati** <note>The preceptor of the gods</note> are not fully able. [11] 
### What then of mere men, especially in the **Iron Age** <term>Kali Yuga</term>? 
### Especially regarding lost objects and the results of the **Decans** <term>Drekkana</term> and so forth. [12]

**Commentary—** With the intention of showing that the subject mentioned is not an invention of his own mind <note>original: *svakapola-kalpita*; literally "conceived in one's own cheek"</note>, he says "Thus..." The phrase "those who know the *Hora*" refers to the **Ascendant** <term>Lagna</term> and the science associated with it. Just as "the fruit of a mango tree is called a mango," <note>A traditional Sanskrit grammatical analogy used to explain how a science takes the name of its subject</note> those who know that are the "Seers" <note>original: *Suribhih*</note>, meaning the experts in the science of light (astrology). "In general" <note>original: *samanyatah*</note> means it has been spoken of in brief within the books they composed. "All this" refers to this very knowledge which "follows the ancient teachers"—meaning those who follow the instructors who originally taught the science of light.

<page-num>( 421 )</page-num>
<header>Second Part, Chapter on the Ashtakavarga, 1.</header>

In that manner, everything has been explained by me, Parashara, in the first half [of this period of instruction]. [10]

He speaks of the extreme difficulty of understanding this science, starting with the word "Lifespan." In this science—the **Science of Light** <note>original: *Jyotih-shastra*; refers to both astronomy and astrology</note>—the primary purpose is the knowledge of the measure of one's **Lifespan** <note>original: *ayu*</note> and the "journey of the world" <note>original: *loka-yatra*</note>, which refers to the people's wandering through the paths of happiness and sorrow. The cause and purpose for these two matters have been previously mentioned. **Vashistha** <note>a legendary Vedic sage</note>, who is the direct son of the Creator Brahma and my own grandfather, or even **Brihaspati** <note>the preceptor of the gods, whose name means "Lord of Prayer"</note>—who protects those eloquent in the Vedas through his mastery of speech and knowledge—even such figures as these are not capable of reaching a definitive certainty in these matters. [11]

What then of others? The implication is: how could men of small intellect and inferior minds be capable of making such determinations? Especially in the **Age of Quarrel** <term>Kali Yuga</term>, regarding lost or stolen items, forgotten things, and the results of the **Third-Divisional Chart** <term>Drekkana</term> and others—such as the **Seventh-Divisional Chart** <term>Saptamsha</term>—which act as indicators for happiness, sorrow, short lifespan, or the recovery of lost goods, they would not be capable of mastery at all. [12]

**Vernacular explanation—** This result has been described in brief by the ancient teachers; in that same manner, I have described it. [10] This science of astrology is very difficult to grasp. In this science, the primary goals are the knowledge of the measure of lifespan and the knowledge of the happiness and sorrow of the people. To determine this lifespan and the balance of happiness and sorrow, even Vashistha and Brihaspati are not capable. [11] Where then would ordinary men find the capability? Especially in the current **Degenerate Age** <note>original: *Kali Yuga*</note>, regarding lost, stolen, or forgotten items and their recovery, even using technical methods like the **Drekkana**, **Saptamsha**, and **Navamsha** <note>various divisional charts used to refine predictions</note>, as per the authoritative sayings such as "thieves are known through the Drekkanas," practitioners will mostly not be capable of declaring the results accurately. [12]

**->A wise person should hear this science from the mouth of a Teacher, following the tradition—one who is peaceful and possesses great intelligence in this science. [13]<-**

**->Just as the Veda is called twofold by those who know Ritual and Knowledge, so too the Science of Hours <term>Hora-shastra</term> is said to be twofold: the "Mixed" and the "Definitive." [14]<-**

<summary>Sage Parashara explains that predicting lifespan and the fluctuations of fate is so complex that even divine sages like Vashistha find it difficult, especially in the spiritually diminished Kali Yuga. He emphasizes that the "Science of Hours" (astrology) must be learned through a traditional lineage from a qualified teacher.</summary>

# The mixed portion has been spoken; now the decisive portion is told.
# He who understands this properly is called a Knower of Fate. [15]

**Commentary**—If one asks, "How then is this science to be thoroughly understood?" the teacher explains the method with the words **"of the teacher."** A wise student—one who is already well-versed in grammar, logic, and other foundational sciences—should hear this science from the mouth of a teacher <note>original: *guru*</note>. The meaning is that one is not entitled to study this on their own. In this way, one who has become "refined by labor" <note>original: *śrāntaḥ*; here implying intense dedication and practice within a tradition</note> through the lineage of transmission reaches the "ripening of knowledge." Based on the root "shram" meaning "to cook" or "to ripen," such a person becomes one of **great intellect** <note>original: *mahāmatiḥ*</note> or vast wisdom in this science. [13]

The author now demonstrates the equality of this science with the **Vedas** <term>the most ancient and sacred Hindu scriptures</term>. **"Action"** <note>original: *karma*</note>—referring to the performance of twilight prayers and other rituals—is known through the **Revealed Scriptures** <term>Shruti</term> via such injunctions as:
> "One should perform the twilight worship every day." <note>original Sanskrit: *aharahaḥ saṃdhyāmupāsīta*</note>
**"Knowledge"**—the knowledge of the Self—is also known through the Revealed Scriptures via such statements as:
> "Brahman is truth, knowledge, and infinity." <note>original Sanskrit: *satyaṃ jñānamanantaṃ brahma*</note>
One who understands those two is a "knower of action and knowledge." Just as the single Veda is spoken of as being two-fold by those experts in the divisions of action and knowledge, so too will I describe this science of **Horoscopy** <term>Horā-shāstra</term>. How so? The science of light <note>original: *jyotiḥ-śāstra*; astrology and astronomy</note> is spoken of as being two-fold through the two divisions of "Mixed" and "Decisive." [14]

He clarifies these two types in the following manner with the words **"The mixed portion has been spoken."** This means the "Mixed Part" <note>original: *saṃkīrṇabhāgaḥ*</note> was covered in the first half of the work. But now, the **"decisive portion"** <note>original: *niścayāṃśaḥ*</note> or the section of final determinations is being told and explained in detail. This also suggests the necessity of re-explaining certain points. He who knows this two-fold science—both what has been said and what is about to be said—properly and according to the method previously described, he alone is a **Knower of Fate** <term>Daivajña</term>. One who knows "Fate" <note>original: *daivaṃ diṣṭam*</note> is described as such. [15]

---

**Vernacular Commentary**—Now, regarding how the thorough knowledge of this science is obtained: Having heard this science from the mouth of a teacher, if one always exerts effort in studying it, then their intellectual skill and cleverness will increase more and more. [13] This science is equal to the Vedas; just as the Veda is of two types—the Path of Action and the Path of Knowledge—so too is the science of light...

<header>Chapter 1 on the Ashtakavarga in the Latter Section.</header>
<page-num>( 423 )</page-num>

It has been said that there are two divisions: the Mixed and the Decisive. [14] Within that, the "Mixed" subjects were described in the previous section. That which is the "Decisive" portion is told here in this latter section. He who understands these two divisions should be called a Knower of Fate <term>Daivajña; a professional astrologer</term>. [15]

->**Having thoroughly considered the meanings spoken regarding the houses, aspects, and so forth, one should collect those that are favorable and reject those that are contradictory. [16]**<-

->**From the divisions of life-span, and subsequently from planetary combinations, as well as from the "Eight-fold Division" <note>original: *Ashtakavarga*; a system of points used to calculate planetary strength</note>, one determines the results for the houses such as the "Body" and others through well-spoken results of the houses and other factors. [17]**<-

->**First, having understood the calculation, the positions, and the dots and lines <note>original: *bindu-rekhe*; refers to the scoring system in Ashtakavarga</note> of the divisions, one should declare the results of the "Eight-fold Division" separately and in order. [18]**<-

**Commentary**—He explains the method of achieving decisive knowledge for what was previously spoken as "Mixed." **"Regarding the houses"** <note>original: *bhaveti*</note>: The "Houses" refer to the "Body" <note>original: *tanu*; the 1st house</note> and others. "Aspects" <note>original: *drishtayah*</note> are those reaching the seventh and other positions as previously mentioned. By the word "and so forth" <note>original: *adi*</note>, he refers to matters like planetary strength and other technical details. Having thoroughly considered <note>original: *samyag-vicharya*</note>—meaning having analyzed with great subtlety—the meanings previously spoken, one should collect <note>original: *sangrihya*</note> those that are favorable <note>original: *samichinan*</note>. This means prioritizing factors that are beneficial due to an abundance of planetary strength. Those that are contradictory—meaning unfavorable due to the weakness of planets or the Ascendant—one should reject <note>original: *parityajet*</note> or set aside. [16]

Now he speaks of the method for declaring auspicious and inauspicious results. **"By the divisions of life-span"** <note>original: *ayurdayairiti*</note> and **"having understood"** <note>original: *jnatveti*</note>. By "divisions of life-span," it means having calculated the length of life via its specific mathematical divisions. "Subsequently, by planetary combinations" <note>original: *param yogaih*</note> refers to the many arrangements of planets, such as the celestial ones <note>original: *nabhasa-adi*</note> involving positions in two or three houses; the word "subsequently" implies those combinations that are extremely powerful. "First" <note>original: *adau*</note> refers to the calculation <note>original: *karanam*</note> and position <note>original: *sthanam*</note> of the **Ashtakavarga** to be described hereafter. One must understand that "dots and lines" <note>original: *bindu-rekhe*</note> are simply synonyms for these calculations and positions. From the Ashtakavarga, for the twelve houses starting with the "Body" <note>original: *tanu*; the self</note>, through well-spoken results <note>original: *suktaih*</note> and results considered purely through the houses and other factors, one understands the results in their entirety. Having thoroughly considered them, one should state the final result—the result obtained through certainty—after also knowing the characteristics of the divisions <note>original: *varganam*</note> to be described. [17–18]

**Vernacular Explanation**—Having considered the subtle strength of the "Body" <note>the 1st house</note> and other <term>Houses; astrological sectors representing areas of life</term>, and the planetary aspects reaching the seventh and other positions, one should accept the superior strength and discard the weak strength. [15] Next, he describes how to state the auspicious and inauspicious results: first, by having full knowledge of the span of life, the results of the combinations <note>celestial patterns like the *Nabhasa* yogas</note>, and the results generated by the <term>Ashtakavarga; an "eight-fold" scoring system used to determine the strength of planets</term>, and seeing their best strengths and weaknesses, the results should be declared. [17–18]

---

Five in the Body, Wealth, Longevity, the Third, and Loss; four in Desire and Happiness; three in Enemies and Fortune; six in the Son; two in the Sky; and one in Gain. [19]
In the Body, Wealth, and Death <note>the 1st, 2nd, and 8th houses</note>, the Ascendant, Moon, Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury [are point-givers]. In the Sky <note>10th house</note> and in Loss <note>12th house</note>, the Sun, Mars, Saturn, Moon, and Jupiter; in Loss <note>12th house</note> also Mercury, Moon, Venus, and Jupiter. [20]

[21]
In the Third, the Sun, Saturn, Venus, Jupiter, and Mars; in the Sky <note>10th house</note>, Jupiter and Venus; in the Son <note>5th house</note>, the Sun, Saturn, Moon, Ascendant, Mars, and Venus are the Point-Givers for the Sun <note>original: *Ravi*</note>. [22]

**Commentary**—He clarifies the inquiry into the <term>Ashtakavarga</term> system, which is included within the subjects of life-span and so forth previously mentioned, starting from the verse "Body" <note>original: *tanu*</note> until the end of the chapter. First, he states the fixed number of <term>Point-Givers; planets that contribute a beneficial mark or 'bindu' to a specific house</term> for the Sun <note>original: *Ravi*</note> in the twelve houses.

Regarding "Body" and so forth: in the 1st, 2nd, 8th, 3rd, and 12th houses, there are five **Point-Givers**; in the pair of houses for "Desire" and "Happiness" <note>7th and 4th</note>, there are "Oceans" <note>a poetic term for the number four</note> of **Point-Givers**; in the pair of "Enemies" and "Fortune" <note>6th and 9th</note>, there are three **Point-Givers**; in the "Son" house <note>5th</note>, there are six **Point-Givers**; in the "Sky" house <note>10th</note>, there are "Hands" <note>a poetic term for the number two</note> of **Point-Givers**; and in the "Gain" house <note>11th</note>, there is "Earth" <note>a poetic term for the number one</note> **Point-Giver**. [19]

Having stated the counts in the previous verse, he now gives their names in the following three verses. In the "Body" (1), "Wealth" (2), and "Death" (8)—in these three places—the Ascendant, Moon, Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury are the five named **Point-Givers** as per the previously stated count. In the "Loss" (12) position: the Sun, Mars, Saturn, Moon, and Jupiter (*Arya* means Jupiter, the rest are clear); these are the five. In the "Happiness" (4) position: Mercury, Moon, Venus, and Jupiter...

### Chapter on the Ashtakavarga in the Latter Section, 1.
(425)

Four [planets] are named as Jupiter and the others. In the 9th <note>Fortune</note> house: the Ascendant, Moon, and Venus. The Ascendant is the precise degree of the rising sign; others are clear. These three are the <term>Karana-pradas; "point-givers" or planets that contribute a beneficial point (bindu) to a specific house</term>. In the 6th <note>Enemies</note> house: the Sun, Saturn, and Mars. These three are the point-givers. In the 7th <note>Desire</note> house: the Ascendant, Mercury, Jupiter, and Moon. These four are the point-givers. In the 11th <note>Gain</note> house: He who is worshipped by the King of the <term>Daityas; a race of celestial titans in Hindu mythology</term>. The King of the Daityas is Vrishaparva, and the one worshipped by him is Venus; he is the only one. In the 3rd <note>Siblings/Valor</note> house: the Sun, Saturn, Venus, Jupiter, and Mars. These five are the point-givers. In the 10th <note>Sky/Profession</note> house: Jupiter and Venus—these two. In the 5th <note>Children/Intelligence</note> house: the Sun, Saturn, Moon, Ascendant, Mars, and Venus. These six are the point-givers. Thus should the point-distribution for the Sun be understood. [20][21][22]

**Explanation**—Now the auspicious and inauspicious results from the <term>Ashtakavarga; a system of "eight-fold" strength scoring</term> are described. In the Ashtakavarga, the primary knowledge is of the "zeros" <note>often called bindus or dots</note> and the "lines" <note>rekhas</note>. For this reason, we first describe the logic of the "zeros" <note>points</note> for the Sun and other planets. In this scripture, a "zero" is called a **Karana**. One should know that the Sun gives five **Karanas** <note>points</note> in the 1st house, 2nd house, 8th house, 3rd house, and 12th house relative to itself. In the 7th and 4th houses, it should be known as giving four **Karanas** each. In the 6th and 9th houses, it gives three **Karanas** each. In the 5th house, it gives six **Karanas**. In the 10th house, it gives two **Karanas**, and in the 11th house, it should be known as giving only one **Karana**. [19]

Having stated these quantities, the names [of the point-giving planets] are now given. Relative to the Sun:
*   In the **1st house, 2nd house, and 8th house**: the Ascendant, Moon, Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury are the five point-givers. 
*   In the **12th house**: the Sun, Mars, Saturn, Moon, and Jupiter are the five point-givers. 
*   In the **4th house**: Mercury, Moon, Venus, and Jupiter are the four point-givers. 
*   In the **9th house**: the Ascendant, Moon, and Venus are the three point-givers. 
*   In the **6th house**: the Sun, Saturn, and Mars are the three point-givers. 
*   In the **7th house**: the Lord of the Ascendant, Mercury, Jupiter, and Moon are the four point-givers. 
*   In the **11th house**: Venus is the single point-giver. 
*   In the **3rd house**: the Sun, Saturn, Venus, Jupiter, and Mars are the five point-givers. 
*   In the **10th house**: Jupiter and Venus are the two point-givers. 
*   In the **5th house**: the Sun, Saturn, Moon, Ascendant, Mars, and Venus are the six point-givers. 

Such are the point-counts and names for the Sun’s Ashtakavarga; the chart for this is also clearly shown. [20][21][22]

# Summary of the Great Parashara Horoscopy

In the houses of <term>Bhagya; the 9th house of fortune</term> and <term>Sva; the 2nd house of wealth</term>, there are six. In the houses of <term>Veshma; the 4th house of home</term>, <term>Mriti; the 8th house of death</term>, and <term>Hora; the 1st house or Ascendant</term>, there are five. In <term>Mana; the 10th house of honor</term> and <term>Dushchikya; the 3rd house of valor</term>, there is one. In the <term>Suta; 5th house of children</term>, there are four <note>original: "veda," meaning the four Vedas</note>. In the <term>Ari; 6th house of enemies</term> and <term>Stri; 7th house of the spouse</term>, there are three. [23] 

In the <term>Vyaya; 12th house of loss</term>, there are eight. In the <term>Aya; 11th house of gain</term>, there is zero. This is certainly the case for the <term>Shitakara; the Moon, literally "the one with cool rays"</term>. The point-givers <note>original: "karana-prada"</note> are the Ascendant, Sun, Mars, Saturn, and Venus; [and then] the Ascendant, Mercury, Sun, Moon, Saturn, and Venus; [24] Jupiter, Sun, Saturn, Moon, Ascendant, Mars; the Ascendant, Moon, Jupiter, and Sun; Venus, Mercury, and Jupiter; Mars, the Ascendant, and Saturn; and Venus, the Moon, and others. [25]

**Commentary**—Having thus stated the number of point-givers for the Sun's houses, the author now declares the number of point-givers for the Moon’s houses in one and a half verses, starting with "In the house of Fortune." In the 9th and 2nd houses, the number of point-givers is six. In the 4th, 8th, and 1st houses, the point-givers are five. In the 10th and 3rd houses, the point-giver is one. In the 5th house, there are four <note>the text uses "Veda" as a symbol for the number 4</note> point-givers. In the 6th and 7th houses, there are three point-givers. In the 12th house, there are eight point-givers. In the 11th house, there is "shunya" or a total absence of points. This should be understood specifically for the Moon <note>original: "Shitakara"</note>. [23]

Having stated the number of point-givers for the Moon, he now provides their names in the verses continuing through verse twenty-five. 

*   In the **1st house** (Ascendant): The Ascendant, Sun, Mars, Saturn, and Venus. These are the five point-givers. 
*   In the **2nd house** (Wealth): The Ascendant, Mercury, Sun, Moon, Saturn, and Venus. These are the six point-givers. 
*   In the **3rd house** (Valor): Jupiter is the only one. 
*   In the **4th house** (Happiness): The Sun, Saturn, Moon, Ascendant, and Mars. These are the five. 
*   In the **5th house** (Children): The Ascendant, Moon, Jupiter, and Sun. These are the four. 
*   In the **6th house** (Enemies): Venus, Mercury, and Jupiter. These are the three. 
*   In the **7th house** (Spouse): Mars, the Ascendant, and Saturn. These are the three. 
*   In the **8th house** (Death): Mars, the Ascendant, Saturn, Venus, and the Moon. These are the five. 
*   In the **9th house** (Fortune): The Ascendant, Sun, Mars, Saturn, Mercury, and Jupiter. These are the six. 
*   In the **10th house** (Profession): Saturn is the only one. 
*   In the **11th house** (Gain): Zero; there is an absence of point-givers. 
*   In the **12th house** (Loss): All planets <note>meaning all seven planets plus the Ascendant</note>, totaling eight. 

In this order, the point-givers for the Moon's houses should be understood. [24–25]

# The Essence of the Great Parasara Hora

In the twelfth and fifth houses, there are five <term>sharas; literally 'arrows,' used here to denote the count of beneficial points</term>. In the third house <term>vikrame</term>, there are four points <term>veda; a traditional term for the number four, referring to the four Vedas</term>. In the tenth house <term>kha</term>, there are three points. In the sixth house <term>kshate</term>, there are two. In the eleventh house <term>bhave</term>, there is zero (0). This constitutes the calculation <term>karana</term> for Mars <term>Bhumija/Bhauma</term>. ॥ 26 ॥ 27 ॥

**Vernacular Explanation—**Now the number of point-givers <term>karana or bindu; the specific planets or the Ascendant that contribute a beneficial point to a house</term> for Mars is stated:
Know that in the twelfth, fourth, fifth, and seventh houses from Mars, the number of point-givers is six. In the second and ninth houses, the number is seven. In the first <term>tanu</term> and eighth houses, the number is five. In the third house, the number is four. In the tenth house <note>The Hindi OCR reads 'second' (dusre) here, but the Sanskrit 'kha' and the logical sequence of the Ashtakavarga confirm it is the 10th house.</note>, the number is three. In the sixth house, the number is two. In the eleventh house, there are none at all. This describes the point totals for the twelve houses relative to Mars. ॥ 26 ॥ 27 ॥

*For Mars: the Sun, Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and the Ascendant are the givers. Then Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn in the houses mentioned. For the ninth house <term>dharma</term>, the list is as stated but without Mars. ॥ 28 ॥*

*The Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, and the Ascendant; then Mars and the Sun. Then Mercury, the Moon, the Sun, Venus, the Ascendant, and Jupiter; but in the eighth house, the same list without Venus. ॥ 29 ॥*

*Without Saturn, in the seventh and ninth houses; Venus, the Moon, and Mercury in the tenth <term>viyat</term>. The Sun, Saturn, Mercury, the Moon, the Ascendant, and Mars are the point-givers declared in order. ॥ 30 ॥*

**Commentary—**Having stated the number of point-givers for the houses relative to Mars, their specific names are now given through these three verses beginning with "For Mars" <note>original: "Kujasya..."</note>.
In the **First House** <term>tanu</term>, there are five: the Sun, Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus.
In the **Second House** <term>dhana</term>, there are seven: those mentioned for the first house (Sun, Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus) plus the Ascendant <term>Lagna</term> and Saturn.
In the **Third House** <term>sahaja</term>, there are four: Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn.
In the **Fourth House**, there are six: these are the same as those mentioned for the ninth house <term>dharma</term> below, but without including Mars. This means the Sun, Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and the Ascendant.
In the **Fifth House** <term>suta</term>, there are six: the Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, and the Ascendant.
In the **Sixth House** <term>ripu</term>, there are only two: Mars and the Sun.
In the **Seventh House** <term>jaya</term>, there are six: Mercury, the Moon, the Sun, Venus, the Ascendant, and Jupiter.
In the **Eighth House** <term>mrityu</term>, there are five: the same as those in the seventh house but without Venus. This means Mercury, the Moon, the Sun, the Ascendant, and Jupiter.
Following this, in the **Ninth House** <term>dharma</term>, excluding Saturn, the givers are the Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury... <note>The text continues describing the ninth house contributors as it nears the end of the page.</note>

...[Mercury, Sun, and Jupiter] are for Mercury. ॥ 32 ॥ Jupiter, Mars, Moon, Saturn, and the Ascendant; Venus, Saturn, and Mars; Mercury, Moon, Ascendant, Sun, Venus, and Jupiter; Mercury and the Sun; Jupiter, Moon, and the Ascendant. ॥ 33 ॥

**Commentary**—Now the author states the number of point-givers <term>karaṇa-prada; planets that contribute a numeric point or 'bindu'</term> for the various houses <term>bhāva</term> of Mercury. In the first (Self), second (Wealth), fourth (Happiness), tenth (Profession), sixth (Enemies), and ninth (Fortune) houses—represented by the numbers 1, 2, 4, 10, 6, and 9—there are "Fire" <note>In Sanskrit numerical notation, "Fire" (Agni) represents the number 3 because of the three sacred fires.</note> or three point-givers. In the eighth house (Death), there are "Hands" <note>Representing the number 2.</note> or two point-givers. In the third (Siblings) and seventh (Spouse) houses, there are "Flavors" <note>Rasa; representing the number 6 based on the six tastes of Indian medicine.</note> or six. In the eleventh house (Gains), there is "Void," meaning an absence of point-givers (zero). In the two houses of the fifth (Children) and twelfth (Loss), there are "Arrows" <note>Shara; representing the number 5, referring to the five flower-arrows of the love-god Kama.</note> or five. ॥ 32 ॥

Having thus stated the quantity of point-givers, he now names the specific point-givers for Mercury's houses over the next two and a half verses. In the first house, the Sun, Moon, and Jupiter are clearly the three point-givers. In the second house, Jupiter, the Sun, and Mercury are the three. In the third house, the Ascendant <term>Lagna</term>, Sun, Mars, Saturn, Moon, and Jupiter are the six. In the fourth house, Mercury, the Sun, and Jupiter are the three. In the fifth house, Jupiter, Mars, Moon, Saturn, and the Ascendant are the five. In the sixth house, Venus, Saturn, and Mars <note>original: "dharāsuta", literally 'Son of the Earth'</note> are the three. In the seventh house, Mercury, Moon, Ascendant, Sun, Venus, and Jupiter are the six. In the eighth house, Mercury and the Sun are the two point-givers. In the ninth house, Jupiter, Moon, and the Ascendant are the three. In the tenth house, the Sun, Jupiter, and Venus are the three. In the eleventh house, there is a "Void" or absence of point-givers. In the twelfth house, the Ascendant <note>original: "horā"</note>, Moon, Mars, Saturn, and Venus are the five. Thus, the point-givers should be understood in sequence for the houses of Mercury. ॥ 32 ॥ 33 ॥

<page-num>436</page-num>
<header>The Essence of the Great Parashara Horoscopy</header>

Excluding the Ascendant and the Sun, there are six contributors who give points in the first and fourth houses. In the second and seventh houses <note>referred to as *Sva* and *Stri* houses in the original Sanskrit</note>, there are seven contributors, excluding the Sun. In the ninth house <note>the house of *Dharma*</note>, there are seven contributors, excluding Mercury. In the tenth house <note>the house of *Mana* or honor</note>, excluding the Ascendant, Sun, and Mars, there are four: the Moon, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn. In the third house <note>the house of brothers, *Bhratri*</note>, there are four: Jupiter, the Sun, Mercury, and Venus. In the sixth house <note>the house of injury or *Kshata*</note>, there is only one: the Sun. In the twelfth house <note>the house of loss or *Vyaya*</note>, there are four clear contributors: the Ascendant, Moon, Saturn, and the Sun. In the fifth house <note>the house of children or *Suta*</note>, there are five contributors: Venus, the Sun, the Moon, Mercury, and the Ascendant. In the eighth house <note>the house of death or *Mriti*</note>, excluding Mercury and the Sun, the remaining six are the contributors. In the eleventh house <note>the house of gains or *Aya*</note>, there is an absence of contributors. Thus, the ancient teachers have understood the providers of these points <term>bindu; points used in the Ashtakavarga system to determine planetary strength</term> for Saturn. The calculation for the body-points <note>Tanukarana</note> will be explained in the sixty-fourth verse. ॥ 43 ॥ 44 ॥ 45 ॥

**Vernacular Explanation**—Now the number of those who give points <note>original: *karanabindu*</note> in the various houses relative to Saturn is stated. In the second, seventh, and ninth houses from Saturn, the number of contributors providing points is seven. In the tenth, third, and twelfth houses, the number of contributors is four. In the sixth house, the number is one. In the fifth house, the number is five. In the eleventh house, there are no contributors. Such is the count of points for Saturn ॥ 42 ॥ Now the names of those providing the points are stated. In the first and fourth houses from Saturn, one should know these six contributors: Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn. In the second and seventh houses, these seven are the contributors: Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, and the Ascendant. In the ninth house, these seven are the contributors: Sun, Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, and the Ascendant. In the tenth house, these four are the contributors: Moon, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn. In the third house: Jupiter... <note>The text cuts off here to introduce the table.</note>

<header>Latter Section: Chapter on Ashtakavarga, 1</header>

The Sun, Mercury, and Venus—these are the ones who give four points. In the sixth house, the Sun alone gives a point. In the twelfth house, the Ascendant <term>Lagna; the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term>, Moon, Saturn, and Sun—these four give points. The wise understand that the others <note>those not mentioned as point-givers in the previous section</note> are the "Givers of Position" (*Sthana-datara*). Now, I shall describe the planets for these positions for the easy understanding of the learned ॥ 46 ॥
Saturn, Mars, and the Sun give points in the second <note>Sva</note>, eighth <note>Ayu</note>, and first <note>Tanu</note> houses. Jupiter and Mercury give points in the fifth house <note>Suta</note>. Mercury, the Moon, and the Ascendant give points in the third house <note>Vikrama</note>. The Ascendant, Sun, Saturn, and Mars give points in the fourth house <note>Griha</note> ॥ 47 ॥ These same three <note>Mercury, Moon, and Ascendant</note> give points in the eleventh house <note>Aya</note>. In the twelfth house <note>Vyaya</note>, all planets provide points except for Venus. **Commentary**—Now, the author briefly describes the "positions" with the first half-verse starting with "The others mentioned." In the preceding section, those who were described as the "Givers of Points" (*Karana-prada*) are distinct; the remaining names should be understood as the "Givers of Position" (*Sthana-datara*). In this way, the wise understand "Position" (*Sthana*) as a synonym for "Line" (*Rekha*) <note>original: "rekha-para-paryayam"</note>. Having stated this briefly, the author begins to explain it in detail through verse sixty-three. Now, for the easy understanding of scholars, he names the planets that provide these positions/lines, starting with the verse "In the second, eighth, and first..." and continuing through verse forty-eight and a half. In the 2nd, 8th, and 1st houses, Saturn, Mars, and the Sun are the three who provide lines. In the 5th house, Jupiter and Mercury provide lines. In the 3rd house, Mercury, the Moon, and the Ascendant—these three. In the 4th house, the Ascendant, Sun, Saturn, and Mars...

<header>Summary of the Great Parashara Hora</header>

# ( 438 ) Summary of the Great Parashara Hora

The Ascendant, Sun, Saturn, and Mars—these four [contribute lines in the houses mentioned previously]. In the 10th house <term>Khabha; literally 'sky-house', referring to the Zenith or Midheaven</term>, there are six: Mercury, Moon, Ascendant, Sun, Saturn, and Mars. In the 11th house <term>Aya; the house of gains</term>, all are present except Venus—meaning seven contributors. In the 12th house <term>Vyaya; the house of loss</term>, there are three: the Ascendant, Venus, and Mercury. In the 6th house <term>Shatru; the house of enemies</term>, there are five: Jupiter, Moon, the Ascendant, Venus, and Mercury. In the 7th house <term>Dyuna; the house of partnership/marriage</term>, there are four: Sun, Mars, Saturn, and Venus. In the 9th house <term>Dharma; the house of fortune and duty</term>, there are five: Jupiter, along with the Sun, Mars, Saturn, and Mercury. <note>original: "अत्र एकवचनं पुंस्त्वं चार्षम्" — This note explains that the use of the singular masculine gender in the Sanskrit verse is an 'Arsha' usage, meaning an archaic or irregular grammatical form used by ancient sages.</note> In this way, the providers of lines for the Sun’s houses should be understood. ॥ 47 ॥ 48 ॥

**Vernacular Commentary**—Having thus concluded the decision regarding the "points" <term>Bindus; often represented as dots in the chart</term> for the seven planets beginning with the Sun, the author now explains the decision regarding the "lines" <term>Rekhas; in this specific system, these represent the complementary values to the points</term> for the Sun and others. Those planets who were not mentioned previously as point-givers are the ones who provide the lines. This has been stated in brief; it is explained in detail hereafter ॥ 46 ॥ Now, the positions (lines) in the twelve houses of the Sun are stated. "Position" is simply another name for the line. The names of those who provide these lines are as follows:

In the second, eighth, and first houses from the Sun, these three—Saturn, Mars, and the Sun—provide the lines. In the fifth house, Jupiter and Mercury provide lines. In the third house, Mercury, the Moon, and the Ascendant provide lines. In the fourth house, the Ascendant, Sun, Saturn, and Mars provide lines. In the tenth house, the Ascendant, Sun, Mars, Saturn, Mercury, and the Moon provide lines. In the eleventh house, the Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn, and the Ascendant provide lines. In the twelfth house, the Ascendant, Venus, and Mercury provide lines. In the sixth house, the Ascendant, Venus, Mercury, Jupiter, and the Moon provide lines. In the seventh house, the Sun, Mars, Saturn, and Venus provide lines. In the ninth...

In the **9th house** <term>Dharma; duty/religion</term>, there are two: Venus and the Moon. 
In the **10th house** <term>Karma; action/career</term>, there are seven: those mentioned for the 8th house and the 9th house, plus the Ascendant and Mars—specifically the Sun, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Moon, Ascendant, and Mars. 
In the **11th house** <term>Aya; gains</term>, all eight <note>The seven planets plus the Ascendant</note> provide lines. 
In the **12th house** <term>Vyaya; loss</term>, there is zero, meaning an absence of line-providers. 
Thus, the "places" or houses for the Moon have been stated. ॥ 49–51 ॥

# Summary of the Great Parashara Horoscopy

> The Ascendant, Moon, Mercury, Moon-sign-lord <note>original: "shashankakarya," referring to the dispositor of the Moon</note>, Saturn, and Venus; Mercury and Mars; zero;
> Venus, Sun, Moon, Jupiter, Ascendant, and Saturn. ॥ 60 ॥
> All except the Sun; Venus, Jupiter, and Saturn in the tenth house;
> All; and Mars, Moon, and Sun;
> These are the sequential point-givers for Venus, the son of Bhrigu. ॥ 61 ॥

**Commentary**—Now, the explanation of providing points <term>rekhas: benefic points used in the Ashtakavarga system to determine the strength of a planet</term> for the planet Venus is given, starting from the word "Lagna" through verse sixty-one. In the **first house** <note>Tanu bhava: the house of self</note>, the Ascendant, Venus, and the Moon—these three; in the **second house**, those same three previously mentioned; in the **third house**, those same three plus Mercury, Saturn, and Mars—making six; in the **fourth house**, those excluding Mercury—namely the Ascendant, Venus, Moon, Mars, and the Sun—making five; in the **fifth house**, the Ascendant, Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn, and Venus—making six; in the **sixth house**, Mercury and Mars—these two; in the **seventh house**, zero—meaning an absence of point-givers; in the **eighth house**, Venus, the Sun, the Moon, Jupiter, the Ascendant, and Saturn—making six; in the **ninth house**, all except the Sun—meaning the other seven planets; in the **tenth house**, Venus, Jupiter, and Saturn—these three; in the **eleventh house**, all eight <note>the seven planets plus the Ascendant</note>; in the **twelfth house**, Mars, the Moon, and the Sun—these three. These are the sequential point-givers for Venus <note>original: "Bhrigusuta," a common title for Venus meaning "son of Bhrigu"</note>. ॥ 59 ॥ 60 ॥ 61 ॥

# Saturn and the Ascendant; the Sun; the Ascendant, Moon, Mars, and Saturn; the Ascendant and Sun; ॥
# Jupiter, Saturn, and Mars; all except the Sun in the house of injury <note>original: "kshate," referring to the 6th house</note>; ॥ 62 ॥ the Sun; the Sun and Mercury;

**Commentary**—Now, the distribution of house-points <term>rekhas: benefic points used to calculate planetary strength</term> for the planet Saturn is explained via the two verses beginning with "Shanair..." In the **first house** <note>Tanu bhava: the house of the body or self</note>, there are two: the Sun and Saturn. In the **second house** <note>Dhana bhava: the house of wealth</note>, there is only one: the Sun. In the **third house** <note>Sahaja bhava: the house of siblings/effort</note>, there are four: the Ascendant, Moon, Mars, and Saturn. In the **fourth house** <note>Suta bhava: usually the 5th, but used here in context for the 4th/Lagna-Arka</note>, there are two: the Ascendant and the Sun. In the **fifth house** <note>Sute bhava</note>, there are three: Jupiter, Saturn, and Mars <note>original: "Jiva-manda-ara"</note>. In the **sixth house** <note>Ksate or Ripu bhava: the house of enemies</note>, there are seven: all planets excluding the Sun. In the **seventh house** <note>Jaya bhava: the house of the spouse</note>, there is only one: the Sun. In the **eighth house** <note>Mrityu bhava: the house of death/longevity</note>, there are two: the Sun and Mercury. In the **ninth house** <note>Dharma bhava: the house of fortune/religion</note>, there is only one: Mercury. In the **tenth house** <note>Karma bhava: the house of action/profession</note>, there are four: the Sun, Mars, Saturn, and the Ascendant. In the **eleventh house** <note>Aya bhava: the house of gains</note>, all eight—including the seven planets and the Ascendant—give points. Following that, in the **twelfth house** <note>Vyaya bhava: the house of loss</note>, there are four: Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus. This is the sequence of locations understood for Saturn. ॥ 62 ॥ 63 ॥ 

Having thus stated the houses where the planets grant points, the author now states the houses where the **Ascendant (Lagna)** itself grants points through the verse and a half beginning with "Tanau..." In the **first** and **fourth** houses, there are "fire" <note>vanni: a numerical code representing the number 3</note>—meaning three point-givers. In the **third house**, there are two. In the **second house**, there are "arrows" <note>shara: a numerical code for 5</note>—meaning five. In the **fifth**, **eighth**, and **twelfth** houses, there are six. In the **tenth**, **eleventh**, and **sixth** houses, there is "form" <note>rupa: a numerical code for 1</note>—meaning one. In the **seventh house**, all seven are point-givers except for Jupiter. This described form is to be known as the distribution for the Ascendant. ॥ 64 ॥

<page-num>448</page-num>
<header>Summary of the Great Parasara Hora Shastra</header>

# Summary of the Great Parasara Hora Shastra

The Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, and the Ascendant—these six provide points. In the ninth house, the Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Saturn, and the Ascendant provide points. In the tenth and eleventh houses, Venus provides one point. In the twelfth house, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, and the Ascendant—these six provide points. O Sage Maitreya! These point counts for the twelve houses of the Ascendant and the names of the givers have been told. || 65 || 66 || 67 ||

**O best of the twice-born, the "Karana" <term>karana: the mechanism or the planets acting as givers of points</term> for this Ascendant has been declared. Now I shall speak of the "Sthana" <term>sthana: the specific positions or houses where points are placed</term> of the Ascendant, O best of the twice-born! || 68 || Saturn, Mercury, Venus, Jupiter, and Mars; [then] Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus. Leaving aside Mercury and Jupiter, the rest [give points]. [Then] the Sun, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn. || 69 || Likewise, Jupiter and Venus [in the fifth]; all except Venus in the sixth; Jupiter alone in the seventh; and Mercury and Venus in the eighth. || 70 || Only Jupiter and Venus in the ninth; all except Venus in the tenth; and the Sun and Moon in the twelfth—this is declared as the "Sthana" of the Ascendant. || 71 ||**

<term>Commentary</term>—Now the author describes the planets that provide points based on their "Sthana" <note>positional favorability</note> for the Ascendant house, continuing through verse 71. After the explanation of the *Karana*, I shall describe the "Sthana," also known as the *Rekha* <term>rekha: a mark or "line" representing a point of influence</term> regarding the Ascendant. O <term>dvija-pungava</term> <note>original: "best among the twice-born"</note> Maitreya! "Listen to that" is the implied meaning here. 

In the **First House** <note>Lagna Bhava</note>, Saturn, Mercury, Venus, Jupiter, and Mars are the five point-givers. 

In the **Second House** <note>Dhana Bhava, the house of wealth</note>, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus are the three point-givers. 

In the **Third House** <note>Sahaja Bhava, the house of siblings/valor</note>, excluding Mercury and Jupiter, the remaining six—the Ascendant, Sun, Moon, Mars, Venus, and Saturn—are the point-givers. 

In the **Fourth House** <note>Sukha Bhava, the house of happiness/home</note>, the Sun, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn are the point-givers. <note>The text uses the syllable "Su" to represent the Sun (Surya), following the grammatical rule that a part of a name can represent the whole.</note>

In the **Fifth House** <note>Suta Bhava, the house of children/intellect</note>, these two, Jupiter and Venus, are the point-givers. 

In the **Sixth House** <note>Kshata Bhava, the house of debts/enemies</note>, all except Venus—namely the Ascendant, Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn—are the seven point-givers. 

In the **Seventh House** <note>Dyuna Bhava, the house of partnership</note>, Jupiter alone is the point-giver.
