# Chapter 11: Description of Lifespan in the Latter Section

This rule is applied everywhere regarding the calculation of the half-portion in cases of debilitation <note>original: *nicardhapakshe*; this refers to a planet at its weakest point in the zodiac, which reduces its "gift" of years</note>. Here follows an example of a calculation for a different period. Now, if the Lord of the Period <term>Dashapati: the planet ruling a major span of life</term> is the Moon, then the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term> is situated in a trine from it. Because it is in the fifth house position, the Ascendant’s enjoyment of a one-third portion is very clearly established. Because Venus <note>Shukra</note> and Mars <note>Bhauma</note> are in the "House of Happiness" <note>the 4th house</note> from the Moon, they enjoy a one-fourth portion. Now, we shall further clarify the placement of the aforementioned planets. 

When these planetary portions are converted to a common denominator, the resulting multipliers are 48, 16, 12, and 12 <note>these represent the relative weights of the Moon (1), Lagna (1/3), Venus (1/4), and Mars (1/4) scaled to a common factor</note>. These become the multipliers for the "Root Contribution" <note>original: *muladaya*</note>. When these are added together, the resulting sum is 88. This number becomes the divisor <note>original: *bhagahara*</note> for the root period values. 

The values of the Root Period are 16, 10, 4, 24, and 12 <note>representing years, months, days, etc.</note>. By multiplying these by the Moon's own share (48), the resulting total is 808, 7, 1, 21, and 36. Dividing this total by the divisor (88), we get **9 years, 2 months, 7 days, 51 minutes, and 23 seconds**. This is the Moon’s sub-period within the Moon’s major period. 

The Root Period of 16, 10, 4, 24, and 12 is then multiplied by the Ascendant’s share (16), resulting in 269, 6, 10, 27, and 12. Dividing this by the divisor (88), the result is **3 years, 0 months, 22 days, 37 minutes, and 1 second**. This is the Ascendant’s sub-period within the Moon's major period. 

When the Root Period of 16, 10, 4, 24, and 12 is multiplied by the share of Venus (12) and the share of Mars (12), the resulting total is 202, 1, 22, 60, and 24. Dividing this by the divisor (88), the result is **2 years, 3 months, 16 days, 57 minutes, and 54 seconds**. This is the sub-period of Venus, and the sub-period of Mars is the same. In this manner, the sub-periods for all should be understood.

**Translation of the Hindi Commentary:** Now the method for determining the sub-periods <note>original: *antardasha*</note> is stated. Here, by finding the individual fractions and a common denominator, one must multiply the total period by the specific portion and divide by the total sum of the parts; then the sub-period will be found. This example is explained in the Sanskrit commentary, and a calculation chart is also shown.

> If there is no debilitation, the calculation arises from the strength of the houses;
> This specific method is not remembered there if many planets are involved. || 37 ||

<header>Chapter 11: On the Description of Lifespan (from the Latter Section)</header>

The author explains the specific details. All planets situated in the angles and other houses—specifically those in the <term>Kendra</term><note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, representing the pillars of the chart.</note>, <term>Panaphara</term><note>The 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses, which follow the angles.</note>, and <term>Apoklima</term><note>The 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses, which are the weakest positions.</note>—respectively cause a reduction of one-half, one-third, or one-fourth of the lifespan. In this context, where there is an absence of the logic for the "common denominator" reduction <note>original: *haranabhava-sammatau*</note>, the remaining portion is granted as the lifespan. This means that the differences in the total lifespan are determined by these specific house intervals. || 38 ||

**Vernacular Commentary**—Now, the places where the "common denominator" reduction <note>original: *samaccheda*</note> does not occur are described. This method of reduction does not apply to the <term>Ashtakavarga</term><note>A system of points based on planetary transits relative to eight points of reference.</note> or <term>Amshayu</term><note>Lifespan calculated based on the fractional degrees (Navamshas) of the planets.</note> systems if a planet is in its debilitation sign. For this reason, if many planets are placed in these three specific types of houses, they grant the full lifespan. || 37 || All planets located in the <term>Kendra</term>, <term>Panaphara</term>, and <term>Apoklima</term> houses respectively reduce the lifespan by one-half, one-third, or one-fourth, and grant the remaining portion as the total life. || 38 ||

# All, two, three, three, and four; three, six, seven, eight, and two. || 39 ||
# These are the divisors for the lords of the Own Sign, Hora, Drekkana, Trishamsha, and Saptamsha; 
# Followed by the lords of the Navamsha, Dwadashamsha, Kala-hora, Shashtiamsha, and Shodashamsha,
# Respectively, for all planets to enjoy during the calculation of sub-periods. || 40 ||

**Detailed Commentary**—Now, the sequence for those who "enjoy" or consume the sub-periods <note>original: *antardaya-upabhoktru-krama*</note> is explained through verses thirty-nine and forty. The lord of a sub-period situated in its own sign <note>original: *svarkshe*</note> enjoys the full portion of the allotted time. If it is the lord of the <term>Hora</term><note>A divisional chart where a sign is split into two halves (30° / 2 = 15°).</note>, it enjoys half (1/2) of the obtained sub-period. Similarly, if it is the lord of the <term>Drekkana</term><note>A division of a sign into three parts (10° each).</note>, it enjoys a third part (1/3). If it is the lord of the <term>Trishamsha</term><note>A division into thirty parts (1° each), used for determining specific strengths.</note>, it also enjoys a third part (1/3). If it is the lord of the <term>Saptamsha</term><note>original: *adribhagapa*, the lord of the 1/7th division.</note>, it enjoys a fourth part (1/4). If it is the lord of the <term>Navamsha</term><note>The 1/9th division of a sign, considered the most important harmonic chart.</note>, it enjoys a third part (1/3). If it is the lord of the <term>Dwadashamsha</term><note>original: *arkamsha*, the 1/12th division.</note>, it enjoys a sixth part (1/6). If it is the lord of the <term>Kala-hora</term><note>The lord of the specific planetary hour.</note>, it enjoys a seventh part (1/7). If it is the lord of the <term>Shashtiamsha</term><note>The 1/60th division, used for extremely fine-tuned predictions.</note>, it enjoys an eighth part (1/8). If it is the lord of the <term>Shodashamsha</term><note>original: *kalashapa*, the 1/16th division.</note>, it enjoys a "hand's" portion, meaning a second part or half (1/2). In this order, all planetary lords of sub-periods enjoy their own portion in the arrangement of the sub-period system. This teaches both the sequence of the sub-period rulers and the sequence of fractional reductions for the allotted time. || 39 || 40 ||

**Vernacular Commentary**—If the lord of the <term>Antardasha</term><note>A sub-period within a larger planetary cycle (Mahadasha), used to time specific life events.</note> is in its own zodiac sign, the person enjoys the full lifespan granted by that period. If it is the lord of the <term>Shodashamsha</term><note>The one-sixteenth division, relating to vehicles and general happiness.</note>, one enjoys the second part <note>1/2</note>. In this manner, all planets during their respective sub-periods experience their own specific portions. This is known as the <term>Pachaka-krama</term><note>The "order of digestion" or distribution, referring to how planetary effects are processed over time.</note> of the sub-periods. || 39 || 40 ||

### In the Latter Section: Chapter 11 on the Description of Longevity Calculation

**Vernacular Commentary**—Now, the fractional portions of the twelve houses as determined by the planets and the <term>Bhavas</term><note>The twelve astrological houses or sectors of life in a natal chart.</note>, as declared by Lord Brahma, are described in the following verses:

The full longevity share is assigned to the first house; a half share to the second house; one-fourth to the third house; one-seventh to the fourth house; one-eighth to the fifth house; one-sixth to the sixth house; one-third to the seventh house; one-ninth to the eighth house; one-tenth to the ninth house; one-seventh to the tenth house; one-fourth to the eleventh house; and one-sixth to the twelfth house. These should be understood as the <term>Haraka Bhagansha</term><note>The fractional parts used as divisors to reduce the calculated lifespan based on house placement.</note> of the planets. ॥ 41-42 ॥

Multiply the longevity share by its own strengths, then divide that strength by the sum of all strengths. This applies to the <term>Ayavyaye</term><note>The 11th (Income) and 12th (Expenditure/Loss) houses.</note> houses and others starting from the third house. ॥ 43 ॥

The fractions for the remaining houses are declared as: full, two, three, five, four, three, five, and seven, applied in sequence. These portions are proclaimed for all the houses. ॥ 44 ॥

**Scholarly Commentary**—Now the arrangement for the remainder is explained: Regarding the two verses, for the two specific houses of income and expenditure (the 11th and 12th), one should multiply the longevity share remaining after reductions by its own strength and then divide by the total sum of strengths. The resulting value should be known as the nature of the <term>Antardasha</term><note>A sub-period within a major planetary cycle.</note> for the 11th and 12th houses. 

Similarly, for the eight houses starting from the third up to the tenth house <note>original: "viyadādiṣu tṛtīyādidashamamaryādeṣvaṣṭasu"</note>, the portions are: full, a second part (1/2), a third part (1/3), a fifth part (1/5), a fourth part (1/4), a third part (1/3), a fifth part (1/5), and a seventh part (1/7). The implication is that these should be applied. For the remaining two houses—the first and the second—the fractional portions that were mentioned previously should be understood as the form of the sub-periods. Thus, it is declared for all houses. ॥ 43-44 ॥

**Vernacular Commentary**—Now the fractional shares of the houses are explained. The decision regarding the twelfth and eleventh houses is that, after performing the <term>Harana</term><note>The process of reduction or subtraction in lifespan calculations.</note>, the remaining longevity share should be multiplied by its individual strength and then divided by the sum of all strengths. The result obtained should be known as the sub-period nature of the eleventh and twelfth houses. For the third house, the full share is used; for the fourth house...

<header>Latter Section, Chapter 12 on the Topic of Longevity. (615)</header>

When all planets are superior in strength, located in their own exaltation degrees, or in the division of the strongest planet; ॥ 
And when they are endowed with full directional strength and motivational strength, there are reductions by half for those in debilitation within the <term>Pindayurdaya</term><note>A method of calculating lifespan based on the sum total of planetary contributions.</note> system. ॥ 1 ॥ 
There are thirty-eight variations, which are properly adjusted according to exaltation and other factors. ॥ 
Based on the different positions of the planets located in the houses starting from the Ascendant... ॥ 2 ॥ 
...these are doubled, and eighty-four variations exist, O best of the twice-born! ॥ 
Due to variations in placement such as exaltation, the variations total one thousand five hundred and twelve. ॥ 3 ॥

**Commentary**—In this twelfth chapter of the book, in the commentary, may the granter of wisdom, the illustrious Ganesha, Lord of success and intelligence, always protect us. ॥ 1 ॥ The determination of longevity previously mentioned through the strength of the planets' rays and other factors is now investigated in detail by the Sage here in this twelfth chapter. ॥ 2 ॥

Now, the illustrious Parashara teaches the determination of longevity in the twelfth chapter through the variations of ray-strength and other factors. First, he counts the variations in <term>Pindayurdaya</term> with the three verses starting with "When all planets..." etc. In the <term>Pindayurdaya</term> systems—of which it was previously said, "The Pindayurdaya is declared to be of twelve types"—there are thirty-eight (38) variations where reductions are made by half for a planet in debilitation. For which planet does this apply? He says: when all planets are superior in strength, or when all are in their own exaltation degrees, or when a planet is in the division of the strongest planet (one possessing the most strength), and is endowed with full <term>Dig-bala</term><note>original: "Dig-virya"; Directional strength gained by being in specific cardinal points.</note> and full <term>Chesta-bala</term><note>Motivational or motional strength based on a planet's speed and retrograde status.</note>. 

Then, those thirty-eight variations, when properly refined by their own exaltation and other factors, become doubled in number, resulting in seventy-six (76). Furthermore, due to the different positions of the planets residing in the twelve houses starting from the Ascendant, there are eighty-four (84) variations. O twice-born <note>A term for a member of the upper three social classes in ancient India, here referring to the student Maitreya.</note>! Due to the influence of being situated in one's own exaltation, <term>Mula-trikona</term><note>A planetary dignity slightly less powerful than exaltation but stronger than being in its own sign.</note>, and so on, the variations reach "Suryesu-bhumayah" (1512), meaning there are one thousand five hundred and twelve variations. ॥ 1 ॥ 2 ॥ 3 ॥

<header>Summary of the Great Parashara Hora</header>

**Vernacular Translation** — Now the different variations of <term>Pindayurdaya</term><note>A method of calculating lifespan based on the "body" or sum total of planetary contributions.</note> are described. First, twelve variations of <term>Pindayurdaya</term> are mentioned. Following this, by applying a reduction of half when a planet is in its sign of debilitation, there are 38 variations. If these 38 variations are adjusted for factors such as the planet being in its sign of exaltation, they are doubled to 76 variations. By considering the combination of the positions of the planets according to the twelve houses, eighty-four variations arise. And, O Maitreya! Due to the specific placements of planets in their own signs, exaltation signs, or <term>Moolatrikona</term><note>A specific favorable position for a planet, similar to but distinct from its own sign or exaltation sign.</note> positions, there are 1,512 possible variations. ॥ 1 ॥ 2 ॥ 3 ॥

->***Selection of the Method of Longevity***<-

According to the relative strength of the planets and the Ascendant, O Brahmin, the methods are as follows: <term>Amshayurdaya</term><note>Longevity based on the divisions of the zodiac.</note>, then <term>Pindayurdaya</term>, and another called <term>Nisargayurdaya</term>. ॥ 4 ॥
The system called <term>Shatasvaramsha</term> is used for Mars; then there are the <term>Nakshatramsha</term> and <term>Amshaka</term> systems. The <term>Svaramsha</term> system is for another, as is the <term>Karadaya</term> method. ॥ 5 ॥

**Commentary** — Now, the author explains the adoption of the various systems of longevity, such as <term>Amshayurdaya</term>, based on the hierarchy of strength between the Ascendant and the planets, spanning the five verses beginning with "According to the relative strength..." 
"The Ascendant and planets" refers to the Sun and the other planets including the Ascendant. Among these eight <note>The seven traditional planets plus the Ascendant (Lagna).</note>, the calculation should be chosen based on which one possesses the greatest strength. 

O Brahmin Maitreya! The implication is that the method of longevity should be accepted in a specific order. That order is explained as follows: 
If the **Ascendant** (<term>Lagna</term>) is the strongest, use <term>Amshodbhava</term> (also known as <term>Amshayurdaya</term>). 
If the **Sun** is the strongest, use <term>Paindya</term> (Pindayurdaya). 
If the **Moon** is the strongest, use the method named <term>Nisargottha</term> (Nisargayurdaya). 
Similarly, regarding Mars: if **Mars** is the strongest, the system is known as <term>Shatasvaramsha</term>. 
If **Mercury** is the strongest, use the system known as <term>Nakshatra</term>. 
If **Jupiter** is the strongest, use the <term>Amshaka</term> system (meaning the <term>Navamsha</term> method). 
If **Venus** is the strongest, use the system known as <term>Svaramsha</term>. 
If **Saturn** is the strongest, the longevity calculation known as <term>Karadaya</term> should be adopted. ॥ 4 ॥ 5 ॥

**Vernacular Translation** — Now it is explained which system of longevity is to be taken based on whose strength. O Maitreya! If the Ascendant is powerful, take <term>Amshayurdaya</term>. If the Sun is powerful, take <term>Pindayurdaya</term>...

For a planet in its own sign of debilitation, the <term>Nisarga</term> method of longevity is to be used. For a planet in a friend's division, the <term>Shatasvaransha</term> method applies. For a planet residing in the <term>Navansha</term><note>The 1/9th subdivision of a sign, crucial for determining the true strength of a planet.</note> sign of its extreme debilitation, the system known as <term>Samudayashtakavarga</term><note>The "Collective Eight-fold Points" method, which looks at the total influence of all planets on a specific house.</note> is declared. In these methods of longevity, if a planet is positioned in its <term>Moolatrikona</term><note>A particularly favorable placement, similar to but distinct from exaltation.</note> or in a friend’s division, an "increase" (<term>Vriddhi</term>) should be performed according to the rules mentioned previously. By implication, placement in the divisions of debilitation or extreme enemy results in the previously mentioned "loss." Furthermore, in the same way, for a planet in a neutral or ordinary enemy division, neither the increase nor the reduction previously described are to be applied. ॥ 7 ॥

### Later Section: Chapter 12 on Determining Longevity

The following systems of longevity are to be applied in this order. These are: **Planetary longevity (<term>Pindya</term>)**; if the Sun or other planets are in their sign of exaltation<note>The sign where a planet is most powerful.</note> while situated in the Ascendant, this method is used. Likewise, if the planet is in a trine sign, the longevity based on its own divisions (<term>Svaransha</term>) should be taken. If it is in its own sign, the fixed longevity (<term>Dhruva</term>) should be taken. If it is in the sign of an "extreme friend," the <term>Prakramansha</term> method applies. If it is in a "friend’s sign," the longevity based on degrees (<term>Anshaka</term>) applies. If it is in an "enemy’s sign," the system of individual eight-fold points (<term>Bhinna Ashtakavarga</term>) should be used. Furthermore, if it is in an "extreme enemy’s sign," the collective eight-fold points (<term>Samudaya Ashtakavarga</term>) applies. If the planet is in its sign of debilitation<note>The sign where a planet is weakest.</note>, the <term>Karadaya</term> or <term>Anshaka</term> method is used. Now, if the question arises: "What if the planet is in a neutral sign?" the answer is that there is an absence [of these specific methods] in that case. If in an extreme friend's sign, take the **Prakramansha** method. If in a friend's sign, take the **Degree-based longevity** (<term>Anshakayurdaya</term>). If in an enemy’s sign, take the **Individual Eight-fold points** (<term>Bhinna Ashtakavarga</term>). If in an extreme enemy’s sign, take the **Collective Eight-fold points** (<term>Samudaya Ashtakavarga</term>). If in its sign of debilitation, take the **Degree-based longevity** (<term>Anshakayurdaya</term>). If in a neutral sign, understand that there is an absence [of these rules]. ॥ 9 ॥ 10 ॥

### Summary of the Great Parashara Horoscopy

For a planet situated in the fourth house, the <term>Dhruva</term><note>Fixed longevity calculation.</note> method should be accepted. For a planet in the sixth house, the <term>Bhinna-Varga</term><note>Longevity based on individual eight-fold points (Ashtakavarga).</note> method is used. Likewise, for one in the eighth house (the house of death), the <term>Samudaya-Ashtakavarga</term><note>Longevity based on collective or total eight-fold points.</note> is used. For a planet in the eleventh house, one may choose between <term>Pindya</term><note>Planetary longevity based on strength.</note>, <term>Svaransha</term><note>Longevity based on the planet's specific divisions.</note>, or <term>Dhruva</term>. If it is in the third, fifth, or ninth house, use **Planetary Longevity** (<term>Pindya</term>). If it is in the sixth house, use the **Individual Eight-Fold Points** (<term>Bhinna Ashtakavarga</term>). If it is in the eighth house, use the **Collective Eight-Fold Points** (<term>Samudaya Ashtakavarga</term>). If it is in the eleventh house, take one of these three: **Planetary**, **Self-Divisional**, or **Fixed**. If it is in the Ascendant (first house), use **Planetary Longevity** (<term>Pindya</term>). ॥ 11 ॥ 12 ॥

In the sixth, twelfth, tenth, or eleventh houses, the sequence involves the Sun, Moon, Venus, Saturn, Mars, Jupiter, and Mercury. Following the orders from Mercury, Mars, and Venus respectively, the results for mixed longevity systems are thus declared in order. ॥ 15 ॥

# Chapter 12: Section on the Determination of Longevity, in the Latter Part.

In these specific houses, <term>Jupiter</term><note>original: "Arya"</note>, <term>Mars</term><note>original: "Bhauma"</note>, <term>Mercury</term><note>original: "Jna"</note>, <term>Sun</term><note>original: "Ravi"</note>, <term>Moon</term><note>original: "Indu"</note>, <term>Saturn</term><note>original: "Manda"</note>, and <term>Venus</term><note>original: "Shukra"</note> are to be understood in this sequence as the providers of longevity. In the <term>tenth house</term><note>original: "Karma-bhava," the house of action.</note>, the method starting from <term>Mars</term><note>original: "Kuja"</note> is to be taken: 3, 5, 4, 1, 2, 6, 7. This is the meaning. Or, in the <term>eleventh house</term><note>original: "Labha-bhava," the house of gain.</note>, another sequence was mentioned first, and as an alternative, the sequence starting from <term>Venus</term><note>original: "Bhargava"</note> according to the previous order should be accepted: 6, 7, 3, 5, 4, 1, 2. In the house, Venus, Saturn, Mars, Jupiter, Mercury, the Sun, and the Moon are said to be the givers of longevity in this specific sequence. || 13 || 14 || 15 ||

### Longevity based on stars, on divisions, and on aggregate sums; the separate eight-fold system and the collective system;
### The systems of vowel-divisions are taught in sequence; I shall speak of these specifically and why they arise. || 16 ||

**Commentary—** Now the previously mentioned types of longevity are calculated: "Based on stars," etc. <term>Nakshatra-daya</term><note>Longevity calculated based on the position of the Moon in the 27 lunar mansions or Nakshatras.</note>, <term>Amsha-daya</term><note>Longevity determined by the planetary divisions (Navamshas).</note>, <term>Pinda-daya</term><note>Longevity calculated from the sum total of planetary contributions.</note>, <term>Bhinnashtavarga-daya</term><note>Longevity based on the individual eight-fold points of each planet.</note>, <term>Samudayashtavarga-daya</term><note>Longevity based on the collective points in the eight-fold system.</note>, <term>Shatsvaramsha</term>, <term>Svaramsha-daya</term>, and <term>Navamsha-daya</term> are the methods mentioned for "mixed" longevity. I shall explain specifically the variations that arise from these different methods of determining the lifespan. || 16 ||

**Language Translation—** Now the calculation of longevity is stated: Nakshatra-ayu, Tryamsha-ayu, Pinda-ayu, Bhinnashtavarga-ayu, Samudayashtavarga-ayu, Svansha-ayu, Shatsvaramsha-ayu, and Navamsha-ayu. The variations that arise from these systems will now be explained. || 16 ||

### There are thirty-eight unmixed types; then, by using the divisions of nine, twelve, and sixteen, 
### there are two hundred and twenty-one sub-varieties; there are exactly thirty types born of planetary rays. || 17 ||
### If two methods apply to the domain of a single planet, the result should be half the sum of those periods. 
### If there are three or more, the period should be determined by the sum and other mathematical totals. || 18 ||

**Commentary—** Now the variations of "unmixed" longevity are stated: "Thirty-eight," etc. There are thirty-eight primary types of <term>Amishra-ayurdaya</term><note>original: "Amishra-ayurdaya," referring to "pure" or "unmixed" systems where only one calculation method is applied.</note>. Among those, by using the <term>Navamsha</term><note>Ninth division</note>, <term>Dwadashamsha</term><note>Twelfth division</note>, and <term>Shodashamsha</term><note>Sixteenth division</note>, there are <term>two hundred and twenty-one</term><note>original: "Murchakshini-bhida," a coded numerical term meaning 221.</note> intermediate sub-varieties. Additionally, it is well known that there are exactly <term>thirty</term><note>original: "Trinshad-eva," 30.</note> types born of planetary rays (<term>Rashmi-ja</term>). || 17 || Now the method for accepting the periods (dashas) of mixed longevity is stated: "If for one..." If two systems of longevity are applicable to the domain of a single planet, the result should be "half the sum"—by adding the two periods together and dividing by half...

**Language Translation—** Now the variations of "Unmixed Longevity" (<term>Amishra-ayurdaya</term>) are stated. There are 38 types of unmixed longevity. When subdivided into the ninth (<term>Navamsha</term>), twelfth (<term>Dwadashansha</term>), and sixteenth (<term>Shodashansha</term>) divisions, these become 221 variations. Furthermore, there are thirty variations of longevity based on the "rays" (<term>Rashmi</term>) of the planets. || 17 || If there are two planets in one house giving longevity, one should sum their contributions and take half. If there are three or more planets, sum their longevity contributions and divide by that number. That is how the longevity period (<term>Ayus-dasha</term>) is determined. || 18 ||

बृहत्पाराशरहोरासारांशः ।
<note>original: "Brihat Parashara Hora Saransha" — Summary of the Great Parashara Horoscopy</note>

In the Earthly Combination (<term>Dhara-yoga</term>), the Lunar Combination (<term>Chandra-yoga</term>), and the Royal Combination (<term>Raja-yoga</term>), if these combinations occur and the Moon is strong, then one should adopt the Aggregate Longevity method (<term>Pindayurdaya</term>); thus says the sage Parashara. || 19 || 20 ||

# Parashara describes the Aggregate Longevity method for all Royal Combinations:
# When Jupiter is in the Ascendant (<term>Lagna</term>), the Sun is in the house of action (10th), 
# and the Moon is in the house of happiness (4th) or the setting house (7th) and is very strong;
# or when benefics are in the full trines or growth houses, 
# and the malefics are not situated in those aforementioned positions.
# || 21 || If the benefics are in the quadrants or the 3rd, 6th, and 11th houses, 
# and the others are in the opposite positions, then the Aggregate Longevity 
# method is prescribed. If the Sun, 
# Mars, and Moon are in the 12th, 8th, and 6th houses 
# respectively, the Aggregate Longevity method should be used. || 22 ||

**Commentary**—Now, the method for adopting Aggregate Longevity (<term>Pindayurdaya</term>) is explained through another approach—starting from "When in the Ascendant" until the end of the twenty-third verse. When Jupiter is in the Ascendant; when the Sun (<term>Bhanu</term>) is in the house of action, meaning the tenth house; when the Moon is in the house of happiness (the fourth house) or in the setting position (the seventh house) and is very strong and full; and in the trines (<term>Trikona</term>) and growth houses (<term>Upachaya</term>) <note>The text here uses a Sanskrit grammatical rule regarding compound words in the neuter singular: "sa napumsakam."</note>—meaning in the fifth, ninth, third, sixth, tenth, and eleventh houses. If a benefic planet is present there, or if they are situated in the positions mentioned here as "not situated," meaning they are in other positions such as the twelfth, the Ascendant, the second, seventh, or eighth houses. Furthermore, if the benefics are in the quadrants (<term>Kendra</term>) or the 3rd, 6th, and 11th houses—meaning if the benefics are in the first, fourth, seventh, tenth, third, sixth, or eleventh. And if "others," meaning the malefic planets, are in the "opposite," meaning they are in the other mentioned houses, then Aggregate Longevity (<term>Pindya</term>) is said to be prescribed. Additionally, if the "thousand-rayed one" (the Sun), the son of the Earth (Mars), and the "cool-rayed one" (the Moon) are situated respectively in the 12th, 8th, and 6th houses, then the Aggregate Longevity method must be taken. Likewise, if malefics are in the Ascendant, the eighth, or the seventh; or if benefics are in the sixth, the house of action (10th), or the twelfth house (<term>Nishfa</term>), provided no planets are in their signs of debilitation, then the period of Aggregate Longevity is prescribed. || 21 || 22 ||

If <term>Shringataka</term>, take <term>Svaranshayu</term>. If <term>Kalakuta</term>, take <term>Rashmayu</term>. || 31 || 

An alternative method is described: If the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> falls in the first <term>Dreshkana</term>, take <term>Pindya</term>. In the second <term>Dreshkana</term>, take <term>Dhruva</term>. In the third <term>Dreshkana</term>, take <term>Svaransha</term>. <header>Summary of the Great Parashara Hora</header>

### ( 630 ) Summary of the Great Parashara Hora

The Pindya method, known as <term>Pindayurdaya</term> <note>a system of longevity based on the summation of planetary influences</note>, is prescribed and determined in a specific order. Similarly, for the numbers 25 (representing the *Tattvas* or elements), 39 (the *Nanda-Agnis*), 29 (the *Ratna-Dasras*), and 23 (the *Tri-Dasras*), the four variations of <term>Dhruvayurdaya</term> <note>fixed-longevity constants</note> are to be accepted in sequence. 

Regarding the range of "one to three"—meaning starting from one ray up to three rays (1, 2, 3)—the method known as <term>Samudaya</term>, specifically the <term>Samudayashtakavargayu</term> <note>longevity based on the collective eight-fold strength chart</note>, should be used. Following that, if there are 4 rays (represented by the word *Veda*), the other <term>Ashtakavarga</term>, meaning the <term>Bhinnashtakavarga</term> <note>the individual eight-fold strength chart</note>, is to be accepted. 

For rays numbering five and above—specifically 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10—the <term>Anshadayu</term> <note>longevity based on divisional portions or Navamshas</note> system is spoken of. If the rays are 11 (the *Rudras*) or 12 (the *Suryas*), then the first <term>Pindya</term> method should be taken. Similarly, for 13 (the *Vishves*) or 14 (the *Manus*) rays, the <term>Svarabhagayu</term> <note>longevity based on sound-vibration portions</note> or <term>Svaranshayurdaya</term> should be used. 

If the ray count is 15 (the *Tithis* or lunar days), the <term>Nakshatradayu</term> <note>longevity based on the 27 lunar mansions</note> is to be taken. For 16 rays (the *Nripas* or kings) and the "Atyashti-three"—meaning 17, 18, and 19 rays—the primary variations of the <term>Pindayurdaya</term> should be accepted. For 20 rays, follow the established order. For 38 rays, the method born of <term>Ashtakavarga</term> is to be used. In the case of the "forty-three"—meaning where the rays are 40, 41, or 42—the <term>Pindya</term> method is taken. 

Furthermore, for the next three numbers—43, 44, and 45—the <term>Nakshatransha</term> <note>portion based on lunar mansions</note> should be taken. For the remaining counts—22, 28, 46, 47, 48, and 49—it should be the <term>Pindya</term> system, meaning its first six variations. 

The sage <term>Garga</term> <note>a legendary ancient astronomer and sage</note> told me that this system of longevity based on rays is determined by the specific count of rays desired. This sequence is stated to be most powerful; while the previous rules applied to the <term>Kendras</term> <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a chart</note> and other positions, this specific sequence of <term>Rashmi-ayurdaya</term> <note>ray-based longevity</note> is declared when there are additional rays in other positions. || 33-39 ||

**Vernacular Explanation**—Now, the different methods for determining longevity according to the theory of Rays (*Rashmi*) are explained. If at the time of birth the Ray count is any of these: 30, 34, 37, 33, 32, 31, 36, 35, 27, 26, 12, or 24—then the <term>Pindayurdaya</term> system should be taken. Also for 25, 39, 29...

<header>Chapter 12: Section on the Determination of Longevity in the Later Part</header>

## Chapter 12: Section on the Determination of Longevity in the Later Part

If there are 33 rays, one should adopt <term>Dhruvayushya</term> <note>a system of fixed or constant longevity values</note>. If there are 11, 12, or 13 rays, one should adopt <term>Samudayashtakavargayu</term> <note>longevity calculated from the collective or "total" eight-fold strength chart</note>. If there are 14 rays, one should adopt <term>Bhinnashtakavarga</term> <note>longevity calculated from the "individual" or separate charts of the planets</note>. If there are 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, or 10 <note>The number 10 appears here in the source text, though it follows 19 in the sequence</note> rays, one should adopt <term>Anshayayu</term> <note>longevity based on divisional portions or Navamshas</note>. If there are 11 or 12 rays, one should take the first <term>Pindayu</term> <note>a method based on the planets' summation of influence</note>. If there are 13 or 14 rays, one should adopt <term>Svaranshayu</term> <note>longevity calculated through a specific division of "vowel-sounds" or portions</note>. If there are 15 rays, one should adopt <term>Nakshatrayu</term> <note>longevity determined by the lunar mansions</note>. If there are 16, 17, 18, or 19 rays, one should take the first <term>Pindayushya</term>. If there are 20 rays, one should adopt <term>Prakramayu</term> <note>longevity based on a specific "progression" or sequence</note>. If there are 38 rays, one should adopt <term>Ashtakavargayu</term>. If there are 40, 41, or 42 rays, one should adopt <term>Pindayu</term>. If there are 43, 44, or 45 rays, one should adopt <term>Nakshatrayu</term>. If there are 22, 28, 46, 47, 48, or 49 rays, one should adopt <term>Paindacyu</term> <note>a derivative of the Pindya calculation system</note>. This "Longevity by Rays" (<term>Rashmyayurdaya</term>) was taught to me by the Sage Garga. ॥ 33-39 ॥

-> Depending on the superiority of strength and the influence of planetary positions, <-
-> And in the sequence of desired results, the method of Rays is applied accordingly. ॥ 40 ॥
-> At the beginning of the <term>Kalpa</term> <note>a vast cosmic age in Hindu cosmology</note>, the Lord Garga, the great sage, appeared; <-
-> Taking refuge in the wisdom of the <term>Kali Age</term> <note>the current age of spiritual decline</note>, he spoke the entire science of horoscopy to the Rishis. ॥ 41 ॥
-> Whatever has not been spoken by me in this Later Section, <-
-> O Maitreya, you should look for all of that within the <term>Garga Hora</term> <note>The specialized astrological treatise attributed to Sage Garga</note>. ॥ 42 ॥

### Thus ends the twelfth chapter, titled "The Section on Longevity," 
### in the Later Section of the Great Parashara Hora Shastra. ॥ 12 ॥

**Commentary**—Now he repeats what has been stated: "Depending on the superiority of strength," etc. This means that by the gradation of superior strength, and by the influence of different positions—such as being in one's own, a friend's, or an enemy's sign—and by the sequence of desired or difficult results, and through the method prescribed by the Rays, I have thus explained the determination of longevity in its proper order. ॥ 40 ॥ Here, he again cites Garga as the authority: "At the beginning of the Kalpa," etc. The Lord Garga, at the beginning of the cosmic age...

The great sage, a deep thinker who knows the past, present, and future, appeared. Taking refuge in the <term>Kali Age</term> <note>The current historical epoch in Hindu chronology, characterized by spiritual decline</note>, he spoke the entire science of birth-charts to the sages who were his disciples, based on the specific results applicable to the Kali era. Regarding the phrase "he will surely speak while taking refuge in the Kali age," the connection is this: having appeared at the beginning of the <term>Kalpa</term> <note>an immense cycle of time</note>, what he previously said may have become corrupted or obscured through a succession of ignorant teachers over a vast period of time; therefore, fearing such impurity, he appeared again in the Kali age to speak/explain it. Everything else remains the same. || 41 || Now, he completes what was left unsaid by referring to the treatise of Garga: "In this..." In this latter part, whatever may not have been spoken or told by me for fear of being too long, "O Maitreya! You should look at and see all of that in detail in the <term>Garga-hora</term> <note>The astrological treatise attributed to the Sage Garga</note>." || 42 ||

In this way, according to my intellect, this commentary has been made for the pleasure of Lord Ganesha. This work should be refined by the best of the wise out of their kindness. || 1 || Thus ends the twelfth chapter in the *Subodhini* commentary composed by the astrologer Shridhara—the son of Jatashankara, who illuminated the ten directions with the flawless knowledge gained from studying the Vedas and Shastras in the lineage of the Dhyangas—within the latter part of the *Shri Brihat Parashara Hora*. || 12 ||

Whatever I have not spoken in this latter part, you should see all of that in the *Garga-hora*. || 42 ||

## Latter Section: Chapter 13 on the Results of Planetary Portions and Other Factors

**Commentary—** I am clearly explaining the thirteenth chapter to the best of my intellectual power, inspired by the grace of <term>Lord Ganesha</term> <note>The elephant-headed deity traditionally invoked at the beginning of Hindu texts to remove obstacles</note>. || 1 || In this thirteenth chapter, the Great Sage has told <term>Maitreya</term> <note>The sage's disciple and the primary interlocutor of this text</note> about "Fortune," <term>Kalāṃśa</term> <note>A technical division of a zodiac sign used for fine-tuned predictions</note>, and their results in great detail. || 2 ||

Now the Blessed Sage Parashara promises to speak in this thirteenth chapter about the investigation of Fortune and other matters, which are the means of achieving happiness in all worldly dealings—starting with the two verses on "Fortune." O Maitreya of good vows! I shall speak to you about Fortune, prosperity, and <term>Karma</term> <note>original: "karma"; here referring to deeds, business, or conduct</note>, both good and bad, in this chapter. "Listen and pay attention"—this address is meant to focus the listener's mind, because success in all human endeavors comes only from Fortune. From Fortune comes wealth and <term>Ayati</term> <note>original: "āyatiḥ"; referring to influence, dignity, or future prospects</note>. From Fortune alone comes fame. Through the reversal of Fortune—that is, misfortune—all these things are destroyed. Therefore, whether the actions one is about to perform indicate fortune or cause misfortune must be known through diligent study. Thus, the Sage promises: "I shall explain that knowledge." || 1 || 2 ||

**Vernacular Summary—** O Maitreya! Now I describe prosperity and good or bad business. The attainment of wealth and fame—all this happens through the "Rising of Fortune"; therefore, I describe the characteristics of how Fortune arises. || 1 || 2 ||

> The ninth house from the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>original: "lagna"; the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note> and from the Moon is considered the House of Fortune, depending on the strength of the planets. It produces good or bad results according to the planets classified as "benefics," "malefics," "enemies," or "friends." || 3 ||
> 
> Growth is expected when a planet is in its fivefold states of <term>Exaltation</term> <note>original: "uccādi-pañcaka"; refers to the five essential dignities of a planet, such as being in its sign of exaltation, its own sign, etc.</note> and so on; from other placements, loss is expected. This applies to one's own affairs or those of others, and within one's own country or in foreign lands. || 4 ||

**Commentary—** Now he explains the method for investigating Fortune in the four and a half verses beginning with "From the Ascendant..." The "House of Fortune" should be understood as the ninth house from the Ascendant and from the Moon. This house becomes the cause of more or less fortune according to the gradation of planetary strength. Similarly, it is influenced by those called "benefics" (gentle planets), "malefics" (cruel planets), and "enemies"...

The increase or decrease of fortune occurs through those planets designated as "enemies," "friends," or "neutrals." Thus, in the matter of fortune, through connection with the "five-fold status"—namely **Exaltation**, <term>Mūlatrikoṇa</term> <note>A highly favorable "root trine" position for a planet, slightly less powerful than exaltation but stronger than its own sign</note>, **Own Sign**, **Friend**, and **Great Friend**—and through benefic or malefic planets situated in the house of fortune, or those acting as indicators of fortune, it is meant that fortune increases. 

Similarly, through connection with others—such as **Neutral**, **Enemy**, **Great Enemy**, and **Debilitation**—all planets situated in the house of fortune cause the destruction or loss of fortune. Likewise, if the "Lord of Fortune" <note>The planet that rules the ninth house from the ascendant</note> is in his own domain, or if he is in a different domain or a different field, there is the attainment of fortune in one's own country or another country respectively. 

Or, O <term>Jyotirvid</term> <note>An astrologer, literally "knower of light"</note> Maitreya! Fortune should be understood to occur in one's own country if planets in the house of fortune are placed in their own <term>Dashavargas</term> <note>A system of ten specific divisions of a zodiac sign used to measure planetary strength</note> (calculated by the ten-fold division); if they are placed in others' divisions, fortune should be known to manifest in a foreign land. || 3 || 4 ||

However, one should predict the increase or decrease of fortune only after observing the strength and weakness therein. If a planet is in the house of fortune while in its exaltation, own house, friendly sign, great friend's sign, or its "root trine," then know there will be an increase in fortune. If it sits in the house of fortune while in debilitation, an enemy’s sign, a great enemy’s sign, or a neutral sign, know there will be a loss of fortune. Furthermore, if the Lord of Fortune is in its own division, the rise of fortune will be in one's own country; if it is in another's division, the rise of fortune will be in a foreign land. || 3 || 4 ||

Therefore—

<header>Chapter 13: On the Results of the Kalāṃśa and Other Divisions</header>

# Chapter 13: Results of the Kalāṃśa and Other Divisions from the Second Section

The author explains the <term>Saptāṃśa</term> <note>The 1/7th division of a sign, traditionally used to understand children and grandchildren</note> beginning with the phrase "Agransha" and continuing to the end. Regarding the <term>Saptāṃśa</term>: take the minutes (<term>liptā</term>) <note>A minute of arc; there are 60 minutes in one degree</note> of the sign's position, and divide those minutes by seven; this is declared to be the <term>Saptāṃśa</term>. 

Next, he describes the <term>Ṣoḍaśāṃśa</term> <note>The 1/16th division, used for matters of vehicles, comforts, and general happiness</note>: divide the 1800 minutes <note>A full zodiac sign consists of 30 degrees, which equals 1800 minutes</note> of a sign by sixteen; this is known as the <term>Kalāṃśa</term> or <term>Ṣoḍaśāṃśa</term>. 

Regarding the <term>Ṣaṣṭyaṃśa</term> <note>The 1/60th division, a highly refined subdivision used for precise predictions</note>: divide the minutes of a sign by sixty; that alone is the <term>Ṣaṣṭyaṃśa</term>. By following this sequence, the lords of the divisions are determined. 

Now, he offers an alternative method for the <term>Ṣoḍaśāṃśa</term>: in a civil day (<term>sāvana divasa</term>), divide the zodiac by twenty-seven; this is also called the <term>Kalāṃśa</term> or <term>Ṣoḍaśāṃśa</term>. He mentions another view held by different teachers: the 1/60th part of a sign is also traditionally called <term>Kalāṃśa</term> or <term>Ṣoḍaśāṃśa</term>. || 5 || 6 || 7 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** Now the <term>Saptāṃśa</term>, <term>Ṣoḍaśāṃśa</term>, and <term>Ṣaṣṭyaṃśa</term> are explained. Convert the degrees of a sign into minutes and divide by seven. The resulting portion is the <term>Saptāṃśa</term>. Dividing the 1800 minutes of a sign by sixteen is called <term>Ṣoḍaśāṃśa</term>. Dividing the minutes of a sign by sixty is called <term>Ṣaṣṭyaṃśa</term>. Dividing the zodiac by twenty-seven according to the civil day is also called <term>Ṣoḍaśāṃśa</term>. || 5 || 6 || 7 ||

> Likewise, through malefic planets, one's fortune becomes inauspicious; however, through friends and other specific relations, there is a distinct rule. || 8 ||

**Commentary—** He explains the results starting with the phrase "from fortune" (<term>bhāgyāt</term>). From the ninth house (the house of fortune) relative to both the Ascendant and the Moon: if benefic planets occupy the trines (<term>trikoṇa</term>—the 5th and 9th positions) or the angles (<term>kendra</term>—the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th positions), then fortune will be auspicious, meaning an increase in prosperity. 

Similarly, if malefic planets occupy those trine or angular positions relative to the ninth house from the Ascendant or the Moon, fortune becomes inauspicious, meaning a loss of fortune. However, due to "friends and others"—meaning a planet's connection to its friend's sign, its own sign, or its sign of exaltation—there is an exception to the rule mentioned previously. In such cases, even a malefic planet situated there [can provide specific benefits].

<header>Summary of the Great Parashara Horoscopy</header>

The increase of fortune <note>original: "bhāgya-vṛddhi"</note> occurs because a planet is situated in a friendly sign and similar favorable positions. In this manner, one should describe the reversal of fortune, the increase of fortune, or the loss of fortune related to the various houses <note>original: "bhāvas"</note> according to the principles mentioned. || 8 ||

**Vernacular Translation—**Now, the specific results of the house of fortune <note>The Ninth House, representing luck, grace, and destiny</note> are explained. If there are benefic planets <note>Planets like Jupiter, Venus, or a waxing Moon that bring positive influences</note> in the 1st, 4th, 5th, 7th, 9th, or 10th houses from either the Ascendant or the Moon, one should know that the rise of fortune will be excellent. However, if there are malefic planets <note>Planets like Saturn or Mars that often represent challenges</note> in these aforementioned houses, it signifies a loss of fortune. 

Furthermore, there is a specific rule regarding the planets: if the planets situated in those houses are in their own zodiac sign, a friend’s sign, or their sign of exaltation <note>The position where a planet is at its maximum strength</note>, they will grant exceptionally good results. If they are in their sign of debilitation <note>The position where a planet is at its weakest</note> or other weak states, they will yield ruined or negative results. || 8 ||

->Thus, one should speak of the reversal of fortune for the houses likewise. ||<-
->The difference between the house and the planet in minutes, divided by two hundred, gives the years and so on. || 9 ||<-
->Multiplied by two and divided by sixty, the result is the years and so on.<-
->Then, multiplying by the desired result, the timing for the house of fortune is found. || 10 ||<-

**Commentary—**Now, the author explains the general results of the houses in one and a half verses, beginning with "Bhāva." <term>Bhāva-graha-antara-kalā</term>: take the difference between the house cusp and the planet, and convert that distance into minutes of arc <note>one degree equals 60 minutes</note>. Divide those minutes by two hundred <note>original: "dvi-śatyāptāḥ"</note>. The resulting quotient represents the "years and so forth" <note>original: "samādayaḥ," meaning years, months, and days</note> when an event will occur. These values for years, etc., are to be placed in two positions. In one place, multiply them by two and divide by sixty to get the refined time. By multiplying this by the "desired result," the specific timing for the house of fortune is determined. || 9 || 10 ||

**Vernacular Translation—**Now, the determination of in which year the rise of fortune and other house-related results will occur is explained. Calculate the difference between the house <note>the cusp or starting point of the astrological house</note> and the planets, convert this into minutes, and divide by 200. The result obtained should be known as the years, months, and days. Afterward, to refine the calculation, double the years of the planets and write them down in two separate places. Then, double the years in one place...

...multiply and then divide by 60. ## Then, multiplied by ten times the result and by the rays of the planets... || 11 ||
## From the years arising from the house’s Eight-Fold Strength <term>Ashtakavarga: a system of points used to predict the strength of houses and planets</term>, and from the difference between those planets, the years and time units are determined. Multiplied by the years arising from those specific planets, the results of fortune are thus known there. || 12 ||
## Hear now the results of fortune concerning their positions and the Nine Divisions <term>Navavarga: the nine specific divisional charts used in Vedic astrology to fine-tune predictions</term>.

**Commentary—** Now, the author explains another method for calculating years and other time periods <note>original: "samadyanayana"</note>. "By the result"—meaning the result derived from the difference between the house and the planet—multiplied by ten, and then multiplied by the "rays" <note>original: "rashmi": a specific numerical strength assigned to planets</note> of that specific planet. || 11 || The years arising from the house’s Eight-Fold Strength <note>original: "Ashtakavarga"</note> and those arising from the interval between specific planets—specifically, those generated from the calculation of planetary house boundaries—become the more distinct years and time units. He speaks of this collectively by saying "that specific" <note>original: "tattat"</note>. In this way, the years and other time periods for all houses, multiplied by the years arising from those specific planets, will become clear. || 12 || Now, how should the results be understood there? There are planetary positions and the Nine Divisions <note>original: "Navavargas"</note>; "hear," I shall speak of the fortune related to them—this is the implied meaning.

**Vernacular Translation—** Now another method is described. Take the difference between the planet and the house; multiply that remaining result by ten, and then divide it <note>The Hindi text says "divide" (bhag lena), whereas the Sanskrit text says "multiply" (hata); this reflects a common variation in astrological calculation manuscripts</note> by the rays <note>original: "rashmi"</note> of that planet. The remainder should be known as the time of fortune in years and other units. Alternatively, one should state the result of the rise of fortune based on the years derived from the Eight-Fold Strength <note>original: "Ashtakavarga"</note>. || 11 || In this manner, the timing of the attainment of results for all houses should be stated according to the aforementioned method in connection with the respective lords of those houses. And the specific determination of the house results should be stated through the Nine Divisions <note>original: "Navavarga"</note>. || 12 ||

16. In taking a wife, i.e., marriage. 
17. In the work of writing. 
These are the results of the Sun. || 13 || 14 || 15 ||

If Mercury is in the sixteenth division <term>Shodashamsha: a sub-divisional chart representing general luck and luxury</term>, there will be acquisition of wealth through disputes with relatives, wealth obtained by traveling to other countries, success in land-related matters, victory, gain of knowledge, and an increase in grain. Next, the results for Jupiter in the House of Fortune when in a friend’s sign: 11. Acquisition of knowledge—gaining education. 12. Performing service—professional duties or tasks. 

Finally, the results for Jupiter in a "great friend's" sign <term>Adhimitra: a planet that is exceptionally well-disposed toward the planet in question</term>: 13. Prosperity—various fortunes. 14. Income of wealth through sons and friends. 15. Through women and through one's own business activities—the arrival of wealth. 16. Marriage. 17. Gain of wealth. One should state the results in this order and in this manner. — Verses 29, 30, 31.

**Vernacular Translation**—If Jupiter is in the House of Fortune, the person will be: 1. Prosperous, 2. Happy, 3. Virtuous, 4. Blessed with many gains, 5. Attain the position of a leader, 6. Possess all kinds of wealth. If Jupiter is in an enemy's zodiac sign...

Multiply the planet by its own rays <term>Rashmi: a measure of a planet’s strength or influence</term>, and if a planet is joined in that house of fortune, multiply it by those rays as well. Then, divide the result by three. If there is no remainder, and the planet is in an odd-numbered zodiac sign and in its ninth-part division <term>Navamsha: a 1/9th subdivision of a zodiac sign, used to fine-tune predictions</term> || 38 ||

The results will manifest in the beginning, middle, or end [of life]. In an even-numbered sign and its ninth-part division, it happens in the beginning, middle, and end. In even and odd ninth-parts || 39 ||

In the middle, end, and beginning; and in even signs, in the middle, end, and beginning. If it is in the beginning, middle, or end, such is the character of one's fortune. || 40 ||

If in an odd-numbered sign and ninth-part, [the order is] middle, end, and beginning. If in an even sign and ninth-part, or even in an odd sign, it is in the middle and the end. || 41 ||

Even in the first period of life, in an even sign, it is in the middle, end, and beginning. If two remain, it is one; the time should be understood through reversal. || 42 ||

Similarly, when multiplied by the minutes of arc <note>original: "kala"</note>, if the ninth-part is in a movable sign <term>Chara-rashi: signs like Aries or Cancer that indicate change and movement</term>, it occurs in the beginning, middle, and end. In a fixed sign, it is at the end, middle, and beginning. || 43 ||

**Commentary**—Having thus described the results based on the planets situated in the House of Fortune <note>original: "Bhagya-sthana," the 9th house</note>, the author now explains the timing of the arrival of those results through the variations of the ninth-part divisions <gloss>Navamsha</gloss>. This continues through the middle of verse forty-three. For those signs situated in one’s own House of Fortune—whether the signs or ninth-parts currently occupied are lesser or greater—one should multiply them by their own rays <gloss>Rashmi</gloss>. When a planet is present in the House of Fortune, multiply by the rays of that planet. Subsequently, divide the total by the number three. If the division is complete with no remainder <note>original: "nish-shesha"</note>, and the planet is in an odd sign <note>odd signs include Aries, Gemini, Leo, etc.</note>, the fruit of fortune is known to occur in the beginning, middle, or end of life respectively based on the ninth-part division. Similarly, if it is an even sign with an odd ninth-part, it occurs in the middle, end, and first part. Or, in an even sign, in the middle, end, and first...

# Chapter 13 on the Results of the Minutes of Arc and Divisions, etc. in the Later Section

If the ninth-part <term>Navamsha: a 1/9th subdivision of a zodiac sign</term> is in an even-numbered sign, the signs of fortune manifest at the beginning, middle, or end [of life] in that specific order. Similarly, in an odd-numbered sign <note>original: "Oja-rashi"</note>, the order is middle, end, and beginning. If the ninth-part is in an even sign, or if it is an even-numbered sign and the ninth-part is odd, or if it is an even sign and the ninth-part is even, the result should be understood to manifest during the previously mentioned times. This specific interpretation is to be used when the division by three results in a remainder of zero. However, after dividing by three, if the remainder is one or two, the timing should be understood in the reverse order.

Regarding the time of fortune, if the Ascendant of fortune is in a movable sign <term>Chara-rashi: signs like Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn that indicate action and change</term>, and after multiplying by the minutes of arc <note>original: "kala"</note>—specifically the minutes of the planet combined with the minutes of the house of fortune—and dividing by three as before, the result depends on the sign type. In movable signs, the result occurs at the beginning, middle, and end. In fixed signs <term>Sthira-rashi: signs like Taurus or Leo that indicate stability</term>, the result occurs at the end, middle, and beginning. In dual-natured signs <term>Dvisvabhava-rashi: signs like Gemini or Pisces that have a dual character</term>, the result manifests in the middle, then the end, and finally the beginning. These are the proclaimed effects of the divisions || 37-43 ||

**Commentary**—The timing for when the results of the **House of Fortune** <term>Bhagya-sthana: the 9th house in a horoscope, governing luck and destiny</term> will be obtained is now explained. Multiply the **ninth-part** <term>Navamsha</term> sign of the **House of Fortune** by the **rays** <term>Rashmi: a measurement of a planet's spiritual or mathematical strength</term> of the **House of Fortune**, and then multiply that by the rays of the planet situated in that house. Afterward, divide by three. If the remainder is zero, the results are as follows:

If the **House of Fortune** is in an **odd-numbered sign**, the results manifest in the beginning, middle, and end of life in a chronological order corresponding to the movable signs, etc. If it is an **even-numbered ninth-part**, the results follow the order of beginning, middle, and end. Furthermore, if the sign of fortune is even but the ninth-part is odd, the results manifest in the middle, end, and beginning. If both the sign and the **ninth-part** are even, then the timing is middle, end, and then beginning, followed by the sequence of beginning, middle, and end. This subject is explained clearly in the technical commentary. || 37-43 ||

->In dual signs, the results are in the middle, the end, and the beginning; thus it is proclaimed.<-
->This applies to all the houses, calculated from both the Moon sign and the Ascendant.<- || 44 ||

**Commentary**—Now, the number of brothers and other relatives is explained, starting from the phrase "of the houses" until the end of the chapter. A thorough consideration of all twelve houses should be made from both the Moon's sign <term>Chandra-lagna: the zodiac sign the moon occupied at birth</term> and the Ascendant <term>Janma-lagna: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term>. This should be done by first performing the mathematics as previously described for the life-span based on divisions <term>Anshayurdaya: a specific system of determining longevity and results based on the planetary degrees/divisions</term>. Then, multiply this by the influence of the planets: in one instance, multiply by the benefic <note>original: "shubha"</note> planetary aspects, and in another, by the malefic <note>original: "papa"</note> planetary aspects. In that order, divide the results by sixty and then by the strength of the house <term>Bhava-bala: the calculated potency or "strength" of an astrological house</term>. The resulting quotient should be understood as the remaining number or the lost number <note>likely referring to deceased vs. living relatives</note> of brothers and others. Furthermore, that same calculation from the division of longevity should be multiplied by the rays <term>Rashmi: the "light" or numerical units of planetary influence</term> and then divided by the strength. The result of this indicates the misfortunes, the exceptions, and the auspicious outcomes. || 44 || 45 || 46 || Thus, this commentary on the thirteenth chapter has been composed according to my best understanding. For the pleasure of Lord Ganesha, may the learned scholars correct it with joy. || 1 ||

-> Thus ends the thirteenth chapter in the commentary written by Shridhara, <-
-> the son of Vishnu, a scholar of the Vedas and Astrology of the Dhvangu family, <-
-> in the later part of the Great Parashara [Horoscopy]. || 13 || <-

**Translation in Common Language**—Now the consideration of the twelve houses is described. One should analyze from the Moon's sign and also from the time of birth (Ascendant). First, calculate the life-span based on divisions as before. Note this math in two places: in one place, multiply it by the sum of benefic aspects, and in the other, by the sum of malefic aspects. Then, divide both results by 60. Then, divide by the strength of the house. The remaining number should be known as the count of the relatives associated with that house. In another method, multiply the previously mentioned calculation by the "rays" and divide by the strength of the house. The remainder indicates the auspicious or inauspicious results. || 44 || 45 || 46 ||

-> Thus ends the thirteenth chapter of the illustrious Great Parashara Horoscopy. || 13 || <-

# Later Section: Chapter 14 — Description of the Yearly Cycle #

<page-num>641</page-num>

**Two *nadis* make one *muhurta*; likewise, two *vinadis* are mentioned.** <note>original: "nāḍidvayaṃ muhūrtaḥ syād vināḍidvayam eva ca"</note>
**From the rising of the Sun, starting from Aries, the sequence of the "All-Conqueror" is known. || 1 ||**

**Ardra, Ashlesha, Anuradha, Magha, and then Dhanishta;**
**the one named Uttarashadha, the "All-Conqueror," and then Rohini; || 2 ||**

**Vishakha, then Jyeshtha, Mula, and Shatataraka;**
**Bharani, Purva-Phalguni, and then the "World-Conqueror" follows. || 3 ||**

**Uttara-Proshthapada, then Revati follows thereafter;**
**Abhijit, then Uttara, then Krittika, and then Rohini; || 4 ||**

**Mula, then Rohini, then Mrigashirsha and Hasta;**
**Pushya, Shravana, Hasta, Chitra, and Swati are known in this sequence. || 5 ||**

**Commentary**—Now, in this fourteenth chapter, inspired by Lord Ganesha, I provide this explanation according to my intellect; may the learned scholars refine it. || 1 || Now, the great sage Parasara, in this fourteenth chapter, teaches the "Yearly Course" <term>Varshacharya: the study of planetary influences over the span of a single year</term>.

First, he describes the characteristics of a *muhurta* <term>Muhurta: a traditional unit of Indian time measurement, roughly equivalent to 48 minutes</term> in the first half-verse. Two *nadis* <term>Nadi: also known as a Ghatika, a unit of 24 minutes</term> constitute one *muhurta*. This is the general standard based on a day-length of thirty *ghatikas* (12 hours). 

However, when the day-length is shorter or longer, one must account for the "two *vinadis*" <note>The commentator explains that the length of the *muhurta* must be proportionally adjusted if the sun stays above the horizon for more or less than the standard 12 hours</note>. Specifically, if the day is less than thirty *ghatikas*, the *muhurta* will be two *nadis* minus a certain number of seconds (*palas*); if the day is longer, it will be two *nadis* plus a proportional amount. The same logic applies to determining the *muhurtas* of the night based on the length of the night.

Next, he speaks of the Ascendants <term>Lagna: the sign of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</term> in the second part of the verse. Starting from the rising of the Sun <note>original: "raverudayataḥ"</note>, the twelve signs from Aries <term>Mesha</term> to Pisces <term>Mina</term> occur in sequence until the next sunrise. 

Regarding the thirty names of the constellations associated with the *muhurtas*—fifteen for the day and fifteen for the night—he begins with the "All-Conqueror" <note>original: "Sarvajit"</note> and continues through the middle of the fifth verse. These are called "All-Conquerors" because these daily constellations "conquer" or dominate those specific units of time by giving results consistent with their nature.

# Summary of the Essence of the Great Parasara Horoscopy #

<page-num>650</page-num>

The names of the thirty *muhurtas* <term>Muhurta: A unit of time roughly equal to 48 minutes, consisting of two nadis</term>, which are calculated daily starting from sunrise, are remembered as follows: 1. Ardra, 2. Ashlesha, 3. Anuradha, 4. Magha, 5. Dhanishta, 6. Uttarashadha, 7. Abhijit (specifically known as the "All-Conqueror" or *Sarvajit*), 8. Rohini, 9. Vishakha, 10. Jyeshtha, 11. Mula, 12. Shatataraka, 13. Bharani, 14. Purva-Phalguni, and 15. Vishvajit (also called Abhijit). These fifteen are the names of the daytime *muhurtas*, collectively known as the **Sarvajit** group.

Now, O Twice-born <note>original: "dvija," a term for the initiated or scholarly class</note> Maitreya! The fifteen nighttime *muhurta* names are: 1. Uttara-Proshthapada (Uttara-Bhadrapada), 2. Revati, 3. Abhijit, 4. Uttara, 5. Krittika, 6. Rohini, 7. Mula, 8. Rohini, 9. Mrigashirsha, 10. Hastaka, 11. Pushya, 12. Shravana, 13. Hasta, 14. Chitra, and 15. Swati. These fifteen are the names for the nighttime *muhurtas* of two *nadis* each, collectively known as the **Vishvajit** group. **|| 1–5 ||**

**Commentary** — Now, the characteristics of a *muhurta* are described. A *muhurta* consists of two *ghadis* <term>Ghadika/Nadi: A unit of 24 minutes</term>. There are always exactly 15 *muhurtas* for the day and 15 for the night; this total does not change. While the standard measure is given as two *ghadis*, the actual duration of a *muhurta* will increase or decrease based on the lengthening or shortening of the day <note>This refers to seasonal changes in daylight hours; if the day is longer than 12 hours, each "daytime" muhurta will be slightly longer than 48 minutes</note>.

Now, the characteristics of the *Lagna* <term>Lagna: The rising sign or Ascendant on the eastern horizon</term> are explained. The sign in which the Sun is currently positioned is the *lagna* that rises first at sunrise. Thereafter, in their proper sequence, all twelve zodiac signs pass through until the next morning's sunrise.

As stated, there are 30 *muhurtas* in a full day and night. Their names are:
The fifteen daytime *muhurtas* are called **Sarvajit**:
1. Ardra, 2. Ashlesha, 3. Anuradha, 4. Magha, 5. Dhanishta, 6. Uttarashadha, 7. Abhijit (named Sarvajit), 8. Rohini, 9. Vishakha, 10. Jyeshtha, 11. Mula, 12. Shatataraka, 13. Bharani, 14. Purva-Phalguni, 15. Abhijit. These should be known as the daytime *muhurtas*.

Now, the nighttime *muhurtas* are listed:
1. Uttara-Bhadrapada, 2. Revati, 3. Abhijit, 4. Uttara, 5. Krittika, 6. Rohini, 7. Mula, 8. Rohini, 9. Mrigashirsha, 10. Hasta, 11. Pushya, 12. Shravana, 13. Hasta, 14. Chitra, 15. Swati. These fifteen nighttime *muhurtas* should be known as **Vishvajit**. **|| 1 || 2 || 3 || 4 || 5 ||**

**Commentary** — Thus, the names for the two-*nadi* <term>Nadi: A unit of time equal to 24 minutes; also called a ghatika</term> *muhurtas* and the two-*vinadi* <term>Vinadi: A unit of time equal to 24 seconds</term> *muhurtas* have been stated. <header>Summary of the Great Parashara Horoscopy</header>

# Summary of the Great Parashara Horoscopy

He now describes the sequence of the twelve planets: 1. Moon, 2. Mercury, 3. Venus, 4. Smoke <term>Dhuma: A mathematical "shadow planet" or Upagraha</term> as mentioned in the first half, 5. Sun, 6. The Halo <term>Parivesha: Another mathematical point used in calculations</term> as mentioned in the first half, 7. Mars, 8. The Rainbow <term>Karmuka: A shadow planet</term> as mentioned in the first half, 9. Jupiter, 10. The Node <term>Pata: Specifically referring to Vyatipata, a calculated sensitive point</term> as mentioned in the first half, 11. Saturn, and 12. The Comet <note>original: "Ketu"</note>. 

These twelve planets, in the order stated, occur within the context of the **Zodiacal Degree Divisions** <term>Chakraliptansha: A precise division of the 360 degrees of the zodiac</term> starting from the rising of Leo <note>original: "Simha-lagna"</note> through the twelve rising signs; this means they "rise" at the time of those specific ascendants. 

Similarly, in the context of the **Stellar Portions** <term>Tarakansha: Divisions based on the 27 Nakshatras or lunar mansions</term>, starting from Aries <note>original: "Mesha-lagna"</note>, the sequence begins with Ketu and follows the previously mentioned order in reverse <note>original: "vilo-mata"</note> until reaching the constellation Chitra. 

Furthermore, in the context of the **Hour Divisions** <term>Ghatikansha: Divisions of time where one ghatika equals 24 minutes</term>, the sequence from the Sun to Smoke—following the first mentioned order—is applied to the twelve risings starting from Sagittarius <note>original: "Chapa" or "Dhanu"</note>. || 13-15 ||

**Vernacular Explanation**—The sequence for the daily rising ascendants is now clear in the commentary. Now, the method for determining the twelve **Momentary Planets** <term>Tatkalika Graha: Planets whose positions are calculated for a specific moment, such as birth</term> is described. 

First, one must examine the birth ascendant <note>original: "Janma-lagna"</note> to see if it begins with Leo, Sagittarius, or Aries. Depending on which of the three systems the ascendant falls into, that sequence is considered primary. From that starting point, one assigns the planets in order: 1. Moon, 2. Mercury, 3. Venus, 4. Smoke, 5. Sun, 6. Halo, 7. Mars, 8. Rainbow, 9. Jupiter, 10. Node, 11. Saturn, and 12. Comet. Whatever sign arises, one should place that planet within it. 

For example, if the birth ascendant is Scorpio, it belongs to the "Leo-starting" sequence. Therefore, at that moment, the Moon is assigned to Leo, Mercury to Virgo, Venus to Libra, Smoke to Scorpio, and so on, ending with Ketu in Cancer. 

In the **Constellation Sequence** <note>original: "Nakshatra-krama"</note>, using the Aries-based order, one counts from Ketu toward the Moon until the constellation corresponding to the previous sign is reached. For instance, if one starts counting from Ketu at the constellation Ashwini, the Moon would fall in the fourth quarter <note>original: "charana"</note> of the constellation Uttara Phalguni. Similarly, by calculating for the constellation Purva Bhadrapada a third time, Ketu appears again; if calculated further, Ketu is found in the fourth quarter of Purva Bhadrapada in the sign of Pisces. These specific details are made clear in the specialized commentary. || 13 || 14 || 15 ||

It provides three distinct systems of alignment starting from Leo, Aries, or Sagittarius.</summary>

**Commentary—** Now he describes the duration of the daily experience—the measure of time—for the rising of the aforementioned signs starting from Aries, through to verse eighteen. O Twice-born Maitreya! The daily measure for the rising signs of Aries <note>original: "Mesha"</note> and Pisces <note>original: "Mina"</note> is three and one-third hours. This means three hours and twenty minutes <note>Sanskrit "dvaya" (two) in the commentary likely a typo for "traya" (three) to match the verse "tisrah" and the Hindi calculation of 3:20</note>. For Aquarius <note>original: "Kumbha"</note> and Taurus <note>original: "Vrisha"</note>, the daily measure of experience is four hours. In that same manner, for Capricorn <note>original: "Makara"</note> and Gemini <note>original: "Mithuna"</note>, it is five less one-third. This means four hours and forty minutes <note>Sanskrit "pancacatvarimsat" (forty-five) is likely a typo for "catvarimsat" (forty) to match the "vitryanshah" (1/3rd less) calculation</note>. This should be known as the daily measure. For Cancer <note>original: "Karka"</note> and Sagittarius <note>original: "Dhanus"</note>, the daily measure is clearly stated as five and one-third, which means five hours and twenty minutes. For Leo <note>original: "Simha"</note> and Scorpio <note>original: "Vrishchika"</note>, the daily measure is six hours. For the remaining two—meaning Virgo <note>original: "Kanya"</note> and Libra <note>original: "Tula"</note>—it is seven minus a portion. Here, the word "portion" <note>original: "ansha"</note> refers to one-third of an hour. This means six hours and forty minutes. Thus, the measure for the signs as they rise on the horizon, starting from Aries, has been described. ॥ 16 ॥ 17 ॥ 18 ॥

# In the Later Section, Chapter 14: Description of the Yearly Effects
<page-num>657</page-num>

Famous, victorious, timid, intelligent, wealthy, and well-behaved. One who is devoted to the wives of others <note>original: "paradararataḥ"; a common trope in ancient texts indicating a lack of social restraint</note>, yet prosperous, good-natured, strong, and virtuous. ॥ 23 ॥

A traveler, occupied with the study of the scriptures <note>original: "nigamavyagraḥ"; can also refer to being busy with commerce or traditional laws</note>, a sinner, and yet one who practices penance. Devoted to others' wives, attached to prostitutes, and driven by base desires. ॥ 24 ॥

One who sits upon a throne <note>a metaphor for high status or political power</note>, or one who is destitute; one with matted hair like an ascetic, or a disgrace to his family lineage. A practitioner of yoga <term>Yogi: a spiritual seeker</term>, an enlightened one, a wandering monk <term>Sanyasi: one who has renounced worldly life</term>, a military commander, intelligent, and happy. ॥ 25 ॥

One with a withered hand or suffering from skin diseases, prosperous, and blessed with only one son. An expert in the scriptures <term>Shastras: traditional legal, social, or religious treatises</term>, one who performs the work of a servant, and one possessed of fierce anger. ॥ 26 ॥

Brave, a hero, fierce in temperament, and capable, yet suffering from diseases of the stomach. A village leader, a sensualist, a rogue, the husband of a virtuous woman, and a subduer of foes. ॥ 28 ॥

The husband of a barren woman, a drinker of wine, the master of failed or empty goals, and yet happy. Victorious in life but afraid of battle; a thief, intolerant of others, and an earner of wealth. ॥ 29 ॥

One who constantly performs hundreds of misdeeds for the sake of earning money. The husband of a low-born woman, a lordly figure like the god Indra, a commander, truthful, and pure. ॥ 30 ॥

# Final Section, Chapter 14: Description of the Movement of the Celestial Sphere

**Vernacular Commentary**—Now, the fruits of the combinations <term>Yogaphala: the karmic results of specific planetary alignments</term> based on the ten divisional charts <term>Dashavarga: a system of ten sub-charts used in Vedic astrology for fine-tuning predictions</term> are explained. These names of the Yogas are clearly written in the scholarly commentary, so they are not repeated here in the vernacular language. || 21–38 ||

These 155 Yogas, starting from "The Fortunate One" <note>Shriman</note> up to "The Learned One" <note>Vidvan</note>, have been described. One should count starting from the "Fortunate One" yoga if the Ninth-Division <term>Navamsha: a 3°20' subdivision of a sign</term> falls in an odd-numbered zodiac sign. If it is an even-numbered sign, the sequence should be understood as starting from the "Learned One" yoga and moving backwards to "The Fortunate One." In moveable signs, follow the regular order; in fixed signs, follow the reverse; in dual-natured signs, start the sequence from the midpoint. || 39–40 ||

> Rahu moves backwards from Aries; Ketu moves forwards from Taurus. || 41 ||

**Scholarly Commentary**—Now he describes the movement of Rahu and Ketu with the verse beginning "From Aries." Rahu, from the sign of Aries <gloss>original: "Meṣarāśisakaśāt"</gloss>, moves in a reverse or retrograde motion <gloss>original: "viparītagatikrameṇa"</gloss>. Similarly, Ketu moves from the sign of Taurus <gloss>original: "Vṛṣarāśeḥ sakāśāt"</gloss> in a direct or forward motion <gloss>original: "anulomagatikrameṇa"</gloss>. || 41 ||

**Vernacular Commentary**—Now the movement of Rahu and Ketu is explained: Rahu travels in reverse order starting from Aries, and Ketu travels in forward order starting from Taurus. || 41 ||

> One born at the junction of the stars, or one who asks a question then, surely perishes.
> Death occurs if the junction of signs falls where Ketu and Rahu are situated. || 42 ||
> In the presence of the other three, one is afflicted by disease.
> If they do not die, they become weak and devoid of intelligence. || 43 ||

**Scholarly Commentary**—He explains the purpose of the aforementioned rules with the verse beginning "At the junction." During the junction of the stars <gloss>original: "ṛkṣasandhyantare"</gloss>—which refers to the transitional entry point of Rahu and Ketu—if a questioner <gloss>original: "praṣṭā"</gloss> or a newborn <gloss>original: "jātaśca"</gloss> is situated there, they certainly <gloss>original: "bhṛśam iti niścayena"</gloss> perish or meet with ruin. Furthermore, death occurs for the questioner at the junction of the signs <gloss>original: "rāśisandhiḥ"</gloss> when that junction is occupied by Ketu and Rahu. Likewise...
