**Commentary—** Even so, having heard the inquiry, the sage begins to explain the remedy in the four verses starting with "In the Krita age..."

O best of the twice-born <term>Dvija: "twice-born," a term for members of the three upper social classes in traditional India who have undergone spiritual initiation</term> Maitreya! In the Krita Age <term>Satya Yuga: the first and most perfect age of the world</term>, because righteousness was complete, all people were filled with the power of spiritual penance <term>Tapas: intensive meditation or austerity that grants spiritual power</term>. For this reason, they "knew"—meaning they instinctively understood—this scripture. Through that power, they perceived the past, the present, and the future.

Following that, in the Treta Age <note>the second age</note>, certain Brahmins <note>priests and scholars</note> who practiced penance knew it; however, not everyone possessed this knowledge. In the Dvapara Age <note>the third age</note>, people perceived it through a combination of penance and the study of the scriptures. Thus, in these three ages, there were those who properly understood this science. 

In this current Age of Discord <term>Kali Yuga: the current age of spiritual decline</term>, righteousness stands on only one of its four pillars <note>original: "dharma-pada-matra-vyavasthitih," an image of a bull representing Righteousness losing its legs as the ages progress</note>. Therefore, without the power of penance, humans on earth are not capable of knowing this scripture. For this reason, your question is entirely appropriate. || 2 || 3 || 4 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** Parashara says: O Maitreya! In the Satya Age, all people lived in a state of penance. For this reason, they knew this scripture and could speak of the three divisions of time <note>past, present, and future</note>. Afterward, in the Treta Age, people lived with penance, and some Brahmins knew it, but not everyone. In the Dvapara Age, they perceived it through penance and the study of the scriptures. In this way, there were excellent knowers of this science in those three ages. In this Kali Age, righteousness has remained in only one-fourth of its strength. Because of this, without the power of penance, humans on earth are not capable of knowing this science; therefore, your question is correct. || 2 || 3 || 4 ||

And here, the Supreme Lord Shiva <note>original: "Shambhu"</note>, desiring to bless the worlds, ||
Focused upon His own energy <note>original: "Shakti"</note> and established this knowledge. || 5 ||
Even in the Kali Age, it grants devotees the knowledge of the three times <note>past, present, and future</note>. ||
Like a cow yielding the milk of speech from the Vedas, it speaks non-dual truth from the mountain. || 6 ||
To attain supreme divine power, this mantra of the "Essence of Speech" <note>original: "Vagbhava-manu"</note> should be used: ||
Place the word "All-knowing" <note>original: "Sarvajna"</note> first, then "O Master" <note>original: "Natha"</note>, then "O Lord of Parvati" <note>original: "Parvatipate"</note>. || 7 ||
Then "O Guru of all the worlds" <note>original: "Sarvalokaguro"</note>, followed by the two syllables "Shiva." ||
Then the word "Refuge" <note>original: "Sharanam"</note>, and finally, "I have surrendered to You" <note>original: "Tvam prapanno'smi"</note>. || 8 ||

<summary>Sage Parashara explains that while ancient people knew astrology through spiritual merit, modern people in the Kali Yuga require a specific mantra dedicated to Lord Shiva to gain the same insight. He outlines the structure of this sacred chant intended to grant "tri-kala-jnana" or knowledge of past, present, and future.</summary>

<header>Concluding Section, Chapter 18: Inquiry</header>
<sig>47</sig>

**Commentary—** Now the means of attaining knowledge is described through the following eight and a half verses. Seeing humans on this earth with diminished understanding, the Supreme Sadashiva <term>Sadashiva: the eternal, auspicious form of the Divine, often viewed as the source of all knowledge</term>, desiring to bless the world and act for the benefit of others, focused upon his own power of knowledge and formulated the Primal Wisdom. 

*The construction of the mantra is as follows:* First is the beginning of the Vedas <note>the sacred syllable Om</note>, then the seed-syllable of speech <note>original: "Vagbhava-bija," the syllable Aiṁ</note>, then the address "O Gauri," then the doubled word "Speak, Speak" <note>original: "Vada Vada"</note>, then "Giri" <note>meaning speech or the mountain-goddess</note>, followed by the phrase "for the purpose of attaining supreme lordship," and concluding with the syllable "Aiṁ."

->“Oṁ Aiṁ Gauri Vada Vada Giri Parameśvarya-siddhyartham Aiṁ”<-

This is the Mantra of Power <term>Shakti Mantra: a sacred formula dedicated to the feminine creative energy of the universe, intended to awaken the intellect</term>. Next, the construction of the Shiva Mantra: First is the word "All-knowing," then the word "Lord," then the phrase "Husband of Parvati," then "Teacher of all worlds," then the name "Shiva," then the word "Refuge," then the phrase "I have surrendered to you," then "Protect," then "Knowledge," and finally the word "Grant."

->“All-knowing Lord, Husband of Parvati, Teacher of all worlds, Shiva, I have come to you for refuge; protect me and grant me knowledge.”<-

This is the clear conclusion of the mantra. These two—the Shakti and Shiva mantras—were created as the "Great Wisdom" <term>Mahavidya: a term for highly potent systems of mantra and meditation</term> for the sake of mastering the science of astrology. || 5 || 6 || 7 || 8 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** Now the remedy for attaining knowledge is told. Seeing humans with inferior knowledge in this world, the supreme Sadashiva, for the sake of helping others, remembered his power of knowledge and created this wisdom. Both the Shakti and Shiva mantras are clearly shown:

->“Oṁ Aiṁ Gauri Vada Vada Giri Parameśvarya-siddhyartham Aiṁ”<-

This is the Mantra of Power. Now the Shiva mantra is told:

->“All-knowing Lord, Husband of Parvati, Teacher of all worlds, Shiva, I have come to you for refuge; protect me and grant me knowledge.”<-

This is the spoken Shiva mantra. || 5 || 6 || 7 || 8 ||

The word "Protect" and then "Grant knowledge" follows thereafter.
The Seer <term>Rishi: the sage who first 'saw' or received the mantra</term> is Dakshinamurti <note>the form of Shiva who teaches in silence, facing South</note>; the Goddess is Gauri. || 9 ||
The deity is the All-knowing Shiva, and the meter is said to be Gayatri <term>Gayatri Chhandas: a classical poetic meter of twenty-four syllables, regarded as the mother of the Vedas</term>.

<header>Summary of the Great Parashara Hora</header>

## Summary of the Great Parashara Hora

The meter is Anushtup, and there are six ritual limbs [for placement], beginning with the heart, using the seed-syllable of speech. || 10 ||
By these two mantras, O best of the twice-born <note>meaning the Brahmins, specifically Maitreya</note>, the intellect becomes stainless.
By mere recitation, success is achieved, and the status of an astrologer <note>original: "daivajñatva," the quality of a knower of fate</note> is illuminated. || 11 ||

**Commentary—** Now, it is well known in the sacred traditions <note>the Tantras</note> that without remembering the Seer (*Rishi*) and other ritual details, success with a mantra is impossible. Without ritual placement <term>Nyasa: the practice of "placing" parts of the mantra on different parts of the body to sanctify the practitioner</term>, the mantra remains like a serpent <note>meaning it is either dormant, dangerous, or slippery to hold</note>. Without meditation (*Dhyana*), the desired goal cannot be achieved. Therefore, the author describes the Seers and other details from verse eleven onwards. 

For these two mantras, the Seer is Dakshinamurti <term>Dakshinamurti: an aspect of Shiva as the supreme universal teacher of yoga, music, and wisdom</term>. The deities are Gauri Paramesvari <note>the Great Goddess</note> and the All-knowing Shiva. The meters are Gayatri and Anushtup. The placement on the heart and the fingers is to be done with the "Vagbhava" seed-syllable, which is **Aiṁ**. 

O best of the twice-born! By the recitation of these two mantras according to this method, the intellect becomes pure. Success is achieved through mere recitation—preliminary rites <note>original: "purashcharana," intensive preparatory rituals</note> are not strictly required here. By this, the status of an astrologer shines forth, meaning one's skill in providing answers to queries <note>original: "prashna-kathana-patavam," the ability to read a moment in time</note> increases. || 9 || 10 || 11 ||

**Language—** Now the Seer, Deity, and Meter for both the Shakti and Shiva mantras are stated.
> “The Seer of these two mantras is Dakshinamurti; the Deities are Gauri Paramesvari and the All-knowing Shiva; the meters are Gayatri and Anushtup; the application is for the attainment of knowledge in the science of astrology, which reveals the three divisions of time.” <note>original: "anayoḥ mantrayoḥ dakṣiṇāmūrti-ṛṣiḥ gaurī parameśvarī sarvajñaḥ śivaśca devate gāyatry-anuṣṭubhau chandasī mama trikāl-adarśaka-jyotiḥśāstra-jñāna-prāptaye jape viniyogaḥ"</note>

After reciting this dedication <term>Viniyoga: a formal statement of intent made before beginning a mantra</term>, one should perform the placement on the fingers and the heart using the seed-syllable **Aiṁ**. O Maitreya! By performing the preparatory rites for these two mantras, a stainless intellect and the true knowledge of astrology will be revealed. || 9 || 10 || 11 ||

Under a single tree in a garden on the snowy Himalayas, O twice-born, 
[Visualize] the decorated Gauri playing, dressed in white, with a pure smile. || 12 ||
There in the forest of pines, [visualize Shiva] with eyes stilled in meditation, 
Four-armed, three-eyed, with matted hair and the crescent moon upon his head. || 13 ||

**Commentary—** Now the meditation is described in these two and a half verses. "In a garden," meaning a grove, "under a single tree," specifically at the base of a great Banyan tree, "on the snowy [mountains]," meaning the Himalayas...

...on a supreme seat—this is the implied meaning. In that garden, one should also meditate on the Great God <note>original: "Mahadeva," a primary title for Shiva</note>, the supreme Lord who controls all, who is the best among all gods. His eyes are stilled in meditation, his gaze closed in contemplation. He is three-eyed, four-armed, wearing matted hair, with the moon upon his forehead. Thus should one meditate. || 12 || 13 ||

**Vernacular Language Translation**—Having performed the ritual placements <note>Nyasa</note> in this manner, the meditation on Shakti <note>the feminine power</note> and Shiva is described. Upon the Himalayan mountains, there is a great garden. Within it stands a Banyan tree. Beneath its shade, upon an excellent seat, one should meditate on Gauri. She appears beautiful, wearing white garments, her face graced with a holy smile, as she engages in play. In that same garden, one should meditate on Mahadeva, who has closed his eyes in meditation. He has three eyes and four arms, wears matted hair, and is beautified by the moon on his forehead. His complexion is white. He is the controller of all, the most excellent, the best among all gods—the manifest Supreme Absolute. || 12 || 13 ||

> One should meditate on the white-colored Mahadeva, the supreme Lord. 
> Having mastered the two-fold mathematics and reflected upon the branches and the trunk [of the Veda] || 14 ||
> Having heard the meaning of the sections of the horary limb and grasped it, 
> the excellent twice-born <note>original: "dvija-varo," referring to the learned Brahmin class</note> who is eloquent—his speech shall never be barren. || 15 ||

**Commentary**—Now, the author describes the qualifications of the calculator <note>original: "ganaka," meaning the astrologer/mathematician</note> in the section ending with verse fifteen. He who has mastered the two-fold mathematics—concerning the celestial sphere <term>Khagola: the study of the heavens and planetary motions</term> and the terrestrial sphere <term>Bhugola: the study of the earth and geography</term>—and has reflected upon the "branches and trunk" <note>the various subdivisions of Vedic and astrological knowledge</note>, and has heard the two types of the "horary limb" <term>Hora-skandha: the branch of astrology dealing with individual birth charts and time</term> from the mouth of his teacher—meaning he has studied them—and has determined their true meaning: such a person becomes a "best among the twice-born" who is eloquent in speech. This does not apply to Jain or Shudra astrologers <note>This reflects the historical sectarian competition and social hierarchy of the era in which the commentary was written</note>. The speech of such a qualified practitioner is never barren; it never fails to come true. || 14 || 15 ||

**Vernacular Language**—Now the characteristics of an astrologer are described. A man who understands geography <note>original: "bhugola"</note>, astronomy <note>original: "khagola"</note>, and mathematics, and who has thoroughly learned the two divisions of horoscopy <term>Jataka: the branch of astrology dealing with individual birth charts</term> from the mouth of a teacher, and speaks with refined speech after careful consideration—such a person is an excellent fate-knower <note>original: "Daivajña," an astrologer or diviner</note>. It is specified that he should be of the Brahmin class, and not an astrologer from the Jain or Shudra communities. The speech of such an astrologer never fails to come true. || 14 || 15 ||

**Non-greedy, devoted, pure, endowed with humility and modesty. Gems, gold, wealth, clothing, or even flowers, roots, and fruits... || 16 ||**

**Commentary**—Now the characteristics of the querent <note>the person asking the question; original: "prashtuh"</note> are stated with a verse and a half. The one who asks should be devoted, honest, sincere, and possessed of humility. They should be free from greed and should offer the astrologer some item such as a fine gem, gold, money, or clothing. If they are unable to provide these, they may offer a flower, a root, or a fruit. Placing this before the astrologer, they should ask their desired question with a joyful heart, and not with a mind saddened by the act of giving. || 16 ||

**Vernacular Language**—The querent should be devoted, sincere, humble, and free from greed. They should take gold, gems, clothing, or grain in their hand. If they are poor, they should take any item among flowers, fruits, or roots, place it before the astrologer, and with a happy mind, ask the question they desire. || 16 ||

**Having given these before the astrologer, one should ask their desire with a happy heart. Now, sitting facing East, purified before the deity and the fire... || 17 ||**
**One should draw four lines horizontally and four lines vertically, straight as cords. One should then merge the four central squares into one... || 18 ||**
**There, one should draw a lotus with a pericarp <note>the seed vessel at the center of the lotus</note> in the middle of the lines. Starting from the Northeast corner, the zodiac signs beginning with Pisces follow in order. || 19 ||**

# Concluding Section: Chapter 18 on Questions

The paths <term>Vithi: specific groupings of zodiac signs used to determine directions or the flow of events</term> of Aries are Taurus and the signs following it; those of Gemini are Scorpio and its followers. The paths of Pisces and Aries [form a set], and Libra and Virgo belong to the path of Taurus. || 20 ||

Calculate the distance from the Arudha <term>Arudha: the 'mounted' sign, determined by where a seeker stands or a random number chosen</term> to the sign of the path (Vithi); that same distance from the Ascendant (Lagna) determines the "Umbrella" <note>original: "Chhatram"</note> sign. If the Arudha sign is the same as the Ascendant, then that itself becomes the Umbrella. || 21 ||

Whatever outcomes have been described in the science of birth horoscopy <term>Jataka: natal astrology</term> based on the birth chart, the wise astrologer should apply all those same principles to the query chart at the time the question is asked. || 22 ||

**Commentary**—Now the duty of the knower of fate <note>original: "Daivajña," the astrologer</note> is described up until the twenty-second verse. After the question is posed, the astrologer, being in a state of purity and sitting facing the East, should draw four straight lines—horizontal and vertical—in front of him to create a grid. He should unify the four central squares. In that center, he should draw a lotus <note>a symbolic representation of the heart or the divine center</note> with its central seed-head. Then, starting from the Northeast corner, he should write the zodiac signs in order, beginning with Pisces. In this system, the paths of Aries are Taurus and those following it, and the paths of Gemini are Scorpio and those following it. The paths of Pisces and Aries [are linked], and for Taurus, the paths are Libra and Virgo. Having calculated the distance from the Arudha to the Vithi sign, that same distance from the Ascendant determines the Umbrella sign. If the Arudha and Ascendant are the same, that is the Umbrella. After considering this, the wise one should proclaim all results from the Ascendant of the query time, just as one would from a birth chart. || 17 || 18 || 19 || 20 || 21 || 22 ||

**Vernacular Language**—Now the duty of the astrologer is stated. After the seeker <note>original: "pṛcchaka"</note> has asked a question, the astrologer should sit facing East in a state of purity and draw the zodiac chart <note>original: "rashichakra"</note> as shown below. Drawing a lotus in the middle, he should consider the Arudha Lagna. The direction in which the seeker is sitting or the sign they touch should be known as the Arudha sign among the twelve signs. In the four signs starting with Taurus, one should know the Aries-Path <note>original: "Meshavithi"</note>. In the four signs starting with Scorpio, one should know the Gemini-Path. In the signs of Aries, Pisces, Virgo, and Libra...

->Summary of the Great Parashara Hora<-

To know the path of Taurus: Calculate the number of signs from the Arudha <term>Arudha: the sign determined by the seeker's position or a chosen number</term> to the sign representing the Path (*Vithi*). Count that same number of signs from the current Ascendant <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</term>; the resulting sign is known as the "Umbrella" sign <note>original: "Chhatra-rashi"</note>. || 17-22 ||

### For the duration that the Ascendant remains, within that timeframe, ||
### one should determine the longevity of the person based on the strength of the planets. || 23 ||
### The first and last decans <term>Drekkana: a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</term> respectively ||
### become the bringers of death for Capricorn, Scorpio, Cancer, and Pisces, based on the Arudha sign. || 24 ||

**Commentary**—Now, the author explains the determination of the life span and the results of the decans from the Arudha sign in two verses. As long as the Ascendant is active, during that period, when a question regarding the determination of the life span is asked, the decision regarding longevity is made based on the strength of those planets. This means the life span is judged by planetary power. || Now, for Capricorn, Scorpio, Cancer, and Pisces: if the Ascendant falls in the first decan of these signs relative to the Arudha, it becomes a giver of death. || 23-24 ||

**Vernacular Commentary**—Now the determination of the life span and the results of the decans are described from the Arudha sign. The determination of the life span is said to last as long as the duration of the current Ascendant. For Capricorn, Scorpio, Cancer, and Pisces, if the first or last decan is rising from the Arudha, that Ascendant should be known as a cause of death. || 23-24 ||

### If the Ascendant is a back-rising sign and malefic planets ||
### are situated in the fourth, seventh, or twelfth houses; ||
### and if Mars or Saturn are in the second or ninth houses, ||
### while the Moon is in the eighth house, death occurs. || 25 ||

**Commentary**—Now the signs of death are described. When the sign rising at the time of the query is a "back-rising" sign <term>Prishthodaya: signs like Aries, Taurus, or Cancer that are said to rise with their backs first, often viewed as less auspicious</term>, and if cruel <note>original: "krura," referring to malefic planets like Sun, Mars, or Saturn</note> planets are placed in the fourth, seventh, or twelfth houses from that Ascendant; and further, if Mars or Saturn are in the second or ninth houses, and the Moon is in the eighth house <note>original: "randhra," a technical name for the 8th house associated with death and vulnerabilities</note>, then death will occur. || 25 ||

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions for horary astrology (Prashna) from the previous discussion on "Umbrella" signs and longevity. It shifts focus specifically to the "indications of death" (Marana Yoga) based on the positions of malefic planets and the timing of Rahu.</meta>

<page-num>743</page-num>
->**Section: On Questions, Chapter 18**<-

**Vernacular Commentary**—Now the characteristics of death are described. If there is a "rear-rising" sign <term>Pristhodaya Lagna: zodiac signs that appear to rise from their back, traditionally considered less auspicious in certain queries</term> at the moment of the query, and malefic planets <term>Papagraha: planets like Mars, Saturn, Rahu, and Ketu</term> are situated in the 4th, 7th, or 12th houses from the Ascendant, or if Mars is in the 2nd or 9th house while the Moon is in the 8th house, then death is indicated. || 25 ||

> If a *Durudhara* yoga <term>Durudhara Yoga: a planetary combination formed when planets occupy the signs on both sides of a specific point, in this case, the Moon or Ascendant</term> is formed by malefic planets, and if the Moon is in the Ascendant, the 7th, or the 4th house, or if the Sun is in the Ascendant, the person will die a painful death due to disease. || 26 ||

**Commentary**—Now another combination for death is described with the verse starting with "By malefics" <note>original: "papaih"</note>. When a *Durudhara* yoga is formed by malefic planets, or when the Moon is in the birth Ascendant or in the 7th or 4th houses, or when the Sun is in the horary Ascendant <term>Prashna Lagna: the zodiac sign rising at the exact moment the question is asked</term>, death occurs severely due to illness. Furthermore, if there is a conjunction with the "Time of Rahu" <term>Rahu Kaal: an inauspicious period of the day ruled by the shadow planet Rahu</term> at the moment of the query, death will certainly occur. || 26 ||

**Vernacular Commentary**—Now another combination for death is described. If a *Durudhara* yoga of malefic planets occurs in the horary Ascendant or the birth Ascendant, or if the Moon is in the 7th or 4th houses, or if the Sun is in the horary Ascendant and there is a conjunction with *Rahu Kaal* at the time of the query, then death occurs due to the cause of a disease. || 26 ||

> Death is certain during the conjunction of *Rahu Kaal*. Rahu moves in reverse order starting from Aries, while *Kaal* <note>the personification of Time/Death</note> moves in regular order starting from Taurus. || 27 ||
> In every zodiac sign, the period of transit is fifty *Vinadikas* <term>Vinadika: a traditional unit of time equal to 24 seconds</term>. Both Rahu and *Kaal* consume this time repeatedly, starting from sunrise. || 28 ||
> The specific timings for Rahu starting from Sunday onwards are stated as one, twenty-one, four, three, six, and eight *Nadikas* <term>Nadika: a unit of time equal to 24 minutes</term> respectively; his movement at night is described similarly. || 29 ||
> Rahu moves in reverse from the East, and *Kaal* moves in the regular direction. Both move through all twelve signs in the span of one and a half *Vinadikas*. || 30 ||
> They are positioned across the directions and houses belonging to Indra, the Moon, Fire, the Demon, Yama, the Lord of Waters, the Wind, and the Lord of Wealth <note>referring to the guardians of the eight directions</note>, and are located in the centers of the malefic planets. || 31 ||

Rahu moves in reverse order <term>Viloma-rītyā: backward or retrograde motion</term> starting from Aries <note>Meṣa</note>. At the same time, "Time" <term>Kāla: a personified mathematical point used in calculation</term> moves in the regular order starting from Taurus <note>Vṛṣa</note> through the twelve signs. In each zodiac sign, the period of occupancy <term>Bhoga-kāla: the duration a planet "enjoys" or stays in a particular segment</term> is fifty *vinadikas* <term>Vināḍikā: a unit of time approximately equal to 24 seconds</term>.

Starting from sunrise, both Rahu and Time move through the signs again and again. Starting from Sunday, the duration of Rahu's influence over the seven days of the week is respectively: 1, 2, 4, 3, 5, 6, and 8 *ghatikas* <term>Ghaṭikā: a unit of time equal to 24 minutes</term>.

Both of them move through all twelve zodiac signs in a period of two and a half *ghatikas* <note>sārdha-ghaṭikā-dvayena</note>. In that context, Rahu moves toward the left <note>vama</note> through the directions; this connects with the second half of the thirty-fifth verse.

<header>Section on Questions (Prashna), Chapter 38 of the Latter Part</header>

Rudra, the Moon, Indra, Fire, the Demon, the Wind—or rather, the Demon, the Moon, Indra, the Lord <note>original: "Isha" (Shiva)</note>, the Purifier <note>Agni</note>, the Ender <note>Yama</note>, and the Lord of Waters <note>Varuna</note>. Rahu moves through these directions in order across the seven days of the week, starting with Sunday. || 27–34 ||

**Vernacular Commentary**—Now, the method for knowing the combinations for the "Time of Rahu" <term>Rāhukāla: an inauspicious period of the day ruled by the shadow planet Rahu, traditionally avoided for starting new projects</term> is described. Rahu moves in the order of Aries, Pisces, and Aquarius <note>this is a reverse or retrograde zodiacal movement</note>. Time <term>Kāla: here refers to a personified mathematical point used alongside Rahu for calculation</term> moves in the regular order of Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer. In each zodiac sign, the period of occupancy <term>Bhoga-kāla: the duration a planet "enjoys" or stays in a particular segment</term> is fifty *palas* <term>Pala: a traditional unit of time equal to 24 seconds</term>. In this manner, both Rahu and Time repeatedly traverse the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</term> and other points. 

Because of this, during the seven days of the week starting from Sunday <note>ruled by the Sun</note>, Rahu's influence lasts for 1, 2, 4, 3, 5, 6, and 8 *ghatis* <term>Ghaṭī: a unit of time equal to 24 minutes</term> respectively. At night, Rahu traverses the East, Northeast, North, and Northwest in sequence. Similarly, "Time" moves through the East, Southeast, South, and Southwest. The duration of stay for each of these in any single direction is 2 *ghatis* and 30 *palas*. The previously mentioned duration of 50 *palas* refers specifically to the time spent in the Ascendant. The specific directions occupied during each weekday are clarified in the technical commentary. || 27–34 ||

> Starting from Sunday, Rahu moves in reverse order through the directions:
> The Lord <note>Northeast</note>, the Wind <note>Northwest</note>, the Moon <note>North</note>, Fire <note>Southeast</note>, the Ender <note>South</note>, the Demon <note>Southwest</note>, and the Waters <note>West</note>. || 35 ||
> Based on the Lunar Mansion <term>Nakṣatra</term>, the Weekday, and the Lunar Day <term>Tithi</term>, in both reverse and forward order,
> Rahu and Time move from the last to the first and the first to the last respectively.
> When they both coincide, death is predicted; when only one is present, illness is said to occur. || 36 ||

**Technical Commentary**—Now the author explains the sequence of directions based on the Lunar Mansions, the Weekdays, and the Lunar Days—beginning with the word "Rudra" and spanning two verses. Regarding the Lunar Mansion, Weekday, and Lunar Day: 
- "Rudra" represents the Northeast <note>Ishanya</note>.
- "The Wind" <note>Samira</note> represents the Northwest <note>Vayu</note>.
- "The Moon" <note>Soma</note> represents the North <note>Uttara</note>.
- "Fire" <note>Agni</note> represents the Southeast <note>Agneya</note>.
- "The Ender" <note>Yama</note> represents the South <note>Dakshina</note>.
- "The Demon" <note>Nirriti</note> is self-evident <note>Southwest</note>.
- "The Waters" <note>Jalam</note> represent the West <note>Pashchima</note>. 

In these directions, Rahu moves in reverse order starting from the last, while Time moves in forward order starting from the first, beginning with the first lunar mansion <note>Ashvini</note>, the first weekday <note>Sunday</note>, and the first lunar day <note>Pratipat</note>. Thus, both move through the directions. In this movement, if one of these factors (Lunar Mansion, Day, or Date) coincides with the position of Rahu or Time, it results in illness; if two factors coincide, it is said to result in death. || 35–36 ||

**Vernacular Commentary**—Now, the movement of Rahu and Time <term>Kāla: a personified mathematical point used in divination</term> is described according to the sequence of constellations <term>Nakshatra: the 27 lunar mansions</term>, lunar days <term>Tithi: a day in the lunar month</term>, and weekdays. They move through seven directions:
1. North-East <note>original: "Ishana"</note>
2. North-West <note>original: "Vayu"</note>
3. North <note>original: "Uttara"</note>
4. South-East <note>original: "Agni"</note>
5. South <note>original: "Dakshina"</note>
6. South-West <note>original: "Nairitya"</note>
7. West <note>original: "Pashchima"</note>

The movement is calculated from the first constellation <note>Ashwini</note> to the current one, from Sunday to the current day, and from the first lunar day <note>Pratipada</note> to the current one. Rahu moves in reverse order, starting from the West and South-West. Time moves in the starting order, beginning with the North-East and North-West. If these two forces coincide at one point in the calculation of the lunar day and other factors, it indicates disease <term>Vyādhi: sickness or physical distress</term>; if they coincide at two points, it indicates death. || 35–36 ||

The values for the houses are: Kings (16), Faintings (21), Arrows (5), Elements (25), Lunar Days (15), sixteen (16), and five (5). 
These apply to the second through the eighth houses, and the values between them are determined by proportion. || 37 ||

For the zodiac signs starting from Aries, the "rays" <term>Rashmi: a numeric value representing the strength or influence of a sign or planet</term> are declared as: Serpents (8), Years (8), Arrows (5), Qualities (3), Rudras (11), Horses (7), Vedas (4), Limbs (6), Rows (10), ten (10), five (5), and eight (8). || 38 ||

If there is one overlap among all these factors, disease occurs; with two, death occurs. 
However, if any "Wealth Combinations" <term>Lakshmī-yoga: auspicious planetary alignments that indicate prosperity and protection</term> are present, the disease may or may not occur even with one overlap. || 39 ||

**Scholarly Commentary**—Now, he describes the rays from the second house to the eighth house: "Kings" refers to the number 16. Specifically:
- Second House: 16
- Third House: 21 <note>original: "murcha" (fainting/senses)</note>
- Fourth House: 5 <note>original: "shara" (arrows)</note>
- Fifth House: 25 <note>original: "tattva" (the primary elements of reality)</note>
- Sixth House: 15 <note>original: "tithi" (lunar days)</note>
- Seventh House: 16
- Eighth House: 5

Regarding the houses between these, their values should be taken according to proportion, a subject already clarified in the previous section on rays. || 37 ||

Next, he describes the rays for the zodiac signs starting with Aries over a verse and a half. The numerical values are:
- Aries: 8 <note>original: "naga" (serpents)</note>
- Taurus: 8 <note>original: "abda" (years)</note>
- Gemini: 5 <note>original: "ishu" (arrows)</note>
- Cancer: 3 <note>original: "guna" (qualities)</note>
- Leo: 11 <note>original: "rudra" (forms of Shiva)</note>
- Virgo: 7 <note>original: "vaji" (horses)</note>
- Libra: 4 <note>original: "veda" (sacred scriptures)</note>
- Scorpio: 6 <note>original: "anga" (limbs/limbs of the Vedas)</note>
- Sagittarius: 10 <note>original: "pankti" (rows/decades)</note>
- Capricorn: 10
- Aquarius: 5
- Pisces: 8

These numeric values for the rays are proclaimed in order for the signs from Aries onwards. If Rahu and Time align within these, it results in death from disease. Similarly, an alignment of one factor among all these causes disease. || 38 ||

Now, he states an exception to this in the final half-verse. Even when an overlap occurs among the previously mentioned factors, if "Wealth Combinations" <note>Lakshmi-yoga</note> are present, the disease might only occur sometimes, or not at all. || 39 ||

### Chapter 18: On Queries — Latter Section

**Vernacular Commentary—** Now, the divisions of time are described according to the <term>Nakshatra-paratva</term><note>the sequence or precedence of the constellations</note>. One should understand the twenty-seven divisions of time, corresponding to the parts of the body from the head down to the feet, starting from the constellation <term>Ashwini</term> and ending with <term>Revati</term>. || 46-47 ||

The thighs, the knees, the shanks, the ankles, and the feet correspond in order starting from the Ashvini constellation.
If the <term>Prashta</term><note>the querent; the person asking the astrological question</note> is smeared with oil, or is physically "unclean," or is standing near a pool of water—
Or if the <term>Daivavid</term><note>the astrologer or "knower of fate"</note> himself is in such a state, then one should predict the death of the patient. || 48 ||
Benefic planets located in the first, third, fifth, seventh, sixth, ninth, tenth, or eleventh houses from the query ascendant bring about the healing of disease—
Unless they are situated in the signs of their enemies or in their signs of debilitation. || 49 ||

**Scholarly Commentary—** The author describes the knowledge of bad omens regarding the querent: "Smeared with oil" refers to one who has rubbed oil on their body; "unclean" refers to one in a state of <term>Sutaki</term><note>ritual impurity following a birth or death in the family</note>; and "near a pool" refers to being in the vicinity of a lake or reservoir. If the querent is in this state at the time of the query, or if the <term>Jyotishi</term><note>astrologer</note> himself is in such a state, then one must predict the death of the person the question is about. || 48 || Now, the author discusses the effects of "benefic" and "malefic" planets in the houses of the query chart: If <term>Shubha-grahas</term><note>benefic planets, typically Jupiter, Venus, a waxing Moon, or well-associated Mercury</note> are in the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th, 6th, 9th, 10th, or 11th houses, they grant relief from disease. However, this is only if they are not in the signs of their enemies or in their signs of debilitation. Conversely, if <term>Papa-grahas</term><note>malefic planets, such as Saturn, Mars, or Rahu</note> are in these same houses, they cause death—unless those malefic planets are positioned in their own zodiac signs, their signs of exaltation, or the signs of their friends. || 49 ||

**Vernacular Commentary—** Now the bad omens of the querent are described. If a person asks a question while having bathed in oil, while in a state of ritual impurity, or while sitting near a pool of water—or if an astrologer possessing these same traits answers the question—one should know that the patient will die. || 48 || Now, the auspicious or inauspicious nature of the medical query is described: if benefic planets are in houses 3, 5, 6, 9, 10, or 11 from the query ascendant, the disease will be cured. If malefic planets are in these houses, death will occur. However, this result only holds true if the benefics are not in debilitated positions and the malefics are not in exalted positions. || 49 ||

In these houses, malefic planets cause death unless they are in their own signs, signs of exaltation, or signs of friends.
Whether it be for good or ill, planets situated in the <term>Rihpha-sthana</term><note>the 12th house of the zodiac, often associated with loss, hidden things, or the end of life</note> are generally considered auspicious in this context. || 50 ||

### Summary of the Great Parashara Horoscopy

**Scholarly Commentary—** Now the author describes another set of auspicious and inauspicious conditions with the two half-verses beginning with "Whose..." For any individual, if benefic <term>Grahas</term><note>planets</note> are situated in the <term>Rihpha</term><note>the 12th house</note> or in the <term>Trikona</term><note>trines; the 1st, 5th, and 9th houses</note> or <term>Kendra</term><note>angles; the 1st, 4, 7th, and 10th houses</note>—specifically in the 9th, 5th, 1st, 4, 7th, or 10th houses—then good fortune follows for that person, because these planets are "givers of the auspicious" or grantors of benefit. || 50 ||

**Vernacular Commentary—** If at the time of birth or at the time of a query, benefic planets are located in the 12th, 9th, 5th, 1st, 7th, or 10th houses, the result is beneficial. || 50 ||

> Or if situated in the trines or angles, they grant auspiciousness to that person.
> From Capricorn or Cancer onwards, the Sun [determines the solstice]; from the first or second halves of the signs—
> Saturn, Venus, Mars, the Moon, Mercury, and Jupiter [determine the seasons] beginning with the dewy season. || 51 ||

**Scholarly Commentary—** Now the author explains how to determine the <term>Ayana</term><note>solstice</note> and <term>Ritu</term><note>season</note> at the time of a query. "From Capricorn and Cancer onwards" means that if the Sun is currently in the six signs starting from Capricorn, it is <term>Uttarayana</term><note>the Northern Solstice</note>. Similarly, if the Sun is in the six signs starting from Cancer, it is <term>Dakshinayana</term><note>the Southern Solstice</note>. This solstice is understood through the <term>Prashna Lagna</term><note>the rising sign at the moment of the query</note> or the birth chart.

Next, regarding "from the first or second halves of the signs," this is what is being said: In the six signs from Capricorn onwards, if a planet is in the first half of the sign, or in the six signs from Cancer onwards, if a planet is in the second half of the sign, the <term>Ritu</term><note>season</note> at birth is determined by five-degree divisions of the sign in the sequence of <term>Shishira</term><note>the dewy season or late winter</note> and so on.

Specifically:
*   If Saturn is in the first half of Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces, Aries, Taurus, or Gemini, it indicates the **Dewy Season** (<term>Shishira</term>).
*   If Venus is there, it is **Spring** (<term>Vasanta</term>).
*   If Mars is there, it is **Summer** (<term>Grishma</term>).
*   If the Moon is there, it is the **Rainy Season** (<term>Varsha</term>).
*   If Mercury is there, it is **Autumn** (<term>Sharad</term>).
*   If Jupiter is there, it is **Early Winter** (<term>Hemanta</term>).

The same sequence applies to Saturn and the others if they are in the second half of the six signs starting from Cancer. This planetary combination should be understood as the indicator of the season specifically for the query or birth ascendant. For example, if the birth or query ascendant is Capricorn and one of these planets like Saturn is in its first half, the season is understood to be the dewy season. This applies similarly to any of the six signs starting with Cancer when a planet is in the second half. || 51 ||

**Vernacular Commentary—** Now the method for knowing the solstice and season at the time of a query or birth is described. From the sign of Capricorn through the next six signs, if the Sun is present, it is the Northern Solstice. From Cancer through the next six signs...

# Chapter on Queries in the Latter Section, 18. ( 751 )

If the Sun is so placed, know it to be the <term>Dakshinayana</term><note>the Southern Solstice, when the Sun moves south of the celestial equator</note>. Now, the knowledge of the seasons is explained: if Saturn is in the first half of the <term>Prashna-lagna</term><note>the ascendant at the time of a query</note> or the <term>Janma-lagna</term><note>birth ascendant</note>—specifically in Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces, Aries, Taurus, or Gemini—then know it to be the <term>Shishira</term><note>Dewy or Late Winter</note> season. Similarly, if Venus is so placed, know it is Spring; if Mars, know it is Summer; if the Moon, know it is the Rainy season; if Mercury, know it is Autumn; and if Jupiter, know it is <term>Hemanta</term><note>Early Winter</note>. In this same manner, if Saturn and the other planets are in the latter half of Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, and Sagittarius, know the seasons as previously stated. This method is largely used for the subject of <term>Nashta-patrika</term><note>the reconstruction of lost birth charts</note>. || 51 ||

**If the Sun is present, it is Summer; or by the others in turn; or the season is from the solstice. ||**
**Venus, Mars, Saturn, the Moon, Mercury, and Jupiter are rotated. || 52 ||**

**Scholarly Commentary—** Regarding the verse beginning with "If the Sun": If the Sun is in the query ascendant, it is the Summer season. From there, the other seasons follow the other planets in sequence. This is what is meant: if any one of the six planets from the Sun to Venus is in the ascendant, the seasons from Summer onwards occur in order. Alternatively, the knowledge of the seasons is derived from the solstice based on the Sun’s position beginning with Capricorn or Cancer, as previously mentioned. Furthermore, if there is no planet in the ascendant, the author says: "Venus, Mars, etc." Venus, Mars, Saturn, the Moon, Mercury, and Jupiter are the <term>Drekkana-patis</term><note>lords of the decans; a decan is a 10-degree division of a zodiac sign</note> of the ascendant. When these are applied, the season is determined through the sight of the decan. Or, according to another opinion, the season is determined by the <term>Navamsha</term><note>the ninth-part subdivision of a sign</note> occupied by the query ascendant, following the rules previously described. || 52 ||

**Vernacular Commentary—** If the Sun is in the query ascendant, know it is Summer; if the Moon, know it is the Rainy season; if Mars, Autumn; if Mercury, Early Winter; if Jupiter, Late Winter; and if Venus, know it is Spring. Alternatively, Venus, Mars, Saturn, the Moon, Mercury, and Jupiter are the lords of the ascendant's decans; the seasons from Summer onwards should be known by their order. Or, the season can be known through the sequence of the <term>Navamsha</term><note>the 9th-part division</note>. || 52 ||

**The lords of the ascendant's decans are declared; or others say by the ninth-part divisions. ||**
**The two months are before and after that; the lunar date comes from the onset of the season. || 53 ||**

**Commentary—** Now, the knowledge of the month and the lunar day is explained in the following half-verse. The "prior and subsequent" months are derived from that [season]. **Vernacular—** Now the knowledge of the month and lunar day is stated. Alternatively, in the first half of Summer is Jyeshtha and in the second half is Ashadha—this is a different scholarly opinion. The lunar day is known by this same proportion, based on the elapsed and remaining parts of the season. || 53 ||

->If Jupiter is placed in a trine from the ascendant, or if it is in its Navamsha,<-

**Commentary—** Now, the year of birth is explained based on the query ascendant. If Jupiter (<term>Jiva</term>) is in a <term>Trikona</term><note>a trine; the 1st, 5th, or 9th house</note> from the query ascendant, then the birth year is known to be the time when Jupiter was last in that particular sign. If Jupiter is not in a trine, then the birth occurred when Jupiter was in the sign corresponding to its <term>Navamsha</term><note>the ninth-part harmonic division of a sign</note>. 

But what if the person is more than twelve years old? To this, it is said: determine the years by estimating the person's age. For instance, if Jupiter's Navamsha sign is Aries, and currently Jupiter is in Taurus, and the person appears to be over twelve years old, one should estimate and declare the birth year as the previous time Jupiter was in Aries (its second cycle). Likewise, if the estimated age is over twenty-four, the birth is known from Jupiter's presence in Aries during its third cycle back. In this same manner—

In the case where the estimated age is over thirty-six, the birth year is determined by the fourth cycle of Jupiter <note>Jupiter returns to the same zodiac sign every 12 years; the fourth cycle would correspond to ages 36–48</note> when the Sun was in Aries. ## One should contemplate the hour from the minutes up to the half-hour as stated. ||
## Setting aside the ascendant <term>Lagna</term> <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of the query</note> converted into minutes, multiply it again by its multipliers. || 60 ||
## Multiply this by the multiplier of whichever is stronger between the Arudha and the Chhatra. <note>The 'Arudha' is the sign corresponding to where the querent is standing or a direction they point to; 'Chhatra' (literally 'umbrella') is a mathematical point derived from the sun's position and the query time.</note> ||

**Commentary**—Now, the determination of months and other time units is stated through another method, starting from the phrase "Setting aside the minutes" up to the middle of verse sixty-one. Then, multiply it by the multipliers of whichever is the stronger between the Arudha and the Chhatra signs. If the result is odd <note>original: "विषमे" (vishame)</note>, the addition of the separated part should be performed. If it is even, then there is a subtraction from the result of the separated part. This is the method for its calculation. Then, by dividing that total by the respective parts—by twelve for the months, by thirty for the days, and so on—the months and other units are calculated as per the previously mentioned method. || 60 || 61 ||

**Vernacular**—Now, the knowledge of months and other units is explained via another method. Write down the ascendant <term>Lagna</term> in two places, convert the value into minutes, and multiply it by its own multiplier. Then, multiply it by the multiplier of whichever is stronger between the Arudha and Chhatra points. If the result is odd, add it to the separated value. If it is even, subtract it from the separated value. Afterwards, divide the result by 12 to determine the month. If divided by thirty, the result indicates the day. || 60 || 61 ||

### The Moon, the Sun, the Teacher <note>original: "Acharya" — referring to Jupiter</note>, Venus, and the Knower <note>original: "Jna" — referring to Mercury</note> cast a quarter-sight on the houses of "Friends" and "Action" <note>The 3rd and 10th houses</note>. ###
### Saturn, however, casts a full sight on these, while all planets cast a half-sight on the houses of "Piety" and "Sons" <note>The 9th and 5th houses</note>, though Jupiter casts a full sight there. || 66 || ###
### All planets cast a half-sight on "Kinship" and "Death" <note>The 4th and 8th houses</note>, but the Son of the Earth <note>original: "Bhumija" — referring to Mars</note> sees them with a full sight. ###
### Others cast a three-quarter sight on these, and all planets cast a full sight on the seventh house. || 67 || ###

**Commentary**—Now the author describes the "aspects" <term>Drishti</term> <note>The mathematical glance or influence one planet casts upon another or a specific house</note> of the planets in two verses. The Moon, Sun, Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury, as well as Mars, cast a "quarter-sight" <note>A 25% strength aspect</note> on the third and tenth houses. Saturn, however, sees the third and tenth houses with a "full sight" <note>A 100% strength aspect</note>. Similarly, all planets cast a "half-sight" <note>A 50% strength aspect</note> on the ninth and fifth houses, but Jupiter sees these two locations with a full sight. In the same way, regarding the houses of "Kinship" and "Death" (the fourth and eighth), Mars sees them with a full sight, while all other planets see these two locations with a "three-quarter sight" <note>A 75% strength aspect</note>. Finally, all planets, from the Sun to Saturn, cast a full sight on the seventh house. || 66 || 67 ||

**Vernacular Translation**—Now the planetary aspects are described. The Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus look upon the 3rd and 10th houses with a quarter-sight; Saturn looks upon the 3rd and 10th houses with a full sight. All planets look upon the 9th and 5th houses with a half-sight, but Jupiter looks with a full sight. Similarly, Mars looks upon the 4th and 8th houses with a full sight, while other planets look with a three-quarter sight. And all seven planets, starting with the Sun, look upon the 7th house with a full sight. || 66 || 67 ||

### When situated in its exaltation, root-trine, friend’s sign, its own sign, its own decan, or its own ninth-division, ###
### a planet gains "Positional Strength." Mars and the Sun gain strength in the tenth house; Saturn in the seventh; || 68 || ###
### Mercury and Jupiter in the Ascendant; and the Moon and Venus in the house <note>The 4th house</note>. ###
### These are endowed with "Directional Strength" <term>Dig-virya</term>; this applies specifically to the work of queries <term>Prashna</term>, and not elsewhere. || 69 || ###

**Commentary**—Having described the "Aspect Strength" <term>Drig-bala</term> of the planets, the author now describes "Positional Strength" <term>Sthana-bala</term> and "Directional Strength" <term>Dig-bala</term> in two verses. When a planet is in its sign of exaltation <term>Uccha</term>, its root-trine <term>Mula-trikona</term>, a friend's sign, its own zodiac sign, its own decan <term>Drekkana</term>...

It specifically identifies which houses grant planets "Positional" and "Directional" strength within the context of horary astrology.</summary>

While the previous page focused on the "aspects" or mathematical glances (Drishti) that planets cast upon specific houses, this page defines the various categories of "Virya" or "Bala" (strength). Specifically, it details the positional, directional, and temporal factors that make a planet powerful enough to yield results in a horary chart—a chart cast to answer a specific question.</meta>

<header>Essence of the Great Parashara Horoscopy</header>

...in its own ninth-part division <note>original: "Svanavamshake" — a 3°20' subdivision of a sign</note>. This phrase uses the singular form to represent a collection. It should be understood that a planet situated in these specific places possesses "Positional Strength" <term>Sthanavirya</term> <note>The power a planet gains based on its specific location in the zodiac</note>. Now, regarding "Directional Strength" <term>Digvirya</term>: if the Sun and Mars are in the tenth house from the query-ascendant, Saturn in the seventh, Mercury and Jupiter in the first house <note>the Ascendant</note>, and the Moon and Venus in the fourth house, these planets are considered to possess "Sight-Strength" <note>original: "Drigvirya" — here used interchangeably with directional potency</note> in the context of horary astrology. This specific rule does not apply to other astrological branches. || 68 || 69 ||

**Interpretation**—The author now describes the Positional Strength <term>Sthanabala</term> and Directional Strength <term>Digbala</term> of the planets. If a planet occupies its own sign, its sign of exaltation, its primary "root-trine" <term>Mulatrikona</term> <note>A highly favorable area within certain signs</note>, or the sign of a friend or a "great friend," and if it is in its own ninth-part <term>Navamsha</term> or its own third-part <term>Drekkana</term>, then it is said to have Positional Strength. 

Now for Directional Strength: in the chart for a query <note>Prashna-lagna</note>, the Sun and Mars are strong in the 10th house. Saturn is strong in the 7th house. Mercury and Jupiter are strong in the 1st house. The Moon and Venus are strong in the 4th house. This specific distribution of directional strength is intended for the practice of answering questions <term>Prashna-karma</term>. It should not be applied to general birth charts <note>Jataka</note> or for selecting auspicious timings for rituals <note>Muhurta</note>. || 68 || 69 ||

> The Moon, Sun, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus are powerful when located in the six signs starting from Capricorn <note>Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces, Aries, Taurus, and Gemini</note>. Mars and Saturn, however, are strong in the six signs starting with Cancer <note>Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, and Sagittarius</note>. || 70 ||

**Commentary**—The author now describes Equinoctial Strength <term>Ayanabala</term> <note>Strength derived from a planet's declination or its position relative to the celestial equator</note>. If the five planets—Sun, Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus—are in the six signs from Capricorn through Gemini, they possess Equinoctial Strength. If Mars and Saturn are in the six signs from Cancer through Sagittarius, they are considered strong in this regard. || 70 ||

> Benefic planets are strong during the bright fortnight <note>the waxing moon</note>, and malefic planets are strong during the dark fortnight <note>the waning moon</note>. Retrograde planets <note>planets that appear to move backward from Earth's perspective</note> are also strong, possessing the strength of motion <term>Cheshthabala</term>. || 71 ||
> 
> Benefics are strong during the day and malefics are strong at night, respectively. Natural strength <term>Nisargabala</term> is determined as previously stated. These rules are to be applied in the work of horary queries. || 72 ||

<header>Second Part: Chapter on Queries 18.</header>

**Commentary**—The author now describes the strengths derived from the lunar fortnight, motion, day/night, and nature <term>Nisarga-bala</term> <note>original: "Paksha-chesta-diva-ratri-nisarga-balani"</note> in two verses. In the context of a query, one should know "Fortnight Strength" <term>Paksha-bala</term> as follows: Benefic planets <note>original: "Shubha" — generally Jupiter, Venus, Mercury, and the Waxing Moon</note> are strong during the "Bright Fortnight" <note>original: "Shukla-paksha" — the period of the waxing moon</note>, while Malefic planets <note>original: "Papa" or "Khala" — generally Saturn, Mars, and the Sun</note> are strong during the "Dark Fortnight" <note>original: "Krishna-paksha" — the period of the waning moon</note>.

Next, "Motional Strength" <term>Chesta-bala</term> is explained: planets in retrograde motion <term>Vakrin</term> <note>appearing to move backward from Earth's perspective</note> are considered to be endowed with this strength. 

Then, "Day-Night Strength" <term>Diva-ratri-bala</term> is described: Benefics are strong during the day, and Malefics are remembered as being strong at night, respectively. 

Natural Strength <term>Nisarga-bala</term> should be understood as previously described <note>this refers to the inherent brightness/power of planets: the Sun is strongest, followed by the Moon, Venus, Jupiter, Mercury, Mars, and Saturn</note>. Thus, the "Sixfold Strength" <term>Shadbala</term> used in the practice of query-astrology has been declared. || 71 || 72 ||

**Vernacular Interpretation**—Now the Fortnight Strength is stated: Know that Benefics are powerful in the light half of the month, and Malefics are powerful in the dark half. Now for Motional Strength: Retrograde planets are to be known as possessing Chesta-strength. Now for Day-Night Strength: Benefics are strong during the day, and Malefics are strong at night. Natural strength is as before. In this way, the six types of planetary strength at the time of a query are explained. || 71 || 72 ||

## The Ascendant, the Hour, the Third, the Twelfth-part, the Ninth-part, the Seventh-part; || 73 ||
## The Sixteenth-part, the Hour-of-Time, the Thirtieth-part, and the Sixtieth-division;
## Each preceding one is said to be strong, while each succeeding one is less strong.

**Commentary**—The author now describes the strength of the "Ten Divisions" <term>Dashavarga-bala</term> in one and a half verses. 
1. The Ascendant <term>Lagna</term> 
2. The Hour-division <term>Hora</term> (1/2 of a sign) 
3. The Third-division <term>Drekkana</term> (1/3 of a sign) 
4. The Twelfth-part <term>Arka/Dwadashamsha</term> (1/12 of a sign) 
5. The Ninth-part <term>Navamsha</term> (1/9 of a sign) 
6. The Seventh-part <term>Saptamsha</term> (1/7 of a sign) 
7. The Sixteenth-part <term>Kalansha/Shodashamsha</term> (1/16 of a sign) 
8. The Time-Hour-part <term>Kalahoramsha</term> 
9. The Thirtieth-part <term>Trimshamsha</term> (1/30 of a sign) 
10. The Sixtieth-division <term>Shashtibhagaka</term> (1/60 of a sign). 

Among these ten divisions, each earlier one <note>original: "Purva-purva"</note> is declared stronger than the one that follows it <note>original: "Uttara-apekshayā"</note>. Conversely, each succeeding one is "not strong" <note>original: "na bali"</note>, meaning it possesses less strength than the one before it. This concludes the explanation of the strength of the Ten Divisions. || 73 ||

**Vernacular Interpretation**—Now the descending order of strength for the Ten Divisions is stated: 1. Ascendant, 2. Hora, 3. Drekkana, 4. Dwadashamsha, 5. Navamsha, 6. Saptamsha, 7. Shodashamsha, 8. Kalahoramsha, 9. Trimshamsha, 10. Shashtyansha. These should be known as progressively weaker in strength. || 73 ||

## Convert the Query-Ascendant into minutes, multiply by nine, and divide by the signs; || 74 ||
## The result is the Ninth-part to be known, while the remainder stays in its own place.

<meta>This page transitions from the calculation of planetary strengths (Shadbala) discussed on page 759 to the application of "Horary Astrology" or Queries (Prashna). Specifically, it deals with "Lost Horoscopy"—the mathematical art of reconstructing a person's birth details (Birth Ascendant and Birth Star) using only the time a question is asked.</meta>

<page-num>760</page-num>
<header>Essence of the Great Parashara Horoscopy</header>

### The quotient multiplied by seven and divided by four gives the remainder, which is the degree here. || 75 ||
### The birth ascendant is similar to the ninth-division, or the remainder when multiplied by three and divided by twelve.
### The remainder when divided by seven is the ascendant in the seventh month, if certain. || 76 ||

**Commentary**—Now, the author explains how to determine the birth ascendant <term>Janma Lagna</term> <note>the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note> from the query ascendant <term>Prashna Lagna</term> <note>the zodiac sign rising when the seeker asks the question</note> through three verses. 

First, convert the query ascendant into minutes of arc <term>Kala</term> <note>a mathematical step to turn degrees/minutes into a single total of minutes</note>. Multiply this by nine, then divide by twenty-seven. The resulting quotient is known as the "ninth-division" <term>Navamsha</term> <note>a 3°20' segment of a zodiac sign used for precision</note>. Set aside the remainder. 

Then, multiply the number of the ascendant sign by seven and divide by four. The resulting quotient indicates the ninth-division designation of the birth ascendant. 

Alternatively, take the previously set-aside remainder, multiply it by three, and divide by twelve; the remainder from this calculation should be understood as the birth ascendant. 

Another method: divide the remainder by seven; the result indicates the ascendant for the seventh month of pregnancy. If that zodiac sign is occupied by a benefic planet <note>original: "Shubha-graha" — usually Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury</note>, then it should be recognized as the "Action Star" <term>Karma-nakshatra</term> <note>the 10th lunar mansion from birth, relating to one's profession</note> or the "Birth Star" <term>Janma-nakshatra</term> <note>the lunar mansion the moon occupied at birth</note>. || 74 || 75 || 76 ||

**Vernacular**—Now the time of birth is described through the query. Convert the query ascendant into minutes and multiply by nine, then divide by twenty-seven. The quotient obtained is the ninth-division. Keep the remainder aside. Then, multiply the quotient by seven and divide by four. This quotient is the ninth-division. The birth ascendant is known through this ninth-division. Alternatively, multiply that remainder by three and divide by twelve. That remainder is the birth ascendant. Or, divide the remainder by seven; the result is the ascendant in the seventh month. If it is a sign of a benefic planet, then it is the "Action Star" or "Birth Star." || 74 || 75 || 76 ||

### If a benefic planet is present, it is the Action Star or Birth Star that is powerful.
### This science <term>Shastra</term> has been told by me from beginning to end to you, O man of good vows. || 77 ||
### It should never be given to a non-disciple, nor ever to one who is not a son.

This knowledge, which is called a Limb of the Vedas <term>Vedanga</term> <note>original: "Vedanga"; one of the six auxiliary disciplines used to support Vedic rituals, specifically astrology/astronomy</note>, must be given with great care only to a student who is endowed with virtue and good character, and who is twice-born <note>original: "dvijataye"; referring to those initiated into Vedic study</note>. || 78 ||

->Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, titled "On Queries,"<-
->in the Second Part of the Great Parashara Horoscopy.<-

**Commentary—**Now, the author concludes by establishing this science as a Limb of the Vedas and stating the qualifications for studying it, using two verses. O Maitreya, you of excellent conduct! This science of stars <term>Jyotish-shastra</term>, in its entirety from beginning to end, has been told to you. It should never be given to a non-disciple—meaning a bad student—nor to a non-son—meaning a wicked son. Because this science is supreme, it is excellent for revealing the "three times" <note>past, present, and future</note>. Furthermore, it is a Limb of the Vedas, an integral part of the Vedic body, and because it is rooted in the Vedas, it is respected by all. || 77 || 78 || Thus, in the sage-transmitted lineage of Horoscopy spoken by the teacher Parashara, I have explained the eighteenth chapter of the second half. Thus concludes the eighteenth chapter, titled "On Queries," in the *Subodhini* commentary composed by the astrologer Shridhara on the Second Part of the Great Parashara Horoscopy.

**Translation—**Now the status of the science as a Limb of the Vedas is established. O Maitreya! This science of stars, from beginning to end, should never be given to a wicked son or a bad disciple. It should be given with effort only to one who is virtuous and well-behaved. This science grants knowledge of the three times. It is the most excellent Limb of the Vedas, acting as the "eyes of the Veda" <note>a traditional metaphor where Jyotisha is the sight of the personified Veda</note>. It is rooted in the Veda and is therefore universally respected. || 77 || 78 || Thus ends the eighteenth chapter in the Great Parashara vernacular commentary.

<header>Latter Section, Chapter 19: Description of the Sequence of Chapters (763)</header>

### Latter Section, Chapter 19: Description of the Sequence of Chapters

There are five chapters on the combinations for long life and similar matters; then come the Royal Yogas <note>original: "raja-yoga"; planetary combinations indicating power, status, or success</note>; then the consideration of planetary states; then the method for sub-periods <note>original: "antardaya-vidhi"</note>; then the results of the major periods in seven chapters; then the sub-periods in thirteen chapters; then the characteristics of the royal divisions; and then the strength of the remaining combinations is explained. In this way, the eighty chapters of the First Part, which make known the stated subjects, are recounted in order. Such is the sequence of the First Half. || 1 || 2 || 3 || 4 || 5 || 6 || 7 ||

**Language—** Now, in this nineteenth chapter, the subject sequence of the First Part and the Latter Part is being stated. In the first chapter, the origin of the science was told. In the second, the manifestation of the Sun and other planets. In the third, the nature of Aries and the other zodiac signs. In the fourth chapter, the description of planetary aspects <note>original: "drishti"; how planets "look at" or influence other positions</note>. In the fifth chapter, the determination of conception. In the sixth chapter, the regulations for childbirth. In the seventh chapter, combinations for misfortune <note>original: "arishta-yoga"; combinations suggesting early death or illness</note>. In the eighth chapter, the consideration of the son, mother, and father. In the ninth, the consideration of maternal uncles and others. In the tenth chapter, the consideration of the cancellation of yogas <note>original: "yoga-bhanga"; when a negative influence is neutralized or a positive one is blocked</note>. In the eleventh chapter, the consideration of the shadow planets <note>original: "dhuma-adi"; mathematical points like 'Smoke' used in calculations</note>. From the twelfth chapter up to the twenty-third chapter (across twelve chapters), the mixed results, the results of the five limbs of the calendar <note>original: "panchanga"; the traditional almanac</note>, the results of the significator planets, and the results of the twelve houses are told. 

There are six chapters for the results of combinations of two or more planets, and then the description of the Eight-fold Strength <note>original: "ashtakavarga"; a system of points used to calculate planetary strength</note>. In the 20th chapter, the description of celestial combinations <note>original: "nabhasa yoga"</note>. After that, the consideration of combinations for long life in 5 chapters; further, the description of Royal Yogas; then the consideration of planetary states in 1 chapter. Following that, the method for sub-periods in one chapter; the results of the period-givers in seven chapters; the consideration of sub-periods in 13 chapters; the characteristics of the royal divisions in 1 chapter; and then, in the remaining chapters, the strength and weakness <note>original: "balabala"</note> regarding combinations and other matters is considered. Thus, the sequence of the 80 chapters of the First Part has been told. || 1 || 2 || 3 || 4 || 5 || 6 || 7 ||

Then, in the Age of Iron <note>original: "Kali Yuga"</note>, the following was declared: in the first, the Eight-fold Strength <note>original: "ashtakavarga"</note>. || 8 ||
In the second, the strength of the houses and aspects, and then the strength of auspicious and inauspicious points. 
In the fourth, the manifestation of rays <note>original: "rashmi"; a measure of planetary influence</note> and the auspicious and inauspicious results, O Best of the Twice-born <note>original: "dwijottama"; a respectful address to a Brahmin or someone of high spiritual learning</note>. || 9 ||

<header>The Essence of the Great Parasara Horoscopy</header>

In the fifth chapter, a partial aspect of the journey of life <note>original: "loka-yātrā"; referring to the course of human affairs and worldly conduct</note> is discussed; thereafter, in the eighth, the interruption <note>original: "bhaṅga"</note> of those same partial aspects of life's journey. || 10 ||

In the ninth, the journey of life; in the tenth, the major planetary periods <note>original: "dāya"; another term for "daśā," the system of timing events in a person's life</note>; then in the next chapter [the eleventh], the sub-periods <note>original: "antar-dāya"</note>; and then the general subject of these periods follows. || 11 ||

In the thirteenth, fortune <note>original: "bhāgya"</note> and the results of the Kalāmśa <note>original: "kalāṃśa"; a specific harmonic division of a zodiac sign</note> and other divisions are explained, O Twice-born <note>original: "dvija"; a title for the upper castes, here addressing the student Maitreya</note>. In the fourteenth, know the "year-course" <note>original: "abda-caryā"; the study of annual solar returns</note> and what follows. || 12 ||

Next come the results of the year-course; then the results of the month-course <note>original: "māsa-caryā"</note>; then the day-course <note>original: "dina-caryā"</note>; and finally, it speaks of query-horoscopy <note>original: "praśna-jātaka"; the branch of astrology that answers specific questions based on the time they are asked</note>. || 13 ||

Finally, in the twentieth chapter, O Twice-born, the sequence of chapters and the fruits <note>the benefits or results</note> of this science are given. Thus, this "Hundred Chapters of Horoscopy" <note>original: "Horā-śatādhyāyī"</note> destroys all sins. || 14 ||

It provides visible, direct results throughout all the four ages <note>original: "yuga"; the cycles of time in Hindu cosmology</note>. || 15 ||

### Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, titled "Description of the Sequence of Chapters," in the Latter Section of the Great Parasara Horoscopy. || 19 ||

**Commentary—** Now, the index for the second half is being stated with the phrase starting with "In the Kali Age" <note>referring to verse 8 of this chapter</note> across seven and a half verses. After the description of the first half, the sequence of what was spoken in the second half regarding men in the Kali Age <note>the current age of spiritual decline</note> is as follows:

In the first chapter, the Eight-fold divisions <note>original: "aṣṭakavarga"; a system for calculating the strength of planets based on their positions relative to others</note>. In the second, the strength of the Houses <note>original: "bhāva"</note> and planetary aspects. In the third, the strength of auspicious and inauspicious influences. In the fourth, the manifestation of "rays" <note>original: "raśmi"; a technical measure of planetary power</note> and the results produced by them. In the fifth, a portion of the journey of life. In the sixth and seventh, the interruption of that journey. In the eighth, again a partial aspect of life's journey. In the ninth, the journey of life in full. In the tenth, the major planetary periods. In the eleventh, the sub-periods. Then, the twelfth chapter covers the subject of these periods. 

In the thirteenth chapter, fortune and the results of divisions such as the Kalāmśa and the sixteenth-part division <note>original: "ṣoḍaśāṃśa"</note>. O Twice-born! Know that the year-course is in the fourteenth. After that, in the fifteenth chapter, the results of said year-course. Next, in the sixteenth chapter, the results of the month-course. Then, in the seventeenth, the day-course. Then, in the eighteenth chapter, it surely speaks of—that is, explains—query-horoscopy. After that, the nine... <note>the text cuts off mid-sentence while describing the 19th chapter</note>

<header>Latter Section: Chapter 19, Description of the Chapter Index</header>

# Latter Section: Chapter 19, Description of the Chapter Index

In the nineteenth chapter, the sequence of chapters—the index—is given, O Twice-born <note>original: "dvija"; a title for the upper castes, here addressing the student Maitreya</note>! In the twentieth, the fruits <note>the benefits or results</note> of the science are told. In this way, in the science of horoscopy <term>horā-śāstra</term>, this work consisting of one hundred chapters, including the first and second halves, destroys all sins for both the reader and the listener. In all four ages <note>the Yugas or world-cycles: Satya, Treta, Dwapara, and Kali</note>, it gives direct results; it provides the fruit of knowledge where even the unseen is perceived as if it were directly before one's eyes. || 8 || || 9 || 10 || 11 || 12 || 13 || 14 || 15 ||

---

->This explanation was composed in the nineteenth chapter according to my best understanding.<-
->May Ganesha, the giver of intellect, be forever pleased with me. || 1 ||<-
->Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, titled "Description of the Chapter Sequence,"<-
->in the *Subodhini* <note>The "Easy to Understand" commentary</note> written for the Latter Section of the *Great Parasara Horoscopy*.<-
->It was composed by the astrologer Shridhara, son of Jatashankar, of the Dhoreya family,<-
->aided by Shri Krishna. Shridhara is one whose fame illuminates the circles of the ten directions<-
->through his flawless knowledge of the Vedic sciences.<-

---

**Vernacular Commentary**—Now the sequence of the Latter Section is stated. In the first chapter, the consideration of the eight-fold strength <term>aṣṭakavarga</term>; in the second, the strength of the houses <term>bhāva-bala</term> and the strength of aspects; in the third chapter, the consideration of propitious and unpropitious factors <term>iṣṭa-kaṣṭa</term>; and in the fourth chapter, the manifestation of planetary rays, and the strength of propitious and unpropitious factors. In the fifth chapter, the consideration of the happiness and sorrow of the people; in the sixth and seventh, the cancellation <note>original: "bhanga"; the breaking or reversal of planetary combinations</note> of those states; in the eighth chapter, the journey of life <note>original: "loka-yātrā"; worldly affairs and conduct</note>; in the ninth chapter, the journey of life continues. In the tenth chapter, the consideration of the major planetary periods <term>dāya</term>; in the eleventh chapter, the consideration of sub-periods; in the twelfth chapter, subjects relating to planetary periods; in the thirteenth chapter, the consideration of fortune, and the results of the Kalāmsha <note>the 16th division of a sign</note> and other divisions, including the results of the Shodashāmsha. In the fourteenth chapter, the consideration of the "year-course" <note>annual solar return predictions</note>; in the fifteenth chapter, the results of the year-course; in the sixteenth chapter, the monthly course; in the seventeenth, the daily course; in the eighteenth chapter, the science of queries <note>horary astrology, or answering specific questions</note>; in the nineteenth chapter, the index of the book; and in the twentieth chapter, the declaration of the results of the science. 

Whosoever reads or listens to this science of horoscopy, which consists of one hundred chapters including the first and second halves, will have their sins destroyed. It gives direct results in all four ages, and it is especially effective in this present Age of Darkness <note>original: "kali-yuga"</note>. || 8 || || 9 || 10 || 11 || 12 || 13 || 14 || 15 ||

->Thus ends the nineteenth chapter in the Great Vernacular Commentary. || 19 ||<-

It emphasizes that the completed 100-chapter work provides direct spiritual and practical benefits, especially in the current Kali Yuga.</summary>

<header>The Essence of the Great Parashara Horoscopy</header>
